a0poster -- Support for designing posters on large paper
--------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/a0poster
name:             a0poster
caption:          Support for designing posters on large paper
author:           Gerlinde Kettl
author:           Matthias Weiser
copyright:        Gerlinde Kettl and Matthias Weiser (1997-2004)
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          1.22b
description:      (no language specified) Provides fonts in sizes of 12pt up to 107pt and also makes sure that in math formulas the symbols appear 
                  in the right size. Can also create a PostScript header file for  dvips (https://ctan.org/pkg/dvips) which 
                  ensures that the poster will be printed in the right size. Supported sizes are DIN A0, DIN A1, DIN A2 
                  and DIN A3.

a2ac -- AFM to AFM plus Composites
----------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/a2ac
name:             a2ac
caption:          AFM to AFM plus Composites
author:           Petr Olšák
license:          other-nonfree = License that prevents distribution (not free)
version:          2
description:      (no language specified) Enables the use of PostScript fonts while typesetting texts in languages where inflected letters are 
                  used. The font will typically not contain the complete alphabet of a given language; the program will 
                  derive composite glyph structures using accent glyphs, and output their details in the derived AFM file.

                  The configuration files of the program are independent of the PostScript font encoding and of the typesetting 
                  system encoding. The program may be used to prepare a font for any typesetting system, especially TeX.

documentation:    Package documentation (Czech): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/utilities/a2ac/a2ac-cz.txt
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/utilities/a2ac/README

on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/utilities/a2ac
keyword:          font-proc (process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation))
see also:         accfonts (accfonts -- Utilities to derive new fonts from existing ones)
year:             without year
language(s):      cs: Czech; en: English

a2ping -- Advanced PS, PDF, EPS converter
-----------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/a2ping
name:             a2ping
caption:          Advanced PS, PDF, EPS converter
author:           Péter Szabó
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          2.84p (2019-11-17)
last changes:     2019-11-17
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) a2ping is a Perl script command line utility written for Unix that converts many raster image and vector 
                  graphics formats to EPS or PDF and other page description formats. Accepted input file formats are: PS 
                  (PostScript), EPS, PDF, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, PNM, BMP, GIF, LBM, XPM, PCX, TGA. Accepted output formats are: 
                  EPS, PCL5, PDF, PDF1, PBM, PGM, PPM, PS, markedEPS, markedPS, PNG, XWD, BMP, TIFF, JPEG, GIF, XPM. a2ping 
                  delegates the low-level work to Ghostscript (GS), pdftops and  sam2p (https://ctan.org/pkg/sam2p) . 
                  a2ping fixes many glitches during the EPS to EPS conversion, so its output is often more compatible and 
                  better embeddable than its input.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/a2ping/README.txt
contact:          repository: https://github.com/pts/a2ping
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/a2ping
on MikTeX:        a2ping
on TeXLive:       a2ping
keyword:          graphics-prep (prepare graphics for use with *TeX)
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14


a4 -- Support for A4 paper sizes
--------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/a4
name:             a4
caption:          Support for A4 paper sizes
author:           Johannes L. Braams
author:           Nico Poppelier
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.2g
description:      (no language specified) Provides support for A4 paper sizes, superseding a LaTeX 2.09 package of the same name (the package was 
                  developed from a now-extinct package called a4dutch).

                  The package is mostly superseded by the  a4paper option of LaTeX itself and by the geometry 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/geometry) package. Its margins are slightly narrower than those of the a4paper option 
                  (there are those that claim this is a typographically poor choice), but it also has a widemargins option.

                  The package is now distributed as part of the  ntgclass (https://ctan.org/pkg/ntgclass) bundle.

on MikTeX:        ntgclass
on TeXLive:       ntgclass

keyword:          geometry (change geometry of page layout)

year:             without year

abbrevs -- Text abbreviations in LaTeX
--------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/abbrevs
name:             abbrevs
caption:          Text abbreviations in LaTeX
author:           Matt Swift
copyright:        Matt Swift (1995-2001)
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          1.4
description:      (no language specified) A LaTeX package defining abbreviation macros, which expand to defined text and insert following space 
                  intelligently, based on context. They can also expand to one thing the first time they are used and another 
                  thing on subsequent invocations. Thus they can be abbreviations in two senses, in the source and in the 
                  document. Also includes a facility for suffixes like 1900\BC and 6:00\PM which correctly handles following 
                  periods.

                  The package is part of the  frankenstein (https://ctan.org/pkg/frankenstein) bundle.

documentation:    Bundle README (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/frankenstein/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/frankenstein/abbrevs.pdf
-- local file:    ./4792192500-abbrevs.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/frankenstein
on MikTeX:        frankenstein
on TeXLive:       frankenstein
keyword:          abbrev (macros for defining abbreviations in documents)
year:             2001
language(s):      nls: no language specified

abc2mtex -- Notate tunes stored in ABC notation
-----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/abc2mtex
name:             abc2mtex
caption:          Notate tunes stored in ABC notation
author:           Chris Walshaw
license:          nosell = Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement (not free)
version:          1.6.1
description:      (no language specified) A package to notate tunes stored in an ascii format (abc notation, commonly used to notate traditional 
                  music). One of the most important aims of ABC notation, and perhaps one that distinguishes it from most, 
                  if not all, computer-readable musical languages is that it can be easily read by humans. The package 
                  produces files that can be processed with  MusicTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/musictex) .

aboensis -- A late medieval OpenType cursive font
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/aboensis
name:             Aboensis
caption:          A late medieval OpenType cursive font
author:           Tommi Syrjänen
copyright:        Tommi Syrjänen (2021)
license:          ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
license:          cc-by-4 = CC BY 4.0 (free)
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          (2021-07-24)
last changes:     2021-07-24
year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) The package contains the free OpenType medieval cursive font Aboensis and a style file to use it in XeLaTeX 
                  documents.

                  The font is based on Codex Aboensis, that is a law book written in Sweden in the 1430s. Since medieval 
                  cursive is very difficult to read for modern people, the font is not suitable for use as an ordinary 
                  book font, but is intended for emulating late medieval manuscripts.

                  The font contains two sets of initials: Lombardic and cursive to go with the basic alphabet, and there 
                  is support for writing two-colored initials and capitals. There are also a large number of abbreviation 
                  sigla that can be accessed as ligature substitutions.

                  The style file contains macros that help to use the extended features of the font such as initials and 
                  two-colored capitals. There are also macros to help achieve even pages with consistent line spacing.

abspos -- Absolute placement with coffins
-----------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/abspos
name:             abspos
caption:          Absolute placement with coffins
author:           Magnus Lie Hetland
copyright:        Magnus Lie Hetland (2021-2022)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          0.1 (2022-09-22)
last changes:     2022-09-22
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) This package lets you place contents at an absolute position, anchored at some specified part of the 
                  contents, similar to how  TikZ (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) nodes work, though without using the 
                  two-pass strategy of TikZ (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) . It also avoids messing with the order of beamer 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer) overlays, which is what happens when one uses the textpos (https://ctan.org/pkg/textpos) package 
                  with the overlay option.

                  The solution used is quite straightforward, combining  'coffins' (using l3coffins (https://ctan.org/pkg/l3kernel) ) 
                  with the placement mechanisms of atbegshi (https://ctan.org/pkg/atbegshi) .

                  it. 
I know the general concept is very important, and so I’m looking at getting support from various 
                  funding agencies to employ someone to completely refactor the code in a more future-proof fashion. I’ll 
                  coordinate this with the core LaTeX Team once I have more solid ideas.”

accfonts -- Utilities to derive new fonts from existing ones
------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/accfonts
name:             accfonts
caption:          Utilities to derive new fonts from existing ones
author:           John Smith
copyright:        John D. Smith (1997, 2008)
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          0.25
description:      (no language specified) The accfonts package contains three utilities to permit easy manipulation of fonts, in particular the 
                  creation of unusual accented characters. Mkt1font works on Adobe Type 1 fonts, vpl2vpl works on TeX virtual 
                  fonts and vpl2ovp transforms a TeX font to an Omega one. All three programs read in a font (either the 
                  font itself or a property list), together with a simple definition file containing lines such as ‘           28 
                  z acute ’; they then write out a new version of the font with the requested new characters in the 
                  numerical slots specified. Great care is taken over the positioning of accents, and over the provision 
                  of kerning information for new characters; mkt1font also generates suitable “hints” to enhance quality 
                  at small sizes or poor resolutions. The programs are written in Perl.

documentation:    Package Readme and documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/utilities/accfonts/README

acroflex -- Create a graphing widget in a PDF file
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/acroflex
name:             acroflex
caption:          Create a graphing widget in a PDF file
author:           Donald P. Story
copyright:        D. P. Story (2008-2016)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          1.7 (2020-08-07)
last changes:     2020-08-07
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) The acroflex package is part of the  AeB Pro (https://ctan.org/pkg/aeb-pro) family of packages. 
                  It is a package that creates a graphing screen using the rmannot (https://ctan.org/pkg/rmannot) package. 
                  The user can type in functions and graph them. A graphing screen can be populated with pre-packaged functions 
                  for the user to scrutinize and interact with. The package can graph functions of a single variable 'x' , 
                  a pair of parametric equations that are functions of 't' , and a polar function of 't' .

                  The graphing screen is a rich media annotation what uses a specially developed SWF file, called the AcroFLeX 
                  Graphing widget. This package takes advantage of rich media annotations, which is a version 9 feature 
                  of Acrobat. This package requires Acrobat Pro and Distiller version 9. The user needs to use Adobe Reader 
                  9.0 in order to obtain the graphing functionality.

                  This package has become obsolete as of December 2020. Since December 2020, Adobe no longer supports Flash 
                  player (SWF, FLV). This package uses a custom SWF file ( acroflex.swf ); as a result this package 
                  will no longer function in Adobe Acrobat Reader DC. The package will continue to produce PDFs as designed, 
                  but only if built using Acrobat XI (or a version Acrobat prior to December 2020) and viewed in Adobe 
                  Acrobat Reader XI (or a version of Reader prior to December 2020).

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): pkg:/doc/acroflex_man.pdf

Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/acrotex-web
name:             acrotex-web
caption:          Establish a page layout for an on-screen (PDF) document
author:           Donald P. Story
copyright:        D. P. Story (1999-2021)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          6.1.7 (2021-05-06)
last changes:     2021-05-06
year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) The AcroTeX web package (for LaTeX — nothing to do with literate programming) is a set of macros that 
                  establishes a page layout for a (PDF) document that is designed to be read on-screen and  'not' meant 
                  to be printed. The package also redefines the table of contents to a web style and defines optional navigational 
                  aids. The package has options for use with pdfTeX, dvips, dvipdfm, dvipsone and dviwindo.

                  The package is part of the  AcroTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/acrotex) bundle.

documentation:    Bundle Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/acrotex/README.md
documentation:    AcroTeX packages manual (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/acrotex/doc/aeb_man.pdf
-- local file:    ./5280040777-aeb_man.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/acrotex
on MikTeX:        acrotex
keyword:          layout (layout of objects on the page)
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

actuarialsymbol -- Actuarial symbols of life contingencies and financial mathematics
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/actuarialsymbol
name:             actuarialsymbol
caption:          Actuarial symbols of life contingencies and financial mathematics
author:           David Beauchemin
author:           Vincent Goulet
copyright:        David Beauchemin, Vincent Goulet (2017-2019)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.1 (2019-06-13)
last changes:     2019-06-13
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) This package provides commands to compose actuarial symbols of life contingencies and financial mathematics 
                  characterized by subscripts and superscripts on both sides of a principal symbol. The package also features 
                  commands to easily and consistently position precedence numbers above or below statuses in symbols for 
                  multiple lives contracts.

                  Since the actuarial notation can get quite involved, the package defines a number of shortcut macros 
                  to ease entry of the most common elements.

                  Appendix A of the package documentation lists the commands to typeset a large selection of symbols of 
                  life contingencies.

                  This package requires  actuarialangle (https://ctan.org/pkg/actuarialangle) .

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/actuarialsymbol/README.md

addfont -- Easier use of fonts without LaTeX support
----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/addfont
name:             addfont
caption:          Easier use of fonts without LaTeX support
author:           Palle Jørgensen
copyright:        Palle Jørgensen (2016-2021)
license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
version:          1.1 (2021-03-20)
last changes:     2021-03-20
year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) This package is intended for use by users who know about fonts. It is a quick-fix for fonts which do 
                  not have genuine LaTeX support. It is not meant as a replacement of the LaTeX font definition files.

                  It is meant as something more useable for LaTeX users than the  \newfont command. With addfont 
                  the loaded font scales along with the usual LaTeX size selection.

                  Using this package still requires some knowledge on how to use fonts with LaTeX.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/addfont/README

description:      (no language specified) Addindex is C/Lex program to add index entries to a LaTeX document. You start with a ‘names database’,

adjustbox -- Graphics package-alike macros for “general” boxes
--------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/adjustbox
name:             adjustbox
caption:          Graphics package-alike macros for “general” boxes
author:           Martin Scharrer
copyright:        Martin Scharrer (2011-2025)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.3c (2025-02-26)
last changes:     2025-02-26
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) The package provides several macros to adjust boxed content. One purpose is to supplement the standard 
                  graphics (https://ctan.org/pkg/graphics) package, which defines the macros \resizebox , \scalebox and \rotatebox , 
                  with the macros \trimbox and \clipbox . The main feature is the general \adjustbox macro 
                  which extends the “ key=value ” interface of \includegraphics from the graphics (https://ctan.org/pkg/graphics) package 
                  and applies it to general text content. Additional provided box macros are \lapbox , \marginbox , \minsizebox , \maxsizebox and \phantombox .

                  All macros use the  collectbox (https://ctan.org/pkg/collectbox) package to read the content as 
                  a box and not as a macro argument. This allows for all forms of content including special material like 
                  verbatim content. A special feature of collectbox (https://ctan.org/pkg/collectbox) is used to 
                  provide matching environments with the identical names as the macros.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): pkg:/README.txt
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): pkg:/adjustbox.pdf
home page:        https://github.com/MartinScharrer/adjustbox
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/MartinScharrer/adjustbox/issues
contact:          repository: https://github.com/MartinScharrer/adjustbox.git
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/adjustbox
on MikTeX:        adjustbox
on TeXLive:       adjustbox
keyword:          box-breaking (breaking boxes over a page boundary, etc)
keyword:          typesetting (support for variations of typographic style)
keyword:          tagged-pdf-partially (tagged PDF partially compatible)
keyword:          box-manip (manipulating boxes)
see also:         gincltex (gincltex -- Include TeX files as graphics (<span>.tex</span> support for \includegraphics))

author:           Luis Rivera
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) The package provides a set of virtual fonts (built from the standard Concrete fonts) providing a set 
                  of fonts that almost cover the T1 encoding.

                  The main characters missing, of those specified in the T1 specification are eth, thorn, and the Sami 
                  letter eng. Sometimes the £ (pound sterling) character is also missing. For the typewriter fonts, the 
                  situation is  'worse' .

                  According to the author, the purpose of this package is nowadays better served by a combination of the 
                  MLTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/mltex) and ccfonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/ccfonts) packages.

afterpage -- Execute command after the next page break
------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/afterpage
name:             afterpage
caption:          Execute command after the next page break
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
author:           David Carlisle
copyright:        The LaTeX3 Project et al. (1993-2023)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.08 (2023-07-04)
last changes:     2023-07-04
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) Implements a command that causes the commands specified in its argument to be expanded after the current 
                  page is output. For example, LaTeX's float positioning mechanism sometimes gets overloaded and all floating 
                  figures and table drift to the end of the document. One may flush out all the unprocessed floats by issuing 
                  a  \clearpage command, but this has the effect of making the current page end prematurely. Now 
                  you can issue \afterpage{\clearpage} and the current page will be filled up with text as usual, 
                  but then the \clearpage command will flush out all the floats before the next text page begins.

                  This package is part of the  latex-tools (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-tools) bundle in the LaTeX required 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/required) distribution.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools/afterpage.pdf
-- local file:    ./2900151276-afterpage.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools
installation:     https://ctan.org/tex-archive/install/macros/latex/required/latex-tools.tds.zip
on MikTeX:        latex-tools
on TeXLive:       tools
keyword:          macro-supp (support for development of (La)TeX macros)
keyword:          tagged-pdf-partially (tagged PDF partially compatible)
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-08-02

                  (Generative AI Delegation Taxonomy), letting authors mark which tasks were delegated to AI, list the 
                  tools used (or state that none were), add optional numbered or unnumbered comments, and automatically 
                  typeset a formatted disclosure section or chapter with a task-based checklist.

                  Configuration uses a key-value interface, and citations for the taxonomy and the package can be managed 
                  automatically. The package detects the document language through  babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) or polyglossia 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia) and ships translations for fourteen languages, falling back to 
                  English. A companion web generator/configurator is available at https://aidisclose.org (https://aidisclose.org/) .

aifont -- Remap Computer Modern fonts
-------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/aifont
name:             aifont
caption:          Remap Computer Modern fonts
author:           Skip Collins
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
description:      (no language specified) Virtual fonts and other related files for remapping the BSR/Y&amp;Y/AMS Type 1 Computer Modern fonts; 
                  the remapping creates fonts which have no characters in the numeric range 0–31 (mod 128), and the virtual 
                  fonts map Knuth’s original encodings to the remapped fonts.

                  These mechanisms aid the production of robust PDF output from TeX-related systems, when they use CM fonts.

                  The original impetus for developing this bundle came from problems with Adobe Illustrator (hence the 
                  first two letters of the bundle name). Current versions of Adobe Illustrator can apparently use the CM 
                  fonts without remapping, so the bundle is not needed for such use.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/obsolete/fonts/cm/ai/README.aifont
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/obsolete/fonts/cm/ai

name:             algobox
caption:          Typeset Algobox programs
author:           Julien Rivaud
copyright:        RIVAUD Julien (2016-2019)
license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
version:          1.3 (2019-09-29)
last changes:     2019-09-29
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) This LaTeX package can typeset Algobox programs almost exactly as displayed when editing with  Algobox 
                  (https://www.xm1math.net/algobox/) itself, using an input syntax very similar to the actual Algobox 
                  program text.

                  It gives better results than Algobox’s own LaTeX export which does not look like the editor rendition, 
                  produces standalone documents cumbersome to customize, and has arbitrary and inconsistent differences 
                  between the input syntax and the program text.

                  This package depends upon the following other LaTeX packages:  expl3 (https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3) , TikZ 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) , environ (https://ctan.org/pkg/environ) , xparse (https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse) , 
                  and xcolor (https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor) .

almfixed -- Arabic-Latin Modern Fixed extends TeX-Gyre Latin Modern Mono 10 Regular to full Arabic Unicode support
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/almfixed
name:             almfixed
caption:          Arabic-Latin Modern Fixed extends TeX-Gyre Latin Modern Mono 10 Regular to full Arabic Unicode support
author:           Idris Samawi Hamid
license:          gfl = The GUST Font License (GFL) (free)
version:          0.92
description:      (no language specified) Arabic-Latin Modern Fixed is an extension of TeX-Gyre Latin Modern Mono 10 Regular. Every glyph and OpenType 
                  feature of the Latin Modern Mono has been retained, with minor improvements. On the other hand, we have 
                  changed the vertical metrics of the font. Although the Arabic script is designed to use the same x-size 
                  as Latin Modern Mono, the former script needs greater ascender and descender space.

                  Every Arabic glyph in each Unicode-code block is supported (up to Unicode 7.0): Arabic, Arabic Supplement, 
                  Arabic Extended, Arabic Presentation-Forms A, and Arabic Presentation-Forms B.

                  There are two versions of the font: otf and ttf. The ?penType version is for print applications (and 
                  usually the default for TeX). The TrueType version is for on-screen applications such as text editors. 
                  Hinting in the ttf version is much better for on-screen, at least on Microsoft Windows.

                  The unique feature of Arabic-Latin Modern is its treatment of vowels and diacritics. Each vowel and diacritic 
                  (ALM Fixed contains a total of 68 such glyphs) may now be edited horizontally within any text editor 
                  or processor. The author believes this is the very first OpenType Arabic font ever to have this capability. 
                  Editing complex Arabic texts will now be much easier to input and to proofread.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/almfixed/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/almfixed/doc/almfixed-dtk.pdf

amscdx -- Enhanced commutative diagrams
---------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/amscdx
name:             amscdx
caption:          Enhanced commutative diagrams
author:           Martin Vermeer
copyright:        American Mathematical Society (1995, 1999)
copyright:        LaTeX3 Project and American Mathematical Society (2016-2017)
copyright:        Martin Vermeer (2019)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.2x (2019-07-02)
last changes:     2019-07-02
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) The original  amscd (https://ctan.org/pkg/amscd) package provides a CD environment that emulates 
                  the commutative diagram capabilities of AMS-TeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/amstex) version 2.x. This 
                  means that only simple rectangular diagrams are supported, with no diagonal arrows or more exotic features.

                  This enhancement package implements double (“fat”), dashed, and bidirectional arrows (left-right and 
                  up-down), and color attributes for arrows and their annotations. The restriction to rectangular geometry 
                  remains. This nevertheless allows the drawing of a much broader class of “commutative-diagram-like” diagrams.

                  This update, 2.2x of 2019-07-02, fixes the dashed-arrows parts placement bug, and adds the package option 
                  'lyx', for use with lyx to prevent conflict with the already loaded amscd. The packages xcolor and graphicx 
                  are made required.

description:      (no language specified) This collection comprises a set of four manuals, or Author Handbooks, each documenting the use of a class 
                  of publications based on one of the AMS document classes  amsart (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsart) , amsbook 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsbook) , amsproc (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsproc) and one “hybrid”, as

                  Handbooks comprise the user documentation for the pertinent document classes.

                  different documents, the principles underlying this collection can be used as a model for similar projects. 
                  The manual “Compiling the AMS Author Handbooks” provides information about the structure of and interaction 
                  between the various components.

amsfonts -- TeX fonts from the American Mathematical Society
------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/amsfonts
name:             amsfonts
caption:          TeX fonts from the American Mathematical Society
author:           The American Mathematical Society
license:          ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
version:          3.04
description:      (no language specified) An extended set of fonts for use in mathematics, including: extra mathematical symbols; blackboard bold 
                  letters (uppercase only); fraktur letters; subscript sizes of bold math italic and bold Greek letters; 
                  subscript sizes of large symbols such as sum and product; added sizes of the Computer Modern small caps 
                  font; cyrillic fonts (from the University of Washington); Euler mathematical fonts. All fonts are provided 
                  as Adobe Type 1 files, and all except the Euler fonts are provided as Metafont source.

                  The distribution also includes the canonical Type 1 versions of the  Computer Modern family of fonts 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/cm) .

                  Basic LaTeX support for the symbol fonts is provided by  amsfonts.sty , with names of individual 
                  symbols defined in amssymb.sty . The Euler fonts are supported by separate packages; details can 
                  be found in the documentation.

amsmath -- AMS mathematical facilities for LaTeX
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath
name:             amsmath
caption:          AMS mathematical facilities for LaTeX
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
copyright:        American Mathematical Society (1995, 2000, 2013)
copyright:        LaTeX3 Project and American Mathematical Society (2016-2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.17z (2025-07-09)
last changes:     2025-07-09
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) The principal package in the AMS-LaTeX distribution. It adapts for use in LaTeX most of the mathematical 
                  features found in AMS-TeX; it is highly recommended as an adjunct to serious mathematical typesetting 
                  in LaTeX.

                  When amsmath is loaded, AMS-LaTeX packages  amsbsy (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsbsy) (for bold symbols), amsopn 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsopn) (for operator names) and amstext (https://ctan.org/pkg/amstext) (for 
                  text embedded in mathematics) are also loaded.

                  amsmath is part of the LaTeX required distribution; however, several contributed packages add still further 
                  to its appeal; examples are  empheq (https://ctan.org/pkg/empheq) , which provides functions for 
                  decorating and highlighting mathematics, and ntheorem (https://ctan.org/pkg/ntheorem) , for specifying 
                  theorem (and similar) definitions.

amstex -- American Mathematical Society plain TeX macros
--------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/amstex
name:             amstex
caption:          American Mathematical Society plain TeX macros
author:           The American Mathematical Society

version:          2.01 (2021-08-26)
last changes:     2021-08-26
year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) AMS-TeX is a TeX macro package, originally written by Michael Spivak for the American Mathematical Society 
                  (AMS) during 1983–1985 and is described in the book  ‘The Joy of TeX’ (https://ctan.org/pkg/joy-of-tex) . 
                  It is based on Plain TeX, and provides many features for producing more professional-looking maths formulas 
                  with less burden on authors.

                  This is the final archival distribution of AMS-TeX. AMS-TeX is no longer supported by the AMS, nor is 
                  it used by the AMS publishing program. The AMS does not recommend creating any new documents using AMS-TeX; 
                  this distribution will be left on CTAN to facilitate processing of legacy documents and as a historical 
                  record of a pioneering TeX macro collection that played a key role in popularizing TeX and revolutionizing 
                  mathematics publishing.

                  In addition to the  “User’s Guide to AMS-TeX” (https://mirrors.ctan.org/macros/amstex/doc/amsguide.pdf) , 
                  the AMS has also made the full text of the most recent reprint of the second edition of “The Joy of 
                  TeX” (https://ctan.org/pkg/joy-of-tex) by Michael Spivak available as a pdf file.

                  AMS-TeX is the historical basis of  amslatex (https://ctan.org/pkg/amslatex) , which should now 
                  be used to prepare submissions for the AMS.

anima -- Create slideshows with simple animations
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/anima
name:             anima
caption:          Create slideshows with simple animations
author:           Adriano Gomes de Santana
copyright:        Adriano Gomes de Santana (2009-2024)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.1 (2024-12-14)
last changes:     2024-12-14
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) The idea for this package arose from noticing that including the  \pause command from the beamer 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer) class within the \foreach loop command from the TikZ (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) package 
                  creates a sequence of frames, where each slide presents a step in the construction of the image. The 
                  purpose of the anima class is to provide macros that simplify the use of this effect for creating 
                  animated slide presentations.

                  Although the functionality of this class can be compared to the transition effects of the  beamer 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer) class, it is not a dependency of the anima class. However, the 
                  class makes extensive use of the image creation language provided by the TikZ (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) package.

                  Lastly, it is worth noting a comparison between this class and the  animate (https://ctan.org/pkg/animate) package. 
                  The animate (https://ctan.org/pkg/animate) package can create embedded animations within the document, 
                  while the anima class produces an animation where each frame corresponds to a page of the document. 
                  This distinction highlights the different design goals of the anima class.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/anima/README.txt
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/anima/anima-doc.pdf
-- local file:    ./7474294634-anima-doc.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/anima
on MikTeX:        anima
on TeXLive:       anima
keyword:          class (alternative LaTeX class(es))
keyword:          graphics-motion (motion graphics)
keyword:          presentation (slides, beamers, handouts, etc.)
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-08-02

author:           Brett A. Becker

license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.0 (2020-05-09)
last changes:     2020-05-09
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) Academics often need to submit anonymous versions of their papers for peer-review. This often requires 
                  anonymization which at some future date needs to be reversed. However de-anonymizing an anonymized paper 
                  can be laborious and error-prone.

                  This LaTeX package allows anonymization options to be specified at the time of writing for authors using 
                  acmart.cls (https://ctan.org/pkg/acmart) , the official Association of Computing Machinery (ACM) 
                  master article template. Anonymization or deanonymization is carried out by simply changing one option 
                  and recompiling.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

name:             antp
caption:          Antykwa Półtawskiego: a Type 1 family of Polish traditional type
author:           Janusz Marian Nowacki
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
version:          0.50
description:      (no language specified) 'This package is obsolete, its replacement is the new'  poltawski (https://ctan.org/pkg/poltawski)  'package' .

                  A replica of Antykwa Półtawskiego font in PostScript Type 1 format — preliminary version. This font was 
                  designed in the 1920s and 1930s of the twentieth century by Polish graphic artist and typographer Adam 
                  Półtawski. It was widely used by Polish printing houses as long as metal types were in use (until approximately 
                  the 1960s). Antykwa Półtawskiego was perhaps the first complete font family programmed and parametrized 
                  in MetaPost.

anyfontsize -- Select any font size in LaTeX
--------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/anyfontsize
name:             anyfontsize
caption:          Select any font size in LaTeX
author:           Péter Szabó
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          (2007-11-22)
last changes:     2007-11-22
year:             2007
description:      (no language specified) The package allows the to user select any font size (via e.g.  \fontsize{...}{...}\selectfont ), 
                  even those sizes that are not listed in the .fd file. If such a size is requested, LaTeX will search 
                  for and select the nearest listed size; anyfontsize will then scale the font to the size actually requested.

                  Similar functionality is available for the  CM family (https://ctan.org/pkg/type1cm) , for the EC 
                  family (https://ctan.org/pkg/type1ec) , or for either computer modern encoding (https://ctan.org/pkg/fix-cm) ; 
                  the present package generalises the facility.

author:           Petr Olšák
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
version:          1.7
description:      (no language specified) The basic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, power to an integer) are implemented 
                  by TeX macros in this package. Operands may be numbers with arbitrary numbers of digits; scientific notation 
                  is allowed.

                  The expression scanner is also provided.

                  As of version 1.4 (December 2015) the calculation of common functions (sqrt, exp, ln, sin, cos, tan, 
                  asin, acos, atan, pi) with arbitrary precision in the result has been added.

                  Exhaustive documentation (including detailed TeXnical documentation) is included. The macro includes 
                  many optimizations and uses only TeX primitives (from classic TeX) and  \newcount macro.

appendixnumberbeamer -- Manage frame numbering in appendixes in beamer
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/appendixnumberbeamer
name:             appendixnumberbeamer
caption:          Manage frame numbering in appendixes in beamer
author:           Jérôme Lelong
copyright:        Jérôme Lelong (2007-2026)
license:          gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
version:          1.2.1
description:      (no language specified) This package fixes the frame numbering in  beamer (https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer) when using an appendix 
                  such that the slides from the appendix are not counted in the total frame number of the main part of 
                  the document. The total frame number counter is reset to 0 when entering the appendix.

                  The standard usage is to include  \usepackage{appendixnumberbeamer} in the preamble and then declare 
                  the beginning of the appendix as usual using the \appendix command.

apxproof -- Proofs in appendix
------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/apxproof
name:             apxproof
caption:          Proofs in appendix
author:           Pierre Senellart
copyright:        Pierre Senellart (2016-2026)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.4.1 (2026-06-02)
last changes:     2026-06-02
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package makes it easier to write articles where proofs and other material are deferred to the appendix.

                  The appendix material is written in the LaTeX code along with the main text which it naturally complements, 
                  and it is automatically deferred.

                  The package can automatically send proofs to the appendix, can repeat in the appendix the theorem environments 
                  stated in the main text, can section the appendix automatically based on the sectioning of the main text, 
                  and supports a separate bibliography for the appendix material.

                  It depends on the following packages:  amsthm (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsthm) , bibunits (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibunits) (if 
                  the bibliography option is set to separate ), environ (https://ctan.org/pkg/environ) , etoolbox 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox) , fancyvrb (https://ctan.org/pkg/fancyvrb) , ifthen (https://ctan.org/pkg/ifthen) , 
                  and kvoptions (https://ctan.org/pkg/kvoptions) .

                  The collection consists of four packages:  arabdoc-setup (core RTL stack), arabdoc document classes 
                  ( arabdoc-article , arabdoc-book , arabdoc-report , arabdoc-thesis ), arabdoc-glossary (bilingual 
                  glossary and acronym management), and arabdoc-bib (Arabic bibliography with biblatex (https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex) ). 
                  Options include font selection, numeral style, calendar, caption overrides, and legal-style section numbering.

                  The bundle requires XeLaTeX with  bidi (https://ctan.org/pkg/bidi) , polyglossia (https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia) , 
                  and fontspec (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec) .

arabi -- (La)TeX support for Arabic and Farsi, compliant with Babel
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/arabi
name:             arabi
caption:          (La)TeX support for Arabic and Farsi, compliant with Babel
author:           Youssef Jabri
copyright:        Youssef Jabri (2006)
license:          lppl1.3b = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3b (free)
version:          1.1
description:      (no language specified) The package provides an Arabic and Farsi script support for TeX without the need of any external pre-processor, 
                  and in a way that is compatible with  babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) . The bi-directional capability 
                  supposes that the user has a TeX engine that knows the four primitives \beginR , \endR , \beginL and \endL . 
                  That is the case in both the TeX--XeT and e-TeX engines. Arabi will accept input in several 8-bit encodings, 
                  including UTF-8.

                  Arabi can make use of a wide variety of Arabic and Farsi fonts, and provides one of its own. PDF files 
                  generated using Arabi may be searched, and text may be copied from them and pasted elsewhere.

arabluatex -- ArabTeX for LuaLaTeX
----------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/arabluatex
name:             arabluatex
caption:          ArabTeX for LuaLaTeX
author:           Robert Alessi
copyright:        Robert Alessi (2016-2020)
license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
license:          cc-by-sa-4 = CC BY-SA 4.0 (free)
version:          1.20 (2020-03-23)
last changes:     2020-03-23
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) This package provides for LuaLaTeX an  ArabTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/arabtex) -like interface to 
                  generate Arabic writing from an ascii transliteration. It is particularly well-suited for complex documents 
                  such as technical documents or critical editions where a lot of left-to-right commands intertwine with 
                  Arabic writing. arabluatex is able to process any ArabTeX input notation. Its output can be set 
                  in the same modes of vocalization as ArabTeX, or in different roman transliterations. It further allows 
                  many typographical refinements. It will eventually interact with some other packages yet to come to produce 
                  from .tex source files, in addition to printed books, TEI xml compliant critical editions and/or 
                  lexicons that can be searched, analyzed and correlated in various ways.

arabxetex -- An ArabTeX-like interface for XeLaTeX
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/arabxetex
name:             arabxetex
caption:          An ArabTeX-like interface for XeLaTeX
author:           bidi-tex GitHub Organisation
author:           Vafa Khalighi
author:           François Charette
copyright:        François Charette (2007-2010)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.2.1
description:      (no language specified) ArabXeTeX provides a convenient  ArabTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/arabtex) -like user-interface for 
                  typesetting languages using the Arabic script in XeLaTeX, with flexible access to font features. Input 
                  in ArabTeX notation can be set in three different vocalization modes or in roman transliteration. Direct 
                  UTF-8 input is also supported. The parsing and converting of ArabTeX input to Unicode is done by means 
                  of TECkit mappings. Version 1.0 provides support for Arabic, Maghribi Arabic, Farsi (Persian), Urdu, 
                  Sindhi, Kashmiri, Ottoman Turkish, Kurdish, Jawi (Malay) and Uighur. The documentation covers topics 
                  such as typesetting the Holy Quran and typesetting bidirectional critical editions with the package ednotes.

arev -- Fonts and LaTeX support files for Arev Sans
---------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/arev
name:             arev
caption:          Fonts and LaTeX support files for Arev Sans
author:           Stephen Hartke
license:          lppl1.3a = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3a (free)
description:      (no language specified) The package arev provides type 1 and virtual fonts, together with LaTeX packages for using  Arev Sans 
                  (http://tavmjong.free.fr/FONTS/) in both text and mathematics. Arev Sans is a derivative of Bitstream 
                  Vera Sans created by Tavmjong Bah, adding support for Greek and Cyrillic characters. Bah also added a 
                  few variant letters that are more appropriate for mathematics. The primary purpose for using Arev Sans 
                  in LaTeX is presentations, particularly when using a computer projector. In such acontext, Arev Sans 
                  is quite readable, with large x-height, “open letters”, wide spacing, and thick stems. The style is very 
                  similar to the SliTeX font lcmss, but heavier.

                  Arev is one of a very small number of sans-font mathematics support packages. Others are  cmbright 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/cmbright) , hvmath (https://ctan.org/pkg/hvmath) and kerkis (https://ctan.org/pkg/kerkis) .

last changes:     2025-12-13
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) In 2011 Andrij’s typeface became a winner of the Ukrainian Type Design Competition “Mystetsky Arsenal” 
                  in which three main criteria were sought for: being zeitgeist, practical, and Ukrainian. Andrij’s winning 
                  entry was crowned Arsenal and made publicly available.

                  Arsenal is a semi-grotesque with traditional forms. It is primarily designed for body text and intended 
                  for various professional communication. Its special qualities of letter shapes and subtle contrast modulation 
                  articulate grace and expressivity. Arsenal’s somewhat lyrical sentiment abides to the Ukrainian nature 
                  of the font.

                  This package provides the fonts and LaTeX support for them with matching math. It needs LuaLaTeX or XeLaTeX.

artex -- Make filecontents environments of non-standard files or packages
-------------------------------------------------------------------------

name:             artex
caption:          Make filecontents environments of non-standard files or packages
author:           Nick Efford
copyright:        Nick Efford (1995)
license:          noinfo = noinfo 
version:          1.00b
description:      (no language specified) ArTeX is a Perl script which simplifies the exchange of LaTeX documents between collaborating authors 
                  or between author and publisher.

                  ArTeX analyzes a LaTeX2e document to determine whether it loads any non-standard files. If non-standard 
                  files are identified, ArTeX creates filecontents or filecontents* environments for them and adds these 
                  environments to the input document. The new document can be processed successfully on any system with 
                  a standard installation of LaTeX2e.

artthreads -- Support for article threads
-----------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/artthreads
name:             artthreads
caption:          Support for article threads
author:           Donald P. Story
copyright:        D. P. Story (2016-2020)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          1.3.1 (2020-07-09)
last changes:     2020-07-09
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) This package facilitates the creation of PDF article threads, a concept/feature of Adobe Reader/Acrobat 
                  that has been around since the product’s beginning. The use of article threads typically only makes sense 
                  in a document in which the text is in a multi-column format.

                  Set the article threads after the composition of the document is completed. The method of setting the 
                  threads is very visual, not automatic as in the  threadcol (https://ctan.org/pkg/threadcol) package 
                  of Scott Pakin (available for pdftex only).

                  This package supports all drivers:  dvips (https://ctan.org/pkg/dvips) , pdflatex , lualatex , xelatex , dvipdfm 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/dvipdfm) , and dvipdfmx (https://ctan.org/pkg/dvipdfmx) .

year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The asmeconf class provides a LaTeX template for ASME conference papers, following ASME’s guidelines 
                  for margins, fonts, headings, captions, and reference formats as of 2025.

                  This LaTeX template is intended to be used with the asmeconf.bst BibTeX style, for reference formatting, 
                  which is part of this distribution. Unlike older ASME conference LaTeX templates, asmeconf pdfs will 
                  contain hyperlinks, bookmarks, and metadata; and the references can include the DOI and URL fields. This 
                  LaTeX template enables inline author names, following ASME’s current style, but it can also produce the 
                  traditional grid style. Options include line numbering, final column balancing, various math options, 
                  government copyright, archivability and accessibility (PDF/A), and multilingual support. The code is 
                  compatible with pdfLaTeX or LuaLaTeX.

                  This LaTeX template is not a publication of ASME, but it does conform to ASME’s currently published guidelines 
                  for conference papers.

                  or 'protocol narrations' .

                  Optionally, the Aspen package also implements LaTeX commands for Burrows–Abadi–Needham logic (BAN logic).

                  The name Aspen can be an abbreviation for  'A Security Protocol Engineering Notation' , but another 
                  possible abbreviation is 'Anderson-inspired Standard Protocol Engineering Notation' , in memory 
                  of the late Professor Ross J. Anderson who has meant so much for the fields of computer security, distributed 
                  systems, and, in particular, security engineering.

description:      (no language specified) This package allows the creation of association matrices in an clear and concise fashion, without having 
                  to deal with manually generating and modifying the tables while working. All you have to do is define 
                  the rows and the columns by their unique identifier, and then specify which cells should be marked as 
                  associated. Then, the  \amxgenerate command generates a table that shows in the cells with a blip 
                  (•) where the association was added.

                  The package depends on  etoolbox (https://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox) , forloop (https://ctan.org/pkg/forloop) , ifthen 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/ifthen) , textcomp (https://ctan.org/pkg/textcomp) , and xparse (https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse) .

atenddvi -- Provides the \AtEndDvi command
------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/atenddvi
name:             atenddvi
caption:          Provides the \AtEndDvi command
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
author:           Heiko Oberdiek
copyright:        Heiko Oberdiek (2007)
copyright:        Oberdiek Package Support Group (2016-2020)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.5 (2020-11-11)
last changes:     2020-11-11
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) This package is unneeded and does nothing when used with a LaTeX format 2020-10-01 or newer as in this 
                  case the  'format' provides the \AtEndDvi command.

                  For older formats it implements  \AtEndDvi , a counterpart to \AtBeginDvi . The execution 
                  of its argument is delayed to the end of the document at the end of the last page. Thus \special and \write remain 
                  effective, because they are put into the last page. This is the main difference to \AtEndDocument .

attachfile -- Attach arbitrary files to a PDF document
------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/attachfile
name:             attachfile
caption:          Attach arbitrary files to a PDF document
author:           Scott Pakin
copyright:        Scott Pakin (2010, 2015-2016)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.9
description:      (no language specified) Starting with PDF 1.3 (Adobe Acrobat 4.0), PDF files can contain file attachments — arbitrary files that 
                  a reader can extract, just like attachments to an e-mail message. The attachfile package brings this 
                  functionality to pdfLaTeX and provides some additional features not available in Acrobat, such as the 
                  ability to use arbitrary LaTeX code for the file icon — including things like \includegraphics, tabular, 
                  and mathematics. Settings can be made either globally or on a per-attachment basis. Attachfile makes 
                  it easy to attach files and customize their appearance in the enclosing document.

                  The package supports the Created, Modified, and Size keys in the EmbeddedFile’s Params dictionary.

Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/attrib
name:             attrib
caption:          Attribution of block quotations in LaTeX
author:           Matt Swift
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          1.3
description:      (no language specified) A LaTeX package that defines the command  \attrib , used to provide attribution for block elements 
                  of a text. The argument of \attrib may be pretty much anything; the command will print the attribution 
                  at the right margin of the block. If the block is prose, \attrib will attempt to fit the attribution 
                  at the end of the last line.

                  The package is part of the  frankenstein (https://ctan.org/pkg/frankenstein) bundle of packages.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/frankenstein/attrib.pdf

auncial -- Artificial Uncial manuscript book-hand font
------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/auncial
name:             auncial
caption:          Artificial Uncial manuscript book-hand font
author:           Peter R. Wilson
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
description:      (no language specified) The auncial and allauncl packages provide Metafont fonts based on the Artificial Uncial manuscript book-hand 
                  used between the 6th and 10th century AD. The font consists of minuscules and digits, with some appropriate 
                  period punctuation marks. Both normal and bold versions are provided. Note that the font is available 
                  separately in Adobe Type 1 format, as the  artificial uncial ‘new’ (https://ctan.org/pkg/auncial-new) package.

                  This is one of a  set of manuscript fonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/bookhands) . Access to the docmfp 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/docmfp) package is desirable but not essential.

caption:          Artificial Uncial font and LaTeX support macros
author:           Peter R. Wilson
copyright:        Peter R. Wilson (1999-2005)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.0
description:      (no language specified) The auncial-new bundle provides packages and fonts for a script based on the Artificial Uncial manuscript 
                  book-hand used between the 6th &amp; 10th century AD. The script consists of minuscules and digits, with 
                  some appropriate period punctuation marks. Both normal and bold versions are provided, and the font is 
                  distributed in Adobe Type 1 format. This is an experimental new version of the  auncial (https://ctan.org/pkg/auncial) bundle, 
                  which is one of a series of bookhand fonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/bookhands) .

                  The font follows the  B1 encoding (https://ctan.org/pkg/b1encoding) developed for bookhands. Access 
                  to the encoding is essential. The encoding mainly follows the standard T1 encoding.

caption:          Header files for dvips to make colour separations
author:           T. Graham Freeman
copyright:        Graham Freeman (1994)
license:          nocommercial = No Commercial Use (not free)
description:      (no language specified) Offset printers need separate camera-ready copies for each ink they will use in printing a document. 
                  Aurora is a PostScript program for producing colour separates from a colour PostScript document. Aurora 
                  can be run from any type of computer, as it depends only on a black-and-white PostScript printer for 
                  its execution. It is capable of handling colour images as well as ordinary graphics, though image handling 
                  is very slow.

author:           Andreas Wettstein
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          (2019-07-27)
last changes:     2019-07-27
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) This package allows the user to create an index of all authors cited in a LaTeX document. Each author 
                  entry in the index contains the pages where these citations occur. Alternatively, the package can list 
                  the labels of the citations that appear in the references rather than the text pages.

                  The package relies on  BibTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) being used to handle citations. Additionally, 
                  it requires Perl (version 5 or higher).

description:      (no language specified) The package uses  -  -shell-escape to execute pst-pdf (https://ctan.org/pkg/pst-pdf) when

                  Matlab figures via laprint (https://ctan.org/pkg/psfragx) , Mathematica figures via MathPSfrag, 
                  and regular psfrag figures can all be input consistently and easily.

autoaffil -- Automatic deduplicated affiliation numbering
---------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/autoaffil
name:             autoaffil
caption:          Automatic deduplicated affiliation numbering
author:           Philip Bittihn
copyright:        Philip Bittihn (2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0 (2026-06-06)
last changes:     2026-06-06
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package provides the author and affiliation layout style common in physics and related fields. All 
                  authors appear in a single block with superscript numbers linking each name to a list of affiliations 
                  printed below. This is the style native to  revtex4-2 (https://ctan.org/pkg/revtex) with the superscriptaddress option, 
                  and is familiar from journals such as Physical Review Letters. The package brings this style to the standard 
                  article class and compatible classes, without requiring a specialised document class.

autosp -- A Preprocessor that generates note-spacing commands for MusiXTeX scores
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/autosp
name:             autosp
caption:          A Preprocessor that generates note-spacing commands for MusiXTeX scores
author:           Bob Tennent
license:          gpl2+ = GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer (free)
version:          (2025-11-05)
last changes:     2025-11-05
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This program simplifies the creation of  MusiXTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/musixtex) scores by converting 
                  (non-standard) commands of the form \anotes … \en into one or more conventional note-spacing commands, 
                  as determined by the note values themselves, with \sk spacing commands inserted as necessary. The 
                  coding for an entire measure can be entered one part at a time, without concern for note-spacing changes 
                  within the part or spacing requirements of other parts.

                  For example,  \anotes\qa J\qa K&amp;\ca l\qa m\ca n\en generates \Notes\qa J\sk\qa K\sk&amp;\ca 
                  l\qa m\sk\ca n\en .

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/autosp/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/autosp/doc/autosp.pdf

axessibility -- Access to formulas in PDF files by assistive technologies
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/axessibility
name:             axessibility
caption:          Access to formulas in PDF files by assistive technologies
author:           Sandro Coriasco
author:           Nadir Murru
copyright:        Anna Capietto, Sandro Coriasco, Tiziana Armano, Boris Doubrov, Alexander Kozlovskiy, Nadir Murru, Dragan Ahmetovic, Cristian Bernareggi (2018-2020)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          3.0
description:      (no language specified) PDF documents containing formulas generated by LaTeX are usually not accessible by assistive technologies 
                  for visually impaired people and people with special educational needs (i.e., by screen readers and braille 
                  displays). The axessibility package manages this issue, allowing to create a PDF document where the formulas 
                  are read by these assistive technologies, since it automatically generates hidden comments in the PDF 
                  document (by means of the /ActualText attribute and/or suitable tags) in correspondence to each formula.

axodraw2 -- Feynman diagrams in a LaTeX document
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/axodraw2
name:             axodraw2
caption:          Feynman diagrams in a LaTeX document
author:           John Collins
author:           Jos Vermaseren
copyright:        John Collins and Jos Vermaseren (1994-2021)
license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
version:          2.1.1c (2021-03-05)
last changes:     2021-03-05
year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) This package defines macros for drawing Feynman graphs in LaTeX documents.

                  It is an important update of the  axodraw (https://ctan.org/pkg/axodraw) package, but since it 
                  is not completely backwards compatible, we have given the style file a changed name.

                  Many new features have been added, with new types of line, and much more flexibility in their properties.

                  In addition, it is now possible to use  axodraw2 with pdfLaTeX, as well as with the LaTeX-dvips 
                  method. However with pdfLaTeX (and also LuaLaTeX and XeLaTeX), an external program, axohelp , is 
                  used to perform the geometrical calculations needed for the pdf code inserted in the output file. The 
                  processing involves a run of pdfLaTeX, a run of axohelp , and then another run of pdfLaTeX.

babel -- Multilingual support for LaTeX, LuaLaTeX, XeLaTeX, and Plain TeX
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/babel
name:             babel
caption:          Multilingual support for LaTeX, LuaLaTeX, XeLaTeX, and Plain TeX
author:           Javier Bezos López
author:           Johannes L. Braams
copyright:        Javier Bezos and Johannes L. Braams (2012-2026)
copyright:        Johannes Braams et al. (1989-2012)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          26.11 (2026-08-21)
last changes:     2026-08-21
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) Babel is the multilingual environment for LaTeX (tailored for LuaTeX, pdfTeX and XeTeX), and sometimes 
                  Plain. Its aim is to provide a comprehensive localization framework for different languages, scripts 
                  and cultures based on the latest advances on international standards (Unicode, W3C, OpenType). It supports 
                  about 300 languages (with various levels of coverage) across about 45 scripts, including complex (like 
                  CJK, Indic) and RTL ones.

                  Besides the traditional  .ldf files, there are many locales built on a modern core that utilizes 
                  descriptive .ini files, with tools providing precise control over hyphenation and line breaking, 
                  captions, date formats (across various calendars), spacing, transliteration, numbering and other locale-specific 
                  typographical rules.

documentation:    Code documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/babel/base/babel-code.pdf
-- local file:    ./2221028058-babel-code.pdf
documentation:    User guide (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/babel/base/babel.pdf
-- local file:    ./3376270017-babel.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/babel/base/README.md
home page:        https://latex3.github.io/babel/
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/latex3/babel/issues
contact:          repository: https://github.com/latex3/babel
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/babel/base
installation:     https://ctan.org/tex-archive/install/macros/latex/required/babel-base.tds.zip

babel-hebrew -- Babel support for Hebrew

author:           Johannes L. Braams

copyright:        Boris Lavva and Johannes Braams (1997-2005)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.5 (2026-02-16)
last changes:     2026-02-16
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package provides the language definition file for support of Hebrew in  babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) . 
                  Macros to control the use of text direction control of TeX--XeT and e-TeX are provided (and may be used 
                  elsewhere).

                  Some shortcuts are defined, as well as translations to Hebrew of standard LaTeX names. For questions, 
                  bug reports, or support, please open an issue in the repository.

                  Note: the package is in maintenance mode. Bugs will be fixed, but no new features will be added.

                  The  .ldf file is only compatible with pdfLaTeX or LaTeX. Even then, for documents containing more 
                  than a short text in Hebrew, it is strongly recommended to use LuaTeX (with babel's .ini file or 
                  polyglossia). For short texts with pdfTeX, use the .ini file. Consult the documentation of babel 
                  for better settings for Hebrew.

version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) We recently (February, 2026) developed a hyphenation dictionary for the Kazakh language. After completing 
                  this project, the natural question arose of developing official support for the Kazakh language in TeX. 
                  Kazakh language support has been implemented to work with XeLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, and pdfLaTeX macro packages, 
                  they all work with babel package. TeX Live 2025 on Linux was used for testing. Hyphenation patterns support 
                  files were sent to maintainers.

                  XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support is also compatible with polyglossia.

                  We provide also sample files, to show the work of our package. BibTeX database file is also included 
                  to demonstrate compatibility with BibLaTeX. Notice that BibLaTeX support is not complete yet in this 
                  initial version, 1.0, it will be completed soon.

version:          0.3 (2015-05-20)
last changes:     2015-05-20
year:             2015
description:      (no language specified) The package provides very simplified (or ultra sloppy) support for Spanish in  Babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) , 
                  mostly as a fallback in case spanish.ldf (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel-spanish) fails for some reason. 
                  The package provides basic support for Spanish hyphenation, captions, date, frenchspacing, indentfirst, 
                  symbolic footnotes, enumerations, small caps roman numerals, and a handful of shorthands and Spanish 
                  mathematical operators. No options or attributes for customization are provided.

                  According to the author, the purpose of this package is nowadays better served by the  babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) package 
                  with option spanish.mexico .

bakoma-games -- BaKoMa modules for music and games
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bakoma-games
name:             bakoma-games
caption:          BaKoMa modules for music and games
author:           Basil Malyshev
license:          shareware = Shareware: A fee is required (not free)
description:      (no language specified) This module includes popular macro packages described in chapters 7 (Preparing music scores: MusiXTeX) 
                  and 8 (Playing games: Chess, Xiangqi — Chinese Chess, Go, Backgammon, Bridge, Crosswords) of the ‘LaTeX 
                  graphics Companion’. They are precompiled for use, together with fonts and documentation, directly in 
                  BaKoMa TeX. Fonts used by some packages are converted into formats suitable both for printing and for 
                  PDF generation. For example, for Chess the diagram fonts are converted into vector Type 3 font format. 
                  Board black squares are coded as a gray color instead of dashing. This approach gives the best results 
                  on printers and displays. Fonts for in-line notation are in Type 1 font format. For Go the special fonts 
                  are too hard to convert automatically and have been efficiently coded in Type 3 font format. For Backgammon 
                  the fonts were originally dithered as halftone, making them unsuitable for PDF. The halftone was emulated 
                  by using a grey colour in Type 3 fonts.

documentation:    Summary of the bundle (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/systems/win32/bakoma/macros/games.html
