bankstatement -- A LaTeX class for bank statements based on csv data
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bankstatement
name:             bankstatement
caption:          A LaTeX class for bank statements based on csv data
author:           Josef Kleber
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.9.2 (2015-11-14)
last changes:     2015-11-14
year:             2015
description:      (no language specified) More and more banks allow their customers to download posting records in various formats. By using the 
                  bankstatement class, you can create bank statements, as long as a csv format is available. At 
                  the moment, the csv-mt940 and csv-camt formats — used by many german Sparkassen — are supported. You 
                  can quite easily add support for other csv formats. Simply define the order of the keys in the csv data 
                  file and how to use them.

                  The terminology in this class — such as BIC (Business Identifier Code) or IBAN (International Bank Account 
                  Number) — is based on usage in the SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area).

                  The user may adjust the terminology to suit local needs.

                  currently includes upright and italic or oblique shapes in each of regular, bold and heavy weights. All 
                  fonts include the slashed zero and additional non-standard ligatures. The support package renames them 
                  according to the Karl Berry fontname scheme and defines two families. One of these primarily provides 
                  access to the “standard” or default characters while the other supports additional ligatures. The included 
                  package files provide access to these features in LaTeX.

bath-bst -- Harvard referencing style as recommended by the University of Bath Library
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bath-bst
name:             bath-bst
caption:          Harvard referencing style as recommended by the University of Bath Library
author:           Alex Ball
copyright:        University of Bath (2016-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          7.2 (2026-01-29)
last changes:     2026-01-29
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package provides a BibTeX style to format reference lists in the  Harvard style (https://www.bath.ac.uk/library/infoskills/referencing-plagiarism/harvard-bath-style.html) recommended

beamer -- A LaTeX class for producing presentations and slides
--------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer
name:             beamer
caption:          A LaTeX class for producing presentations and slides
author:           Joseph Wright
author:           Till Tantau
author:           Vedran Miletić
author:           samcarter
author:           Louis Stuart
copyright:        Vedran Miletić, Joseph Wright (2011-2015)
copyright:        Till Tantau (2003-2007)
copyright:        Joseph Wright, samcarter (2019-2026)
copyright:        Vedran Miletić (2010)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
license:          fdl = Free Documentation License (free)
license:          gpl2+ = GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer (free)
version:          3.78 (2026-08-20)
last changes:     2026-08-20
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The beamer LaTeX class can be used for producing slides. The class works in both PostScript and direct 
                  PDF output modes, using the  pgf (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) graphics system for visual effects.

                  Content is created in the frame environment, and each frame can be made up of a number of slides using 
                  a simple notation for specifying material to appear on each slide within a frame. Short versions of title, 
                  authors, institute can also be specified as optional parameters. Whole frame graphics are supported by 
                  plain frames. The class supports figure and table environments, transparency effects, varying slide transitions 
                  and animations. Beamer also provides compatibility with other packages like  prosper (https://ctan.org/pkg/prosper) .

                  The package now incorporates the functionality of the former  translator package, which is used 
                  for customising the package for use in other language environments.

                  Beamer depends on the following other packages:  atbegshi (https://ctan.org/pkg/atbegshi) , etoolbox 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox) , hyperref (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref) , ifpdf (https://ctan.org/pkg/ifpdf) , pgf 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) , and translator (https://ctan.org/pkg/translator) .

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/beamer/doc/beameruserguide.pdf

version:          1.10 (2026-04-08)
last changes:     2026-04-08
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) Beamer (https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer) is a very powerful and convenient document class to create 
                  presentations and slides. However, integrating multimedia in it, is still a bit of a faff. The (limited) 
                  functionality heavily relies on the availability of acroread. This package allows you to convert your 
                  beamer presentation to the reveal.js framework, rendering your presentation as an HTML website in your 
                  browser. This allows for easy incorporation of videos, audio fragments, iframe chunks, images and LaTeX 
                  animations.

beamerposter -- Extend beamer and a0poster for custom sized posters
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/beamerposter
name:             beamerposter
caption:          Extend beamer and a0poster for custom sized posters
author:           Philippe Dreuw
author:           Thomas Deselaers
copyright:        Philippe Dreuw and Thomas Deselaers (2015,2018)
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.13
description:      (no language specified) The package enables the user to use  beamer (https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer) style operations on a 
                  canvas of the sizes provided by a0poster (https://ctan.org/pkg/a0poster) ; font scaling is available 
                  (using packages such as type1cm (https://ctan.org/pkg/type1cm) if necessary).

                  In addition, the package allows the user to benefit from the nice colour box handling and alignment provided 
                  by the beamer class (for example, with rounded corners and shadows). Good looking posters may be created 
                  very rapidly.

                  Features include:

                  + scalable fonts using the fp and type1cm packages;
                  + posters in A-series sizes, and custom sizes like double A0 are possible;
                  + still applicable to custom beamer slides, e.g. 16:9 slides for a wide-screen (i.e. 1.78 aspect ratio);

                  + orientation may be portrait or landscape; a debug modeis provided.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/beamerposter/README

last changes:     2026-02-23
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package provides the Durham Beamer Theme, a content-first presentation theme for LaTeX  Beamer 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer) designed for teaching, research, and long-form academic presentations.

                  The theme emphasizes structural clarity, pacing awareness, and layout stability under dense textual and 
                  mathematical content. It is implemented entirely from first principles and not derived from any existing 
                  Beamer theme.

                  Conceptual inspiration from established themes such as  Metropolis (https://ctan.org/pkg/beamertheme-metropolis) is 
                  acknowledged; no external code is reused. The color palette is inspired by the visual identity of Durham 
                  University. This package is an independent academic contribution and not an official or endorsed Durham 
                  University template.

                  The package includes a modular theme implementation, a demo document with compiled PDF, and a user manual.

beamertheme-trigon -- A modern, elegant, and versatile theme for Beamer
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/beamertheme-trigon
name:             beamertheme-trigon
caption:          A modern, elegant, and versatile theme for Beamer
author:           Thomas Lambert
copyright:        Thomas Lambert (2021-2023)
license:          cc-by-sa-4 = CC BY-SA 4.0 (free)
version:          0.7.0 (2023-02-20)
last changes:     2023-02-20
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) This package provides a modern, elegant and versatile theme for  Beamer (https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer) , 
                  with a high degree of customization.

                  Trigon found its origin and inspiration in the graphical guidelines resulting from the visual identity 
                  overhaul of the University of Liège. Although directly inspired from these guidelines, the theme was 
                  stripped out of any mention or specificities related to the University and its faculties. This makes 
                  the Trigon theme perfectly suitable for many different contexts.

                  The final product provides a modern, elegant and versatile theme with a high degree of customization. 
                  The main design focuses on triangular shapes for major layout elements and noise minimization for the 
                  main body of the work.

                  The theme’s implementation is heavily inspired from the  Metropolis theme (https://ctan.org/pkg/beamertheme-metropolis) . 
                  Most options from Metropolis (https://ctan.org/pkg/beamertheme-metropolis) have been ported to 
                  Trigon in order to improve customization and ease-of-use. Trigon also includes different styles and layouts 
                  for the main title page, the section page and the default slide background.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/beamer-contrib/themes/beamertheme-trigon/README.md

beastie -- Beastie is an experiment in parsing and processing BibTeX files
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/beastie
name:             beastie
caption:          Beastie is an experiment in parsing and processing BibTeX files
author:           Norman Gray
license:          0bsd = Zero-Clause BSD (free)
license:          bsd2 = Simplified BSD License (free)
version:          0.14.1
description:      (no language specified) Beastie is:

                  + A parser for .bib files, amongst others.
                  + A implementation of the .bst BibTeX Style Language.
                  + That .bst implementation is hosted in a dialect of Scheme, extended with suitable parsing and processing 
                    primitives.
The goals of this project are:

                  + to explore ways of processing .bib files which  'aren't' exclusively based on .bst;
                  + to provide a second implementation of the BST language; and
                  + to initiate some sort of conversation about BibTeX standards, broadly construed.
There was an article about Beastie v0.12 in TUGboat, 46:2, pp.220–227 (2025), doi: 10.47397/tb/46-2/tb143gray-beastie 
                  (https://doi.org/10.47397/tb/46-2/tb143gray-beastie) .

bestpapers -- A BibTeX package to produce lists of authors’ best papers
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bestpapers
name:             bestpapers
caption:          A BibTeX package to produce lists of authors’ best papers
author:           Boris Veytsman
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) Many people preparing their résumés find the requirement “please list five (or six, or ten) papers authored 
                  by you”. The same requirement is often stated for reports prepared by professional teams. The creation 
                  of such lists may be a cumbersome task. Even more difficult is it to support such lists over the time, 
                  when new papers are added.

                  The BibTeX style  bestpapers.bst is intended to facilitate this task. It is based on the idea that 
                  it is easier to score than to sort: We can assign a score to a paper and then let the computer select 
                  the papers with highest scores.

                  This work was commissioned by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, United States Treasury.

                  This package is in the public domain.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/contrib/bestpapers/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/contrib/bestpapers/bestpapers-guide.pdf

bezierplot -- Approximate smooth function graphs with cubic bezier splines for use with TikZ or MetaPost
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bezierplot
name:             bezierplot
caption:          Approximate smooth function graphs with cubic bezier splines for use with TikZ or MetaPost
author:           Linus Romer
copyright:        Linus Romer (2018-2024)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.6 (2024-11-02)
last changes:     2024-11-02
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) This package consists of a Lua program as well as a (Lua)LaTeX  .sty file.

                  Given a smooth function,  bezierplot returns a smooth bezier path written in TikZ notation (which 
                  also matches MetaPost) that approximates the graph of the function. For polynomial functions of degree 
                  ≤ 3 and their inverses the approximation is exact (up to numeric precision).

                  bezierplot also finds special points such as extreme points and inflection points and reduces 
                  the number of used points.

bib2gls -- Command line application to convert .bib files to glossaries-extra.sty resource files
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bib2gls
name:             bib2gls
caption:          Command line application to convert .bib files to glossaries-extra.sty resource files
author:           Nicola Talbot
copyright:        Nicola L. C. Talbot (2017-2025)
license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
version:          4.7 (2025-11-13)
last changes:     2025-11-13
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This Java command line application may be used to extract glossary information stored in a  .bib file 
                  and convert it into glossary entry definition commands.

                  This application should be used with  glossaries-extra.sty (https://ctan.org/pkg/glossaries-extra) ’s 
                  ‘record’ package option. It performs two functions in one:

                  + selects entries according to records found in the  .aux file (similar to bibtex (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) ),

                  + hierarchically sorts entries and collates location lists (similar to  makeindex (https://ctan.org/pkg/makeindex) or xindy 
                    (https://ctan.org/pkg/xindy) ).
The glossary entries can then be managed in a system such as  JabRef (https://ctan.org/pkg/jabref) , 
                  and only the entries that are actually required will be defined, reducing the resources required by TeX.

                  The supplementary application  convertgls2bib can be used to convert existing .tex files 
                  containing definitions ( \newglossaryentry etc.) to the .bib format required by bib2gls .

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): pkg:/README.md

bib2xhtml -- Convert BibTeX Files into XHTML

name:             bib2xhtml
caption:          Convert BibTeX Files into XHTML
author:           David Hull
author:           Diomidis Spinellis
copyright:        Diomidis Spinellis (2002-2010)
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          2.35
description:      (no language specified) bib2xhtml is a program that converts BibTeX files into HTML (specifically XHTML 1.0). The conversion 
                  is mostly done by specialized BibTeX style files, derived from a converted bibliography style template. 
                  This ensures that the original BibTeX styles are faithfully reproduced. Some postprocessing is performed 
                  by Perl code.

                  This is an update of the bib2html program written by David Hull in 1996 and maintained by him until 1998. 
                  I have been a happy user of the program since 1995, using the program to keep my publication list up 
                  to date, and, lately, to generate the on-line bibliography list for my book Code Reading: The Open Source 
                  Perspective (Addison-Wesley 2003). After 1998 no other changes were made to the program, and I failed 
                  to locate an active program home page. Since there were a number of changes I needed to bring the program 
                  up to date with evolving web standards, I decided to adopt bib2html for maintenance, evolution, and further 
                  distribution. The first new public release made in 2004, features support for XHTML 1.0.

bibarts -- “Arts”-style bibliographical information

Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bibarts
name:             BibArts
caption:          “Arts”-style bibliographical information
author:           Timo Baumann
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          2.6
description:      (no language specified) BibArts is a LaTeX package to assist in making bibliographical features common in the arts and the humanities 
                  (history, political science, philosophy, etc.).

                  bibarts.sty provides commands for quotations, abbreviations, and especially for a formatted citation 
                  of literature, journals (periodicals), edited sources, and archive sources. In difference to earlier 
                  versions, BibArts 2.x helps to use slanted fonts (italics) and is able to set ibidem automatically in 
                  footnotes. It will also copy all citation information, abbreviations, and register key words into lists 
                  for an automatically generated appendix. These lists may refer to page and footnote numbers. BibArts 
                  has nothing to do with BibTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) . The lists are created by bibsort (see 
                  below).

                  BibArts requires the program  bibsort , for which the sources and a Windows executable are provided. 
                  This program creates the bibliography without using MakeIndex (https://ctan.org/pkg/makeindex) or BibTeX 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) . Its source is not written with any specific operating system in mind. 
                  A summary of contents is in English; the full documentation is in German.

bibextract -- Utilities to extract BibTeX data
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bibextract
name:             bibextract
caption:          Utilities to extract BibTeX data
author:           Nelson H. F. Beebe
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          1.09
description:      (no language specified) A set of scripts for extracting entries from .bib file, in particular those cited in a particular document.

                  Bibextract itself extracts from a list of BibTeX .bib files those bibliography entries that match a pair 
                  of specified regular expressions, sending them to stdout, together with all BibTeX  @Preamble{...} and @String{...} commands.

                  Citefind from a list of BibTeX .bib files those bibliography entries that match a specified list of citation 
                  tags, possibly produced by citetags.

                  Citetags extracts BibTeX citation tags from a LaTeX source file or .aux file and sends them to stdout, 
                  possibly for later input to citefind.

bibfile-reformat-pages -- Puts .bib file page ranges into uniform format
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bibfile-reformat-pages
name:             bibfile-reformat-pages
caption:          Puts .bib file page ranges into uniform format
author:           Barak A. Pearlmutter
copyright:        Barak A. Pearlmutter (2004)
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
description:      (no language specified) This is a small gawk script to put all the  pages= page ranges in a .bib file into a uniform 
                  format, either 1234-1256 or upon request 1234-56; null ranges such as 1234-1234 are always scrunched 
                  to just 1234. The script squeezes out spaces around the separator; can make all separators one- or two-hyphens 
                  upon request. The script is very conservative: it is probably impossible for it actually to mess up a 
                  file.

bibfilex -- A free bibliographic manager for BibLaTeX
-----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bibfilex
name:             bibfilex
caption:          A free bibliographic manager for BibLaTeX
author:           Massimo Nardello
copyright:        Massimo Nardello (2013-2016)
license:          gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
version:          1.2.8
description:      (no language specified) Bibfilex is a free bibliographic manager for GNU/Linux, Windows and OS X. It is useful for creating and 
                  managing archives of bibliographical items with possible attachments of any kind according to BibLaTeX 
                  structure and rules, but it may also be used with a wordprocessor like Writer or Word.

                  Bibfilex is less advanced than other bibliographic managers like  JabRef (https://jabref.sourceforge.net/) or 
                  KBibTeX and allows only few customizations. Its strength is simplicity and speed, since it's a compiled 
                  software and uses a fast database, Sqlite, for storing data.

                  Bibfilex is written in Free Pascal with Lazarus.

                  like grep, only it prints the whole entry (paragraph) and not just the line that matches. The program

bibhtml -- BibTeX support for HTML files

Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bibhtml
name:             bibhtml
caption:          BibTeX support for HTML files
author:           Norman Gray
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          2.0.2 (2013-09-08)
last changes:     2013-09-08
year:             2013
description:      (no language specified) Bibhtml consists of a Perl script and a set of  BibTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) style files, 
                  which together allow you to output a bibliography as a collection of HTML files. The references in the 
                  text are linked directly to the corresponding bibliography entry, and if a URL is defined in the entry 
                  within the BibTeX database file, then the generated bibliography entry is linked to this. The package 
                  provides three different style files derived from each of the standard plain.bst and alpha.bst, as well 
                  as two style files derived from abbrv.bst and unsrt.bst (i.e., eight in total).

biblatex -- Sophisticated Bibliographies in LaTeX
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex
name:             BibLaTeX
caption:          Sophisticated Bibliographies in LaTeX
author:           Philip Kime
author:           Philipp Lehman
copyright:        Philip Kime, Moritz Wemheuer (2018-2025)
copyright:        Philip Kime, Audrey Boruvka, Joseph Wright (2012-2025)
copyright:        Philipp Lehman (2006-2012)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          3.21 (2025-07-10)
last changes:     2025-07-10
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) BibLaTeX is a complete reimplementation of the bibliographic facilities provided by LaTeX. Formatting 
                  of the bibliography is entirely controlled by LaTeX macros, and a working knowledge of LaTeX should be 
                  sufficient to design new bibliography and citation styles. BibLaTeX uses its own data backend program 
                  called  “biber” (https://ctan.org/pkg/biber) to read and process the bibliographic data. With biber 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/biber) , BibLaTeX has many features rivalling or surpassing other bibliography 
                  systems. To mention a few:

                  + Full Unicode support
                  + Highly customisable sorting using the Unicode Collation Algorithm + CLDR tailoring
                  + Highly customisable bibliography labels
                  + Complex macro-based on-the-fly data modification without changing your data sources
                  + A tool mode for transforming bibliographic data sources
                  + Multiple bibliographies and lists of bibliographic information in the same document with different sorting

                  + Highly customisable data source inheritance rules
                  + Polyglossia and babel support for automatic language switching for bibliographic entries and citations

                  + Automatic bibliography data recoding (UTF-8 -&gt; latin1, LaTeX macros -&gt; UTF-8 etc)
                  + Remote data sources
                  + Highly sophisticated automatic name and name list disambiguation system
                  + Highly customisable data model so users can define their own bibliographic data types
                  + Validation of bibliographic data against a data model
                  + Subdivided and/or filtered bibliographies, bibliographies per chapter, section etc.
Apart from the features unique to BibLaTeX, the package also incorporates core features of the following 
                  packages:  babelbib (https://ctan.org/pkg/babelbib) , bibtopic (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtopic) , bibunits 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibunits) , chapterbib (https://ctan.org/pkg/chapterbib) , cite (https://ctan.org/pkg/cite) , inlinebib 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/inlinebib) , mcite (https://ctan.org/pkg/mcite) and mciteplus (https://ctan.org/pkg/mciteplus) , mlbib 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/mlbib) , multibib (https://ctan.org/pkg/multibib) , splitbib (https://ctan.org/pkg/splitbib) .

                  The package strictly requires

                  +  e-TeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/etex) 
                  +  BibTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) , bibtex8 , or Biber (https://ctan.org/pkg/biber) 

                  +  etoolbox (https://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox)            .1 or later
                  +  logreq (https://ctan.org/pkg/logreq) 1.0 or later
                  +  keyval (https://ctan.org/pkg/keyval) 
                  +  ifthen (https://ctan.org/pkg/ifthen) 
                  +  url (https://ctan.org/pkg/url) 
 Biber (https://ctan.org/pkg/biber) , babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) / polyglossia 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia) , and csquotes (https://ctan.org/pkg/csquotes) 4.4 or later 
                  are strongly recommended.

documentation:    Package documentation (English): pkg:/doc/biblatex.pdf
documentation:    Release notes for current version (English): pkg:/CHANGES.md

biblatex-abs-annote -- Annotated bibliographies with abstracts and annotations for BibLaTeX
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-abs-annote
name:             biblatex-abs-annote
caption:          Annotated bibliographies with abstracts and annotations for BibLaTeX
author:           Cameron Wimpy
copyright:        Cameron Wimpy (2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.1.1 (2026-04-19)
last changes:     2026-04-19
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package extends any BibLaTeX style with an annotated-bibliography presentation: below each reference 
                  it renders the entry's abstract and the user's annotation, both drawn from standard BibLaTeX fields (abstract, 
                  and annotation or annote). Either field may be omitted on a per-entry basis, so the same bibliography 
                  can mix plain and annotated citations freely. The package patches the sixteen standard BibLaTeX drivers 
                  via xpatch, so it composes with any bibliography style that uses the standard driver names (authoryear, 
                  apa, numeric, chicago-authordate, etc.). All visual aspects (e.g., labels, fonts, indentation, and spacing) 
                  are controlled by redefinable commands and lengths. The package is the LaTeX component of the cross-format 
                  ab-annotate toolchain, which shares the same .bib conventions with companion packages for Typst and Quarto.

biblatex-accursius -- Citing features for Italian jurists
---------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-accursius
name:             biblatex-accursius
caption:          Citing features for Italian jurists
author:           Francesco Contini
copyright:        Francesco Contini (2024)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) This style is primarily aimed at Italian legal jurists and provides them with the ability to cite legal 
                  materials, such as legislative acts, regulations, soft law, treaties and case law. Additionally, the 
                  style codifies the most prevalent citation practices amongst Italian legal scholars.

                  Specifically, with regard to the citation of legal materials, this style, instead of developing the entry 
                  types  @jurisdiction , @legal , and @legislation , creates a new one: @itprov , 
                  which can describe a wide range of legal sources. Furthermore, it creates a second new entry type: @notetoprov , 
                  which is used specifically to cite so-called “note a sentenza” (notes to judgement), which closely mirrors @itprov , 
                  but is literature and, therefore, is intended to have the same treatment as standard entry types.

                  The citation commands are the standard ones.

                  The  @itprov entry type comprises the list institution to indicate which authority adopted 
                  the cited act; the kindprov , nprov , provtitle (or titleparties ) fields to 
                  indicate the minimal ‘ID’ of the act and many others. Finally, the entry type allows to specify where 
                  the cited act was consulted, whether from an official bulletin (the ofbull field), an official 
                  portal or a private database (the ofportal field), or a journal or collection.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-accursius/biblatex-accursius.pdf
-- local file:    ./4169125432-biblatex-accursius.pdf

license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.2.0 (2026-08-15)
last changes:     2026-08-15
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package extends  biblatex-apa (https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-apa) with support for Traditional 
                  Chinese citation and bibliography formatting according to APA 7.

                  The package provides:

                  + full-width Chinese punctuation for citations in Traditional Chinese text;
                  + entry-specific name strings and bibliography punctuation based on the langid field;
                  + mixed Chinese and Western entries within a single bibliography;
                  + separate control of the language of citation text and the language of individual bibliography entries;

                  + operation without babel or polyglossia, making it suitable for xeCJK documents.
The provided formatting follows Traditional Chinese academic conventions used in Taiwan. Simplified Chinese 
                  conventions are not supported.

                  A test suite for checking the rendered output is included.

biblatex-claves -- A tool to manage claves of old literature with BibLaTeX
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-claves
name:             biblatex-claves
caption:          A tool to manage claves of old literature with BibLaTeX
author:           Maïeul Rouquette
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.2.1 (2017-11-19)
last changes:     2017-11-19
year:             2017
description:      (no language specified) When studying antique and medieval literature, we may find many different texts published with the same 
                  title, or, in contrary, the same text published with different titles.

                  To avoid confusion, scholars have published claves, which are books listing ancient texts, identifying 
                  them by an identifier — a number or a string of text. For example, for early Christianity, we have the 
                  Bibliotheca Hagiographica Graeca, the Clavis Apocryphorum Novi Testamenti and other claves.

                  It could be useful to print the identifier of a texts in one specific clavis, or in many claves. The 
                  package allows us to create new field for different claves, and to present all these fields in a consistent 
                  way.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-claves/documentation/biblatex-claves.pdf
-- local file:    ./9074888347-biblatex-claves.pdf

on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-claves
on MikTeX:        biblatex-claves
on TeXLive:       biblatex-claves
keyword:          biblatex (BibLaTeX bibliography support)
language(s):      nls: no language specified

biblatex-greifswald -- The author-date BibLaTeX Greifswald style
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-greifswald
name:             biblatex-greifswald
caption:          The author-date BibLaTeX Greifswald style
author:           Jonathan Garbe
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          1 (2026-05-25)
last changes:     2026-05-25
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) Greifswald bibliographies consist of two columns: The left one contains the publication date, while title 
                  and other bibliographical data (the body) are printed in the right column. The author names are printed 
                  in bold face and span both columns. Titles are printed upright and not surrounded by quotation marks.

                  The body of dependent publications (@article, @inCollection, etc.) is divided into two paragraphs: The 
                  first contains information that relates to the dependent publication itself, such as title, DOI and URL; 
                  data relating to the parent publication, such as that one's title, editor and ISBN, is printed in the 
                  second.

                  The publisher and its location are printed only if neither DOI, ISBN nor ISSN are known.

documentation:    Example of Use (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-greifswald/biblatex-greifswald-example.pdf
-- local file:    ./5849232167-biblatex-greifswald-example.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-greifswald/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-greifswald/biblatex-greifswald-documentation.pdf
-- local file:    ./9298140949-biblatex-greifswald-documentation.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-greifswald
on MikTeX:        biblatex-greifswald

name:             biblatex-ieee
caption:          IEEE style files for BibLaTeX
author:           Joseph Wright

license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.4f (2025-08-01)
last changes:     2025-08-01
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This is a  BibLaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex) style that implements the bibliography style 
                  of the IEEE for BibLaTeX. The implementation follows standard BibLaTeX conventions, and can be used simply 
                  by loading BibLaTeX with the appropriate option:

                  \usepackage[style=ieee]{biblatex} 

                  A demonstration database is provided to show how to format input for the style.

                  biblatex-ieee requires BibLaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex)            .7 or later, and works 
                  with both BibTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) and Biber (https://ctan.org/pkg/biber) as 
                  the database back-end.

last changes:     2017-01-25
year:             2017
description:      (no language specified) This package adds new fields of “name” type to the standard entry types of BibLaTeX.
For example:

                  + maineditor, for a  @collection , means the editor of @mvcollection , and not the editor of 
                    the @collection .
                  + bookineditor, for a  @bookinbook , means the editor of the entry, and not, as the standard editor 
                    field, the editor of the volume in which the entry is contained.

biblatex-ms -- Sophisticated Bibliographies in LaTeX (multiscript version)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-ms
name:             biblatex-ms
caption:          Sophisticated Bibliographies in LaTeX (multiscript version)
author:           Philip Kime
copyright:        Philipp Lehman, Joseph Wright, Audrey Boruvka, Philip Kime (2012-2023)
copyright:        Philipp Lehman (2006-2012)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          4.0-1
description:      (no language specified) This package is the “multiscript” version of the  BibLaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex) package 
                  intended to solve the issues faced by those wishing to create multilingual bibliographies. It is intended 
                  to be backwards-compatible with the standard BibLaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex) package and 
                  includes significantly enhanced optional functionality:

                  + Fields in data files can have different form/language alternates in the same entry
                  + Options to select/print a specific alternate are generally available
                  + babel/polyglossia language switching is done automatically based on the language associated with a field

The intention is that this version will eventually replace standard BibLaTeX and is being released as 
                  an independent package to allow for wider testing and feedback. It can be installed in parallel with 
                  standard BibLaTeX and the package name is  biblatex-ms . It requires the use of the multiscript 
                  version of biber (biber-ms).

biblatex-opcit-booktitle -- Use op. cit. for the booktitle of a subentry
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-opcit-booktitle
name:             biblatex-opcit-booktitle
caption:          Use op. cit. for the booktitle of a subentry
author:           Maïeul Rouquette
copyright:        Maïeul Rouquette (2015-2018)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.9.0 (2018-10-24)
last changes:     2018-10-24
year:             2018
description:      (no language specified) The default citation styles verbose-trad1+; verbose-trad2 ; verbose-trad3 use the op. cit. form in order 
                  to have a shorter reference when a title has already been cited. However, when you cite two entries which 
                  share the same booktitle but not the same  title , the op. cit. mechanism does not work.

                  This package enables to obtain references like this:

                  + Author1, Title, in Booktitle, Location, Publisher, Year, pages
                  + xxx
                  + Author2, Title2, in Booktitle, op. cit, pages.

biblatex-oxref -- BibLaTeX styles inspired by the Oxford Guide to Style
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-oxref
name:             biblatex-oxref
caption:          BibLaTeX styles inspired by the Oxford Guide to Style
author:           Alex Ball
copyright:        Alex Ball (2016-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          3.4 (2026-04-14)
last changes:     2026-04-14
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This bundle provides four BibLaTeX styles that implement (many of) the stipulations and examples provided 
                  by the 2014  'New Hart’s Rules' and the 2002 'Oxford Guide to Style' :

                  + ‘oxnotes’ is a style similar to the standard ‘verbose’, intended for use with footnotes;
                  + ‘oxnum’ is a style similar to the standard ‘numeric’, intended for use with numeric in-text citations;

                  + ‘oxalph’ is a style similar to the standard ‘alphabetic’, intended for use with alphabetic in-text citations;

                  + ‘oxyear’ is a style similar to the standard ‘author-year’, intended for use with parenthetical in-text 
                    citations.
The bundle provides support for a wide variety of content types, including manuscripts, audiovisual resources, 
                  social media and legal references.

Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-readbbl
name:             biblatex-readbbl
caption:          Read a .bbl file created by biber
author:           Herbert Voß
copyright:        Herbert Voss (2020)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          0.01 (2022-01-09)
last changes:     2022-01-09
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) This small package modifies the  biblatex (https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex) macro which reads a .bbl file 
                  created by Biber (https://ctan.org/pkg/biber) . It is thus possible to include a .bbl file 
                  into the main document with the filecontents environment and send it to a publisher who does not need 
                  to run the Biber (https://ctan.org/pkg/biber) program.

                  However, when the bibliography changes one has to create a new  .bbl file.

biblatex-shortfields -- Use short forms of fields with BibLaTeX
---------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-shortfields
name:             biblatex-shortfields
caption:          Use short forms of fields with BibLaTeX
author:           Maïeul Rouquette
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.0.1
description:      (no language specified) The BibLaTeX package provides  shortseries and shortjournal field, but the default styles 
                  don't use them.

                  It also provides a mechanism to print the equivalence between short forms of fields and long fields ( \printbiblist ), 
                  but this mechanism does not allow to mix between different type of short fields, for example, between 
                  short forms of journal title and short forms of series titles.

                  This package provides a solution to these two problems: 
                  + If a  shortjournal field is defined, it prints it instead of the \journal field.
                  + If a  shortseries field is defined, it prints it instead of the \series field.
                  + It provides a  \printbibshortfields command to print a list of the sort forms of the fields.
                  + This list also includes the claves defined with the  biblatex-claves (https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-claves) package 
                    version 1.2 or later.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-shortfields/documentation/biblatex-shortfields.pdf
-- local file:    ./4744547614-biblatex-shortfields.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-shortfields/README
contact:          bugs: https://framagit.org/maieul/biblatex-shortfields/issues
contact:          repository: https://framagit.org/maieul/biblatex-shortfields
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-shortfields

biblatex2bibitem -- Convert BibLaTeX-generated bibliography to bibitems
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex2bibitem
name:             biblatex2bibitem
caption:          Convert BibLaTeX-generated bibliography to bibitems
author:           Nikolai Avdeev
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.2.2 (2022-01-17)
last changes:     2022-01-17
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) Some journals accept the reference list only as  \bibitem s. If you use BibTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) , 
                  there is no problem: just paste the content of the .bbl file into your document. However, there 
                  was no out-of-the-box way to do the same for biblatex (https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex) , and you 
                  had to struggle with searching appropriate .bst files, or formatting your reference list by hand, 
                  or something like that.

                  Using the workaround provided by this package solves the problem.

name:             bibleref

author:           Nicola Talbot
author:           Maïeul Rouquette

description:      (no language specified) The bibleref package offers consistent formatting of references to parts of the Christian bible, in a 
                  number of well-defined formats.

bibtex -- Process bibliographies (bib files) for LaTeX or other formats
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex
name:             bibtex
caption:          Process bibliographies (bib files) for LaTeX or other formats
author:           Oren Patashnik
license:          knuth = Knuth License (free)
version:          0.99e
description:      (no language specified) BibTeX allows the user to store his citation data in generic form, while printing citations in a document 
                  in the form specified by a BibTeX style, to be specified in the document itself (one often needs a LaTeX 
                  citation-style package, such as  natbib (https://ctan.org/pkg/natbib) , as well).

                  BibTeX knows nothing about Unicode sorting algorithms or scripts, although it will pass on whatever bytes 
                  it reads. Its descendant  bibtexu (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtexu) does support Unicode, via the 
                  ICU library. The older alternative bibtex8 (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex8) supports 8-bit character 
                  sets.

                  Another Unicode-aware alternative is the (independently developed)  biber (https://ctan.org/pkg/biber) program, 
                  used with the BibLaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex) package to typeset its output.

documentation:    Using BibTeX (no language specified): pkg:/btxdoc.pdf
documentation:    Writing BibTeX styles (no language specified): pkg:/btxhak.pdf
documentation:    BibTeX Frequently Asked Questions (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/contrib/doc/btxFAQ.pdf

bibtools -- Bib management tools
--------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtools
name:             bibtools
caption:          Bib management tools
author:           David Kotz
author:           Daniel Gildea
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
description:      (no language specified) A set of bibliography tools. Includes:

                  +  aux2bib , a perl script which will take an .aux file and make a portable .bib file 
                    to go with it;
                  +  bibify , a shell script that will optimise away one pass of the LaTeX/BibTeX cycle, in some cases;

                  +  bibkey , a shell script that finds entries whose “ keyword ” field matches the given keys 
                    (uses sed and awk);
                  +  cleantex , a shell script to tidy up after a LaTeX run;
                  +  looktex , a shell script to list entries that match a given regexp;
                  +  makebib , a shell script to make an exportable .bib file from an existing (set of) .bib file(s) 
                    and an optional set of citations (uses sed)
                  +  printbib , a shell script to make a dvi file from a .bib file, sorted by cite key, 
                    and including fields like “ keyword ”, “ abstract ”, and “ comment ”.
                  +  bib2html , a perl script that makes a browsable HTML version of a bibliography (several .bst files 
                    are supplied); and
                  +  citekeys , a shell script that lists the citation keys of a .bib file.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/utils/bibtools/README
documentation:    Demo of bib2html (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/utils/bibtools/demo.html

bibtopic -- Include multiple bibliographies in a document
---------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtopic
name:             bibtopic
caption:          Include multiple bibliographies in a document
author:           Stefan Ulrich
author:           Pierre Basso
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          1.1a
description:      (no language specified) The package allows the user to include several bibliographies covering different ‘topics’ or bibliographic 
                  material into a document (e.g., one bibliography for primary literature and one for secondary literature). 
                  The package provides commands to include either all references from a  .bib file, only the references 
                  actually cited or those not cited in your document. The user has to construct a separate .bib file 
                  for each bibliographic ‘topic’, each of which will be processed separately by BibTeX.

                  If you want to have bibliographies specific to one part of a document, see the packages  bibunits 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibunits) or chapterbib (https://ctan.org/pkg/chapterbib) .

bibutils -- A collection of bibliography format convertors
----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bibutils
name:             bibutils
caption:          A collection of bibliography format convertors
author:           Chris Putnam
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          6.6
description:      (no language specified) The bibutils program set interconverts between various bibliography formats using a common MODS-format 
                  XML intermediate. For example, one can convert RIS-format files to BibTeX by doing two transformations: 
                  RIS-&gt;MODS-&gt;BibTeX. By using a common intermediate for N formats, only 2N programs are required 
                  and not N^2-N. These programs operate on the command line and are styled after standard UNIX-like filters.

                  The author reckons to use the tools at the command line, but they are suitable for scripting and have 
                  been incorporated into a number of different bibliographic projects.

on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/utils/bibutils

keyword:          bibtex-gen (derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries)

author:           Denys Duchier
license:          noinfo = noinfo

year:             1993
description:      (no language specified) Defines a  Tabular environment, which is (in effect) a tabular* environment that can split 
                  across pages. The major distinction is that \Tabular doesn't take an optional argument. It behaves 
                  much like \begin{tabular*}{\linewidth} with \Tabularleftskip and \Tabularrightskip used 
                  as the stretchable glue on either side.

                  The package feels as if it were a predecessor of the current LaTeX  longtable (https://ctan.org/pkg/longtable) package.

bitelist -- Split list, in TeX’s mouth
--------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bitelist
name:             bitelist
caption:          Split list, in TeX’s mouth
author:           Uwe Lück
copyright:        Uwe Lück (2012)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.1
description:      (no language specified) The package provides commands for “splitting” a token list at the first occurrence of another (specified) 
                  token list. I.e., for given token lists  's' , 't' return 'b' and the shortest 'a' , 
                  such that 't = a s b' .

                  The package’s mechanism differs from those of packages providing similar features, in the following ways:

                  
                  + the method uses TeX’s mechanism of reading delimited macro parameters;
                  + splitting macros work by pure expansion, without assignments;
                  + the operation is carried out in a single macro call.
A variant of the operation is provided, that retains outer braces.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/bitelist/bitelist.pdf
-- local file:    ./4252055192-bitelist.pdf

on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/bitelist
installation:     https://ctan.org/tex-archive/install/macros/generic/bitelist.tds.zip
on MikTeX:        bitelist

author:           David Carlisle
copyright:        David Carlisle (1992, 1999, 2015)

version:          0.07
description:      (no language specified) An experimental package which implements an environment, blockarray, that may be used in the same way 
                  as the array or tabular environments of standard LaTeX, or their extended versions defined in  array 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/array) . If used in math-mode, blockarray acts like array, otherwise it acts 
                  like tabular.

                  The package implements a new method of defining column types, and also  block and block* environments, 
                  for specifying sub-arrays of the main array. What’s more, the \footnote command works inside a 
                  blockarray.

bodeplot -- Draw Bode, Nyquist and Nichols plots with gnuplot or pgfplots
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/bodeplot
name:             bodeplot
caption:          Draw Bode, Nyquist and Nichols plots with gnuplot or pgfplots
author:           Rushikesh Kamalapurkar
copyright:        Rushikesh Kamalapurkar (2021-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          3.1 (2026-05-19)
last changes:     2026-05-19
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This is a LaTeX package to plot Bode, Nichols, and Nyquist diagrams. It provides added functionality 
                  over the similar  bodegraph (https://ctan.org/pkg/bodegraph) package:

                  + New  \BodeZPK and \BodeTF commands to generate Bode plots of any transfer function given 
                    either poles, zeros, gain, and delay, or numerator and denominator coefficients and delay
                  + Support for unstable poles and zeros.
                  + Support for complex poles and zeros.
                  + Support for general stable and unstable second order transfer functions.
                  + Support for both  Gnuplot (https://ctan.org/pkg/gnuplot) (default) and pgfplots (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgfplots) (package 
                    option pgf ).
                  + Support for linear and asymptotic approximation of magnitude and phase plots of any transfer function

--------------------------------------------------------

name:             bondgraphs
caption:          Draws bond graphs in LaTeX, using PGF/TikZ
author:           Geert Folkertsma
copyright:        Geert Folkertsma (2014)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.0.1 (2015-03-23)
last changes:     2015-03-23
year:             2015
description:      (no language specified) The package is used to draw bond graphs in LaTeX. It uses a recent version (3.0+) of  PGF and TikZ 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) for the drawing, hence, it is mainly a set of TikZ styles that makes the 
                  drawing of bond graphs easier.

                  Compared to the  bondgraph (https://ctan.org/pkg/bondgraph) package this package relies more on 
                  TikZ styles and less on macros, to generate the drawings. As such it can be more flexible than his, but 
                  requires more TikZ knowledge of the user.

boolexpr -- A boolean expression evaluator and a switch command
---------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/boolexpr
name:             boolexpr
caption:          A boolean expression evaluator and a switch command
author:           Florent Chervet
copyright:        Florent Chervet (2009)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          3.14
description:      (no language specified) The  \boolexpr macro evaluates boolean expressions in a purely expandable way.

                  \boolexpr{ A \OR B \AND C } expands to 0 if the logical expression is TRUE. A, B, C may be: numeric 
                  expressions such as: x=y , x&lt;&gt;y , x&gt;y or x&lt;y ;
– boolean switches: \iftrue 
                  0\else 1\fi ;
– conditionals: \ifcsname whatsit\endcsname 0\else 1\fi ;
– another \boolexpr : \boolexpr{ 
                  D \OR E \AND F }: 

                  \boolexpr may be used with \ifcase: 
 |
\ifcase\boolexpr{ A \OR B \AND C }
What to do if true
\else
What to do if false
\fi
| 

                  The  \switch command (which is also expandable) has the form: |
\switch
\case{&lt;boolean expression&gt;} ...
\case{&lt;boolean expression&gt;} ...
...
\otherwise ...
\endswitch
|

boustrophedon -- A LaTeX package for boustrophedon typography
-------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/boustrophedon
name:             boustrophedon
caption:          A LaTeX package for boustrophedon typography
author:           Aris Chatzichristos
copyright:        Aris Chatzichristos, PhD (2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.1.0
description:      (no language specified) This package typesets text in  'boustrophedon' style, alternating the writing direction on each 
                  line.

                  Have you ever wondered why most Western languages are written left-to-right, while many Middle Eastern 
                  languages are written right-to-left? Both conventions may seem arbitrary today — but this was not always 
                  the case. In one of the earliest fully developed alphabets, the Archaic Greek alphabet (from  'alpha' and 'beta' , 
                  hence “ 'alphabet' ”), writing was often performed 'boustrophedon' , meaning “as the ox turns 
                  in ploughing.” Text was written left-to-right on one line, then right-to-left on the next, with both 
                  the direction of the text and the letterforms themselves mirrored accordingly.

                  This method creates a continuous flow of reading, as the reader does not need to jump back to the start 
                  of each new line, but instead follows the text in a natural back-and-forth motion. Reading takes some 
                  getting used to, but after a while it becomes surprisingly natural.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/boustrophedon/boustrophedon.pdf
-- local file:    ./3190218494-boustrophedon.pdf

documentation:    Template (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/boustrophedon/examples/boustrophedon_template.pdf
-- local file:    ./5875229871-boustrophedon_template.pdf

boxhandler -- Flexible Captioning and Deferred Box/List Printing
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/boxhandler
name:             boxhandler
caption:          Flexible Captioning and Deferred Box/List Printing
author:           Steven B. Segletes
copyright:        Steven B. Segletes (2008)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.30
description:      (no language specified) The package allows the user to optimise presentation of LaTeX tables and figures. Boxhandler will lay 
                  out table and figure captions with a variety of stylistic appearances, and will also allow figures and 
                  tables to be “wrapped” in a manner consistent with many business and government documents.

                  For a document that might appear in different venues with different formatting, boxhandler permits the 
                  creation of a LaTeX source document that can, with a single-line change in the source code, produce an 
                  output that has very different layout from the baseline configuration, not only in terms of caption style, 
                  but more importantly in terms of the locations where figures, tables and lists appear (or not) in the 
                  document.

                  Deferral routines also allow one to keep all figure and table data in a separate source file, while nonetheless 
                  producing a document with figures and tables appearing in the desired location.

breqn -- Automatic line breaking of displayed equations
-------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/breqn
name:             breqn
caption:          Automatic line breaking of displayed equations
author:           Joseph Wright
author:           Lars Madsen
author:           Michael J. Downes
author:           Morten Høgholm
author:           Will Robertson
copyright:        Ulrike Fischer (2020)
copyright:        Morten Høgholm (2007-2008)
copyright:        Michael J. Downes (1997-2003)
copyright:        Will Robertson (2007-2020)
copyright:        Lars Madsen (2007-2014)
copyright:        Joseph Wright (2010-2017)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.98l (2021-10-28)
last changes:     2021-10-28
year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) The package provides solutions to a number of common difficulties in writing displayed equations and 
                  getting high-quality output. For example, it is a well-known inconvenience that if an equation must be 
                  broken into more than one line, ‘left...right’ constructs cannot span lines. The breqn package makes 
                  them work as one would expect whether or not there is an intervening line break.

                  The single most ambitious goal of the package, however, is to support automatic linebreaking of displayed 
                  equations. Such linebreaking cannot be done without substantial changes under the hood in the way formulae 
                  are processed; the code must be watched carefully, keeping an eye on possible glitches.

                  The bundle also contains the  flexisym (https://ctan.org/pkg/flexisym) and mathstyle (https://ctan.org/pkg/mathstyle) packages, 
                  which are both designated as support for breqn.

version:          3.6 (2026-05-16)

year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The bundledoc package is a post-processor for the  snapshot (https://ctan.org/pkg/snapshot) package 
                  that bundles together all the classes, packages and files needed to build a given LaTeX document. It 
                  reads the .dep file that snapshot (https://ctan.org/pkg/snapshot) produces, finds each of 
                  the files mentioned therein, and archives them into a single .tar.gz (or .zip, or whatever) file, suitable 
                  for moving across systems, transmitting to a colleague, etc.

                  A script,  arlatex , provides an alternative “archiving” mechanism, creating a single LaTeX file 
                  that contains all of the ancillary files of a LaTeX document, together with the document itself, using 
                  the filecontents* environment.

businesscard-qrcode -- Business cards with QR-Code
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/businesscard-qrcode
name:             businesscard-qrcode
caption:          Business cards with QR-Code
author:           Marc Wäckerlin
license:          lgpl = GNU Lesser General Public License (free)
version:          1.2 (2018-08-15)
last changes:     2018-08-15
year:             2018
description:      (no language specified) What happens when you give your visiting card to someone? Either they manually type the text into their 
                  computer or mobile phone, or it will end up in a box and be forgotten. Nowadays data is required electronically, 
                  not on paper. Here is the solution: A visiting card with QR-Code that contains a full  vcard (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6350) so 
                  that it can be scanned with an app on the mobile phone and thereby automatically imported into the electronic 
                  contacts. This also works well when you are offline and bluetooth transfer fails. So here is the highly 
                  configurable business card or visiting card with full vcard as QR-Code, ready to send to online printers. 
                  You can specify the exact size of the paper and the content within the paper, including generation of 
                  crop marks.

                  The package depends on the following other LaTeX packages:  calc (https://ctan.org/pkg/calc) , crop 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/crop) , DejaVuSans (https://ctan.org/pkg/dejavu) , etoolbox (https://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox) , fontawesome 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontawesome) , fontenc (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontenc) , geometry (https://ctan.org/pkg/geometry) , kvoptions 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/kvoptions) , marvosym (https://ctan.org/pkg/marvosym) , qrcode (https://ctan.org/pkg/qrcode) , varwidth 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/varwidth) , and wrapfig (https://ctan.org/pkg/wrapfig) .

                  The package needs XeLaTeX for working properly.

license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          1.1
description:      (no language specified) This package lets users output color emojis in LaTeX documents. Compared to other packages with similar 
                  functionality, this package has the following merits:

                  + It supports all major LaTeX engines.
                  + Emojis can be entered as the characters themselves, as their Unicode code values, or as their short names.

                  + It works reasonably well in PDF strings when using hyperref.
                  + Emojis can be handled properly even in Japanese typesetting environments.
This package has been widely used among the Japanese LaTeX community, but there are already many emoji 
                  packages on CTAN and in TeX Live. To avoid uploading a large amount of emoji image data that are essentially 
                  identical, the package was revised in version 1.0 so that the image output was delegated to the twmojis 
                  package. Therefore, this package now contains no image data.

year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The  hologo (https://ctan.org/pkg/hologo) package provides many useful logos of popular (and not 
                  so popular) TeX-family software. However, its interface is a bit cumbersome because you must type \hologo{BibTeX} instead 
                  of \BibTeX .

                  This package makes it possible to import some of the logos provided by  hologo (https://ctan.org/pkg/hologo) as 
                  single commands, such as \BibTeX .

                  Additionally, the package provides logos of some TeX-family software that is popular mainly in Japan. 
                  These logos can be imported in the same way as those provided by the  \hologo command.

                  bxtexlogo depends on hologo (https://ctan.org/pkg/hologo) and cjhebrew (https://ctan.org/pkg/cjhebrew) (if \logoAleph and \logoLamed are 
                  used).

bxwareki -- Convert dates from Gregorian to Japanese calender

caption:          Convert dates from Gregorian to Japanese calender
author:           Takayuki Yato
copyright:        Takayuki YATO (aka. “ZR”) (2018-2026)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          0.8
description:      (no language specified) This LaTeX package provides commands to convert from the Gregorian calendar (e. g. 2018/8/28) to the 
                  Japanese rendering of the Japanese calendar (e. g. Heisei 30 nen 8 gatsu 28 nichi; actually with kanji 
                  characters). You can choose whether the numbers are written in Western numerals or kanji numerals.

                  Note that the package only deals with dates in the year 1873 or later, where the Japanese calendar is 
                  really a Gregorian calendar with a different notation of years.

c2latex -- Simple conversion of C programs to LaTeX
---------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/c2latex
name:             c2latex
caption:          Simple conversion of C programs to LaTeX
author:           John D Ramsdell
copyright:        John D. Ramsdell (1991)
license:          other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
version:          1.1
description:      (no language specified) c2latex provides simple support for documentation of C programming. Given a C source file in which the 
                  comments have been written in LaTeX, c2latex converts the C source file into a LaTeX source file. It 
                  can be used to produce typeset listings of C programs and/or documentation associated with the program.

                  The C source given to c2latex usually has the following form: It starts with a large comment containing 
                  LaTeX commands that start a document along with any initial text. Then there is a sequence of comment 
                  and code pairs, with the comment explaining the code to follow. The source file is ended by a comment 
                  containing LaTeX commands that finish the document. The source of c2latex is distributed in this form.

on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/c2latex
keyword:          listing (computer code listing)
year:             1991
language(s):      nls: no language specified

caption:          A humanist Sans Serif font, with LaTeX support
author:           Bob Tennent

license:          ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
version:          (2023-09-25)
last changes:     2023-09-25
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) Cabin is a humanist sans with four weights and true italics and small capitals. According to the designer, 
                  Pablo Impallari, Cabin was inspired by Edward Johnston's and Eric Gill's typefaces, with a touch of modernism. 
                  Cabin incorporates modern proportions, optical adjustments, and some elements of the geometric sans.

                  cabin.sty supports use of the font under LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX; it uses the mweights 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/mweights) , to manage the user’s view of all those font weights.

                  An  sfdefault option is provided to enable Cabin as the default text font. The fontaxes (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontaxes) package 
                  is required for use with [pdf]LaTeX.

caption:          Hyphenation patterns for the Catalan language
author:           Gonçal Badenes Guia
author:           Francina Turon
copyright:        Gonçal Badenes (1991-2003)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          1.11
description:      (no language specified) The macros used were created for  ghyph31.tex by Bernd Raichle (see the German hyphenation pattern 
                  files (https://ctan.org/pkg/dehyph) for further details); the patterns were created using standard, 
                  conservative hyphenation rules for Catalan. The results were then refined by running them through patgen , 
                  which increased the number of hits.

                  The results were checked against “Diccionari Ortogràfic i de Pronúncia, Enciclopèdia Catalana”; no incorrect 
                  results were detected, and misses amounted to less than 1%.

                  For Catalan, both  \lefthyphenmn and \righthyphenmin should be set to 2.

calcfrac -- Calculates the value of an expression containing fractions
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/calcfrac
name:             calcfrac
caption:          Calculates the value of an expression containing fractions
author:           TeXpérimental
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.2 (2023-10-28)
last changes:     2023-10-28
year:             2023
description:      (English) This package is an engine for calculating numerical expressions containing fractions. The numerical value 
                  of the expression is calculated with a non-expandable method and displayed in the form of an irreducible 
                  fraction or, where appropriate, an integer.

                  This package is intended for educational purposes. The videos showing its writing from scratch are available 
                  on youtube from episode 24:  https://youtu.be/6lF4P6B3msw . This is why it is delivered with only 
                  a minimalist documentation.

calculation -- Typesetting reasoned calculations,  also called calculational proofs
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/calculation
name:             calculation
caption:          Typesetting reasoned calculations,  also called calculational proofs
author:           Maarten Fokkinga
copyright:        Maarten Fokkinga (2014-2015)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) The  calculation environment formats reasoned calculations, also called calculational proofs.

                  The notion of reasoned calculations or calculational proofs was originally advocated by Wim Feijen and 
                  Edsger Dijkstra. The package accepts options  fleqn and leqno (with the same effect as the 
                  LaTeX options fleqn and leqno , or may inherit the options from the document class). It allows 
                  steps and expressions to be numbered (by LaTeX equation numbers, obeying the LaTeX \label command 
                  to refer to these numbers), and a step doesn't take vertical space if its hint is empty. An expression 
                  in a calculation can be given a comment; it is placed at the side opposite to the equation numbers. Calculations 
                  are allowed inside hints although numbering and commenting is then disabled.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/calculation/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/calculation/calculation.pdf
-- local file:    ./2866114314-calculation.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/calculation
on MikTeX:        calculation
on TeXLive:       calculation
keyword:          maths (support for typesetting mathematics)
keyword:          proof (typeset proofs and proof diagrams)
year:             2015
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14
