euenc -- Unicode font encoding definitions for XeTeX
----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/euenc
name:             EUenc
caption:          Unicode font encoding definitions for XeTeX
author:           Khaled Hosny
author:           Élie Roux
author:           Will Robertson
copyright:        Will Robertson (2006-2010)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.1h
description:      (no language specified) Font encoding definitions for unicode fonts loaded by LaTeX in XeTeX or LuaTeX. The package provides 
                  two encodings:

                  + EU1, designed for use with XeTeX, which the  fontspec (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec) uses for 
                    unicode fonts which require no macro-level processing for accents, and
                  + EU2, which provides the same facilities for use with LuaTeX.
Neither encoding places any restriction on the glyphs provided by a font; use of EU2 causes the package 
                  euxunicode (https://ctan.org/pkg/euxunicode) to be loaded (the package is part of this distribution).

                  The package includes font definition files for use with the Latin Modern OpenType fonts.

eulervm -- Euler virtual math fonts
-----------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/eulervm
name:             eulervm
caption:          Euler virtual math fonts
author:           Walter A. Schmidt
author:           Keiran Harcombe
license:          lppl1.1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.1 
version:          4.0
description:      (no language specified) The well-known Euler fonts are suitable for typesetting mathematics in conjunction with a variety of 
                  text fonts which do not provide mathematical character sets of their own. Euler-VM is a set of  'virtual' mathematics 
                  fonts based on Euler and CM. This approach has several advantages over immediately using the 'real' Euler 
                  fonts: Most noticeably, less TeX resources are consumed, the quality of various math symbols is improved 
                  and a usable \hslash symbol can be provided. The virtual fonts are accompanied by a LaTeX package 
                  which makes them easy to use, particularly in conjunction with Type1 PostScript text fonts. They are 
                  compatible with amsmath (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath) . A package option allows the fonts to be 
                  loaded at 95% of their nominal size, thus blending better with certain text fonts, e.g., Minion.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/eulervm/doc/latex/eulervm/eulervm.pdf

eurion -- EURion constellation overlay for LaTeX documents

author:           originalsouth
license:          other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
version:          0.1.0
description:      (no language specified) This package overlays the five-circle EURion anti-photocopy constellation on document pages. It provides 
                  three modes: scatter, for banknote-style tiling across every page; corner, for a single discreet mark 
                  in a selected corner; and manual, for user placement with the  \eurion command.

                  The color, size, density, rotation, and random seed are configurable. The package provides a visual reproduction

                  in almost any desired way. Write, e.g.,  \ATS{17.6} to get something like ‘17,60 öS (1,28 Euro)’

eurofont -- Provides a command that prints a euro symbol
--------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/eurofont
name:             eurofont
caption:          Provides a command that prints a euro symbol
author:           Rowland McDonnell
copyright:        Rowland McDonnell (1998)
license:          other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
version:          1.1.3
description:      (no language specified) The particular symbol printed by  \euro will in general change depending on the font family, weight, 
                  and shape in use at the time. This symbol can come from any source, and the package user has complete 
                  control over which euro symbol is used in any given situation. The package is pre-configured to behave 
                  sensibly with many common text fonts and available euro symbols. The \euro command can print ‘faked’ 
                  euro symbols from a C with two lines across it when no suitable real euro symbol is available; the package 
                  also includes code for printing fake bold euro symbols for use when no real bold symbol exists, as well 
                  as pre-configured support for a faked italic version of the marvosym (https://ctan.org/pkg/marvosym) font. 
                  Eurofont comes set up to use euro symbols from Adobe’s Eurofonts, the marvosym (https://ctan.org/pkg/marvosym) font, 
                  the Eurosym (https://ctan.org/pkg/eurosym) font, and any available Text Companion fonts. The selection 
                  between these can be done using options passed to the package. The eurofont package also ‘knows’ about 
                  the China2e (https://ctan.org/pkg/china2e) font’s euro symbol, and can be configured to use it.

documentation:    Package Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/eurofont/readme.txt

description:      (no language specified) Provides access to Adobe’s Euro currency symbol fonts from LaTeX. The fonts are named using Karl Berry’s 
                  naming scheme, providing fd files and a style file to use the fonts directly, and providing four macros: 
                  \EURtm, \EURhv, \EURcr and \EUR (from  marvosym (https://ctan.org/pkg/marvosym) ). The actual symbol

                  the fonts are free of charge, the licence conditions prevent CTAN from distributing them). Metrics and 
                  maps for using the fonts (at all) are available via the adobe-euro (https://ctan.org/pkg/adobe-euro) package.

exam -- Package for typesetting exam scripts
--------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/exam
name:             exam
caption:          Package for typesetting exam scripts
author:           Philip S. Hirschhorn
copyright:        Philip S. Hirschhorn (1994,1997,2000,2004,2008,2011,2015,2017,2021,2023)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.704
description:      (no language specified) Provides a class  exam.cls , which eases production of exams, even by a LaTeX novice. Simple commands 
                  are provided to:

                  + create questions, parts of questions, subparts of parts, and subsubparts of subparts, all with optional 
                    point values;
                  + create a grading table, indexed either by question number (listing each question and the total possible 
                    points for that question) or by page number (listing each page with points and the total possible points 
                    for that page);
                  + create headers and footers that are each specified in three parts: one part to be left justified, one 
                    part to be centered, and one part to be right justified, in the manner of  fancyhdr (https://ctan.org/pkg/fancyhdr) .

Headers and/or footers can be different on the first page of the exam, can be different on the last page 
                  of the exam, and can vary depending on whether the page number is odd or even, or on whether the current 
                  page continues a question from a previous page, or on whether the last question on the current page continues 
                  onto the following page.

                  Multiple line headers and/or footers are allowed, and it's easy to increase the part of the page devoted 
                  to headers and/or footers to allow for this.

                  Note that the bundle  exams (https://ctan.org/pkg/exams) also provides a file exam.cls ; 
                  the two bundles therefore clash, and should not be installed on the same system.

documentation:    Package Readme (no language specified): pkg:/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): pkg:/examdoc.pdf
home page:        http://www-math.mit.edu/~psh/
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/exam

on TeXLive:       exam

author:           Jason Alexander

description:      (no language specified) This bundle provides a class examdesign. The class provides several features useful for designing tests 
                  or question sets:

                  + it allows for explicit markup of questions and answers;
                  + the class will, at the user’s request, automatically generate answer keys;
                  + multiple versions of the same test can be generated automatically, with the ordering of questions within 
                    each section randomly permuted so as to minimize cheating;

                  + environments are provided to assist in constructing the most common types of test question: matching, 
                    true/false, multiple-choice, fill-in-the-blank, and short answer/essay questions.

examplep -- Verbatim phrases and listings in LaTeX
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/examplep
name:             examplep
caption:          Verbatim phrases and listings in LaTeX
author:           Péter Szabó
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          0.04
description:      (no language specified) Examplep provides sophisticated features for typesetting verbatim source code listings, including the 
                  display of the source code and its compiled LaTeX or MetaPost output side-by-side, with automatic width 
                  detection and enabled page breaks (in the source), without the need for specifying the source twice. 
                  Special care is taken that section, page and footnote numbers do not interfere with the main document. 
                  For typesetting short verbatim phrases, a replacement for the  \verb command is also provided in 
                  the package, which can be used inside tables and moving arguments such as footnotes and section titles. 
                  The listings (https://ctan.org/pkg/listings) package is used for syntax highlighting.

                  The accompanying codep package and the wrfiles.pl Perl script provide a convenient interface to the examplep 
                  package for authors of manuals. With codep it is possible to generate the source code, the LaTeX or MetaPost 
                  output and the compilable example file from a single source embedded into the appropriate place of the 
                  .tex document file.

documentation:    Article from EuroTeX 2005 talk (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/examplep/eurotex_2005_examplep.pdf

caption:          Get data from Excel files into LaTeX
author:           Hans-Peter Doerr
copyright:        Hans-Peter Doerr (2004-2006)
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          0.5.1
description:      (no language specified) Exceltex is a LaTeX package combined with a helper program written in Perl. It provides an easy to use 
                  yet powerful and flexible way to get data from Spreadsheets into LaTeX.

                  In contrast to other solutions, exceltex does not seek to make the creation of tables in LaTeX easier, 
                  but to get data from Spreadsheets into LaTeX as easily as possible.

                  The Excel (TM) file format only acts as an interface between the spreadsheet application and exceltex 
                  because it is easily accessible (via the  Spreadsheet::ParseExcel Perl module) and because most 
                  spreadsheet applications are able to read and write Excel files.

excludeonly -- Prevent files being \include-ed
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/excludeonly
name:             excludeonly
caption:          Prevent files being \include-ed
author:           Donald Arseneau
author:           Daniel H. Luecking
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) The package defines an  \excludeonly command, which is (in effect) the opposite of \includeonly . 
                  If both \includeonly and \excludeonly exist in a document, only files “allowed” by both will 
                  be included.

                  The package redefines the internal  \@include command, so it conflicts with packages that do the 
                  same. Examples are the classes paper.cls (https://ctan.org/pkg/paper) and thesis.cls (https://ctan.org/pkg/thesis) .

description:      (no language specified) The exesheet package is designed for typesetting exercise or exam sheets. The primary advantage of exesheet 
                  is its ability to display a detailed scoring guide and correction instructions as needed. This feature 
                  is especially beneficial for grading papers with multiple graders.

                  The exesheet package provides:

                  + macros for organizing exercises and subparts,
                  + specific settings for enumeration lists,
                  + environments for questions and answers, which can be displayed or hidden,
                  + macros for detailed comments and grading instructions in the margins which can be displayed or hidden.

Additionally, the  exesheet class loads the schooldocs (https://ctan.org/pkg/schooldocs) package 
                  which manages the page layout, the main title, headers and footers.

expex-glossonly -- Help gb4e, linguex, and covington users use the ExPex glossing macros
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/expex-glossonly
name:             expex-glossonly
caption:          Help gb4e, linguex, and covington users use the ExPex glossing macros
author:           Alan Munn
copyright:        Alan Munn (2016-2024)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.9b (2024-02-14)
last changes:     2024-02-14
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) The  ExPex (https://ctan.org/pkg/expex) package by John Frampton provides very fine-grained control 
                  over glossing and example formatting, including unlimited gloss lines and various ways of formatting 
                  multiline glosses. By contrast the cgloss4e glossing macros provided with gb4e (https://ctan.org/pkg/gb4e) , linguex 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/linguex) , and covington (https://ctan.org/pkg/covington) , although very 
                  capable at basic glossing, lack the degree of customization that is sometimes needed for more complex 
                  glossing.

                  On the other hand, for those users who have heavily invested in using either  gb4e (https://ctan.org/pkg/gb4e) or linguex 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/linguex) , or covington (https://ctan.org/pkg/covington) , shifting to ExPex 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/expex) can be quite daunting and burdensome, especially since the basic syntax 
                  of the examples is quite different.

                  This package is an attempt to have the best of both worlds: it allows  gb4e (https://ctan.org/pkg/gb4e) , linguex 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/linguex) and covington (https://ctan.org/pkg/covington) users to keep 
                  using those packages for basic example numbering and formatting, but also allows them to use the glossing 
                  macros that ExPex (https://ctan.org/pkg/expex) provides.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/expex-glossonly/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/expex-glossonly/expex-glossonly.pdf
-- local file:    ./4969317165-expex-glossonly.pdf

contact:          repository: https://github.com/amunn/expex-glossonly

expkv-bundle -- An expandable key=val implementation and friends
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/expkv-bundle
name:             expkv-bundle
caption:          An expandable key=val implementation and friends
author:           Jonathan P. Spratte
copyright:        Jonathan P. Spratte (2020-2024)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          (2024-12-26)
last changes:     2024-12-26
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) This is a collection of different packages that provide  key=value functionality in plainTeX, LaTeX, 
                  and ConTeXt.

                  At the core, the  expkv package implements two expandable key=value parsers that are somewhat 
                  fast and robust against common bugs in many key=value implementations (no accidental brace stripping, 
                  no fragility for active commas or equals signs).

                  expkv-cs enables users to define expandable key=value macros in a comfortable and straightforward 
                  way.

                  expkv-def provides an interface to define common key types for expkv similar to the key 
                  defining interfaces of widespread key=value implementations.

                  expkv-opt allows to parse package or class options in LaTeX via expkv .

                  expkv-pop is a utility package to define prefix oriented parsers that allow a somewhat natural 
                  formulation (it provides the core functionality for the key-defining front ends of both expkv-cs and expkv-def ).

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/expkv-bundle/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/expkv-bundle/expkv-bundle.pdf
-- local file:    ./3333436258-expkv-bundle.pdf
contact:          repository: https://gitlab.com/islandoftex/texmf/expkv-bundle
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/expkv-bundle
installation:     https://ctan.org/tex-archive/install/macros/generic/expkv-bundle.tds.zip

description:      (no language specified) This package provides macros to allow for embedding exercises and solutions in the LaTeX source of an 
                  instructional text (e.g., a book or a course text) while generating the following separate documents:

                  
                  + your original text that only contains the exercises, and
                  + a solution book that contains only the solutions to the exercises (optionally, the exercises themselves 
                    can also be copied to the solution book).
The exercise data are generated when running LaTeX on your document; the first run also writes the solutions 
                  to a secondary file that may be included in a simple document harness, may be processed by LaTeX, to 
                  generate a nice solution book.

                  The code of the package was derived (in large part) from  fancyvrb (https://ctan.org/pkg/fancyvrb) .

extract -- Extract parts of a document and write to another document
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/extract
name:             extract
caption:          Extract parts of a document and write to another document
author:           Hendri Adriaens
copyright:        Hendri Adriaens (2004-2019)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.9a
description:      (no language specified) The package provides the means to extract specific content from a source document and write that to a 
                  target document. One could, for instance, use this to extract all exercises from lecture notes and generate 
                  an exercises book on the fly.

                  The package also provides an environment which writes its body entirely to the target file. Another environment 
                  will write to the target file, but will also execute the body. This allows to share code (for instance, 
                  a preamble) between the source document and the target file.

                  Finally, the package provides an interface to conditionally extract content. With a single package option, 
                  one can specify exactly which commands (counted from the start of the document) should be extracted and 
                  which not. This might be useful for extracting specific slides from a presentation and use them in a 
                  new file.

extractpdfmark -- Extract page mode and named destinations as PDFmark from PDF
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/extractpdfmark
name:             extractpdfmark
caption:          Extract page mode and named destinations as PDFmark from PDF
author:           Masamichi Hosoda
copyright:        Masamichi Hosoda (2016-2022)
license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
version:          1.1.1 (2022-09-30)
last changes:     2022-09-30
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) PDFmarks is a technique that accompanies PDF and that is used to store metadata such as author or title, 
                  but also structural information such as bookmarks or hyperlinks.

                  When Ghostscript reads the main PDF generated by the TeX system with embedded PDF files and outputs the 
                  final PDF, the PDF page mode and name targets etc. are not preserved. Therefore, when you open the final 
                  PDF, it is not displayed correctly. Also, remote PDF links do not work correctly.

                  This program is able to extract the page mode and named targets as PDFmark from PDF. In this way, you 
                  can obtain embedded PDF files that have kept this information.

                  Usage:

                  |
$ extractpdfmark TeX-System-Outputted.pdf &gt; Extracted-PDFmark.ps
| 

                  |
$ gs -q -dBATCH -dNOPAUSE -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -dPDFDontUseFontObjectNum 
-sOutputFile=Final.pdf TeX-System-Outputted.pdf Extracted-PDFmark.ps
|

documentation:    Readme (Japanese): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/extractpdfmark/README.ja.md
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/extractpdfmark/README.md
contact:          repository: https://github.com/trueroad/extractpdfmark
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/extractpdfmark
keyword:          pdf-feat (access PDF features)
language(s):      ja: Japanese
last access:      2026-07-14

version:          2.1 (2018-10-27)
last changes:     2018-10-27

description:      (no language specified) This package can be used to generate invoices for Belgian individuals who do not have a VAT number and 
                  who wish to do occasional work, or to carry out paid additional activities during their free time up 
                  to 6,000 euros per calendar year (amount indexed annually) without having to pay tax or social security 
                  contributions (see the website  Activités complémentaires (https://finances.belgium.be/fr/particuliers/avantages-fiscaux/activites-complementaires) ).

                  The package can also generate expense reports.

                  All totals are calculated automatically, in the invoice and in the expense report.

                  The package depends on  calctab (https://ctan.org/pkg/calctab) , ifthen (https://ctan.org/pkg/ifthen) , hyperref 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref) , fancyhdr (https://ctan.org/pkg/fancyhdr) , multirow (https://ctan.org/pkg/multirow) , eurosym 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/eurosym) , color (https://ctan.org/pkg/color) , and colortbl (https://ctan.org/pkg/colortbl) .

name:             fancyhandout
caption:          A LaTeX class for producing nice-looking handouts
author:           Sebastian Friedl
copyright:        Sebastian Friedl (2017-2018)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          (2018-01-22)
last changes:     2018-01-22
year:             2018
description:      (no language specified) This package breaks with some of LaTeX’s principles and redefines basic LaTeX commands with the aim of 
                  producing well-designed and clearly structured handouts: A sans-serif font is used by default; sections 
                  are not numbered, but highlighted by underlining; head- and footline display document information; and 
                  in order to avoid too much whitespace around the text the margin sizes are adjusted to smaller values.

                  All in all,  fancyhandout provides a means of typesetting documents not exclusively consisting 
                  of running text in a beautiful way.

                  fancyhandout depends on the following other LaTeX packages: csquotes (https://ctan.org/pkg/csquotes) , enumitem 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/enumitem) , etoolbox (https://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox) , fancyhdr (https://ctan.org/pkg/fancyhdr) , geometry 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/geometry) , and xcolor (https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor) .

                  and ABNT NBR 6023:2002 (Bibliographic References).

description:      (no language specified) The bundle provides two packages, fenxitok and fenixpar.

                  The fenixtok package provides user macros to add material to a token register; the material will be (automatically) 
                  removed from the token register when the register is executed. Material may be added either to the left 
                  or to the right, and care is taken not to override any redefinition that may be included in the token 
                  register itself.

                  The fenixpar package uses the macros of fenixtok to provide a user interface to manipulation of the  \everypar token 
                  register.

                  The packages require the  e-TeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/etex) extensions; with them, they work either 
                  with Plain TeX or with LaTeX.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/fenixpar/README

keyword:          macro-supp (support for development of (La)TeX macros)

fetchcls -- Fetch the current class name
----------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fetchcls
name:             fetchcls
caption:          Fetch the current class name
author:           Ruben Giannotti
copyright:        Ruben Giannotti (2015)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0 (2015-08-11)
last changes:     2015-08-11
year:             2015
description:      (no language specified) With standard LaTeX you are able to check for the class in use invoking the kernel command  \@ifclassloaded . 
                  However, doing so you cannot get the explicit class name, unless you want to loop over every possible 
                  class name until \@ifclassloaded returns true — don't do that!

                  With the help of the present package you can obtain the name of the current class with significantly 
                  less effort. Just load the package as usual:  \usepackage{fetchcls} ; then, the control sequence \classname will 
                  hold the name you were looking for.

figsize -- Auto-size graphics
-----------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/figsize
name:             FigSize
caption:          Auto-size graphics
author:           Anthony A. Tanbakuchi
license:          lppl1.1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.1 
version:          0.1
description:      (no language specified) The FigSize package enables automatic sizing of graphics, especially when including graphics with the 
                  graphicx (https://ctan.org/pkg/graphicx) package. The user only has to specify the number of graphics 
                  that should fit to a page or fraction there of and the package will dynamically calculate the correct 
                  graphics sizes relative to the page size. Thus, graphics can be auto-sized to fill a whole page or fraction 
                  and manual changes of graphic sizes are never needed when changing document layouts. Finally, the package's 
                  dynamic lengths can be used to allow other document element sizes to be dynamic.

filecontents -- Create an external file from within a LaTeX document
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/filecontents
name:             filecontents
caption:          Create an external file from within a LaTeX document
author:           Scott Pakin
copyright:        Scott Pakin (2011-2023)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.5a (2023-04-02)
last changes:     2023-04-02
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) LaTeX2e’s  filecontents and filecontents* environments enable a LaTeX source file to generate 
                  external files as it runs through LaTeX. However, there are two limitations of these environments: they 
                  refuse to overwrite existing files, and they can only be used in the preamble of a document. The filecontents 
                  package removes these limitations, letting you overwrite existing files and letting you use filecontents / filecontents* anywhere.

                  As of September 2019 the author tells us: “This package is no longer necessary due to its functionality 
                  having moved into recent LaTeX kernels. It’s probably better not to move the package to obsolete because 
                  users may need it to rebuild old documents. Version 1.5 provides full functionality when run with an 
                  older kernel but issues a warning message and disables itself when run with a newer kernel.”

                  Supply the  overwrite option to LaTeX’s built-in filecontents environment to mimic this package’s 
                  behavior:

                  |\begin{filecontents}[overwrite]{my-file}...\end{filecontents}|

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/filecontents/filecontents.pdf
-- local file:    ./2570949192-filecontents.pdf
documentation:    Package Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/filecontents/README
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/filecontents
on MikTeX:        filecontents
on TeXLive:       filecontents
keyword:          file-mgmt (TeX-related-file management)
keyword:          tagged-pdf (tagged PDF compatible)

filecontentsdef -- filecontents + macro + verbatim
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/filecontentsdef
name:             filecontentsdef
caption:          filecontents + macro + verbatim
author:           Jean-François Burnol
copyright:        Jean-François Burnol (2016-2019)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.5 (2019-09-29)
last changes:     2019-09-29
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) The package provides two environments called  filecontentsdef and filecontentshere . They 
                  are derived from the LaTeX filecontents environment as provided by Scott Pakin's filecontents 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/filecontents) package. In addition to the file creation they either store the 
                  (verbatim) contents in a macro ( filecontentsdef ) or typeset them (verbatim) on the spot ( filecontentshere ).

                  The author developed the package to display TeX code verbatim in documentation and the same time produce 
                  the corresponding files during the LaTeX run in order to embed them in the PDF as file attachment annotations 
                  (by using Scott Pakin's package  attachfile (https://ctan.org/pkg/attachfile) ).

filemod -- Provide file modification times, and compare them
------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/filemod
name:             filemod
caption:          Provide file modification times, and compare them
author:           Martin Scharrer
copyright:        Martin Scharrer (2011)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.2
description:      (no language specified) The package provides macros to read and compare the modification dates of files. The files may be  .tex files, 
                  images or other files (as long as they can be found by LaTeX). It uses the \pdffilemoddate primitive 
                  of pdfLaTeX to find the file modification date as PDF date string, parses the string and returns the 
                  value to the user. The package will also work for DVI output with recent versions of the LaTeX 
                  compiler which uses pdfLaTeX in DVI mode. The functionality is provided by purely expandable macros 
                  or by faster but non-expandable ones.

firstindexletter -- Enlarged initials for the first entries of index letter groups
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/firstindexletter
name:             firstindexletter
caption:          Enlarged initials for the first entries of index letter groups
author:           Zsolt Bihari
copyright:        Zsolt Bihari (2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) This LaTeX package helps to visually emphasize the first item of each index letter group by enlarging 
                  its initial letter.

                  The package is intended primarily for indexes generated with  xindy (https://ctan.org/pkg/xindy) /texindy. 
                  It works at LaTeX macro level: instead of modifying the generated .ind file, it hooks into the 
                  index environment and formats the first entry of each effective letter group.

                  The package provides configurable initial size, font family and color, and includes simple optical kerning 
                  adjustments for selected initial-letter pairs. It also supports Hungarian multi-character initials such 
                  as Cs, Gy, Ly, Ny, Sz, Ty and Zs, with configurable handling of Dz and Dzs.

                  The distribution includes the package file, documentation, examples, and a Hungarian manual.

fitr -- Set a rectangular destination and jump to it
----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fitr
name:             FitR
caption:          Set a rectangular destination and jump to it
author:           Donald P. Story
copyright:        D. P. Story (2012-2020)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          1.3.2 (2020-07-09)
last changes:     2020-07-09
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) The package is an implementation of the FitR view-type destination as described in the PDF Reference; 
                  it defines one new command  \jdRect . The command (optionally) sets a jump to and/or sets a destination 
                  of a FitR (Rectangle). (Can you see where \jdRect comes from?).

                  The package requires  eforms (https://ctan.org/pkg/eforms) (part of the AeB) and collectbox 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/collectbox) (by Martin Scharrer). Drivers supported are dvips and dvipsone (using 
                  Adobe Distiller as the PDF creator); pdfTeX (including LuaTeX); and dvipdfm, dvipdfmx, and XeTeX.

                  The package was developed in response to a user of the AeB Bundle who was interested in developing documents 
                  for students with low vision; the idea is to magnify regions of the document so the student can read 
                  more comfortably. Optional special effects are included (JavaScript functions) to help focus one the 
                  rectangle as it is magnified, and as the previous view is restored.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fitr/README.md

fixmath -- Make maths comply with ISO 31-0:1992 to ISO 31-13:1992
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fixmath
name:             fixmath
caption:          Make maths comply with ISO 31-0:1992 to ISO 31-13:1992
author:           Walter A. Schmidt
author:           Keiran Harcombe
copyright:        Walter Schmidt (2000-2003)
copyright:        Keiran Harcombe (2022)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.9.1 (2022-10-06)
last changes:     2022-10-06
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) LaTeX’s default style of typesetting mathematics does not comply with the International Standards ISO 
                  31-0:1992 to ISO 31-13:1992 which require that uppercase Greek letters always be typeset upright, as 
                  opposed to italic (even though they usually represent variables) and allow for typesetting of variables 
                  in a boldface italic style (even though the required fonts are available). This package ensures that 
                  uppercase Greek be typeset in italic style, that upright  $\Delta$ and $\Omega$ symbols are 
                  available through the commands \upDelta and \upOmega ; and provides a new math alphabet \mathbold for 
                  boldface italic letters, including Greek.

                  This package used to be part of the  was (https://ctan.org/pkg/was) bundle, but has now become 
                  a package in its own right.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fixmath/fixmath.pdf
-- local file:    ./4369525533-fixmath.pdf
documentation:    Bundle readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fixmath/README
contact:          repository: https://gitlab.com/kjhtex/fixmath
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fixmath
on MikTeX:        was
on TeXLive:       fixmath
keyword:          tagged-pdf (tagged PDF compatible)
keyword:          maths (support for typesetting mathematics)

fixme -- Collaborative annotation tool for LaTeX
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fixme
name:             FiXme
caption:          Collaborative annotation tool for LaTeX
author:           Didier Verna
copyright:        Didier Verna (1998-2002, 2004-2007, 2009, 2013, 2017-2019)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          4.5 (2019-01-03)
last changes:     2019-01-03
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) FiXme is a collaborative annotation tool for LaTeX documents. Annotating a document here refers to inserting 
                  meta-notes, that is, notes that do not belong to the document itself, but rather to its development or 
                  reviewing process. Such notes may involve things of different importance levels, ranging from simple 
                  “fix the spelling” flags to critical “this paragraph is a lie” mentions. Annotations like this should 
                  be visible during the development or reviewing phase, but should normally disappear in the final version 
                  of the document.

                  FiXme is designed to ease and automate the process of managing collaborative annotations, by offering 
                  a set of predefined note levels and layouts, the possibility to register multiple authors, to reference 
                  annotations by listing and indexing etc. FiXme is extensible, giving you the possibility to create new 
                  layouts or even complete “themes“, and also comes with support for AUCTeX.

on MikTeX:        fixme
on TeXLive:       fixme
keyword:          editorial (editor’s marks, highlights, etc.)
keyword:          tagged-pdf (tagged PDF compatible)
keyword:          notes (general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes))

fixtounicode -- Utility functions for setting tounicode mappings for 7/8 bit fonts
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fixtounicode
name:             fixtounicode
caption:          Utility functions for setting tounicode mappings for 7/8 bit fonts
author:           Clea F. Rees
copyright:        Clea F. Rees (2025-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.1.1
description:      (no language specified) This package provides utility functions in  expl3 (https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3) and LaTeX2e syntax 
                  for setting tounicode mappings for 7/8 bit fonts. The package provides a unified interface which enables 
                  mappings for both pdfTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/pdftex) and LuaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/luatex) .

                  The aim is to make it easier to make legacy (text) symbol packages, which often use arbitary glyph names 
                  and encodings, accessible for the two engines currently capable of producing accessible PDFs.

                  The package provides a limited workaround for LuaTeX 1.22 and earlier, which make the provision of such 
                  mappings more challenging.

                  Full support requires pdfTeX or LuaTeX 1.24 or later.

flashcards -- A class for typesetting flashcards
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/flashcards
name:             flashcards
caption:          A class for typesetting flashcards
author:           Matthew Vernon
author:           Alexander M. Budge
copyright:        Alexander M. Budge (2000)
copyright:        Matthew Vernon (2022)
license:          gpl2+ = GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer (free)
version:          1.0.2
description:      (no language specified) The FlashCards class provides for the typesetting of flash cards. By flash card, we mean a two sided

fldigigal -- Create a Flash slide show of digital photos
--------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fldigigal
name:             fldigigal
caption:          Create a Flash slide show of digital photos
author:           Donald P. Story
copyright:        D. P. Story (2010-2020)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          0.6 (2020-08-08)
last changes:     2020-08-08
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) The package uses the  rmannot (https://ctan.org/pkg/rmannot) package (thus requiring an Adobe Distiller 
                  workflow) to create what the author calls “an AcroTeX Flash Digital Gallery”; that is, a Flash slide 
                  show that displays a series of digital images (PNG, JPG or GIF formats). The document author describes 
                  the digital images (path and caption) from the LaTeX source; on compilation, fldigigal writes an XML 
                  file, which Distiller embeds in the PDF. The digital images may be embedded in the PDF, or be accessed 
                  remotely (reducing filesize). Three layouts are offered: vertical thumbnails, horizontal thumbnails, 
                  or no thumbnails.

                  This package has become obsolete after December 2020. Since December 2020, Adobe no longer supports Flash 
                  player (SWF, FLV). This package uses a custom SWF file ( fdg_ht1.swf , eg); as a result this package 
                  will no longer function in Adobe Acrobat Reader DC. The package will continue to produce PDFs as designed, 
                  but only if built using Acrobat XI (or a version Acrobat prior to 2021) and viewed in Adobe Acrobat Reader 
                  XI (or a version of Reader prior 2021).

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): pkg:/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): pkg:/doc/fdg_man.pdf

flowframtk -- Vector graphics application with support for flowfram.sty
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/flowframtk
alias:            jpgfdraw
name:             FlowframTk
caption:          Vector graphics application with support for flowfram.sty
author:           Nicola Talbot
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          0.8.4
description:      (no language specified) FlowframTk is a graphics application written in Java designed for use with  flowfram (https://ctan.org/pkg/flowfram) and pgf 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) , but can also be used to create standalone image files.

                  You can use FlowframTk to:

                  + Construct frames for use with the  flowfram (https://ctan.org/pkg/flowfram) package.
                  + Construct shapes using lines, moves and cubic Bezier segments.
                  + Edit shapes by changing the defining control points.
                  + Add symmetry to shapes.
                  + Convert shapes into patterns (rotational, scaled, spiral).
                  + Incorporate text and bitmap images (for annotation and background effects).
                  + Display text along a shape.
                  + Extract the parameters for TeX’s  \parshape command and for \shapepar (defined in the shapepar 
                    (https://ctan.org/pkg/shapepar) package).
Pictures can be saved in FlowframTk’s native binary format (JDR) or native ascii format (AJR) or can 
                  be exported as:

                  + a  pgfpicture environment for use in LaTeX documents with the pgf (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) package;

                  + a LaTeX class or package that loads the  flowfram (https://ctan.org/pkg/flowfram) package;
                  + a PostScript file;
                  + a PDF file;
                  + a PNG image file; or
                  + an SVG image file.
Alternative text can be specified to use when exporting to a LaTeX file (e.g. if the text contains symbols 
                  or if it should be set in maths mode).

                  Mappings can be used to specify what LaTeX font declarations should be used when exporting to a LaTeX 
                  file.

                  To install, download and run the installer application  flowframtk-  'version'  -installer.jar (where 'version' is 
                  the version number).

                  This application replaces the now obsolete JpgfDraw.

fntproof -- A programmable font test pattern generator
------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fntproof
name:             fntproof
caption:          A programmable font test pattern generator
author:           Daniel H. Luecking
copyright:        Daniel H. Luecking (2010)
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
version:          (2010-11-30)
last changes:     2010-11-30
year:             2010
description:      (no language specified) The package implements all the font testing commands of Knuth’s  testfont.tex (https://ctan.org/pkg/testfont) , 
                  but arranges that information necessary for each command is supplied as arguments to that command, rather 
                  than prompted for. This makes it possible to type all the tests in one command line, and easy to input

fnumprint -- Print a number in ‘appropriate’ format
---------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fnumprint
name:             fnumprint
caption:          Print a number in ‘appropriate’ format
author:           Robin Schneider
copyright:        Robin Schneider (2012)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.1a
description:      (no language specified) The package defines two macros which decide to typeset a number either as an Arabic number or as a word 
                  (or words) for the number. If the number is between zero and twelve (including zero and twelve) then 
                  words will be used; if the number is outside that range, it will be typeset using the package  numprint 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/numprint) 

                  Words for English representation of numbers are generated within the package, while those for German 
                  are generated using the package  zahl2string (https://ctan.org/pkg/zahl2string) .

foliono -- Use folio numbers to replace page numbers

name:             foliono
caption:          Use folio numbers to replace page numbers
author:           Tommi Syrjänen

version:          1.000 (2021-03-25)
last changes:     2021-03-25
year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) This package adds functionality to create several styles of folio numbers. Folio numbering preceded the 
                  modern page numbering convention and was in common use until the 18th century. In folio numbering the 
                  numbers are placed only on odd (right-side) pages and the numbers typically comprise of two parts: quire 
                  and folio numbers.

                  The intended use for this package is to help creating old-style books.

name:             font-change-xetex
caption:          Macros to change text and mathematics fonts in plain XeTeX
author:           Amit Raj Dhawan
license:          other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
version:          2016.1
description:      (no language specified) This package consists of macros that can be used to typeset “plain” XeTeX documents using any OpenType 
                  or TrueType font installed on the computer system.

                  The macros allow the user to change the text mode fonts and some math mode fonts. For any declared font 
                  family, various font style, weight, and size variants like bold, italics, small caps, etc., are available 
                  through standard and custom TeX control statements. Using the optional argument of the macros, the available 
                  XeTeX font features and OpenType tags can be accessed.

                  Other features of the package include activating and deactivating hanging punctuation, and support for 
                  special Unicode characters.

description:      (no language specified) The package adds several new font axes on top of LaTeX’s New Font Selection Scheme. In particular, it 
                  splits the shape axis into a primary and a secondary shape axis, and it adds three new axes to deal with

fontch -- Changing fonts, sizes and encodings in Plain TeX
----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fontch
name:             fontch
caption:          Changing fonts, sizes and encodings in Plain TeX
author:           Rodrigo Medina
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.2
description:      (no language specified) The fontch macros allow the user to change font size and family anywhere in a plain TeX document. Sizes 
                  of 8, 10, 12, 14, 20 and 24 points are available. A sans serif family ( \sf ) is defined in addition 
                  to the families already defined in plain TeX. Optional support for Latin Modern T1 and TS1 fonts is given. 
                  There are macros for non-latin1 letters and for most TS1 symbols. Math mode always uses CM fonts.

                  A command for producing doubled-spaced documents is also provided.

                  The present version of the package is designed to deal with the latest release of the  Latin Modern 
                  fonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/lm) version 1.106. Unfortunately, it can no longer support earlier versions 
                  of the fonts, so an obsolete version of the package (https://ctan.org/pkg/old-fontch) is retained 
                  for users who don't yet have access to the latest version of the fonts.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/plain/contrib/fontch/fontch.pdf

fontinst -- Help with installing fonts for TeX and LaTeX
--------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fontinst
name:             fontinst
caption:          Help with installing fonts for TeX and LaTeX
author:           Sebastian Rahtz
author:           Ulrik Vieth
author:           Lars Hellström
author:           Alan Jeffrey
copyright:        The fontinst maintenance team (1998-2001)
license:          lppl1.1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.1 
version:          1.933
description:      (no language specified) TeX macros for converting Adobe Font Metric files to TeX metric and virtual font format. Fontinst helps 
                  mainly with the number crunching and shovelling parts of font installation. This means in practice that 
                  it creates a number of files which give the TeX metrics (and related information) for a font family that 
                  (La)TeX needs to do any typesetting in these fonts. Fontinst furthermore makes it easy to create fonts 
                  containing glyphs from more than one base font, taking advantage of (e.g.) “expert” font sets.

                  Fontinst cannot examine files to see if they contain any useful information, nor automatically search 
                  for files or work with binary file formats; those tasks must normally be done manually or with the help 
                  of some other tool, such as the pltotf and vptovf programs.

documentation:    Package introduction (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/utilities/fontinst/doc/manual/intro98.pdf

caption:          Tools to simplify using fonts (especially TT/OTF ones)

license:          gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
version:          (2026-07-06)
last changes:     2026-07-06
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package provides tools to simplify using OpenType fonts with LaTeX.

                  By far the most important program in this bundle is autoinst:

                  +  autoinst – a wrapper script around Eddie Kohler’s LCDF TypeTools. Autoinst aims to automate the 
                    installation of OpenType fonts in LaTeX by calling the LCDF TypeTools (with the correct options) for 
                    all fonts you wish to install, and generating the necessary .fd and .sty files.
In addition, this bundle contains a few other, less important utilities:

                  +  afm2afm – re-encode .afm files,
                  +  ot2kpx – extract kerning pairs from OpenType fonts,
                  +  splitttc – split an OpenType Collection file ( ttc or otc ) into individual fonts.

                  by some tools). Primarily designed for fontinst (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontinst) , but can be adapted 
                  for use with other programmes. Default configuration is intended to be cross-platform and require only 
                  tools included in TeX Live, but the documentation includes a simple adaption for integration with FontForge 
                  and GNU make.

footbib -- Bibliographic references as footnotes
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/footbib
name:             footbib
caption:          Bibliographic references as footnotes
author:           Eric Domenjoud
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          2.0.7
description:      (no language specified) The package makes bibliographic references appear as footnotes. It defines a command  \footcite which 
                  is similar to the LaTeX \cite command but the references cited in this way appear at the bottom 
                  of the pages. This ‘foot bibliography’ does not conflict with the standard one and both may exist simultaneously 
                  in a document. The command \cite may still be used to produce the standard bibliography.

                  The foot bibliography uses its own style and bibliographic database which may be specified independently 
                  of the standard one. Any standard bibliography style may be used.

footmisc -- A range of footnote options
---------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/footmisc
name:             footmisc
caption:          A range of footnote options
author:           Robin Fairbairns
author:           Frank Mittelbach
copyright:        Frank Mittelbach (2018-2025)
copyright:        Robin Fairbairns (1995-2011)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          7.0b (2025-05-09)
last changes:     2025-05-09
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) A collection of ways to change the typesetting of footnotes. The package provides means of changing the 
                  layout of the footnotes themselves (including setting them in ‘paragraphs’ — the  para option), 
                  a way to number footnotes per page (the perpage option), to make footnotes disappear in a ‘moving’ 
                  argument ( stable option) and to deal with multiple references to footnotes from the same place 
                  ( multiple option). The package also has a range of techniques for labelling footnotes with symbols 
                  rather than numbers.

                  Some of the functions of the package are overlap with the functionality of other packages. The  para option 
                  is also provided by the manyfoot (https://ctan.org/pkg/manyfoot) and bigfoot (https://ctan.org/pkg/bigfoot) packages, 
                  though those are both also portmanteau packages. (Don’t be seduced by fnpara (https://ctan.org/pkg/fnpara) , 
                  whose implementation is improved by the present package.) The perpage option is also offered by footnpag 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/footnpag) and by the rather more general-purpose perpage (https://ctan.org/pkg/perpage)

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/footmisc/README.md

footnote -- Improve on LaTeX's footnote handling
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/footnote
name:             footnote
caption:          Improve on LaTeX's footnote handling
author:           Mark Wooding
copyright:        Mark Wooding (1996)
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          1.13
description:      (no language specified) The footnote package provides commands for handling footnotes rather more fluently than LaTeX manages. 
                  Several LaTeX commands and environments (for example,  \parbox , minipage and tabular ) 
                  “trap” footnotes. The footnote package provides an environment savenotes , that can be wrapped 
                  around a command or environment; at \end{savenotes} all the footnotes within will emerge. The command \makesavenoteenv will 
                  generate environments that behave as if they've been wrapped in a savenotes environment.

                  The package also provides  footnote and footnotetext environments which you can put verbatim 
                  inside.

                  The package is part of the  mdwtools (https://ctan.org/pkg/mdwtools) bundle.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/mdwtools/footnote.pdf

on TeXLive:       mdwtools

footnoterange -- References to ranges of footnotes
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/footnoterange
name:             footnoterange
caption:          References to ranges of footnotes
author:           Hans-Martin Münch
copyright:        Hans-Martin Münch et al. (2012-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.1c (2026-01-19)
last changes:     2026-01-19
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package provides the environments  footnoterange and footnoterange* . Multiple footnotes 
                  inside these environments are not referenced as (e.g.) “1 2 3” but as “1-3”, i.e., the range (from first 
                  to last referred footnote at that place) is given. If the hyperref (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref) package 
                  is loaded with enabled hyperfootnotes -option, then the references are hyperlinked. (References 
                  to footnotes in footnoterange* environments are never hyperlinked.)

version:          2.1.5 (2017-07-14)
last changes:     2017-07-14
year:             2017
description:      (no language specified) The package provides a PGF/TikZ-based mechanism for drawing linguistic (and other kinds of) trees. Its 
                  main features are:

                  + a packing algorithm which can produce very compact trees;
                  + a user-friendly interface consisting of the familiar bracket encoding of trees plus the key-value interface 
                    to option-setting;
                  + many tree-formatting options, with control over option values of individual nodes and mechanisms for 
                    their manipulation;
                  + the possibility to decorate the tree using the full power of PGF/TikZ; and
                  + an externalization mechanism sensitive to code-changes.

caption:          Manipulate \index commands in a LaTeX file
author:           Guido Milanese
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          0.1
description:      (no language specified) The forindex bundle consists of two programs: doindex and cleanindex.

                  Doindex reads a list of items to index, and processes a LaTeX file to add  \index commands in accordance 
                  with the items in the list.

                  Both programs are written in  SNOBOL IV (http://www.snobol4.com/) ; .exe files compiled with Spitbol 
                  (http://www.snobol4.com/) are available for Windows users.

author:           Donald P. Story

version:          1.3 (2019-03-20)
last changes:     2019-03-20
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) This package provides support for UTF-16BE Unicode character encoding (called a big-endian character 
                  string) for the text string type (PDF Reference, version 1.7, beginning on page 158). Text strings are 
                  used in “text annotations, bookmark names, article threads, document information, and so forth” (to partially 
                  quote page 158). The particular application is to set property values of form fields, at least those 
                  properties that take the text strings as its value.

                  The package contains support for Basic Latin plus the ability to enter any unicode character using the 
                  notation  \uXXXX , where XXXX are four hex digits.

                  The Package works for dvips/Distiller, pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, and XeLaTeX.

                  based TeX typesetting, including an extensive mathematics set and several other symbols. The system is

fpl -- SC and OsF fonts for URW Palladio L
------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fpl
name:             fpl
caption:          SC and OsF fonts for URW Palladio L
author:           Ralf Stubner
copyright:        Ralf Stubner (2004, 2005)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
license:          gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
version:          1.003 (2018-12-11)
last changes:     2018-12-11
year:             2018
description:      (no language specified) The FPL Fonts provide a set of SC/OsF fonts for URW Palladio L which are compatible with respect to metrics 
                  with the Palatino SC/OsF fonts from Adobe. Note that it is not my aim to exactly reproduce the outlines 
                  of the original Adobe fonts. The SC and OsF in the FPL Fonts were designed with the glyphs from URW Palladio 
                  L as starting point. For some glyphs (e.g. ‘o’) I got the best result by scaling and boldening. For others 
                  (e.g. ‘h’) shifting selected portions of the character gave more satisfying results. All this was done 
                  using the free  font editor FontForge (https://fontforge.github.io/) . The kerning data in these 
                  fonts comes from Walter Schmidt’s improved Palatino metrics.

                  LaTeX use is enabled by the mathpazo package, which is part of the  psnfss (https://ctan.org/pkg/psnfss) distribution.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/fpl/README

fragoli -- Macros for constructing complex semantic derivations
---------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fragoli
name:             FraGoLi
caption:          Macros for constructing complex semantic derivations
author:           Paul Eduard Koenig
copyright:        Paul Eduard Koenig (2025-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.3.4 (2026-05-30)
last changes:     2026-05-30
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The primary goal of this package is to provide a minimal and user-friendly syntax for constructing large 
                  and complex  'semantic derivations' , following the specific notational style used at Goethe University 
                  Frankfurt. It includes a comprehensive set of commands for text formatting and various types of bracketing, 
                  ensuring a consistent style — particularly when distinguishing between meta-language and object-language 
                  within a single derivation or formula. The formula style is loosely based on the accompanying material 
                  to an introductory course to linguistic semantics by Prof. Dr. Thomas Ede Zimmermann.

                  The package brings together and refines a collection of LaTeX commands and concepts developed over the 
                  years within the  Department of Linguistics (https://www.linguistik-in-frankfurt.de/) at the Goethe-Universität 
                  at Frankfurt am Main. In the process of preparing research papers, assignments, and examinations, numerous 
                  custom LaTeX headers and commands were shared within the department — some mutually compatible, others 
                  not.

                  Note: The package name is an abbreviation of “Frankfurt Goethe Linguistic”.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fragoli/fragoli_doc.pdf

framed -- Framed or shaded regions that can break across pages
--------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/framed
name:             framed
caption:          Framed or shaded regions that can break across pages
author:           Donald Arseneau
copyright:        Donald Arseneau (1992-2011)
license:          other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
version:          0.96
description:      (no language specified) The package creates three environments:

                  +  framed , which puts an ordinary frame box around the region,
                  +  shaded , which shades the region, and
                  +  leftbar , which places a line at the left side. The environments allow a break at their start 
                    (the \FrameCommand enables creation of a title that is “attached” to the environment); breaks are 
                    also allowed in the course of the framed/shaded matter.
There is also a command  \MakeFramed to make your own framed-style environments.

freemath -- LaTeX maths without backslashes
-------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/freemath
name:             freemath
caption:          LaTeX maths without backslashes
author:           plante
copyright:        plante (2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.1
description:      (no language specified) This package allows for the omission of backslashes from most math mode commands. Specifically, any consecutive 
                  string of at least two (Latin) letters appearing in math mode will automatically be turned into the control 
                  sequence with the same name, if it exists.

                  The package provides the  \freemathon and \freemathoff commands which respectively activate 
                  and deactivate this behaviour. It is 'disabled' by default upon loading.

                  Regular commands initiated by a backslash may of course still be used when freemath is active, and can 
                  furthermore be freely mixed with backslash-free commands.

frege -- Typeset fregean Begriffsschrift

caption:          Typeset fregean Begriffsschrift
author:           Quirin Pamp
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          1.3
description:      (no language specified) The package defines a number of new commands for typesetting fregean Begriffsschrift in LaTeX.

                  It is loosely based on the package  begriff (https://ctan.org/pkg/begriff) , and offers a number 
                  of improvements including better relative lengths of the content stroke with respect to other strokes, 
                  content strokes that point at the middle of lines rather than the bottom, a greater width for the assertion 
                  stroke as compared to the content stroke, a more intuitive structure for the conditional, greater care 
                  taken to allow for the linewidth in the spacing of formulas.

description:      (no language specified) This is a redistribution and repackaging of the late Bernard Gaulle’s “light” package to typeset French 
                  documents according to the rules of the “Imprimerie Nationale”.

                  The package offers a package, two  Babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) language definition files 
                  ( french.ldf and frenchle.ldf ), and a package to enable the non-standard definition files 
                  to be loaded into an unmodified Babel.

                  The user may simply use  frenchle.sty if typesetting a French-only document, but should use Babel 
                  with the frenchle option for a multilingual document.

                  Note that this package is now obsolete; users of the package are advised to switch to using  e-french 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/e-french) .

fullpict -- Full page pictures
------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fullpict
name:             fullpict
caption:          Full page pictures
author:           Bruce Shawyer
license:          noinfo = noinfo 
version:          (2003-10-31)
last changes:     2003-10-31
year:             2003
description:      (no language specified) The package provides picture-mode environments whose size is related to the size of the page. The fullpict 
                  environment takes arguments to specify the dimension of the picture in picture mode ‘unit lengths’; the 
                  value for  \unitlength is defined by the fact that the picture is to be 90% of \textwidth . 
                  Similar environments halfpict (half the width of fullpict), and scalepict (a given percentage of the 
                  width of fullpict), are also defined.

functional -- An intuitive functional programming interface for LaTeX2
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/functional
name:             functional
caption:          An intuitive functional programming interface for LaTeX2
author:           Jianrui Lyu
copyright:        Jianrui Lyu (2022-2024)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2024C (2024-12-18)
last changes:     2024-12-18
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) This package provides an intuitive functional programming interface for LaTeX2, which is an alternative 
                  choice to expl3 or LuaTeX, if you want to do programming in LaTeX.

                  Although there are functions in LaTeX3 programming layer (expl3), the evaluation of them is from outside 
                  to inside. With this package, the evaluation of functions is from inside to outside, which is the same 
                  as other programming languages such as Lua. In this way, it is rather easy to debug code too.

fundus -- Providing LaTeX access to various font families
---------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus
name:             fundus
caption:          Providing LaTeX access to various font families
author:           Gerd Neugebauer
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
description:      (no language specified) Fonts supported are

                  + Peter Vanroose’s  calligra (https://ctan.org/pkg/calligra) font (package fundus-calligra (https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-calligra) );

                  + the emulation of  Peter Vanroose’s handwriting (https://ctan.org/pkg/script-font) (package fundus-script 
                    (https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-pvscript) );
                  + the  Washington University cyrillic (https://ctan.org/pkg/wncyr) fonts (package fundus-cyr (https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-cyr) );

                  + the   'la' and 'lla' children's handwriting fonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/la) (package fundus-la 
                    (https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-la) );
                  + the  Computer Modern outline fonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/cmoutlines) (package fundus-outline 
                    (https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-outline) );
                  + a group of ‘Startrek’ fonts (package  fundus-startrek (https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-startrek) ), 
                    which contains the fonts it supports;
                  + the  Sütterlin (https://ctan.org/pkg/sueterlin) font (package fundus-suetterlin (https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-suetterlin) );

                  + the  twcal (https://ctan.org/pkg/twcal) calligraphic fonts (package fundus-twcal (https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-twcal) ); 
                    and
                  + the   'va'  (https://ctan.org/pkg/va) handwriting font (package fundus-va (https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-va) ).

contact:          bugs: https://codeberg.org/gene-TeX-libraries/fundus/issues
contact:          repository: https://codeberg.org/gene-TeX-libraries/fundus

gamebooklib -- Macros for setting numbered entries in shuffled order
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/gamebooklib
name:             Gamebooklib
caption:          Macros for setting numbered entries in shuffled order
author:           Robert J Lee
copyright:        Robert J Lee (2021-2023)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.4 (2023-07-28)
last changes:     2023-07-28
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) This package provides macros and environments to allow the user to typeset a series of cross-referenced, 
                  numbered “entries”, shuffled into random order, to produce an interactive novel or “gamebook”.

                  This allows entries to be written in natural order and shuffled automatically into a repeatable non-linear 
                  order.

                  Limited support is provided for footnotes to appear at the natural position: the end of each entry, or 
                  the end of each page, whichever is closest to the footnote mark.

                  This is unrelated to the  gamebook (https://ctan.org/pkg/gamebook) package which is more concerned 
                  with the formatting of entries rather than their order. The two packages can be used together or separately.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/gamebooklib/README
documentation:    Example of use (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/gamebooklib/gamebooklib_test.pdf

-- local file:    ./6929570100-gamebooklib.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/gamebooklib
on MikTeX:        gamebooklib
on TeXLive:       gamebooklib
keyword:          games (process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements)
keyword:          random (generate and/or use pseudo-random numbers)

garamond-libre -- The Garamond Libre font face
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/garamond-libre
name:             garamond-libre
caption:          The Garamond Libre font face
author:           Daniel Benjamin Miller
author:           Bob Tennent
copyright:        Daniel Benjamin Miller (2019-2020)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          1.4 (2024-04-23)
last changes:     2024-04-23
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) Garamond Libre is a free and open-source old-style font family. It is a “true Garamond,” i.e., it is 
                  based off the designs of 16th-century French engraver Claude Garamond (also spelled Garamont).

                  The Roman design is Garamond’s; the italics are from a design by Robert Granjon. The upright Greek font 
                  is after a design by Firmin Didot; the “italic” Greek font is after a design by Alexander Wilson.

                  The font family includes support for Latin, Greek (monotonic and polytonic) and Cyrillic scripts, as 
                  well as small capitals, old-style figures, superior and inferior figures, historical ligatures, Byzantine 
                  musical symbols, the IPA and swash capitals.
