gates -- Support for writing modular and customisable code
----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/gates
name:             gates
caption:          Support for writing modular and customisable code
author:           Paul Isambert
author:           Yuri Robbers
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          0.2
description:      (no language specified) The package provides the means of writing code in a modular fashion: big macros or functions are divided 
                  into small chunks (called gates) with names, which can be externally controlled (e.g. they can be disabled, 
                  subjected to conditionals, loops...) and/or augmented with new chunks.

                  Thus complex code may easily be customised without having to rewrite it, or even understand its implementation: 
                  the behavior of existing gates can be modified, and new ones can be added, without endangering the whole 
                  design. This allows code to be hacked in ways the original authors might have never envisioned.

                  The gates package is implemented independently for both TeX and Lua. The TeX implementation, running 
                  in any current environment, requires the  texapi (https://ctan.org/pkg/texapi) package, whereas 
                  the Lua version can be run with any Lua interpreter, not just LuaTeX.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/gates/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/gates/gates-doc.pdf
-- local file:    ./6930744428-gates-doc.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/gates

on TeXLive:       gates

gatherenum -- A crossover of align* and enumerate
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/gatherenum
name:             gatherenum
caption:          A crossover of align* and enumerate
author:           Julien Rivaud
copyright:        Julien RIVAUD (2016-2019)
license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
version:          1.8 (2019-09-29)
last changes:     2019-09-29
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) This package (ab)uses the inline enumeration capabilities of  enumitem (https://ctan.org/pkg/enumitem) to 
                  add a “displayed” enumeration mode, triggered by adding ‘ gathered ’ to the key-value option list 
                  of the enumerate (https://ctan.org/pkg/enumerate) environment. The end result is similar to a regular enumerate 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/enumerate) environment wrapped in a multicols (https://ctan.org/pkg/multicol) environment, 
                  with the following advantages:

                  + Gathered enumerate can pack items depending on their actual width rather than a fixed, constant number 
                    per line.
                  + Gathered enumeration fills items in a line-major order (instead of column-major order), which my students 
                    found less confusing. YMMV.
The package depends on  enumitem (https://ctan.org/pkg/enumitem) , expl3 (https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3) , 
                  and xparse (https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse) ,

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/gatherenum/README.md

---------------------------------------------

name:             gcite

author:           Iain Phillips
author:           Matthew Tylee Atkinson

license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)

description:      (no language specified) The package allows citations in the German style, which is considered by many to be particularly reader-friendly.

                  comment is invited.

geist-font -- LaTeX support for the Geist and Geist Mono typefaces
------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/geist-font
name:             geist-font
caption:          LaTeX support for the Geist and Geist Mono typefaces
author:           Andre Anjos
license:          ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0 (2026-08-24)
last changes:     2026-08-24
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package provides LaTeX support for Geist and Geist Mono, the sans-serif and monospaced typeface families 
                  designed by Vercel and released under the SIL Open Font License. Both families are covered in all nine 
                  weights, from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic.

                  The package works with pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX. Under XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX the OpenType fonts 
                  are used directly through  fontspec (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec) . Under pdfLaTeX the package 
                  uses Type1 fonts and metrics generated from the OpenType originals with autoinst (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontools) , 
                  since pdfTeX cannot subset CFF-flavoured OpenType. Both paths declare the same font series names, so 
                  a document selects the same face whichever engine builds it. Fonts are provided in the OT1, T1 and TS1 
                  encodings.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/geist-font/README.md

gellmu -- LaTeX-like markup for writing XML documents

caption:          LaTeX-like markup for writing XML documents
author:           William F. Hammond
copyright:        William F. Hammond (2001-2006)
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          0.8.4.1
description:      (no language specified) GELLMU is an acronym for “Generalized Extensible LaTeX-Like MarkUp”. With GELLMU one may use LaTeX-like 
                  markup to write consciously for SGML document types such as HTML, DocBook, TEI, or GELLMU's own LaTeX-like 
                  document type ‘article’.

                  The package provides a syntactic translator, which is the project layer for all document types.

                  The article document type is very much like LaTeX with a tightly enforced syntax and vocabulary. For 
                  article, the package provides translators to classic HTML, regular LaTeX and the XML form of HTML extended 
                  by MathML (XHTML). The latter form provides optimal online content that is ‘accessible’ and in the author's 
                  opinion superior to PDF for web presentation.

description:      (no language specified) Pedigree and genealogical tree diagrams are proven tools to visualize genetic and relational connections 
                  between individuals. The naming (“tree”) derives from historical family diagrams. However, even the smallest 
                  family entity consisting of two parents and several children is hardly a ‘mathematical’ tree — it is 
                  a more general graph.

                  The package provides a set of tools to typeset genealogical trees (i.e., to typeset a set of special 
                  graphs for the description of family-like structures). The package uses an autolayout algorithm which 
                  can be customized, e.​g., to prioritize certain paths.

version:          1.0.2
description:      (no language specified) Provides generic commands  \degree , \celsius , \perthousand , \micro and \ohm which 
                  work both in text and maths mode. Various means are provided to fake the symbols or take them from particular 
                  symbol fonts, if they are not available in the default fonts used in the document. This should be perfectly

                  math mode and with arbitrary typefaces. Note that the package has been designed to work in conjunction 
                  with units.sty (https://ctan.org/pkg/units) .

                  This package used to be part of the  was (https://ctan.org/pkg/was) bundle, but has now become 
                  a package in its own right.

last changes:     2025-07-13
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This is a redistribution of the original Gentium and GentiumBook release from SIL, not altered in any 
                  way.

                  Gentium (https://software.sil.org/gentium/) is a typeface family designed to enable the diverse 
                  ethnic groups around the world who use the Latin, Cyrillic and Greek scripts to produce readable, high-quality 
                  publications.

                  The Gentium family includes a complete Greek font, supporting both monotonic and polytonic forms. While 
                  some Greek characters do closely resemble Latin ones, it is a separate design that embraces the robust, 
                  distinctive character of the Greek script, but does so within the design contextof the whole typeface. 
                  As a result, the two scripts can be successfully mixed in a paragraph or page of text.

geometry -- Flexible and complete interface to document dimensions
------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/geometry
name:             geometry
caption:          Flexible and complete interface to document dimensions
author:           Hideo Umeki
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
author:           David Carlisle
copyright:        Hideo Umeki, David Carlisle (2018-2026)
copyright:        Hideo Umeki (1996-2010)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          6.0 (2026-03-07)
last changes:     2026-03-07
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package provides an easy and flexible user interface to customize page layout, implementing auto-centering 
                  and auto-balancing mechanisms so that the users have only to give the least description for the page 
                  layout. For example, if you want to set each margin 2cm without header space, what you need is just  \usepackage[margin=2cm,nohead]{geometry} .

                  The package knows about all the standard paper sizes, so that the user need not know what the nominal 
                  ‘real’ dimensions of the paper are, just its standard name (such as  a4 , letter , etc.).

                  An important feature is the package’s ability to communicate the paper size it’s set up to the output 
                  (whether via DVI  \special s or via direct interaction with pdf(La)TeX).

documentation:    Package Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/geometry/README.md

name:             getargs
caption:          A flexible list-parsing macro with configurable parsing character
author:           Steven B. Segletes
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.01 (2016-05-20)
last changes:     2016-05-20
year:             2016
description:      (no language specified) This short package provides a flexible list-parsing macro with the ability to configure the parsing character, 
                  as well as the macro names in which the parsed list items are placed. The name of the parsing macro is 
                  \getargs .

                  It is a significant improvement over similarly named macros in the same author’s  stringstrings (https://ctan.org/pkg/stringstrings) and readarray 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/readarray) packages. It is the author’s intent to eventually have the parsers 
                  of those other packages point to this package, to achieve a measure of uniformity.

                  Note: This package has been withdrawn by its author in July 2016. It will be replaced by the forthcoming 
                  listofitems package.

gfs -- The GFS font collection
------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/gfs
name:             GFS
caption:          The GFS font collection
author:           George D. Matthiopoulos
author:           The Greek Font Society
author:           Antonis Tsolomitis
license:          other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
description:      (no language specified) The Greek Font Society has made a large number of fonts publicly available, and this collection reflects 
                  those that have been adapted, by Tsolomitis and others, for use with LaTeX. The collection comprises:

                  
                  +  GFS Artemisia (https://ctan.org/pkg/gfsartemisia) , a relatively modern general-purpose font;
                  +  GFS Baskerville (https://ctan.org/pkg/gfsbaskerville) , based on Baskerville’s classic font;
                  +  GFS Bodoni (https://ctan.org/pkg/gfsbodoni) , based on Bodoni’s 19th century work;
                  +  GFS Didot (https://ctan.org/pkg/gfsdidot) , based on Didot’s 1805 font;
                  +  GFS Neo-Hellenic (https://ctan.org/pkg/gfsneohellenic) , a version of a font developed in Britain 
                    in the early 20th century; and
                  +  GFS Porson (https://ctan.org/pkg/gfsporson) , developed from the early 19th century font based 
                    on Porson’s writing.
The fonts, except Baskerville and Porson, support the Latin alphabet as well as the Greek alphabet. Neo 
                  Hellenic has been matched to the existing  CM bright (https://ctan.org/pkg/cmbright) set of mathematics 
                  fonts.

version:          0.3
description:      (no language specified) The package builds on the standard LaTeX packages  graphics (https://ctan.org/pkg/graphics) and/or graphicx 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/graphicx) and allows external LaTeX source files to be included, in the same 
                  way as graphic files, by \includegraphics . In effect, then package adds support for the .tex extension.

                  Some of the lower level operations like clipping and trimming are implemented using the  adjustbox 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/adjustbox) package which includes native pdfLaTeX support and uses the pgf 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) package for other output formats.

ginpenc -- Modification of inputenc for German
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/ginpenc
name:             ginpenc
caption:          Modification of inputenc for German
author:           Harald Harders
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) If the  inputenc (https://ctan.org/pkg/inputenc) is used and German umlauts are input directly, 
                  they are converted to the LICR representation \"a (etc.). This breaks the sort algorithm of makeindex 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/makeindex) , for instance. Ginpenc converts umlauts and the sharp-s to the short 
                  forms defined by babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) , e.g., "a instead, if the text is typeset 
                  in German.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ginpenc/README

description:      (no language specified) If you are using git to control versions of LaTeX-files, you may want to show yourself or other users

gladtex -- LaTeX equations in HTML
----------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/gladtex
name:             GladTeX
caption:          LaTeX equations in HTML
author:           Sebastian Humenda
author:           Martin G. Gulbrandsen
copyright:        Martin G. Gulbrandsen (1999-2010)
copyright:        Jonathan Daugherty (2011-2013)
copyright:        Sebastian Humenda (2013-2016)
license:          lgpl3 = GNU Lesser General Public License 3 (free)
version:          3.0.0
description:      (no language specified) GladTeX is a utility that enables LaTeX equations within HTML code. You write HTML code as usual, but 
                  in addition you can include equations within the special tags  &lt;EQ&gt;..&lt;/EQ&gt; , as if 
                  within $$..$$ in LaTeX. Then you run gladtex, which replaces the equations by images. Features 
                  include image alignment (baseline of equations agree with baseline of text), GIF and PNG support, transparent 
                  backgrounds and antialiasing.

                  Additionally, GladTeX can aid the creation of accessible documents for the blind by providing the LaTeX 
                  equation in the  alt attribute of an image. It also comes with a library which allows embedding 
                  GladTeX into other applications.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/gladtex/README.md

keyword:          cvt-html (generate HTML from TeX-ish sources)
year:             2016
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

glosmathtools -- Mathematical nomenclature tools based on the glossaries package
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/glosmathtools
name:             glosmathtools
caption:          Mathematical nomenclature tools based on the glossaries package
author:           Francis Gagnon
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0.0 (2020-03-26)
last changes:     2020-03-26
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) This package can be used to generate a mathematical nomenclature (also called “list of symbols” or “notation”). 
                  It is based on the  glossaries (https://ctan.org/pkg/glossaries) package.

                  Its main features are:

                  + symbol categories (e.g.: latin, greek)
                  + automatic but customizable symbol sorting
                  + easy subscript management
                  + easy accentuation management
                  + abbreviation support (with first use definition)
                  + bilingual nomenclatures (for bilingual documents)
                  + bilingual abbreviations
The documentation is based on the  ulthese (https://ctan.org/pkg/ulthese) class.

                  The package itself depends on  glossaries (https://ctan.org/pkg/glossaries) , amsmath (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath) , amsfonts 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsfonts) , and etoolbox (https://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox) .

glossaries -- Create glossaries and lists of acronyms
-----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/glossaries
name:             glossaries
caption:          Create glossaries and lists of acronyms
author:           Nicola Talbot
copyright:        Nicola Talbot (2007-2026)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          5.1 (2026-04-21)
last changes:     2026-04-21
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The glossaries package supports acronyms and multiple glossaries, and has provision for operation in 
                  several languages (using the facilities of either  babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) or polyglossia 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia) ). New entries are defined to have a name and description (and 
                  optionally an associated symbol). Support for multiple languages is offered, and plural forms of terms 
                  may be specified. An additional package, glossaries-accsupp (https://ctan.org/pkg/glossaries-accsupp) , 
                  can make use of the accsupp (https://ctan.org/pkg/accsupp) package mechanisms for accessibility 
                  support for PDF files containing glossaries.

                  The user may define new glossary styles, and preambles and postambles can be specified. There is provision 
                  for loading a database of terms, but only terms used in the text will be added to the relevant glossary.

                  The package uses an indexing program to provide the actual glossary; either  makeindex (https://ctan.org/pkg/makeindex) or xindy 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/xindy) may serve this purpose, and a Perl script is provided to serve as interface.

                  This package requires the  mfirstuc (https://ctan.org/pkg/mfirstuc) package.

                  The package supersedes the author’s  glossary (https://ctan.org/pkg/glossary) package (which is 
                  now obsolete).

documentation:    Package code and documentation (PDF) (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/glossaries/glossaries-code.pdf
-- local file:    ./8996909075-glossaries-code.pdf

glossary -- Create a glossary
-----------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/glossary
name:             glossary
caption:          Create a glossary
author:           Nicola Talbot
copyright:        Nicola Talbot (2006)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          2.4
description:      (no language specified) The package supports generation of a glossary with makeindex. It has a certain amount of flexibility 
                  allowing the user to customize the format of the glossary and define new glossary-style objects so that 
                  you can have more than one type of glossary in your document.

                  The package is no longer supported; the author urges users to switch to use of its replacement, the  glossaries 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/glossaries) package. Migration support is available, within the newer package.

on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/obsolete/macros/latex/contrib/glossary

version:          0.993
description:      (no language specified) A LaTeX package and an example class for documenting (La)TeX packages, document classes, .dtx etc., providing 
                  hyperlinks. The package is believed to be compatible with  doc (https://ctan.org/pkg/doc) and permits 
                  minimal markup of code (the macrocode environment is no longer necessary). The package provides automatic 
                  detection of definitions (detecting such things as \def , \newcommand , \DeclareOption etc.).

                  The package needs  hyperref (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref) and the author’s three ‘basic’ packages: gmutils 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/gmutils) , gmverb (https://ctan.org/pkg/gmverb) and gmiflink (https://ctan.org/pkg/gmiflink) .

                  As a bonus (and as an example of doc compatibility) driver files are provided that may be used to typeset 
                  the LaTeX Base.

gnuplottex -- Embed Gnuplot commands in LaTeX documents
-------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/gnuplottex
name:             gnuplottex
caption:          Embed Gnuplot commands in LaTeX documents
author:           Lars Kotthoff
copyright:        Lars Kotthoff (2006-2019)
license:          gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
version:          0.9.5
description:      (no language specified) This package allows you to include  Gnuplot (https://ctan.org/pkg/gnuplot) graphs in your LaTeX 
                  documents.

                  The gnuplot code is extracted from the document and written to  .gnuplot files. Then, if shell 
                  escape is used, the graph files are automatically processed to graphics or LaTeX code files which will 
                  then be included in the document. If shell escape isn't used, the user will have to manually convert 
                  the files by running gnuplot on the extracted .gnuplot files.

version:          0.2 (2019-01-04)
last changes:     2019-01-04
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) The LaTeX package  gobble includes several gobble macros not included in the LaTeX kernel. These 
                  macros remove a number of arguments after them, a feature regulary used inside other macros. This includes 
                  gobble macros for optional arguments.

                  The LaTeX package  gobble-user provides these macros at the user level, i.e. using names without @ so 
                  that these can be used without \makeatletter and \makeatother .

                  The same macros are provided inside  .tex files for use with plain-TeX or other TeX formats. However, 
                  the gobble macros for optional macros require \@ifnextchar to be defined.

gost -- BibTeX styles to format according to GOST
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/gost
name:             gost
caption:          BibTeX styles to format according to GOST
author:           Igor A. Kotelnikov
author:           Maksym Polyakov
copyright:        Leonid Sinev (2017)
copyright:        Maksym Polyakov (1996-2005)
copyright:        Igor A. Kotelnikov (2012-2021)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.2l (2021-02-05)
last changes:     2021-02-05
year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) BibTeX styles to format bibliographies in English, Russian or Ukrainian according to GOST 7.0.5-2008 
                  or GOST 7.1-2003.

                  Both 8-bit and Unicode (UTF-8) versions of each BibTeX style, in each case offering a choice of sorted

description:      (no language specified) This package combines the tools of the graphic, subfigure and float packages in a way that makes their 
                  use simpler and more robust. The  Figure environment (capitalized) differs from the standard LaTeX 
                  figure environment by the addition of a mandatory argument to specify the caption and an optional argument 
                  to be used as a label. These ensure that the \label command appears after the \caption command 
                  to avoid the common labelling error. The commands \graphfig and \graphfig* have the additional 
                  advantage that the image will be automatically centered horizontally.

                  The package is part of the  bosisio (https://ctan.org/pkg/bosisio) bundle.

version:          1.4h (2026-05-17)

description:      (no language specified) The package was designed to accommodate all needs for inclusion of graphics in LaTeX documents, replacing 
                  many earlier packages used in LaTeX 2.09. The package aims to give a consistent interface to including 
                  the file types that are understood in your output, by use of ‘printer drivers’ (now known, simply, as 
                  ‘drivers’). The distribution of the package contains several drivers, but others (for example,  pdfTeX 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pdftex-def) ) are distributed separately. The package also offers several means 
                  of manipulating graphics in the course of inserting them into a document (for example, rotation and scaling).

                  For extended documentation see  epslatex (https://ctan.org/pkg/epslatex) .

                  The package is part of the  graphics bundle (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-graphics) , which is one 
                  of the collections in the LaTeX ‘required’ (https://ctan.org/pkg/required) set of packages.

graphicscache -- Cache includegraphics calls
--------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/graphicscache
name:             graphicscache
caption:          Cache includegraphics calls
author:           Max Schwarz
copyright:        Max Schwarz (2018-2021)
license:          bsd3 = 3-clause BSD License (free)
version:          0.4 (2022-12-20)
last changes:     2022-12-20
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) This LaTeX package provides caching of  \includegraphics calls, with several useful effects:

                  + Recompilations are much faster (10x speedup observed).
                  + Images can be postprocessed with  ghostscript before inclusion, thus:
                  ++ Automatic downscaling to specified DPI
                  ++ Automatic JPEG compression with configurable quality
                  ++ Much smaller files (e.g. 10MB instead of 150MB)!

Note: Due to the one-by-one invocation of  pdflatex and ghostscript for each graphics element, 
                  the first compilation is typically slower than usual.

                  Note:  graphicscache needs the \write18 call (also called shell escape). This is a security 
                  risk if you have untrusted TeX sources.

                  graphicscache supports pdfLaTeX and LuaLaTeX; XeLaTeX is not supported.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/graphicscache/graphicscache.pdf
-- local file:    ./9742294191-graphicscache.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/graphicscache/README.md
contact:          repository: https://github.com/xqms/graphicscache
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/graphicscache
on MikTeX:        graphicscache
on TeXLive:       graphicscache

graphicx-psmin -- Reduce size of PostScript files by not repeating images
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/graphicx-psmin
name:             graphicx-psmin
caption:          Reduce size of PostScript files by not repeating images
author:           Hendri Adriaens
copyright:        Hendri Adriaens (2004-2020)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.2
description:      (no language specified) The package is an extension of the standard  latex-graphics (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-graphics) bundle 
                  and provides a way to include repeated PostScript graphics (ps, eps) only once in a PostScript document. 
                  This leads to smaller PostScript documents when having, for instance, a logo on every page. The package 
                  only works when post-processed with dvips (https://ctan.org/pkg/dvipsk) , which should be version 
                  5.95b or later.

                  The difference for a resulting distilled PDF file is minimal (as Ghostscript and Adobe Distiller only 
                  include a single copy of each graphics file, anyway).

grayhints -- Produce ‘gray hints’ to a variable text field
----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/grayhints
name:             grayhints
caption:          Produce ‘gray hints’ to a variable text field
author:           Donald P. Story
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          (2018-11-01)
last changes:     2018-11-01
year:             2018
description:      (no language specified) The package provides JavaScript code snippets to create ‘gray hints’. Gray hints, as the author terms 
                  them, are text that appears initially in a text field that gives a short hint as to what the contents 
                  of the text field should be. For example, a text field might contain the hint ‘First Name’, or a date 
                  field might read ‘yyyy/mm/dd’. As soon as the field comes into focus, the hint disappears. It reappears 
                  when the field is blurred and the user did not enter any text into the field.

                  The package works for dvips/Distiller, pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, and XeLaTeX.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/grayhints/README.md

greektonoi -- Facilitates writing/editing of multiaccented greek
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/greektonoi
name:             greektonoi
caption:          Facilitates writing/editing of multiaccented greek
author:           Charalampos Cornaros
license:          lgpl3 = GNU Lesser General Public License 3 (free)
version:          (2016-01-01)
last changes:     2016-01-01
year:             2016
description:      (no language specified) The greektonoi mapping extends the  betababel (https://ctan.org/pkg/betababel) package or the babel 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) polutonikogreek option to provide a simple way to insert ancient Greek 
                  texts with diacritical characters into your document using a similar method to the commonly used Beta 
                  Code transliteration, but with much more freedom. It is designed especially for the XeTeX engine and 
                  it could also be used for fast and easy modification of monotonic greek texts to polytonic. The output 
                  text is natively encoded in Unicode, so it can be reused in any possible way. The greektonoi package 
                  provides, in addition to inserting greek accents and breathings, many other symbols used in greek numbers 
                  and arithmetic or in the greek archaic period. It could be used with greektonoi mapping or indepedently.

gridset -- Grid, a.k.a. in-register, setting
--------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/gridset
name:             gridset
caption:          Grid, a.k.a. in-register, setting
author:           Markus Kohm
copyright:        Markus Kohm (2008-2020)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.4 (2024-08-17)
last changes:     2024-08-17
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) Grid setting — also known as strict in-register setting — is something, that should be done for a lot 
                  of documents but is not easy using LaTeX. The package helps to get the information needed for grid setting. 
                  It does not implement auto grid setting, but there is a command  \vskipnextgrid , that moves to 
                  the next grid position. This may be enough under some circumstances, but in other circumstances it may 
                  fail. Thus gridset is only one more step for grid setting, not a complete solution.

                  gtex-letter connects to the gnome-address-book from the gnome-pim package.

hadith -- An easy way to typeset Hadith text using XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/hadith
name:             hadith
caption:          An easy way to typeset Hadith text using XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX
author:           Nibras Abo Alzahab
copyright:        Nibras Abo Alzahab (2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
version:          1.1.0
description:      (no language specified) This package provides an easy way to typeset Hadith text (with full Arabic diacritics/tashkeel) from 
                  the canonical collections of Islamic tradition in XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX documents. It is modeled after 
                  the  quran (https://ctan.org/pkg/quran) package and follows the same architecture: text data in .def files, 
                  macros in .sty .

                  The package currently includes seven collections (36,390 hadiths total): Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, 
                  Sunan Abi Dawud, Jami at-Tirmidhi, Sunan an-Nasa’i, Sunan Ibn Majah, and Muwatta Malik. English translations 
                  and hadith authenticity grades are included.

                  Key features include on-demand chapter loading to avoid TeX memory limits, case-insensitive collection 
                  names, inline citation commands, and metadata commands for section/chapter names.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/unicodetex/latex/hadith/README.md

har2nat -- Replace the harvard package with natbib
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/har2nat
name:             har2nat
caption:          Replace the harvard package with natbib
author:           Bas Straathof
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) This small package allows a LaTeX document containing the citation commands provided by the  Harvard 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/harvard) package to be compiled using the natbib (https://ctan.org/pkg/natbib) package. 
                  Migration from harvard to natbib thus can be achieved simply by replacing

                  |
\usepackage{harvard}
| with

                  |
usepackage{natbib}
usepackage{har2nat}
| It is important that har2nat be loaded after natbib, since it modifies natbib commands.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/har2nat/README

hardwrap -- Hard wrap text to a certain character length
--------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/hardwrap
name:             hardwrap
caption:          Hard wrap text to a certain character length
author:           Will Robertson
author:           Kevin Godby
copyright:        Will Robertson, Kevin Godby (2010, 2011)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.2
description:      (no language specified) The package facilitates wrapping text to a specific character width, breaking lines by words rather than, 
                  as done by TeX, by characters.

                  The primary use for these facilities is to aid the generation of messages sent to the log file or console 
                  output to display messages to the user. Package authors may also find this useful when writing out arbitrary 
                  text to an external file.

harvard -- Harvard citation package for use with LaTeX2e
--------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/harvard
name:             harvard
caption:          Harvard citation package for use with LaTeX2e
author:           Peter Williams
author:           Thorsten Schnier
copyright:        Peter Williams (1994)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.0.5
description:      (no language specified) This is a re-implementation, for LaTeX2e, of the  original Harvard package (https://ctan.org/pkg/harvard-obsolete) . 
                  The bundle contains the LaTeX package, several BibTeX styles, and a ‘Perl package’ for use with LaTeX2HTML 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex2html) .

                  Harvard is an author-year citation style (all but the first author are suppressed in second and subsequent 
                  citations of the same entry); the package defines several variant styles:

                  +  apsr.bst for the American Political Science Review;
                  +  agsm.bst for Australian Government publications;
                  +  dcu.bst from the Design Computing Unit of the University of Sydney;
                  +  kluwer.bst which aims at the format preferred in Kluwer publications;
                  +  nederlands.bst which deals with sorting Dutch names with prefixes (such as van ) according 
                    to Dutch rules,
                  + together with several styles whose authors offer no description of their behaviour.

documentation:    Package Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/harvard/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/harvard/harvard.pdf
-- local file:    ./3316582511-harvard.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/harvard
on MikTeX:        harvard
on TeXLive:       harvard
keyword:          tagged-pdf-incompatible (tagged PDF incompatible)
keyword:          bibtex-supp (BibTeX citation support)
see also:         har2nat (har2nat -- Replace the harvard package with natbib)
year:             1994
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14


harvard-obsolete -- The Harvard bibliography style family
---------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/harvard-obsolete
name:             harvard-obsolete
caption:          The Harvard bibliography style family
author:           Peter Williams
license:          noinfo = noinfo 
version:          (1993-11-25)
last changes:     1993-11-25
year:             1993
description:      (no language specified) There are two primary forms of citation in the Harvard style, dependent upon whether the reference is 
                  used as a noun or parenthetically. The citations themselves are in author-date style, with authors after 
                  the first suppressed in repeat citations.

                  The three original bibliography styles are agsm.bst (for Australian Government publications), dcu.bst 
                  (from the Design Computing Unit of the University of Sydney) and kluwer.bst (aiming at the format preferred 
                  in Kluwer publications).

                  This package is no longer recommended for use: the  harvard package for current LaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/harvard) should 
                  be used instead.

documentation:    Package outline (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/obsolete/biblio/bibtex/contrib/harvard/harvard.description
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/obsolete/biblio/bibtex/contrib/harvard
keyword:          bibtex-supp (BibTeX citation support)
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

hawkdraw -- Draw vector graphics using l3draw with a simple syntax
------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/hawkdraw
name:             hawkdraw
caption:          Draw vector graphics using l3draw with a simple syntax
author:           Jasper Habicht
copyright:        Jasper Habicht (2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.7.0 (2026-08-05)
last changes:     2026-08-05
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This LaTeX package allows the user to use a simple syntax similar to TikZ to generate vector graphic 
                  output based on  l3draw and related LaTeX3 modules such as l3fp which provides very precise 
                  calculations. The syntax is meant to be simple and flexible but also coherent and logical with the aim 
                  of allowing the user to quickly draw graphics. The package name relates to the quickness and agility 
                  of hawks and the preciseness of their eyesight.

                  The package intends to define a set of user-level commands that can be used for drawing simple graphics. 
                  It does not aim be a substitute for the TikZ package or to offer a similar scope of application.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/hawkdraw/README.md

hecthese -- A class for dissertations and theses at HEC Montréal

Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/hecthese
name:             hecthese

copyright:        HEC Montreal (2017-2023)

version:          3.0 (2026-04-20)
last changes:     2026-04-20
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package provides the  hecthese class, a class based on memoir (https://ctan.org/pkg/memoir) and 
                  compatible with LaTeX.

                  Using this class, postgraduate students at HEC Montréal will be able to write their dissertation or thesis 
                  while complying with all the presentation standards required by the University.

                  This class is meant to be as flexible as possible; in particular, there are very few hardcoded features 
                  except those that take care of the document’s layout.

                  Dissertations and theses at HEC Montréal can be written on a per-chapter or per-article basis. Documents 
                  that are written on a per-article basis require a bibliography for each of the included articles and 
                  a general bibliography for the entire document. The  hecthese class takes care of these requirements.

helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation -- Beautiful in-line microtonal just intonation accidentals
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation
name:             helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation
caption:          Beautiful in-line microtonal just intonation accidentals
author:           Thomas Nicholson
copyright:        Thomas Nicholson (2020)
license:          cc-by-4 = CC BY 4.0 (free)
version:          1.1 (2020-05-19)
last changes:     2020-05-19
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) The Helmholtz-Ellis JI Pitch Notation (HEJI), devised in the early 2000s by Marc Sabat and Wolfgang von 
                  Schweinitz, explicitly notates the raising and lowering of the  'untempered' diatonic Pythagorean 
                  notes by specific microtonal ratios defined for each prime. It provides visually distinctive “logos” 
                  distinguishing families of justly tuned intervals that relate to the harmonic series. These take the 
                  form of strings of additional accidental symbols based on historical precedents, extending the traditional 
                  sharps and flats. Since its 2020 update, HEJI ver. 2 (“HEJI2”) provides unique microtonal symbols through 
                  the 47-limit.

                  This package is a simple LaTeX implementation of HEJI2 that allows for in-line typesetting of microtonal 
                  accidentals for use within theoretical texts, program notes, symbol legends, etc.

                  Documents must be compiled using  XeLaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/xetex) .

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation/helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation.pdf
-- local file:    ./3935003203-helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation.pdf
home page:        https://plainsound.org/
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation
on MikTeX:        helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation
on TeXLive:       helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation
keyword:          font-otf (font in OpenType format)
keyword:          font (fonts themselves)

hepnames -- Pre-defined high energy particle names
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/hepnames
name:             hepnames
caption:          Pre-defined high energy particle names
author:           Andy Buckley
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          2.0
description:      (no language specified) Hepnames provides a pair of LaTeX packages, heppennames and hepnicenames, providing a large set of pre-defined 
                  high energy physics particle names built with the  hepparticles (https://ctan.org/pkg/hepparticles) package. 
                  The packages are based on pennames.sty by Michel Goossens and Eric van Herwijnen.

                  Heppennames re-implements the particle names in pennames.sty, with some additions and alterations and 
                  greater flexibility and robustness due to the hepparticles structures, which were written for this purpose.

                  Hepnicenames provides the main non-resonant particle names from heppennames with more “friendly” names.

hepparticles -- Macros for typesetting high energy physics particle names
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/hepparticles
name:             HEPparticles
caption:          Macros for typesetting high energy physics particle names
author:           Andy Buckley
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          2.0
description:      (no language specified) HEPparticles is a set of macros for typesetting high energy particle names, to meet the following criteria:

                  1. The main particle name is a Roman or Greek symbol, to be typeset in upright font in normal contexts.

                  2. Additionally a superscript and/or subscript may follow the main symbol.

                  3. Particle resonances may also have a resonance specifier which is typeset in parentheses following 
                  the main symbol. In general the parentheses may also be followed by sub- and superscripts.

                  4. The particle names are expected to be used both in and out of mathematical contexts.

                  5. If the surrounding text is bold or italic then the particle name should adapt to that contextas best 
                  as possible (this may not be possible for Greek symbols).

                  A consequence of point 5 is that the well-known problems with boldness of particle names in section titles, 
                  headers and tables of contents automatically disappear if these macros are used.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/hepparticles/hepparticles.pdf
-- local file:    ./6122553318-hepparticles.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/hepparticles/README
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/hepparticles
on MikTeX:        hepparticles
on TeXLive:       hepparticles
keyword:          physics (support for typesetting physics documents)

description:      (no language specified) The command  \hhline produces a line like \hline , or a double line like \hline\hline , 
                  except for its interaction with vertical lines. The command takes a preamble (rather like the preamble

hieroglf -- The “poor man's” Egyptian Hieroglyphic font
-------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/hieroglf
name:             hieroglf
caption:          The “poor man's” Egyptian Hieroglyphic font
author:           Peter R. Wilson
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.5
description:      (no language specified) The hieroglf bundle provides a Type 1 rendition of some of the ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs. Hieroglyphic 
                  writing was used between about 3000 BC and 400 AD.

                  The bundle is based on Serge Rosmorduc's comprehensive  hieroglyph (https://ctan.org/pkg/hieroglyph) package, 
                  but only provides about one tenth of his 650-odd hieroglyphs. Sufficient glyphs are provided for writing 
                  a few names like Cleopatra or Ptolomeny (together with cartouches) and some numbers, but the package 
                  is not for serious Egyptologists.

                  The bundle is part of a  set of archaic fonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/archaic) , and requires use 
                  of the oands (https://ctan.org/pkg/oands) fonts from that set.

version:          1.2
description:      (no language specified) The package provides citations according with the house style of the ‘Historische Zeitschrift’, a German 
                  historical journal. The scheme is a fullcite for the first citation and ‘Author, Shorttitle (as note 
                  N, P)’ for later citations (P being the page number). For further details, see the description of the 
                  house style at  the journal's site (https://www.oldenbourg.de/verlag/historische-zeitschrift/hz-richtlinien.htm) .

                  The package depends on BibLaTeX (version 3.3 or higher) as well as etoolbox (version 1.5 or higher).

hitex -- A TeX extension writing HINT output for on-screen reading
------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/hitex
alias:            HINT
name:             hitex
caption:          A TeX extension writing HINT output for on-screen reading
author:           Martin Ruckert
copyright:        Martin Ruckert (null)
license:          x11 = X11 License (free)
description:      (no language specified) An extension of TeX which generates HINT output.

                  The HINT file format is an alternative to the DVI and PDF formats which was designed specifically for 
                  on-screen reading of documents. Especially on mobile devices, reading DVI or PDF documents can be cumbersome. 
                  Mobile devices are available in a large variety of sizes but typically are not large enough to display 
                  documents formated for a4/letter-size paper. To compensate for the limitations of a small screen, users 
                  are used to alternating between landscape (few long lines) and portrait (more short lines) mode.

                  The HINT format supports variable and varying screen sizes, leveraging the ability of TeX to format a 
                  document for nearly-arbitrary values of  \hsize and \vsize .

documentation:    HiTeX documentation, in both PDF and HINT formats (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/systems/doc/hitex
documentation:    TUGboat articles by the author (no language specified): https://tug.org/TUGboat/Contents/listauthor.html#Ruckert,Martin
home page:        https://hint.userweb.mwn.de/
contact:          support: https://lists.tug.org/tex-k
contact:          bugs: https://lists.tug.org/tex-k
contact:          repository: https://tug.org/svn/texlive/trunk/Build/source/texk/web2c/hitexdir
contact:          development: https://github.com/ruckertm/HINT
on TeXLive:       hitex

                  defined a mechanism for concatenating multiple files into a single file for faster loading.

                  The disadvantage is that it introduces hard dependencies between the source files that are included and 
                  complicates distribution and updates.

                  It was principally used with  hyperref (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref) but is not currently used 
                  in any standard packages in TeX Live.

                  The packages are still distributed as simple stubs that reference the included packages via  \RequirePackage rather 
                  than copying their source.

                  The documented source of the original packages is available at  github (https://github.com/LaTeX-Package-Repositories/hobsub) , 
                  but is not distributed to CTAN.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/hobsub/README.md

hook-pre-commit-pkg -- Pre-commit git hook for LaTeX package developers
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/hook-pre-commit-pkg
name:             hook-pre-commit-pkg
caption:          Pre-commit git hook for LaTeX package developers
author:           Maïeul Rouquette
copyright:        Maïeul Rouquette (2014-2016)
license:          gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
version:          1.1.2
description:      (no language specified) This package provides a pre-commit git hook to check basic LaTeX syntax for the use of package developers.

                  It is installed by copying it into the  .git/.hooks file.

                  It then checks the following file types:  .sty , .dtx , .bbx , .cbx , and .lbx .

                  List of performed checks:

                  + Each line must be terminated by a  % , without a space before it. Empty lines are allowed, but 
                    not lines with nothing but spaces in them.
                  +  \begin{macro} and \end{macro} must be paired.
                  +  \begin{macrocode} and \end{macrocode} must be paired.
                  +  \begin{macro} must have a second argument.
                  + One space must be printed between  % and \begin{macro} or \end{macro} . % must 
                    be the first character in the line.
                  + Four spaces must be printed between  % and \begin{macrocode} or \end{macrocode} .
                  +  \cs argument must not start with a backslash.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/hook-pre-commit-pkg/README
documentation:    Tutorial (French): https://geekographie.maieul.net/Hook-de-pre-commit-pour-fichier
contact:          repository: https://github.com/maieul/git-hooks
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/hook-pre-commit-pkg
on TeXLive:       hook-pre-commit-pkg
keyword:          package-devel (support for package development)
year:             2016
language(s):      fr: French
last access:      2026-07-14

hrefhide -- Suppress hyper links when printing
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/hrefhide
name:             hrefhide
caption:          Suppress hyper links when printing
author:           Hans-Martin Münch
copyright:        H.-Martin Münch (2010-2025)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.1b (2025-01-27)
last changes:     2025-01-27
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This package provides the command  \hrefdisplayonly (additionally to \href provided by the 
                  hyperref package). While the (hyperlinked) text appears like an ordinary \href in the compiled 
                  pdf-file, the same text will be “hidden” when printing the text. Hiding is actually achieved by making 
                  the text the same colour as the background, thus preserving the layout of the rest of the text.

                  Further the commands  \hycon and \hycoff (hyper-colour-on/off) can be used to simulate switching 
                  option ocgcolorlinks of the hyperref package on and off.

                  This package is possibly obsolete, see section 3: “Alternatives” in the documentation.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/hrefhide/hrefhide.pdf

huaz -- Automatic Hungarian definite articles and suffixes
----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/huaz
name:             huaz
caption:          Automatic Hungarian definite articles and suffixes
author:           Tibor Tómács
copyright:        Tibor Tómács (2022-2026)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          3.0 (2026-02-02)
last changes:     2026-02-02
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) In Hungarian there are two definite articles, “a” and “az”, which are determined by the pronunciation 
                  of the subsequent word. The definite article is “az”, if the first phoneme of the pronounced word is 
                  a vowel, otherwise it is “a”. The  huaz package helps the user to insert automatically the correct 
                  definite article for cross-references and other commands containing text. Another service offered by 
                  the package is the automatic suffixing of numbers and cross-references, also based on their pronunciation.

hvdashln -- Horizontal and vertical dashed lines in arrays and tabulars
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/hvdashln
name:             hvdashln
caption:          Horizontal and vertical dashed lines in arrays and tabulars
author:           Hiroshi Nakashima
copyright:        Hiroshi Nakashima (1993, 1999)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
description:      (no language specified) Definitions of horizontal and vertical dashed lines for the array and tabular environment. Instead of 
                  building partial horizontal dashed lines using Isozaki's \cline{2-3}, \hdashline fills the full width. 
                  The proportion of the dashed line is defined by the two parameters: \hdashlinewidth=2pt and \hdashlinegap=2pt, 
                  where the former defines the width of the dash and the latter sets their gap.

                  Note that this functionality has been re-implemented, for current LaTeX, in the package  arydshln 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/arydshln) .

on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex209/contrib/misc/hvdashln.sty

-------------------------------------------

name:             hypcap
caption:          Adjusting the anchors of captions
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
author:           Heiko Oberdiek

copyright:        Oberdiek Package Support Group (2016-2024)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.13 (2024-07-26)
last changes:     2024-07-26
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) The package offers a solution to the problem that when you link to a float using  hyperref (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref) , 
                  the link anchors to below the float’s caption, rather than the beginning of the float.

                  Hypcap defines a separate  \capstart command, which you put where you want links to end; you should 
                  have a \capstart command for each \caption command. Package options can be used to auto-insert 
                  a \capstart at the start of a float environment.

caption:          A restricted LaTeX system that also produces HTML
author:           Otfried Cheong
author:           Tom Sgouros
copyright:        Otfried Cheong (1994-2002)
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          2.9
description:      (no language specified) HyperLaTeX defines a form of LaTeX that may be processed in the ordinary way with a  latex command, 
                  for printed output. However, HyperLaTeX documents may also be processed by the program hyperlatex to 
                  produce good-quality HTML.

                  HyperLaTeX is not a LaTeX to HTML converter (see, for example,  tth (https://ctan.org/pkg/tth) or latex2html 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex2html) for that). Rather, HyperLaTeX provides an environment where the 
                  author can prepare a document that may be converted to either print or HTML output.

                  and HTML backends.

                  The package is distributed with the  backref (https://ctan.org/pkg/backref) and nameref (https://ctan.org/pkg/nameref) packages, 
                  which make use of the facilities of hyperref.

                  The package depends on the author’s  kvoptions (https://ctan.org/pkg/kvoptions) , ltxcmds (https://ctan.org/pkg/ltxcmds) and refcount 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/refcount) packages.

hyperxmp -- Embed XMP metadata within a LaTeX document
------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperxmp
name:             hyperxmp
caption:          Embed XMP metadata within a LaTeX document
author:           Scott Pakin
copyright:        Scott Pakin (2011-2024)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          5.13
description:      (no language specified) XMP (eXtensible Metadata Platform) is a mechanism proposed by Adobe for embedding document metadata within 
                  the document itself. The metadata is designed to be easy to extract, even by programs that are oblivious 
                  to the document's file format. Most of Adobe's applications store  XMP metadata when saving files. 
                  Now, with the hyperxmp package, it is trivial for LaTeX document authors to store XMP metadata 
                  in their documents as well.

                  The package integrates seamlessly with  hyperref (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref) and requires virtually 
                  no modifications to documents that already exploit hyperref's mechanisms for specifying PDF metadata. 
                  The current version of hyperxmp can embed the following metadata as XMP : title, authors, primary 
                  author's title or position, metadata writer, subject/summary, keywords, copyright, license URL, document 
                  base URL, document identifier and instance identifier, language, source file name, PDF generating tool, 
                  PDF version, and contact telephone number/postal address/email address/URL. Hyperxmp currently embeds XMP only 
                  within PDF documents; it is compatible with pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX, LaTeX+dvipdfm, and LaTeX+dvips+ps2pdf.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/hyperxmp/hyperxmp.pdf

hyph-utf8 -- Hyphenation patterns expressed in UTF-8
----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/hyph-utf8
name:             hyph-utf8
caption:          Hyphenation patterns expressed in UTF-8
author:           Manuel Pégourié-Gonnard
author:           Mojca Miklavec
author:           Khaled Hosny
author:           Arthur Rosendahl
author:           Élie Roux
copyright:        TeX Users Group (2008-2025)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          (2026-02-21)
last changes:     2026-02-21
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) Modern native UTF-8 engines such as XeTeX and LuaTeX need hyphenation patterns in UTF-8 format, whereas 
                  older systems require hyphenation patterns in the 8-bit encoding of the font in use (such encodings are 
                  codified in the  LaTeX scheme (https://ctan.org/pkg/encguide) with names like OT1, T2A, TS1, OML, 
                  LY1, etc).

                  The present package offers a collection of conversions of existing patterns to UTF-8 format, together 
                  with converters for use with 8-bit fonts in older systems. Since hyphenation patterns for Knuthian-style 
                  TeX systems are only read at iniTeX time, it is hoped that the UTF-8 patterns, with their converters, 
                  will completely supplant the older patterns.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/hyph-utf8/README.md
documentation:    Main documentation for hyph-utf8 (English): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/hyph-utf8/doc/hyph-utf8.pdf

contact:          repository: https://github.com/hyphenation/tex-hyphen
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/hyph-utf8

                  re-coded.

                  editing and production. Further information on this workflow can be found in two articles that were published 
                  by the authors:

                  +  Lowering the Cost of Diamond Open Access Journals (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10424) ,
                  +  A LaTeX publishing workflow (https://tug.org/TUGboat/tb46-3/tb144bos-workflow.html)

author:           Dennis Chen

last changes:     2021-07-22

description:      (no language specified) This package allows you to check whether a string is contained within another set of strings, and perform 
                  an action if it is not. This is done by using the  allfalse environment and passing in a string

author:           Martin Scharrer
author:           The LaTeX Project Team

license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.3 (2019-10-25)
last changes:     2019-10-25
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) The package provides the switch  \ifetex which indicates whether e-TeX is available or not.

                  The package can be loaded as LaTeX package using  \usepackage{ifetex} or in plain TeX using \input 
                  ifetex . In either case it aborts silently if the \ifetex macro is already defined.

                  The package’s test is whether  \eTeXversion is defined as a primitive; if it is, the package assumes 
                  e-TeX features are available.

                  Please note, that  ifetex is now part of iftex (https://ctan.org/pkg/iftex) .

ifnextok -- Utility macro: peek ahead without ignoring spaces
-------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/ifnextok
name:             ifnextok
caption:          Utility macro: peek ahead without ignoring spaces
author:           Uwe Lück
copyright:        Uwe Lück (2011)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.3
description:      (no language specified) The package deals with the behaviour of the LaTeX internal command  \@ifnextchar , which skips 
                  blank spaces. This has the potential to surprise users, since it can produce really unwanted effects. 
                  A common example occurs with brackets starting a line following \\ : the command looks for an optional 
                  argument, whereas the user wants the brackets to be printed.

                  The package offers commands and options for modifying this behaviour, maybe limited to certain parts 
                  of the document source.

---------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/ifplatform
name:             ifplatform
caption:          Conditionals to test which platform is being used
author:           Will Robertson
author:           Johannes Große
copyright:        Will Robertson and Johannes Große (2007-2017)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.4a (2017-10-13)
last changes:     2017-10-13
year:             2017
description:      (no language specified) This package uses the (La)TeX extension  -shell-escape to establish whether the document is being 
                  processed on a Windows or on a Unix-like system (Mac OS X, Linux, etc.), or on Cygwin (Unix environment 
                  over a windows system).

                  Booleans provided are:

                  +  \ifwindows ,
                  +  \iflinux ,
                  +  \ifmacosx and
                  +  \ifcygwin .
The package also preserves the output of  uname on a Unix-like system, which may be used to distinguish 
                  between various classes of Unix systems.

igo -- Fonts and macro to typeset Go diagrams
---------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/igo
name:             igo
caption:          Fonts and macro to typeset Go diagrams
author:           Étienne Dupuis
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.62
description:      (no language specified) This package is based on the package  go (https://ctan.org/pkg/go) written in 1991 by Hanna Kołodziejska 
                  which provides typesetting facilities for Go games and positions. Although igo contains roughly the same 
                  commands as the original package and uses the fonts created by Kołodziejska, it has been improved in 
                  a number of ways. It uses command names less likely to conflict with standard AMS packages. It allows 
                  different board sizes to be used. It understands a standardized notation for board coordinates. And it 
                  provides a facility to work on more than one board. Moreover, a few commands were reworked to define 
                  positions or game sequences more conveniently.

iitem -- Multiple level of lists in one list-like environment
-------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/iitem

caption:          Multiple level of lists in one list-like environment
author:           Ben Vitecek
copyright:        Ben Vitecek (2013)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) The package defines multiple level lists within one list-like environment. instead of writing  |
\begin{enumerate}
\item 1
\begin{enumerate}
\item 2
\begin{enumerate}
\item 3
\begin{enumerate}
\item 4
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\item 2.1
\end{enumerate}
\item 1.1
\begin{enumerate}
\item 2
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
| this package allows you to write |
\begin{enumerate}
\item 1
\iitem 2
\iiitem 3
\ivtem 4
\iitem 2.1
\item 1.1
\iitem 2
\end{enumerate}
|

description:      (no language specified) Impose is used for two-up printing of DSC-compliant PostScript (including that from Netscape, dvips, 
                  and FrameMaker). It makes an effort to remove white space from the printout by probing the original PostScript 
                  for the bounding box of the printed area. This makes the output much more aesthetically satisfying than 
                  does a simple layout of non-cropped original pages.

                  of \index (abbreviated _{word} ) that prints the word being indexed, as well as creating 
                  an index entry for it.

inlinedef -- Inline expansions within definitions
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/inlinedef
name:             inlinedef
caption:          Inline expansions within definitions
author:           Stephen Hicks
copyright:        Stephen D. Hicks (2008)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) The package provides a macro  \Inline that precedes a \def or \gdef . Within the definition 
                  text of an inlined definition, keywords such as \Expand may be used to selectively inline certain 
                  expansions at definition-time. This eases the process of redefining macros in terms of the original definition, 
                  as well as definitions in which the token that must be expanded is deep within, where \expandafter would 
                  be difficult and \edef is not suitable. Another application is as an easier version of \aftergroup , 
                  by defining a macro in terms of expanded local variables, then ending the group with \expandafter\endgroup\macro .

description:      (no language specified) This package optionally modifies four aspects of TeX’s automatic math formatting to improve typesetting:

                  right delimiters in certain situations; and (4) it forces \left and \right delimiters to

inputtrc -- Trace which file loads which

author:           Uwe Lück
copyright:        Uwe Lück (2010)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.3
description:      (no language specified) The package produces screen/log messages of the form ‘&lt;current&gt; INPUTTING &lt;next&gt;’ reporting 
                  LaTeX input commands (&lt;current&gt; and &lt;next&gt; being file names). The message is indented to 
                  reflect the level of input nesting.

                  Tracing may be turned on and off, and the unit of indentation may be adjusted.

                  The implementation somewhat resembles those of packages  FiNK (https://ctan.org/pkg/fink) and inputfile 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/inputfile) .

author:            N. N.
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) The  interlinear package facilitates the creation of interlinear glossed texts, commonly used in 
                  linguistic examples. It is based on the gb4e (https://ctan.org/pkg/gb4e) package and builds upon 
                  its functionality to provide enhanced features. It offers extensive customization options, allowing users 
                  to control font styles, formatting, and layout. With predefined styles and margin note customization, interlinear provides 
                  a flexible solution for presenting linguistic data.

interpol -- Add interpolation to MetaPost graph package
-------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/interpol
name:             interpol
caption:          Add interpolation to MetaPost graph package
author:           Ulrik Vieth
license:          noinfo = noinfo 
version:          1.04
description:      (no language specified) This file declares a new internal quantity interpolating and modifies the  augment and Mreadpath routines 
                  of the MetaPost graph package (part of the base MetaPost distribution (https://ctan.org/pkg/metapost) ) 
                  to construct a path from data points using Bezier curves instead of polygons (line segments) when interpolating is 
                  set positive.

                  Use of this feature can lead to severe distortions if the data isn't suitable. Its usefulness may best 
                  be seen when plotting smooth functions evaluated numerically at discrete intervals.

on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/metapost/contrib/macros/misc/interpol.mp

interpreter -- Translate input files on the fly
-----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/interpreter
name:             interpreter
caption:          Translate input files on the fly
author:           Paul Isambert
author:           Yuri Robbers
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.2
description:      (no language specified) The package preprocesses input files to a Lua(La)TeX run, on the fly.

                  The user defines Lua regular expressions to search for patterns and modify input lines (or entire paragraphs) 
                  accordingly, before TeX reads the material. In this way, documents may be prepared in a non-TeX language 
                  (e.g., some lightweight markup language) and turned into ‘proper’ TeX for processing.

                  The source of the documentation is typed in such a lightweight language and is thus easily readable in 
                  a text editor (the PDF file is also available, of course); the transformation to TeX syntax via Interpreter’s 
                  functions is explained in the documentation itself.

                  Interpreter is implemented using the author’s  gates (https://ctan.org/pkg/gates) (Lua version), 
                  and works for plain TeX and LaTeX, but not ConTeXt.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/generic/interpreter/interpreter-doc.pdf
-- local file:    ./1163267054-interpreter-doc.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/generic/interpreter/README
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/generic/interpreter
on MikTeX:        interpreter
on TeXLive:       interpreter
keyword:          macro-supp (support for development of (La)TeX macros)
