interval -- Format mathematical intervals, ensuring proper spacing
------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/interval
name:             interval
caption:          Format mathematical intervals, ensuring proper spacing
author:           Lars Madsen
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.4 (2019-03-06)
last changes:     2019-03-06
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) When typing an open interval as  $]a,b[$ , a closing bracket is being used in place of an opening 
                  fence and vice versa. This leads to the wrong spacing in, say, $]-a,b[$ or $A\in]a,b[=B$ . The 
                  package attempts to solve this using:
 \interval{a}{b} -&gt; [a,b] 
 \interval[open]{a}{b} -&gt; ]a,b[ 
 \interval[open 
                  left]{a}{b} -&gt; ]a,b] 

                  The package also supports fence scaling and ensures that the enclosing fences will end up having the 
                  proper closing and opening types. TeX maths does not do this job properly.

                  The package depends on  pgfkeys (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgfkeys) .

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/interval/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/interval/interval.pdf
-- local file:    ./5835699529-interval.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/interval
on MikTeX:        interval
on TeXLive:       interval
keyword:          paren-mgmt (match and otherwise manage parentheses)
keyword:          maths (support for typesetting mathematics)
keyword:          tagged-pdf (tagged PDF compatible)
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

intexgral -- A LaTeX package for typesetting integrals
------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/intexgral
name:             intexgral
caption:          A LaTeX package for typesetting integrals
author:           Valentin Dao
copyright:        Valentin Dao (2025-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          4.1.1 (2026-08-01)
last changes:     2026-08-01
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) Typesetting integrals, although common in LaTeX, is not particularly practical. The way in which the 
                  different parts are managed often generates unreadable source code, making modifications laborious. The 
                  package therefore follows a simple philosophy: focus on the essential element of an integral, the integrand. 
                  Everything else (limits, differentials, symbols) can be modified using keys. These keys are designed 
                  to allow you to easily and quickly change the style of an integral. Additionally, the package provides 
                  various auxiliary macros to support some keys which can have lengthy inputs.

documentation:    Package documentation (French): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/intexgral/intexgral-fr.pdf

ionumbers -- Restyle numbers in maths mode
------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/ionumbers
name:             ionumbers
caption:          Restyle numbers in maths mode
author:           Christian Schneider
copyright:        Christian Schneider (2007-2009, 2011, 2012, 2014)
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          0.3.3 (2014-04-06)
last changes:     2014-04-06
year:             2014
description:      (no language specified) ‘ ionumbers ’ stands for ‘input/output numbers’.

                  The package restyles numbers in maths mode. If a number in the input file is written, e.g., as  $3,231.44$ as 
                  commonly used in English texts, the package is able to restyle it to be output as $3\,231{,}44$ as 
                  commonly used in German texts (and vice versa). This may be useful, for example, if you have a large 
                  table and want to include it in texts with different output conventions without the need to change the 
                  table.

                  The package can also automatically group digits left of the decimal separator (thousands) and right of 
                  the decimal separator (thousandths) in triplets without the need of specifying commas (English) or points 
                  (German) as separators. E.g., the input  $1234.567890$ can be output as $1\,234.\,567\,890$ .

                  Finally, an  e starts the exponent of the number. For example, $21e6$ may be output as $26\times10\,^{6}$ .

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ionumbers/ionumbers.pdf
-- local file:    ./4900777505-ionumbers.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ionumbers/README
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ionumbers
on MikTeX:        ionumbers
on TeXLive:       ionumbers
keyword:          numbers (formatting numbers, etc)
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

                  outlined in the Iran Manual of Style (https://imos.irandoc.ac.ir) (1st edn., 2016)—citation guide 
                  to Persian, and English information sources.

                  A collection of illustrative examples showcasing the usage of this package has been meticulously prepared 
                  and is accessible in  the package’s GitHub repository (https://github.com/farshadrasuli/iran-bibtex) under 
                  the ‘examples’ sub-directory.

                  To facilitate alphabetical sorting of references, prioritizing Persian/Farsi items ahead of English/Latin 
                  ones, a dedicated file named  iran-bibtex-cp1256fa.csf is provided for use with this package. This 
                  file, derived from the ascii.csf (https://mirrors.ctan.org/biblio/bibtex/bibtex-x/csf/ascii.csf) file, 
                  serves the purpose of arranging references in the desired order.

                  It is important to note that this package relies on the  natbib (https://ctan.org/pkg/natbib) package, 
                  which is automatically loaded.

isodate -- Tune the output format of dates according to language
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/isodate
name:             isodate
caption:          Tune the output format of dates according to language
author:           Harald Harders
copyright:        Harald Harders (2000-2005)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          2.28
description:      (no language specified) This package provides ten output formats of the commands  \today , \printdate , \printdateTeX , 
                  and \daterange (partly language dependent).

                  Formats available are: ISO (yyyy-mm-dd), numeric (e.g. dd.\,mm.~yyyy), short (e.g. dd.\,mm.\,yy), TeX 
                  (yyyy/mm/dd), original (e.g. dd. mmm yyyy), short original (e.g. dd. mmm yy), as well as numerical formats 
                  with Roman numerals for the month.

                  The commands  \printdate and \printdateTeX print any date. The command \daterange prints 
                  a date range and leaves out unnecessary year or month entries.

                  This package supports German (old and new rules), Austrian, US English, British English, French, Danish, 
                  Swedish, and Norwegian.

license:          noinfo = noinfo 
version:          0.9
description:      (no language specified) The package represents an outdated mechanism for reading ISO Latin-1 (ISO/IEC 8859-1) by means of setting 
                  the printing glyphs in the upper half of the character set to category code “active”, and defining them 
                  all.

                  While this mechanism is broadly that employed by the standard LaTeX  inputenc (https://ctan.org/pkg/inputenc) package, 
                  the standard package has several advantages, including a more satisfactory approach to undefined character 
                  codes, better integration with other input encodings and generally improved robustness.

issuulinks -- Produce external links instead of internal ones
-------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/issuulinks
name:             issuulinks
caption:          Produce external links instead of internal ones
author:           Boris Veytsman
copyright:        Boris Veytsman (2012)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.1
description:      (no language specified) The PDF visualizer  http://issuu.com/ISSUU is a popular service which shows PDF documents “a page 
                  a time”. Due to the way it is implemented, internal links in these documents are not allowed. Instead, 
                  they must be converted to external ones in the form http://issuu.com/action/page?page=PAGENUMBER .

                  The package patches hyperref to produce external links in the required form instead of internal links 
                  created by  \ref , \cite and other commands.

                  Since the package redefines the internals of  hyperref (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref) , it must 
                  be loaded it AFTER hyperref.

description:      (no language specified) This LaTeX package provides macros based on TikZ to draw a game tree. The main idea underlying its core 
                  macros is the completion of a whole tree by using a sequence of simple ‘parent-child’ tree structures,

                  The ‘ist’ prefix stands for “it’s a simple tree” or “In-Sung’s simple tree.”

                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/kurier) typeface, which was designed in 1975 for a diploma in typeface design 
                  at the Warsaw Academy of Fine Arts under the supervision of Roman Tomaszewski.

                  latin (including Vietnamese), Cyrillic and Greek as well as a number of additional symbols (including 
                  mathematical symbols). The fonts are prepared in Type 1 and OpenType formats. For use with TeX the following 
                  encoding files have been prepared: T1 (ec), T2 (abc), and OT2—Cyrillic, T5 (Vietnamese), OT4, QX, texansi 
                  and nonstandard (IL2 for the Czech fonts), as well as supporting macros and files defining fonts for 
                  LaTeX.

jabref -- Graphical frontend to manage BibTeX databases
-------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/jabref
name:             jabref
caption:          Graphical frontend to manage BibTeX databases
author:           Nizar Batada
author:           The JabRef Project
author:           Morten Alver
author:           Oliver Kopp
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          5.15
description:      (no language specified) JabRef is a graphical frontend to manage  BibTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) (and BibLaTeX 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex) ) databases having BibTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) as internal 
                  format. It offers quality checks for entries; fetching complete bibliographic information based on ISBN, 
                  DOI, PubMed-ID and arXiv-ID; searching across many online scientific catalogues such as CiteSeer, CrossRef, 
                  Google Scholar, IEEEXplore, INSPIRE-HEP, Medline PubMed, MathSciNet, Springer, arXiv, and zbMATH.

                  It allows for grouping entries (and storing the group information in the  .bib file itself), advancing 
                  searching and filtering, finding duplicate entries, attaching and renaming PDFs (e.g., according to the BibTeX 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) key), and generating BibTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) keys.

                  Since JabRef fully relies on  BibTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) , additional information such 
                  as ranking, priority, printed-flag, and quality-assured-flag are stored in the BibTeX entry in the .bib file 
                  itself.

jeopardy -- Build a jeopardy game in LaTeX
------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/jeopardy
name:             jeopardy
caption:          Build a jeopardy game in LaTeX
author:           Robert Mařík
copyright:        Robert Mařík (2004)
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          1.1a
description:      (no language specified) The jeopardy package allows to build a jeopardy game with pdfLaTeX. It is based on the  jj_game (http://www.math.uakron.edu/~dpstory/jj_game.html) class 
                  and exerquiz (https://ctan.org/pkg/exerquiz) package, written by D. P. Story. The author of the 
                  game can use multichoice questions or fill-in questions. The answer for fill-in questions is either a 
                  mathematical formula or text string (see the documentation of exerquiz and \RespBoxMath and \RespBoxTxt commands 
                  to learn more about the capabilities). JavaScripts are written to record the score. If the score is greater 
                  than a given value, a hidden string is shown. The user should use the style with some screen presentation 
                  package, such as web (https://ctan.org/pkg/acrotex-web) .

                  The package is distributed with some example games, including both 1- and 2-player games.

                    to the  vftovp / vptovf programs.
                  + The mutual conversion between VF files alone and files in the “ZVP0 format”, which is a subset of the 
                    ZVP format.

description:      (no language specified) JLM is an advanced LaTeX mode for the  Jed (https://www.jedsoft.org/jed) editor. Its aim is to 
                  help the user by taking over annoying and stupid things that need to be done, like adding \usepackage 
                  when you add a command or environment from this package, or placing dollar signs around mathematical 
                  commands and move the cursor to an appropriate point.

                  JLM does not think for you. If you want a tabular but insert an itemize, JLM doesn't prevent this. So, 
                  you should be familiar with LaTeX and know what environments and commands are, and where to place them 
                  in a document; JLM is there to help writing them.

jmsdelim -- A package for compositional delimiter sizing
--------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/jmsdelim
name:             jmsdelim
caption:          A package for compositional delimiter sizing
author:           Jonathan Sterling
copyright:        Jonathan Sterling (2022)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.2.0
description:      (no language specified) Correctly sizing delimiters is very difficult, particularly in well-architected documents: a correctly 
                  engineered mathematical document will include macros for all operations, and these macros necessarily 
                  will include delimiters (such as parentheses). However, the correct size for the delimiter cannot be 
                  chosen ahead of time, because it will depend on the arguments; two options are available:

                  * Provide optional arguments to each notation macro for choosing delimiter sizes. This is nearly intractable 
                     to do in practice.
                  * Ignore delimiter sizes.
With jmsdelim we offer an alternative: the correct delimiter sizes can be set at the leaf nodes of a 
                  mathematical expression, and magically bubble upward through the delimiters.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): pkg:/jmsdelim.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): pkg:/README.md
home page:        https://github.com/jonsterling/latex3-jmsdelim
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/jonsterling/latex3-jmsdelim/issues/6
contact:          repository: https://github.com/jonsterling/latex3-jmsdelim
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/jmsdelim
on TeXLive:       jmsdelim
keyword:          maths (support for typesetting mathematics)
year:             2022
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

jpeg2ps -- Convert JPEG files to PostScript Level 2 or 3 EPS
------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/jpeg2ps
name:             jpeg2ps
caption:          Convert JPEG files to PostScript Level 2 or 3 EPS
author:           Thomas Merz
copyright:        Thomas Merz (1994-1999)
license:          nosell = Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement (not free)
version:          1.8
description:      (no language specified) Converts JPEG files to PostScript Level 2 or 3 EPS. In fact, jpeg2ps is not really a converter but a 
                  “wrapper”: it reads the image parameters (width, height, number of color components) in a JPEG file, 
                  writes the according EPS header and then copies the compressed JPEG data to the output file. Decompression 
                  is done by the PostScript interpreter (only PostScript Level 2 and 3 interpreters support JPEG compression 
                  and decompression).

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/jpeg2ps/jpeg2ps.txt

jurabib -- Extended BibTeX citation support for the humanities and legal texts
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/jurabib
name:             jurabib
caption:          Extended BibTeX citation support for the humanities and legal texts
author:           Jens Berger
copyright:        Jens Berger (1999-2004)
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          0.6
description:      (no language specified) This package enables automated citation with BibTeX for legal studies and the humanities. In addition, 
                  the package provides commands for specifying editors in a commentary in a convenient way. Simplified 
                  formatting of the citation as well as the bibliography entry is also provided. It is possible to display 
                  the (short) title of a work only if an authors is cited with multiple works. Giving a full citation in 
                  the text, conforming to the bibliography entry, is supported. Several options are provided which might 
                  be of special interest for those outside legal studies—for instance, displaying multiple full citations. 
                  In addition, the format of last names and first names of authors may be changed easily. Cross references 
                  to other footnotes are possible. Language dependent handling of bibliography entries is possible by the 
                  special language field.

author:           Adam Zahumensky
license:          bsd = BSD Style License (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) The package provides a kana parser for LuaTeX. It is a set of 4 macros that handle transliteration of 
                  text:

                  * from hiragana and katakana to Latin
                  * from Latin and katakana to hiragana
                  * from Latin and hiragana to katakana
It can be used to write kana directly using only the ASCII character set or for education purposes. The 
                  package has support for obsolete and rarely used syllables, some only accessible via the provided toggle 
                  macro.

kdpcover -- Covers for books published by Kindle Direct Publishing
------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/kdpcover
name:             kdpcover
caption:          Covers for books published by Kindle Direct Publishing
author:           Yegor Bugayenko
copyright:        Yegor Bugayenko (2021-2026)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          0.7.0 (2026-05-28)
last changes:     2026-05-28
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The problem this class solves is  the necessity (https://kdp.amazon.com/en_US/help/topic/G201953020) to 
                  change the size of the cover PDF according to the number of pages in the book — the bigger the book, 
                  the larger the spine of the book must be. The provided class makes the necessary calculations on-the-fly, 
                  using the qpdf tool. Obviously, you need to have it installed. Also, you must run pdflatex with 
                  the --shell-escape option, in order to allow LaTeX to run qpdf .

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/kdpcover/README.md

kerntest -- Print tables and generate control files to adjust kernings
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/kerntest
name:             kerntest
caption:          Print tables and generate control files to adjust kernings
author:           Harald Harders
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.32
description:      (no language specified) This class makes it easy to generate tables that show many different kerning pairs of an arbitrary font, 
                  usable by LaTeX. It shows the kerning values that are used in the font by default.

                  In addition, this class enables the user to alter the kernings and to observe the results. Kerning pairs 
                  can be defined for groups of similar glyphs at the same time. An mtx file is generated automatically. 
                  The mtx file may then be loaded by  fontinst (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontinst) to introduce the user-made 
                  kernings into the virtual font for later use in LaTeX.

keyfloat -- Provides a key/value interface for generating floats
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/keyfloat
name:             keyfloat
caption:          Provides a key/value interface for generating floats
author:           Brian Dunn
copyright:        Brian Dunn (2016-2024)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.09
description:      (no language specified) The keyfloat package provides a key/value user interface for quickly creating figures with a single image 
                  each, figures with arbitrary contents, tables, subfloats, rows of floats, floats located [H]ere, floats 
                  in the [M]argin, and floats with text [W]rapped around them. 

                  Key/value combinations may specify 
                  a caption and label, a width proportional to \linewidth, a fixed width and/or height, rotation, scaling, 
                  a tight or loose frame, an \arraystretch, a continued float, additional supplemental text, and an artist/author's 
                  name with automatic index entry. When used with the tocdata package, the name also appears in the List 
                  of Figures.

                  Floats may be placed into a row environment, and are typeset to fit within the 
                  given number of columns, continuing to the next row if necessary. Nested sub-rows may be used to generate 
                  layouts such as two small figures placed vertically next to one larger figure.

                  Subfloats are 
                  supported by two environments.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/keyfloat/README.txt

knuth-hint -- HINT collection of typeset C/WEB sources in TeX Live
------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/knuth-hint
name:             knuth-hint
caption:          HINT collection of typeset C/WEB sources in TeX Live
author:           Andreas Scherer
license:          knuth = Knuth License (free)
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
version:          2.7 (2026-03-02)
last changes:     2026-03-02
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The  knuth-hint package contains the large collection of HINT documents for many of the CWEB amd 
                  WEB sources of programs in the TeX Live distribution (and, for technical reasons, a PDF document for 
                  XeTeX). Each program is presented in its original form as written by the respective authors, and in the 
                  “changed” form as used in TeX Live. Care has been taken to keep the section numbering intact, so that 
                  you can study the codes and the changes in parallel. Also included are the “errata” for Donald Knuth’s 
                  “Computers &amp; Typesetting”.

                  HINT is the dynamic document format created by Martin Ruckert’s HiTeX engine that was added to TeX Live 
                  2022. The HINT files can be viewed on Linux, Windows, and Android with the hintview application. The 
                  knuth-hint package is a showcase of HiTeX’s capabilities.

                  Knuth created. The central entry point is the “index” file, with links to the individual documents, either 
                  in HTML or in PDF format.

koma-script -- A bundle of versatile classes and packages
---------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script
name:             koma-script
caption:          A bundle of versatile classes and packages
author:           Markus Kohm
copyright:        Markus Kohm (1994-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          3.49.2 (2026-02-02)
last changes:     2026-02-02
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The KOMA-Script bundle provides replacements for the  article (https://ctan.org/pkg/scrartcl) , report 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/scrreprt) , and book (https://ctan.org/pkg/scrbook) classes with emphasis 
                  on typography and versatility. There is also a letter class (https://ctan.org/pkg/scrlttr2) .

                  The bundle also offers:

                  + a  package for calculating type areas (https://ctan.org/pkg/typearea) in the way laid down by the 
                    typographer Jan Tschichold,
                  + packages for easily changing and defining page styles,
                  + a package  scrdate (https://ctan.org/pkg/scrdate) for getting not only the current date but also 
                    the name of the day, and
                  + a package  scrtime (https://ctan.org/pkg/scrtime) for getting the current time.
All these packages may be used not only with KOMA-Script classes but also with the standard classes.

                  Since every package has its own version number, the version number quoted only refers to the version 
                  of  scrbook , scrreprt , scrartcl , scrlttr2 and typearea (which are the 
                  main parts of the bundle).

                  related documents, such as cover letters and cover sheets for job applications. Concretely, the bundle 
                  consists of three packages: komacv-addons, komacv-lco, and komacv-multilang.

                    documents;

                    via babel or polyglossia.

konwerter -- A program for automatic numbering of compounds in chemical publications
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/konwerter
name:             konwerter
caption:          A program for automatic numbering of compounds in chemical publications
author:           Piotr Wawrzyniak
copyright:        Piotr Wawrzyniak (2005-2008)
license:          gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
version:          0.2.4
description:      (no language specified) Konwerter automatically numbers compounds in chemical publications created by  LaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex) . 
                  It is written in C++ and works both in Unix and Windows operating systems. It works similar to LaTeX \label and \ref commands. 
                  Instead of giving number to every compound you give them labels and then refer to the structure in the 
                  text using the same label. The konwerter is able to resolve labels to numbers both in the eps files and 
                  in the text.

kpfonts -- A complete set of fonts for text and mathematics
-----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/kpfonts
name:             kpfonts
caption:          A complete set of fonts for text and mathematics
author:           Christophe Caignaert
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          3.36 (2024-10-27)
last changes:     2024-10-27
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) The family contains text fonts in roman, sans-serif and monospaced shapes, with true small caps and old-style 
                  numbers; the package offers full support of the textcomp package. The mathematics fonts include all the 
                  AMS fonts, in both normal and bold weights.

                  Each of the font types is available in two main versions: default and ‘light’. Each version is available 
                  in four variants: default; oldstyle numbers; oldstyle numbers with old ligatures such as ct and st, and 
                  long-tailed capital Q; and veryoldstyle with long s. Other variants include small caps as default or 
                  ‘large small caps’, and for mathematics both upright and slanted shapes for Greek letters, as well as 
                  default and narrow versions of multiple integrals.

                  The fonts were originally derived from URW Palladio (with URW’s agreement) though the fonts are very 
                  clearly different in appearance from their parent.

documentation:    Package documentation (English): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/kpfonts/doc/kpfonts.pdf
-- local file:    ./8400283586-kpfonts.pdf
documentation:    Summary of features (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/kpfonts/doc/kpfonts-abstract.pdf
-- local file:    ./1128923238-kpfonts-abstract.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/kpfonts/README.txt
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/kpfonts

kpfonts-otf -- OpenType versions of the kpfonts (Type1) designed by Christophe Caignaert
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/kpfonts-otf
name:             kpfonts-otf
caption:          OpenType versions of the kpfonts (Type1) designed by Christophe Caignaert
author:           Daniel Flipo
copyright:        Daniel Flipo (2020-2026)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
license:          ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
version:          0.73 (2026-03-06)
last changes:     2026-03-06
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This bundle provides OpenType versions of the Type1 Kp-fonts designed by Christophe Caignaert. It is 
                  usable with LuaTeX or XeTeX engines only.

                  It consists of sixteen Text fonts (eight Serif, four Sans-Serif, four Monotype) and six Math fonts.

                  Serif and Sans-Serif families have small caps available in two sizes (SmallCaps and PetitesCaps), upper 
                  and lowercase digits, real superscripts and subscripts; ancient ligatures (ct and st), ancient long-s 
                  and a long-tailed capital Q are available via font features.

                  Math fonts cover all usual symbols including AMS’; a full list of available symbols is provided, see 
                  the ‘List of glyphs’.

ktbox -- Framework for semantic color, structured highlighting, and scholarly communication 
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/ktbox
name:             KTBox
caption:          Framework for semantic color, structured highlighting, and scholarly communication
author:           Bhaskar Mangal
copyright:        Bhaskar Mangal (2025)
license:          apache2 = Apache License, version 2.0 (free)
version:          0.0.1
description:      (no language specified) KTBox is a modular LaTeX framework that introduces semantic color palettes, structured highlight boxes, 
                  and ORCID-linked author utilities for scholarly writing. The package is composed of three lightweight 
                  and independent style files:

                  +  'ktbox.sty' – defines highlight boxes (standard, numbered, wide) with semantic theming.
                  +  'ktcolor.sty' – provides semantic color palettes with light and dark modes.
                  +  'ktorcid.sty' – adds ORCID-linked author commands and icons.
The framework separates structure from style, ensuring compatibility with major classes such as  IEEEtran 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/ieeetran) , acmart (https://ctan.org/pkg/acmart) , article (https://ctan.org/pkg/article) , beamer 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer) , and ICLR. Features include numbered key-takeaway boxes, wide-format 
                  environments for emphasis, multi-column layouts, and dual light/dark themes. KTBox aims to improve clarity, 
                  portability, and reproducibility in academic publishing across articles, posters, and presentations.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ktbox/README.md

kurier -- A two-element sans-serif typeface
-------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/kurier
name:             kurier
caption:          A two-element sans-serif typeface
author:           Janusz Marian Nowacki
copyright:        Janusz M. Nowacki (1998-2010)
license:          gfl = The GUST Font License (GFL) (free)
version:          0.995b
description:      (no language specified) Kurier is a two-element sans-serif typeface. It was designed for a diploma in typeface design at the 
                  Warsaw Academy of Fine Arts under the supervision of Roman Tomaszewski.

                  This distribution contains a significantly extended set of characters covering the following modern alphabets: 
                  latin (including Vietnamese), Cyrillic and Greek as well as a number of additional symbols (including 
                  mathematical symbols). The fonts are prepared in Type 1 and OpenType formats. For use with TeX the following 
                  encoding files have been prepared: T1 (ec), T2 (abc), and OT2—Cyrillic, T5 (Vietnamese), OT4, QX, texansi 
                  and—nonstandard (IL2 for the Czech fonts), as well as supporting macros and files defining fonts for 
                  LaTeX.

l3regex -- Regular expression facilities for LaTeX
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/l3regex
name:             l3regex
caption:          Regular expression facilities for LaTeX
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
copyright:        The LaTeX3 Project (2011-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          (2026-04-28)
last changes:     2026-04-28
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package provides regular expression testing, extraction of submatches, splitting, and replacement, 
                  all acting on token lists. The syntax of regular expressions is mostly a subset of the PCRE syntax (and 
                  is very close to Posix), with some additions arising from the fact that TeX manipulates tokens rather 
                  than characters.

                  For performance reasons, only a limited set of features are implemented. Notably, back-references are 
                  not supported.

version:          (2024-04-08)
last changes:     2024-04-08
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) The  l3sys-query script provides a method for TeX runs to obtain system information via shell escape 
                  to Lua. The facilities are more limited than the similar Java script texosquery (https://ctan.org/pkg/texosquery) , 
                  but since it uses Lua, l3sys-query can be used out of the box; with any installed TeX system.

                  The script is written taking account of TeX Live security requirements; it is therefore suitable for 
                  use with restricted shell escape, the standard setting when installing a TeX system.

                  The supported queries are

                  
                  +  ls :Directory listing supporting a range of options
                  +  pwd :Obtaining details of the current working directory

lametex -- A PostScript translator for a subset of LaTeX
--------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/lametex
name:             lametex
caption:          A PostScript translator for a subset of LaTeX
author:           Jonathan Monsarrat
copyright:        Jonathan Monsarrat (1992)
license:          nosell = Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement (not free)
version:          1.1
description:      (no language specified) LameTeX is a direct PostScript generator for a (very limited) subset of LaTeX. One of its original design 
                  goals, the inclusion of PostScript commands directly in a LaTeX document, has been superseded by  PSTricks 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base) . However, one of the side effects of a special-purpose translator 
                  for LaTeX is the ability of that translator to produce different kinds of output, including plain ASCII.

                  The system only understands a subset of LaTeX, and is not set up to use Type 1 fonts; however, it is 
                  capable of doing some interesting tricks.

                  ++  configuration options (https://ctan.org/pkg/cfgguide) and
                  ++  modification of LaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/modguide) .

latex-amsmath -- AMS mathematical facilities for LaTeX
------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-amsmath
name:             latex-amsmath
caption:          AMS mathematical facilities for LaTeX
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
copyright:        American Mathematical Society (2001-2004, 2007, 2008, 2010, 2011, 2013)
copyright:        LaTeX3 Project and American Mathematical Society (2016-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          (2026-06-01)

year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package provides the principal packages in the  AMS-LaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/amslatex) distribution. 
                  It adapts for use in LaTeX most of the mathematical features found in AMS-TeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/amstex) ; 
                  it is highly recommended as an adjunct to serious mathematical typesetting in LaTeX.

                  When amsmath is loaded, AMS-LaTeX packages  amsbsy (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsbsy) (for bold symbols), amsopn 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsopn) (for operator names) and amstext (https://ctan.org/pkg/amstext) (for 
                  text embedded in mathematics) are also loaded.

                  amsmath is part of the LaTeX required distribution; however, several contributed packages add still further 
                  to its appeal; examples are  empheq (https://ctan.org/pkg/empheq) , which provides functions for 
                  decorating and highlighting mathematics, and ntheorem (https://ctan.org/pkg/ntheorem) , for specifying 
                  theorem (and similar) definitions.

                  ‘LaTeX symbol’ fonts.

                  For full support of a LaTeX installation, some Computer Modern font variants cmbsy(6-9), cmcsc(8,9), 
                  cmex(7-9) and cmmib(5-9) from the  amsfonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsfonts) distribution, are also 
                  necessary.

                  The fonts are available as Metafont source, and metric (tfm) files are also provided. Most of the fonts 
                  are also available in Adobe Type 1 format, in the  amsfonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsfonts) distribution.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/latex/README

on TeXLive:       latex-fonts

year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This is a free, open-source, platform-independent tool designed to automate the generation of indexes 
                  for LaTeX documents. It extracts words from  .tex files, generates frequency distributions using PGFplots 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgfplots) , allows users to select and tag terms (including variants and sub-variants),

                  GPL-3, it saves approximately 80% of indexing time, making document creation more efficient.

year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package provides several tools that aim to simplify the compilation of LaTeX documents:

                  +  LaTeX.mk : a Makefile snippet to help compiling LaTeX documents in DVI, PDF, PS, … format. Dependencies 
                    are automatically tracked: one should be able to compile documents with a one-line Makefile containing include 
                    LaTeX.mk . Complex documents (with multiple bibliographies, indexes, glossaries, …) should be correctly 
                    managed.
                  +  figlatex.sty : a LaTeX package to easily insert xfig figures (with \includegraphics{file.fig} ). 
                    It can interact with LaTeX.mk so that the latter automatically invokes transfig if needed.

                  + And various helper tools for  LaTeX.mk .
This package  'requires' GNUmake (&gt;= 3.81).

latex2nemeth -- Convert LaTeX source to Braille with math in Nemeth
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/latex2nemeth
name:             Latex2Nemeth
caption:          Convert LaTeX source to Braille with math in Nemeth
author:           Antonis Tsolomitis
author:           Andreas Papasalouros
copyright:        Andreas Papasalοuros, Antonis Tsolomitis (2016-2022)
license:          gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
version:          1.1.3
description:      (no language specified) After many failed attempts to transcribe real math notes and books to Braille/Nemeth in order to deal 
                  with a real situation (blind student in Math Dept.), we decided to develop a new program that follows 
                  a direct, from LaTeX to Braille/Nemeth, approach.

                  Our main target was the Greek language which is only Braille level 1, but English at level 1 is supported 
                  as well. Simple pictures in  PSTricks (https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base) are also supported in 
                  order to produce tactile graphics with specialized equipment.

                  Note that embossing will need LibreOffice and  odt2braille as this project does not deal with embossers’ 
                  drivers.

                  What’s new in version 1.1

                  In this version, the support of the user level commands of the  amsmath (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath) package 
                  was added, as described in its user guide, with the exception of commutative diagrams ( amscd (https://ctan.org/pkg/amscd) package) 
                  as well as structures that are irrelevant to visually impaired persons.

                  Also, the Unicode mathematics symbols of the  unicode-math (https://ctan.org/pkg/unicode-math) package 
                  that are represented by the Nemeth code are now supported by latex2nemeth.

                  We would like to acknowledge support by TUG's TeX development fund for this project (development fund 
                  project 33).

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/latex2nemeth/README
documentation:    HowTo videos on youtube (no language specified): https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLcBOch-MEQ5o1_7Qd474I3dK_T1lKuvqq
home page:        https://myria.math.aegean.gr/labs/dt/braille/index-en.html
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/latex2nemeth
on MikTeX:        latex2nemeth
on TeXLive:       latex2nemeth

latexalpha2 -- Embed Mathematica code and plots into LaTeX
----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/latexalpha2
name:             latexalpha2
caption:          Embed Mathematica code and plots into LaTeX
author:           Yi Liu
copyright:        Yi Liu (2019)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0 (2019-03-02)
last changes:     2019-03-02
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) This LaTeX package allows you to embed and execute your Wolfram Language (Mathematica) source code in 
                  a LaTeX document. When the document is compiled, the computation results will be inserted into the compiled 
                  file. In addition to general Wolfram Language computations it is also quite easy to generate plots or 
                  animations with this package. Moreover, all the embedded code can be executed either locally (via locally 
                  installed Mathematica) or on the cloud (via Wolfram Cloud).

                  The main features of this package are somewhat similar to  SageTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/sagetex) , 
                  but here we use Wolfram Language (Mathematica) instead of Sage.

                  The package is heavily inspired by  LaTeX-Alpha (https://github.com/Akollek/LaTeX-Alpha) , which 
                  also explains the name “latexalpha2”. Unfortunately, LaTeX-Alpha has been down for a while. The objective 
                  of latexalpha2 is to replace LaTeX-Alpha and at the same time provide various new features.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/latexalpha2/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/latexalpha2/latexalpha2.pdf
-- local file:    ./4044566254-latexalpha2.pdf
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/stevenliuyi/latex-alpha2/issues
contact:          repository: https://github.com/stevenliuyi/latex-alpha2
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/latexalpha2
on MikTeX:        latexalpha2
keyword:          callback (call external code and process the result)
keyword:          graphics-inline (graphics inline for external processing)
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-08-02


latexbangla -- Enhanced LaTeX integration for Bangla
----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/latexbangla
name:             latexbangla
caption:          Enhanced LaTeX integration for Bangla
author:           Adib Hasan
copyright:        Adib Hasan (2016)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.2 (2016-10-31)
last changes:     2016-10-31
year:             2016
description:      (no language specified) This package simplifies the process of writing Bangla in LaTeX and addresses most of the associated typesetting 
                  issues.

                  Notable features:

                  + Automated transition from Bangla to English and vice versa.
                  + Patch for the unproportionate whitespace issue in popular Bangla fonts.
                  + Full support for all the common commands and environments.
                  + Bangla numbering for page, section, chapter, footnotes etc. (extending polyglossia's support).
                  + New theorem, problems, example, solution and other environments, all of which are in Bangla.

latexdiff -- Determine and mark up significant differences between LaTeX files
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/latexdiff
name:             latexdiff
caption:          Determine and mark up significant differences between LaTeX files
author:           Frederik Tilmann
copyright:        F J Tilmann (2004-2024)
license:          gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
version:          (2026-01-02)
last changes:     2026-01-02
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) Latexdiff is a Perl script for visual mark up and revision of significant differences between two LaTeX 
                  files. Various options are available for visual markup using standard LaTeX packages such as  color 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/color) . Changes not directly affecting visible text, for example in formatting 
                  commands, are still marked in the LaTeX source. A rudimentary revision facility is provided by another 
                  Perl script, latexrevise, which accepts or rejects all changes. Manual editing of the difference file 
                  can be used to override this default behaviour and accept or reject selected changes only.

documentation:    Package Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/latexdiff/README
documentation:    Package manual (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/latexdiff/doc/latexdiff-man.pdf

latexmk -- Fully automated LaTeX document generation
----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/latexmk
name:             latexmk
caption:          Fully automated LaTeX document generation
author:           John Collins
author:           David J. Musliner
author:           Evan McLean
copyright:        John Collins (1998-2025)
license:          gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
version:          4.88 (2026-03-09)
last changes:     2026-03-09
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) Latexmk completely automates the process of generating a LaTeX document. Given the source files for a 
                  document, latexmk issues the appropriate sequence of commands to generate a  .dvi , .ps , .pdf or 
                  hardcopy version of the document.

                  An important feature is the “preview continuous mode”, where the script watches all of the source files 
                  (primary file and included TeX and graphics files), and reruns LaTeX, etc., whenever a source file has 
                  changed. Thus a previewer can offer a display of the document’s latest state.

latino-sine-flexione -- LaTeX support for documents written in Peano’s Interlingua
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/latino-sine-flexione
name:             latino-sine-flexione
caption:          LaTeX support for documents written in Peano’s Interlingua
author:           Victore Leve
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
version:          1.2
description:      (no language specified) 'Latino sine Flexione' (or Interlingua) is a language constructed by Giuseppe Peano at the beginning 
                  of the last century. This simplified Latin is designed to be an instrument for international cooperation, 
                  especially in the academic sphere. (Note that this “Interlingua” is different from the “Interlingua” 
                  that was created a few decades after Peano’s work and which is supported by babel-interlingua (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel-interlingua) !)

                  This package provides the necessary translations to use the language within a LaTeX document. It also 
                  imports  fontenc (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontenc) in order to be able to use ligatures and quotation 
                  marks.

                  Finally, it offers a text in Interlingua that can be used as a dummy text:  'Fundamento de intelligentia' . 
                  This article by H. Bijlsma was first published in 'Schola et Vita' Anno I (1926).

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/latino-sine-flexione/README.md
contact:          support: http://reddit.com/r/LatinoSineFlexione/
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/latino-sine-flexione
on MikTeX:        latino-sine-flexione
on TeXLive:       latino-sine-flexione
keyword:          interlingua (support for typesetting interlingua)
year:             without year

last access:      2026-07-14

lcdf-typetools -- A bundle of outline font manipulation tools
-------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/lcdf-typetools
name:             LCDF-typetools
caption:          A bundle of outline font manipulation tools
author:           Eddie Kohler
copyright:        Eddie Kohler (1997-2006)
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
description:      (no language specified) This bundle of tools comprises:

                  + Cfftot1, which translates a Compact Font Format (CFF) font, or a PostScript-flavored OpenType font, into 
                    PostScript Type 1 format. It correctly handles subroutines and hints;
                  +  Mmafm (https://ctan.org/pkg/mmafm) and mmpfb (https://ctan.org/pkg/mmpfb) , which create 
                    instances of multiple-master fonts (mmafm and mmpfb were previously distributed in their own package, 
                    mminstance);
                  + Otfinfo, which reports information about OpenType fonts, such as the features they support and the contents 
                    of their ‘size’ optical size features;
                  + Otftotfm, which creates TeX font metrics and encodings that correspond to a PostScript-flavored OpenType 
                    font. It will interpret glyph positionings, substitutions, and ligatures as far as it is able. You can 
                    say which OpenType features should be activated;
                  + T1dotlessj, creates a Type 1 font whose only character is a dotless j matching the input font’s design;

                  + T1lint, which checks a Type 1 font for correctness;
                  + T1reencode, which replaces a font’s internal encoding with one you specify; and
                  + T1testpage, which creates a PostScript proof for a Type 1 font. It is preliminary software.

lecturer -- On-screen presentations for (almost) all formats
------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/lecturer
name:             lecturer
caption:          On-screen presentations for (almost) all formats
author:           Paul Isambert
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          (2011-09-11)
last changes:     2011-09-11
year:             2011
description:      (no language specified) The package creates slides for on-screen presentations based on PDF features without manipulating TeX’s 
                  typesetting process. The presentation flow relies on PDF’s abilities to display content step by step.

                  Features include:

                  + Free positioning of anything anywhere in painted areas on the slide, as well as in the main textblock;

                  + Numerous attributes to control the layout and the presentation flow, from TeX's primitive dimensions 
                    to the visibility of steps;
                  + Feature inheritance from global to local settings, with intermediate types;
                  + Basic drawing facilities to produce symbols, e.g., for list items or buttons;
                  + Colours, transparency, shades, and pictures;
                  + Navigation with links, pop-up menus, and customizable bookmarks;
                  + Easy switch between presentation and handout; and
                  + PDF transitions.
Besides the traditional documentation, the distribution includes visual documentation and six demo presentations 
                  ranging from geometric abstraction to classic style to silly video game.

                  Lecturer is designed to work with all formats, but presently fails with ConTeXt MkIV (because of clashes 
                  in management of PDF objects, probably), works only with pdfTeX and LuaTeX for the time being, and requires 
                  texapi (https://ctan.org/pkg/texapi) and yax (https://ctan.org/pkg/yax) , both v.1.02.

leiletter -- A letter class for Leiden University

name:             LEIletter
caption:          A letter class for Leiden University
author:           Michiel Kreutzer
copyright:        Michiel Kreutzer (2009)

description:      (no language specified) This package is a LaTeX implementation of the business letter formatting that is used at Leiden University, 
                  using the institute graphic identity as specified on  www.leidenuniv.nl (https://www.leidenuniv.nl) .

                  The LEIletter class is an extension of the standard  KOMA-script (https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script) letter 
                  class scrlttr2 (https://ctan.org/pkg/scrlttr2) . It is intended to be used for writing business 
                  letters. It is compliant to the house style and allows for using windowed envelopes of the DL format, 
                  with right-aligned window.

                  The class requires and uses the following packages that are part of most modern LaTeX distributions: 
                  graphicx (https://ctan.org/pkg/graphicx) , ifthen (https://ctan.org/pkg/ifthen) , array 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/array) , babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) , ragged2e (https://ctan.org/pkg/ragged2e) , hyperref 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref) , textcase (https://ctan.org/pkg/textcase) , microtype (https://ctan.org/pkg/microtype) , scrlayer-scrpage 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/scrlayer-scrpage) , geometry (https://ctan.org/pkg/geometry) , setspace 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/setspace) , lipsum (https://ctan.org/pkg/lipsum) , and minionpro (https://ctan.org/pkg/minionpro) .

                  The package relies on the Minion Pro fonts from Adobe, which are commercial but easily available.

leporello -- A simple LaTeX document class to create folded leaflets using columns and boxes
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/leporello
name:             leporello
caption:          A simple LaTeX document class to create folded leaflets using columns and boxes
author:           Jasper Habicht
copyright:        Jasper Habicht (2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0.3 (2025-09-15)
last changes:     2025-09-15
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) A simple LaTeX document class to create folded leaflets with the following key features:

                  + The document layout consists of a specific number of pages that can have varying widths and are placed 
                    next to each other. Each page contains one frame to contain typeset material.
                  + Material is typeset in boxes, and boxes are positioned in columns which in turn are placed into the frames 
                    on the pages of the document.
                  + Columns are predefined and then placed into the frame of a page in the document layout. This way, columns 
                    can be used on pages with varying widths.
                  + Boxes can have padding (including bleed) and a background and are positioned inside a column.

letgut -- Class for the newsletter “La Lettre GUTenberg” of the French TeX User Group GUTenberg
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/letgut
name:             letgut
caption:          Class for the newsletter “La Lettre GUTenberg” of the French TeX User Group GUTenberg
author:           Association GUTenberg
copyright:        Association GUTenberg (1994-2026)
copyright:        Denis Bitouzé (2022)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.9.15 (2026-02-28)
last changes:     2026-02-28
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The French TeX User Group GUTenberg has been publishing “The GUTenberg Letter”, its irregular newsletter, 
                  since February 1993.

                  For this purpose, a dedicated, in-house (La)TeX class was gradually created but, depending on new needs 
                  and on the people who were publishing the Newsletter, its development was somewhat erratic; in particular, 
                  it would not have been possible to publish its code as it was. In addition, its documentation was non-existent.

                  The Board of Directors of the association, elected in November 2020, wished to provide a better structured, 
                  more perennial and documented class, able to be published on the CTAN. This is now done with the present 
                  ‘letgut’ class.

                  # French

                  L’association GUTenberg publie “La Lettre GUTenberg”, son bulletin irrégulomestriel, depuis février 1993.

                  Pour ce faire, une classe (La)TeX dédiée, maison, a peu à peu vu le jour mais, au gré des nouveaux besoins 
                  et des personnes qui ont assuré la publication de la Lettre, son développement a été quelque peu erratique 
                  ; il n’aurait notamment pas été possible de publier son code en l’état. En outre, sa documentation était 
                  inexistante.

                  Le Conseil d’Administration de l’association, élu en novembre 2020, a souhaité fournir une classe mieux 
                  structurée, davantage pérenne et documentée, à même d’être publiée sur le CTAN. C’est désormais chose 
                  faite avec la présente classe  letgut .

letterspacing -- Letter spacing

caption:          Letter spacing
author:           Philip Taylor
license:          knuth = Knuth License (free)
description:      (no language specified) Space out the letters of text; the command is  \letterspace&lt;\hbox modifier&gt;{&lt;text&gt;} : 
                  the text is placed in an \hbox of the specified size, and space is inserted between each glyph 
                  to make the text fit the box.

                  Note that letterspacing is not ordinarily considered acceptable in modern typesetting of English.

author:           Laurie Field
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) This is a Greek font written in Metafont, with inspiration from the Bodoni typefaces in old books. It 
                  is stylistically a little more exotic than the standard textbook Greek fonts, particularly in glyphs 
                  like the lowercase rho and kappa. It aims for a rather calligraphic feel, but seems to blend well with 
                  Computer Modern.

                  There is a ligature scheme which automatically inserts the breathings required for ancient texts, making 
                  the input text more readable than in some schemes.

lh -- Cyrillic fonts that support LaTeX standard encodings
----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/lh
name:             lh
caption:          Cyrillic fonts that support LaTeX standard encodings
author:           Vladimir Volovich
author:           Olga Lapko
author:           Andrey Khodulev
author:           Alexander Berdnikov
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          3.5g
description:      (no language specified) The LH fonts address the problem of the wide variety of alphabets that are written with Cyrillic-style 
                  characters. The fonts are the original basis of the set of T2* and X2 encodings that are now used when 
                  LaTeX users need to write in Cyrillic languages.

                  Macro support in standard LaTeX encodings is offered through the  latex-cyrillic (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-cyrillic) and t2 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/t2) bundles, and the package itself offers support for other (more traditional) 
                  encodings.

                  The fonts, in the standard T2* and X2 encodings are available in Adobe Type 1 format, in the  CM-Super 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/cm-super) family of fonts.

                  The package also offers its own LaTeX support for OT2 encoded fonts,  CM bright shaped fonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/cmbright) and Concrete 
                  shaped fonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/concrete) .

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/cyrillic/lh/README
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/cyrillic/lh
on MikTeX:        lh
on TeXLive:       lh

lhcyr -- A non-standard Cyrillic input scheme

name:             lhcyr
caption:          A non-standard Cyrillic input scheme
author:           Vadim V. Zhytnikov
license:          other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
description:      (no language specified) A collection of three LaTeX2e styles intended for typesetting Russian and bilingual English-Russian documents, 
                  using the  lh (https://ctan.org/pkg/lh) fonts and without the benefit of babel's (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) language-switching 
                  mechanisms.

                  The packages (lhcyralt and lhcyrwin for use under  emTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/emtex) , and lhcyrkoi 
                  for use under teTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/tetex) ) provide mappings between the input encoding 
                  and the font encoding (which is described as OT1). The way this is done does 'not' match the way inputenc 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/inputenc) would do the job, for output via fontenc (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontenc) to 
                  one of the T2 series of font encodings.

librarian -- Tools to create bibliographies in TeX

caption:          Tools to create bibliographies in TeX
author:           Paul Isambert
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) The package extracts information in bib files, makes it available in the current document, and sorts 
                  lists of entries according to that information and the user’s specifications. Citation and bibliography 
                  styles can then be written directly in TeX, without any use of BibTeX. Creating references thus depends 
                  entirely on the user's skill in TeX.

                  The package works with all formats that use plain TeX’s basic syntactic sugar; the distribution includes 
                  a third-party file for ConTeXt and a style file for LaTeX.

                  As an example of use, an Author (Year) style is given in a separate file and explained in the documentation.

liederbuch -- A LaTeX package for storing songs or other content, and repeated reuse in documents
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/liederbuch
name:             liederbuch
caption:          A LaTeX package for storing songs or other content, and repeated reuse in documents
author:           Gabriel Ruprecht
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.1.0 (2025-01-20)
last changes:     2025-01-20
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This package is meant for content which you reuse regularly, like songs in small booklets. For example 
                  the booklets used at church, weddings or similar events. It has two major parts:

                  * You typeset your content once (most likely a song), garnish it with some meta data and put it into a 
                     sty-file. From there you can insert this content into your document with one single line. The inserted 
                     content can have header and footer that use the meta data (i.e. title, composer, lyricist).
                  * Inside these content fragments, you can use the  \notenzeile (stave line) command to combine an 
                     image of a stave line with song lyrics. If correctly used, the lyrics are placed correctly below the 
                     notes and need most often no or only minor adjustments. With that you can combine any stave image with 
                     LaTeX fonts.
You can find resources and inspiration in a demo project.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/liederbuch/liederbuch-documentation.pdf

light-latex-make -- llmk: A build tool for LaTeX documents
----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/light-latex-make
alias:            llmk
name:             Light LaTeX Make
caption:          llmk: A build tool for LaTeX documents
author:           Takuto Asakura
copyright:        Takuto Asakura (2018-2023)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          1.2.0
description:      (no language specified) Light LaTeX Make (llmk) is yet another build tool specific for LaTeX documents. Its aim is to provide 
                  a simple way to specify a workflow of processing LaTeX documents and encourage people to always explicitly 
                  show the right workflow for each document.

                  The main features of  llmk are all about the above purpose. First, you can describe the workflows 
                  either in an external file llmk.toml or in a LaTeX document source in the form of magic comments. 
                  Further, multiple magic comment formats can be used. Second, it is fully cross-platform. The only requirement 
                  of the program is the texlua command; llmk provides a uniform way to describe the workflows available 
                  for nearly all TeX environments. Third, it behaves exactly the same in any environment. At this point, 
                  llmk intentionally does not provide any method for user configuration. Therefore one can guarantee that 
                  for a LaTeX document with an llmk setup, the process of typesetting the document will be reproduced 
                  in any TeX environment with the program.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/light-latex-make/llmk.pdf

limap -- Typeset maps and blocks according to the Information Mapping® method
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/limap
name:             limap
caption:          Typeset maps and blocks according to the Information Mapping® method
author:           Gerd Neugebauer
copyright:        Gerd Neugebauer (1999-2016)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.3
description:      (no language specified) The Information Mapping® method provides a methodology for structuring and presenting information. It 
                  claims to be useful for readers who are more concerned about finding the right information than reading 
                  the document as a whole. Thus short, highly structured, and contextfree pieces of information are used.

                  A LaTeX style and a LaTeX class are provided. The style contains definitions to typeset maps and blocks 
                  according to the Information Mapping® method. The class provides all definitions to typeset a whole document.

linegoal -- A “dimen” that returns the space left on the line
-------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/linegoal
name:             linegoal
caption:          A “dimen” that returns the space left on the line
author:           Florent Chervet
copyright:        Florent Chervet (2010)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.9
description:      (no language specified) The linegoal package provides a macro  \linegoal to be used with \setlength :
 \setlength&lt; 'some 
                  dimen' &gt;\linegoal 
will set &lt; 'some dimen' &gt; to the horizontal length of the remainder 
                  of the line.

                  This is achieved using the  \pdfsavepos primitive of pdfTeX, through the zref-savepos (https://ctan.org/pkg/zref) package.

                  Example:
 |
Some text: \begin{tabularx}\linegoal{|l|X|} \hline
one &amp; two \\
three &amp; four \\\hline
\end{tabularx}
| will position the table after the initial text, and make the table fill the rest of the line.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/linegoal/linegoal.pdf
-- local file:    ./3150238464-linegoal.pdf

linkedthm -- Hyperlinked theorem–proof environments for LaTeX
-------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/linkedthm
name:             linkedthm
caption:          Hyperlinked theorem–proof environments for LaTeX
author:           Luis Antonio Ortega Andrés
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0 (2025-07-21)
last changes:     2025-07-21
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This package provides lightweight infrastructure for bidirectional linking between theorem-like environments 
                  and their corresponding proofs. It automatically adds a [Proof] hyperlink at the end of a theorem and 
                  a restated version with a [Return] link inside the proof.

                  You can declare any number of custom linked environments (e.g.,  linkeddefinition , linkedexample ) 
                  using \DeclareLinkedTheorem , and base them on any amsthm (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsthm) -compatible 
                  environment.

                  This is useful for mathematical writing and documentation, where proof navigation is essential.

                  The package uses  amsthm (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsthm) , xparse (https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse) , 
                  and hyperref (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref) , and is compatible with all standard LaTeX engines.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/linkedthm/linkedthm-doc.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/linkedthm/README.md
documentation:    Example of use (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/linkedthm/linkedthm-example.pdf

listings -- Typeset source code listings using LaTeX
----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/listings
name:             listings
caption:          Typeset source code listings using LaTeX
author:           Carsten Heinz
author:           Brooks Moses
author:           Jobst Hoffmann
copyright:        Jobst Hoffmann (2013-2025)
copyright:        Carsten Heinz (1996-2004)
copyright:        Brooks Moses (2006-2007)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.11b (2025-11-14)
last changes:     2025-11-14
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) The package enables the user to typeset programs (programming code) within LaTeX; the source code is 
                  read directly by TeX—no front-end processor is needed. Keywords, comments and strings can be typeset 
                  using different styles (default is bold for keywords, italic for comments and no special style for strings). 
                  Support for  hyperref (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref) is provided.

                  To use,  \usepackage{listings} , identify the language of the object to typeset, using a construct 
                  like: \lstset{language=Python} , then use environment lstlisting for inline code. External 
                  files may be formatted using \lstinputlisting to process a given file in the form appropriate for 
                  the current language. Short (in-line) listings are also available, using either \lstinline|...| or |...| (after 
                  defining the | token with the \lstMakeShortInline command).

listofitems -- Grab items in lists using user-specified sep char
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/listofitems
name:             listofitems
caption:          Grab items in lists using user-specified sep char
author:           Christian Tellechea
copyright:        Christian Tellechea (2016-2024)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.65 (2024-03-09)
last changes:     2024-03-09
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) This simple package is designed to read a list of items whose parsing character may be selected by the 
                  user.

                  Once the list is read, its items are stored in a structure that behaves as a dimensioned array. As such, 
                  it becomes very easy to access an item in the list by its number.

                  For example, if the list is stored in the macro  \foo , the item #3 is designated by \foo[3] .

                  A component may, in turn, be a list with a parsing delimiter different from the parent list, paving the 
                  way for nesting and employing a syntax reminiscent of an array of several dimensions of the type  \foo[3,2] to 
                  access the item #2 of the list contained within the item #3 of the top-tier list.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/listofitems/README
documentation:    Package documentation (English): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/listofitems/listofitems-en.pdf
-- local file:    ./8763488636-listofitems-en.pdf
documentation:    Package documentation (French): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/listofitems/listofitems-fr.pdf
-- local file:    ./6911697848-listofitems-fr.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/listofitems
on MikTeX:        listofitems
on TeXLive:       listofitems
