year:             1991
description:      (no language specified) These macros present two macros for inserting marginal notes.

                  The first ( \ihack ) uses an insert to build a margin-full of notes, starting at the top of the 
                  page; the macro requires changes to the output routine.

                  The other macro ( \vhack ) just \vadjust s each note to the horizontal position where it 
                  starts; this requires no change to the output routine, but provides no protection against notes colliding 
                  with each other.

description:      (no language specified) The  mhequ style file simplifies creating multi-column equation environments and tagging equations 
                  therein. It supports sub-numbering of blocks of equations (like (1.2a), (1.2b), etc) and references to

                  example file.

microtype -- Subliminal refinements towards typographical perfection
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/microtype
name:             microtype
caption:          Subliminal refinements towards typographical perfection
author:           Robert Schlicht
copyright:        Robert Schlicht (2004-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          3.2d (2026-03-01)
last changes:     2026-03-01
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package provides a LaTeX interface to the micro-typographic extensions that were introduced by pdfTeX 
                  and have since also propagated to XeTeX and LuaTeX: most prominently, character protrusion and font expansion, 
                  furthermore the adjustment of interword spacing and additional kerning, as well as hyphenatable letterspacing 
                  (tracking) and the possibility to disable all or selected ligatures.

                  These features may be applied to customisable sets of fonts, and all micro-typographic aspects of the 
                  fonts can be configured in a straight-forward and flexible way. Settings for various fonts are provided.

                  Note that character protrusion requires pdfTeX, LuaTeX, or XeTeX. Font expansion works with pdfTeX or 
                  LuaTeX. The package will by default enable protrusion and expansion if they can safely be assumed to 
                  work. Disabling ligatures requires pdfTeX or LuaTeX, while the adjustment of interword spacing and of 
                  kerning only works with pdfTeX. Letterspacing is available with pdfTeX, LuaTeX or XeTeX.

                  The alternative package ‘letterspace’, which also works with plain TeX, provides the user commands for 
                  letterspacing only, omitting support for all other extensions.

documentation:    User manual (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/microtype/microtype.pdf
-- local file:    ./2723874752-microtype.pdf

milog -- A LaTeX class for fulfilling the documentation duties
    according to the German minimum wage law MiLoG
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/milog
name:             milog
caption:          A LaTeX class for fulfilling the documentation duties
    according to the German minimum wage law MiLoG
author:           Josef Kleber
copyright:        Josef Kleber (2016)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) Seit dem 1. Januar 2015 gilt in Deutschland grundsätzlich für alle Arbeitnehmer ein flächendeckender 
                  gesetzlicher Mindestlohn in Höhe von derzeit 8,50€ pro Stunde. Mit Wirkung ab 1. August 2015 wurden die 
                  Dokumentations- und Aufzeichnungspflichten gelockert. Nach §17 MiLoG, muss Beginn, Ende und Dauer der 
                  täglichen Arbeitszeit der in §22 MiLoG definierten Arbeitnehmern (formlos) aufgezeichnet werden. Zusätzlich 
                  ermöglicht milog.cls aus praktischen Gründen die Aufzeichnug von unbezahlten Pausen und Bemerkungen (Ruhetag, 
                  Urlaub, krank, …).

                  Die Erfassung der Arbeitszeiten erfolgt in einer simplen CSV-Datei, aus der die Klasse automatisch einen 
                  Arbeitszeitnachweis erstellt. Alternativ können die Daten auch durch einen CSV-Export – mit eventueller 
                  Nachbearbeitung – einer geeigneteten App erhoben werden.

                  The milog.cls class provides means to fulfill the documentation duties by the German minimum wage law 
                  MiLoG. The recording of working hours is carried out in a simple CSV file from which the class will automatically 
                  create a time sheet. Alternatively, data can also be collected by a CSV export of a suitable app.

year:             2012
description:      (no language specified) MimeTeX parses LaTeX mathematics expressions, emitting either gif images or mime xbitmaps of them, rather 
                  than the usual TeX DVI files. MimeTeX images are therefore easily inserted directly into html documents 
                  using a standard html img tag without intermediate dvi-to-gif conversion, and without storing lots of 
                  little gif image files, one file for each converted expression. This makes your web site and html documents 
                  more easily maintained. See  the mimetex web site (http://www.forkosh.com/mimetex.html#examples) for 
                  many examples demonstrating mimeTeX's features and usage.

description:      (no language specified) The package provides basic arithmetic operations to 8 decimal places for plain TeX or LaTeX. Results 
                  are exact when they fit within the digit limits. Along with the basic package is an optional extension

minim -- A modern plain format for the LuaTeX engine
----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/minim
name:             minim
caption:          A modern plain format for the LuaTeX engine
author:           Esger Renkema
copyright:        Esger Renkema, Michal Vlasák (2022)
license:          eupl = European Union Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          2025/1.7
description:      (no language specified) This is a modern plain format for the LuaTeX engine, adding improved low-level support for many LuaTeX 
                  extensions and newer PDF features. While it can be used as drop-in replacement for plain TeX, it probably 
                  is most useful as a basis for your own formats.

                  Most features included in the format are provided by separate packages that can be used on their own; see the packages 
                  +  minim-mp (https://ctan.org/pkg/minim-mp) for mplib (MetaPost) support
                  +  minim-math (https://ctan.org/pkg/minim-math) for unicode mathematics
                  +  minim-pdf (https://ctan.org/pkg/minim-pdf) for creating Tagged PDF
                  +  minim-xmp (https://ctan.org/pkg/minim-xmp) for XMP (metadata) inclusion

                  This package contains only their shared lowest-level programming interface, along with their combined 
                  format.

description:      (no language specified) The minitoc package allows you to add mini-tables-of-contents (minitocs) at the beginning of every chapter, 
                  part or section. There is also provision for mini-lists of figures and of tables. At the part level, 
                  they are parttocs, partlofs and partlots. If the type of document does not use chapters, the basic provision

                  (analagous to babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel)  .ldf files that do that job for LaTeX”s 
                  own fixed names).

missaali -- A late medieval OpenType textura font
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/missaali
name:             missaali
caption:          A late medieval OpenType textura font
author:           Tommi Syrjänen
copyright:        Tommi Syrjänen (2016)
license:          ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.0
description:      (no language specified) This package contains the free OpenType Textura font Missaali and a style file for using it with XeLaTeX.

                  Textura is a typeface based on the textus quadratus form of the textualis formata that late medieval 
                  scribes used for the most valuable manuscripts. The font Missaali is based on Textura that German printer 
                  Bartholomew Ghotan used for printing missals and psalters in the 1480s.

                  This font has two intended use cases:

                  + as a Gothic display font; and
                  + for emulating late-medieval manuscripts.
In addition to the basic textura letters, the font contains a large number of abbreviation sigla as well 
                  as a set of Lombardic initials.

                  As modern typesetting algorithms are not intended for creating 15th century style layout, the package 
                  contains a XeLaTeX style file that makes it easier to achieve the classic incunabula look.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/missaali/README

caption:          Mathematical symbol font for Adobe MinionPro
author:           Achim Blumensath
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
version:          1.4
description:      (no language specified) MnSymbol is a symbol font family, designed to be used in conjunction with Adobe Minion Pro (via the  MinionPro 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/minionpro) package). Almost all of LaTeX and AMS mathematical symbols are provided; 
                  remaining coverage is available from the MinionPro font with the MinionPro package.

                  The fonts are available both as Metafont source and as Adobe Type 1 format, and a comprehensive support 
                  package is provided.

                  While the fonts were designed to fit with Minon Pro, the design should fit well with other renaissance 
                  or baroque faces: indeed, it will probably work with most fonts that are neither too wide nor too thin, 
                  for example Palatino or Times; it is known to look good with Sabon. There is no package designed to configure 
                  its use with any font other than Minion Pro, but (for example) simply loading mnsymbol after  mathpazo 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/mathpazo) will probably do what is needed.

mnttex -- Tools for the “The Secret History of the Mongols”
-----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/mnttex
name:             mnttex
caption:          Tools for the “The Secret History of the Mongols”
author:           Oliver Corff
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          0.3
description:      (no language specified) The Secret History of the Mongols (Monggol-un niguca tobciyan→MNT) is the oldest work of Mongolian literature 
                  surviving today. Though the language of the text is Middle Mongolian, the text was written entirely in 
                  Chinese characters which were used to render Mongolian phonetically.

                  Modern tools for typing, editing and typesetting Chinese do not easily lend themselves for preparing 
                  research documentation due to peculiarities of the historical source.

                  The MNTTeX package assists the scholar typesetting the complex Chinese material by accessing all characters 
                  either by number or pronunciation as well as offering convenient access to small or combined characters.

                  The MNTTeX package relies on an existing environment for processing Chinese characters and assumes that 
                  the package  CJK (https://ctan.org/pkg/cjk) is installed. It is further required to have a recent 
                  inputenc package with ucs support from the unicode (https://ctan.org/pkg/unicode) package. Without 
                  these, MNTTeX is not likely to work. Furthermore it is required to use the font zysong.ttf or a similar 
                  font in Song style. Since not all characters used in the MNT are provided by modern fonts they had to 
                  be made for this package. Being closely modelled according to Song style, these especially made characters 
                  would stand out in stark contrast from e.g. Kaiti style character sets. Limited in number, these individual 
                  characters were coded as scalable vector images, rather than as font. No difference between these characters 
                  and ordinary characters can be perceived in print even though the on-screen display may appear hardly 
                  intelligible.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/mongolian/MNT/doc/mnttex.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/mongolian/MNT/README
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/mongolian/MNT
keyword:          mongolian (support for typesetting Mongolian)
year:             without year
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

                    definition), explanations (example, remark, note, warning, tip, takeaways), and assessments (exercise, 
                    solution, codebox).
                  + Zero heavy external dependencies: Built with a lightweight, native box engine for seamless compilation 
                    out-of-the-box across TeX Live, MiKTeX, and Overleaf.

modernruler -- Flexible ruler and annotation commands with key-value support and vertical writing compatibility
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/modernruler
name:             modernruler
caption:          Flexible ruler and annotation commands with key-value support and vertical writing compatibility
author:           KKTeX
copyright:        Kosei Kawaguchi (2025-2026)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          2.2.0 (2026-05-19)
last changes:     2026-05-19
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package provides a versatile set of commands for drawing rules and creating annotations in LaTeX. 
                  While standard LaTeX rules can be rigid, this package introduces more flexible alternatives:  \mruleth (horizontal 
                  rules), \mruletv (vertical rules), and \undernote (underlined annotations).

                  Key Features:

                  + Key-Value Interface: All commands support a consistent key-value syntax for adjust dimensions (width, 
                    height, depth), colors, and dash patterns (dash, dash-len, gap-len).
                  + Underline Annotations: The  \undernote command allows users to attach descriptive notes to underlined 
                    text. It automatically handles positioning, spacing between multiple notes, and provides options for 
                    various border styles (solid or dashed boxes).
                  + Vertical Writing Compatibility: Designed with multilingual typesetting in mind, the package is compatible 
                    with vertical writing modes, ensuring that rules and notes are oriented correctly.
                  + Customization: Users can update package-wide dfaults at any point in the document using a dedicated set 
                    of  \SetUNote… commands.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/modernruler/README.md

modroman -- Write numbers in lower case roman numerals
------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/modroman
name:             modroman
caption:          Write numbers in lower case roman numerals
author:           Yvon Henel
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          1
description:      (no language specified) This package provides only two macros viz.  \modromannumeral which writes the number given as argument 
                  in lower case roman numeral with a ‘j’ instead of a ‘i’ as the final letter of numbers greater than 1 
                  and \modroman{MyCounter} which writes the value of a counter in the same way. You use the first 
                  in the same way as the TeX primitive \romannumeral and the second as LaTeX command \roman . 
                  The default option is ‘vpourv’ with which 5 is ‘translated’ as ‘v’ and option ‘upourv’ with which the 
                  same 5 is given as ‘u’.

monoref -- Single-pass cross-references, page totals, and a table of contents for LuaLaTeX
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/monoref
name:             monoref
caption:          Single-pass cross-references, page totals, and a table of contents for LuaLaTeX
author:           Srikanth Mohankumar
copyright:        Srikanth Mohankumar (2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.3 (2026-07-07)
last changes:     2026-07-07
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package resolves forward cross-references ( \ref , \pageref ), the total page count 
                  ( \lastpage ), and a multi-level table of contents in a single LuaLaTeX run — no rerun, no latexmk 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/latexmk) , and no .aux round-trip. It holds every finished page in memory 
                  via the shipout hook and back-patches the still-unknown values at \end{document} . Forward 
                  values are reserved as fixed-width slots that collapse to their natural width when filled, so lines never 
                  reflow and short values leave no gap. When hyperref (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref) is loaded, 
                  references and contents entries become clickable, using the package’s own named destinations so linking 
                  stays single-pass. The package requires LuaLaTeX.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/monoref/monoref.pdf
-- local file:    ./5924886765-monoref.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/monoref/README.md
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/Srikanth-Mohankumar/latex-monoref/issues
contact:          repository: https://github.com/Srikanth-Mohankumar/latex-monoref/
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/monoref
on MikTeX:        monoref
on TeXLive:       monoref
keyword:          luatex (LuaTeX and packages that require it)
keyword:          toc-etc (deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things)
keyword:          label-ref (label and reference systems)

montex -- Mongolian LaTeX
-------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/montex
name:             montex
caption:          Mongolian LaTeX
author:           Oliver Corff
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          IVu.04.092
description:      (no language specified) MonTeX provides Mongolian and Manju support for the TeX/LaTeX community.

                  Mongolian is a language spoken in North East Asia, namely Mongolia and the Inner Mongol Autonomous Region 
                  of China. Today, it is written in an extended Cyrillic alphabet in Mongolia whereas the Uighur writing 
                  continues to be in use in Inner Mongolia, though it is also, legally speaking, the official writing system 
                  of Mongolia.

                  Manju is another language of North East Asia, belonging to the Tungusic branch of the Altaic languages. 
                  Though it is hardly spoken nowadays, it survives in written form as Manju was the native language of 
                  the rulers of the Qing dynasty (1644–1911) in China. Large quantities of documents of the Imperial Archives 
                  survive, as well as some of the finest dictionaries ever compiled in Asia, like the Pentaglot, a dictionary 
                  comprising Manju, Tibetan, Mongolian, Uighur and Chinese. MonTeX provides all necessary characters for 
                  writing standard Mongolian in Cyrillic and Classical (aka Traditional or Uighur) writing, and Manju as 
                  well as transliterated Tibetan texts, for which purpose a number of additional characters was created.

                  In MonTeX, both Mongolian and Manju are entered in romanized form. The retransliteration (from Latin 
                  input to Mongolian and Manju output) is completely realized in TeX/Metafont so that no external preprocessor 
                  is required.

                  Please note that most of the enhanced functions of MonTeX require a working e-LaTeX environment. This 
                  is especially true when compiling documents with Mongolian or Manju as the main document language. It 
                  is recommended to choose pdfelatex as the resulting PDF files are truly portable. Vertical text generated 
                  by MonTeX is not supported in DVI.

name:             montserrat

license:          ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.03
description:      (no language specified) Montserrat is a geometric sans-serif typeface designed by Julieta Ulanovsky, inspired by posters and 
                  signage from her historical Buenos Aires neighborhood of the same name. It is rather close in spirit 
                  to Gotham and Proxima Nova, but has its own individual appearance — more informal, less extended, and 
                  more idiosyncratic.

                  It is provided in a total of nine different weights, each having eight figure styles and small caps in 
                  both upright and italic shapes.

                  There are two quite different versions that don’t fit into the usual LaTeX classifications. The version 
                  having the appellation “Alternates” has letter shapes that are much more rounded than the default version, 
                  reflecting the signage in the neighborhood of Montserrat.

moreenum -- More enumeration options
------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/moreenum
name:             moreenum
caption:          More enumeration options
author:           Seamus Bradley
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.03
description:      (no language specified) The package provides the following new enumerate styles:

                  +  \greek for lowercase Greek letters;
                  +  \Greek for uppercase Greek letters;
                  +  \enumHex for uppercase hexadecimal enumeration;
                  +  \enumhex for lowercase hexadecimal enumeration;
                  +  \enumbinary for binary enumeration;
                  +  \enumoctal for octal enumeration;
                  +  \levelnth for “1st”, “2nd”, “3rd” etc., with the “nth”s on the baseline;
                  +  raisenth for “1st”, “2nd”, “3rd” etc., with the “nth”s raised;
                  +  \nthwords for “first”, “second“, “third” etc.;
                  +  \Nthwords for “First”, “Second”, “Third” etc.;
                  +  \NTHWORDS for “FIRST”, “SECOND”, “THIRD” etc.;
                  +  \nwords for “one”, “two”, “three” etc.;
                  +  \Nwords for “One”, “Two”, “Three” etc.; and
                  +  \NWORDS for “ONE”, “TWO”, “THREE” etc.
Each of these works with  enumitem (https://ctan.org/pkg/enumitem) ’s “starred variant” feature. 
                  So \begin{enumerate}[label=\enumhex*] will output a hex enumerated list. Enumitem provides a start=0 option 
                  for starting your enumerations at 0.

                  The package requires  amsmath (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath) , alphalph (https://ctan.org/pkg/alphalph) , enumitem 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/enumitem) (of course), binhex (https://ctan.org/pkg/binhex) and nth 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/nth) , all of which are widely available.

moremath -- Additional commands for typesetting maths
-----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/moremath
name:             moremath
caption:          Additional commands for typesetting maths
author:           Marcel Ilg
copyright:        Marcel Ilg (2024)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.5.0 (2024-08-20)
last changes:     2024-08-20
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) This package provides several document level commands to ease typesetting of maths with LaTeX.

                  This package provides complementary commands to all operators defined by  amsmath (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath) which 
                  typeset the operators together with delimiters (which can be scaled manually, automatically or not at 
                  all). These commands also accept optional sub- and superscripts.

                  Additionally, this package provides several commands to typeset gradient, divergence, curl, Laplace, 
                  and d’Alembert operators. Those commands also accept an optional subscript and their appearance can be 
                  modified using key-value options.

                  Furthermore several commands for producing row and column vectors, as well as (anti-)diagonal matrices 
                  and identity matrices, utilizing  mathtools (https://ctan.org/pkg/mathtools) ’ matrix* family 
                  of environments, are provided.

                  Most of the document level commands defined by this package can also be disabled using a package load-time 
                  option to avoid clashes with commands defined by other packages.

                  The package depends on  mathtools (https://ctan.org/pkg/mathtools) , bm (https://ctan.org/pkg/bm) (optional), 
                  and amssymb (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsfonts) .

description:      (no language specified) The package aims to solve the error “No room for a new  \write ”, which occurs when the user, or 
                  when the user’s packages have ‘allocated too many streams’ using \newwrite (TeX has a fixed maximum 
                  number – 16 – such streams built-in to its code). The package hooks into TeX primitive commands associated 
                  with writing to files; it should be loaded near the beginning of the sequence of loading packages for 
                  a document.

                  The package uses the  l3kernel (https://ctan.org/pkg/l3kernel) bundle.

mpfonts -- Computer Modern Type 3 fonts converted using MetaPost
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/mpfonts
name:             mpfonts
caption:          Computer Modern Type 3 fonts converted using MetaPost
author:           Daniel Benjamin Miller
license:          other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
license:          knuth = Knuth License (free)
license:          ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
version:          (2020-01-30)
last changes:     2020-01-30
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) The Computer Modern fonts are available in Type 1 format, but these renditions are somewhat thin and 
                  spindly, and produce much lighter results than the originals. It is alternatively possible to use Metafont 
                  bitmaps, but this has its disadvantages in comparison with vector fonts.

                  These fonts are conversions to Type 3 fonts, done entirely in MetaPost; they are vector fonts which are 
                  a direct conversion from the original Metafont files, so they are the design most authentic to the originals.

                  However, these fonts, because they are PostScript Type 3 fonts, are not suitable for on-screen reading, 
                  and should probably only be used for printing.

                  Note: do NOT add the map file to updmap!

msx2msa -- Simulate msxm and msym fonts using msam and msbm
-----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/msx2msa
name:             msx2msa
caption:          Simulate msxm and msym fonts using msam and msbm
license:          noinfo = noinfo 
version:          (1992-08-16)
last changes:     1992-08-16
year:             1992
description:      (no language specified) In the deeps of time, the AMS distributed mathematical symbol fonts called  msxm and msym ; 
                  these fonts were designed using the original (SAIL) version of Metafont and for a long time after the 
                  demise of that system were only available as 300 dpi bitmaps.

                  Eventually, the symbols were re-implemented using ‘modern’ Metafont in fonts called  msam and msbm . 
                  The virtual fonts of this bundle implement the encoding of the old fonts using the glyphs of the new 
                  fonts, and can be used as drop-in replacements in documents (and even when processing DVI files).

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/vf-files/msx2msa/README

language(s):      nls: no language specified

description:      (no language specified) This package provides tools for typesetting Sudoku grids of various sizes in LaTeX. Unlike other Sudoku 
                  packages which are typically limited to the standard 9×9 layout, this package supports a broad range 
                  of grid sizes – from trivial 1×1 puzzles to extended 49×49 Sudokus – that’s the limit for now! Grids 
                  are drawn with our sudoku environment, which is based on using LaTeX’s native tabular environment. We 
                  include intuitive options to control dimensions, font size, and grid thickness. Entries in the grid are 
                  inserted as in a regular table, thus making it simple to create, customise, and fill Sudoku puzzles manually.

multicol -- Intermix single and multiple columns
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/multicol
name:             multicol
caption:          Intermix single and multiple columns
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
author:           Frank Mittelbach
copyright:        Frank Mittelbach (1989-2023)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.0b (2025-10-21)
last changes:     2025-10-21
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) Multicol defines a multicols environment which typesets text in multiple columns (up to a maximum of 
                  10), and (by default) balances the end of each column at the end of the environment. The package enables 
                  you to switch between any (permitted) number of columns at will: there is no imposed “clear page” operation, 
                  as there is in unadorned LaTeX at a switch between \onecolumn and \twocolumn sections. The multicolumn 
                  environment can also be used inside a box, thus allowing multicolumned insets in text.

                  Multicol patches the output routine, and may clash with other packages that do the same (e.g.,  longtable 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/longtable) ); furthermore, there is no provision for single column floats inside 
                  a multicolumn environment, so figures and tables must be coded in-line (using, for example, the H modifier 
                  of the float (https://ctan.org/pkg/float) package).

                  The package is part of the  latex-tools (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-tools) bundle in the LaTeX required 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/required) distribution.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools/multicol.pdf
-- local file:    ./8671963583-multicol.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools
installation:     https://ctan.org/tex-archive/install/macros/latex/required/latex-tools.tds.zip
on MikTeX:        latex-tools
on TeXLive:       tools
keyword:          tagged-pdf (tagged PDF compatible)
keyword:          multicol (more than one column on the page)

version:          (2024-03-24)
last changes:     2024-03-24
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) This package provides several commands for generating footnotes which correspond to multiple footnote 
                  numbers (resp. marks).

                  In some cases, you may wish for certain footnotes to correspond to several places in your text. The traditional 
                  solution usually involves writing the same footnote mark multiple times at the corresponding places. 
                  However, this approach makes it difficult to see at once how many times a footnote has been referred 
                  to. Therefore, the current package proposes another method: writing the footnote marks in linear order, 
                  and allowing a footnote text to match several of these marks.

author:           F.W. Long
license:          noinfo = noinfo 
version:          1.1b
description:      (no language specified) The package redefines  \makeindex , \index and \printindex commands to deal with multiple 
                  indexes. In each case, the command gains a (first) argument specifying the index in question: the name 
                  used there is used as a name for the index files, so one then uses the command
 makeindex &lt;index 
                  file&gt; 
for each index, separately.

                  The package does not work in documents using  AMS classes (https://ctan.org/pkg/amscls) ; the AMS 
                  provide a replacement package amsmidx (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmidx) , which is based on multind.

multinotes -- Typesetting multilingual lecture notes and exercise sheets
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/multinotes
name:             multinotes
caption:          Typesetting multilingual lecture notes and exercise sheets
author:           Dafydd Evans
copyright:        Dafydd Evans (2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.1 (2025-06-25)
last changes:     2025-06-25
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This package provides tools for typesetting multilingual lecture notes, exercise sheets, and general-purpose 
                  documents. Each language is specified via its corresponding  babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) identifier 
                  and is associated with a declaration, macro, and environment used to delimit content written in that 
                  language.

                  Arbitrary combinations of languages can be loaded in a single document to support both monolingual and 
                  multilingual output. The package also defines macros and environments for typesetting lecture notes and 
                  exercise sheets, including configurable inclusion of elements such as proofs, solutions, and sketchboxes.

musixtex -- Sophisticated music typesetting
-------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/musixtex
name:             MusiXTeX
caption:          Sophisticated music typesetting
author:           Hiroaki Morimoto
author:           Jean-Pierre Coulon
author:           Andreas Egler
author:           Olivier Vogel
author:           Bob Tennent
author:           Don Simons
author:           Daniel Taupin
author:           Ross Mitchell
license:          gpl2+ = GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer (free)
version:          1.41 (2025-11-15)
last changes:     2025-11-15
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) MusiXTeX provides a set of macros, based on the earlier  MusicTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/musictex) , 
                  for typesetting music with TeX. To produce optimal spacing, MusiXTeX is a three-pass system: etex 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/etex) , musixflx , and etex again. ( Musixflx is a lua script 
                  that is provided in the bundle.) The three-pass process, optionally followed by processing for printed 
                  output, is automated by the musixtex wrapper script.

                  The package uses its own  specialised fonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/musixtex-fonts) , which must 
                  be available on the system for musixtex to run.

                  This version of MusiXTeX builds upon work by  Andreas Egler (https://ctan.org/pkg/musixtex-egler) , 
                  whose own version is no longer being developed.

                  The MusiXTeX macros are universally acknowledged to be challenging to use directly: the  pmx (https://ctan.org/pkg/pmx) preprocessor 
                  compiles a simpler input language to MusiXTeX macros..

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/musixtex/README

musixtnt -- A MusiXTeX extension library that enables transformations of the effect of notes commands
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/musixtnt
name:             musixtnt
caption:          A MusiXTeX extension library that enables transformations of the effect of notes commands
author:           Bob Tennent
copyright:        Bob Tennent (2015-2016)
license:          gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
version:          (2016-01-30)
last changes:     2016-01-30
year:             2016
description:      (no language specified) The package includes an archive containing a MusiXTeX extension library  musixtnt and C source 
                  code, binaries for Windows (32 bit and 64 bit) and MacOSX, and documentation for two programs: fixmsxpart 
                  and msxlint.

                  musixtnt.tex provides a macro \TransformNotes that enables transformations of the effect 
                  of notes commands such as \notes . In general, the effect of \TransformNotes{input}{output} is 
                  that notes commands in the source will expect their arguments to match the input pattern, but the notes 
                  will be typeset according to the output pattern. An example is extracting single-instrument parts from 
                  a multi-instrument score.

                  fixmsxpart corrects note spacing in a single-part MusiXTeX source (possibly derived from a multi-instrument 
                  score and as a result having irregular note spacing).

                  msxlint detects incorrectly formatted notes lines in a MusiXTeX source file. This should be used before 
                  using  \TransformNotes .

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/musixtnt/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/musixtnt/doc/msxlint.pdf
-- local file:    ./2615760862-msxlint.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/musixtnt
on TeXLive:       musixtnt
keyword:          music (typesetting music and related stuff)
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

mversion -- Keeping track of document versions
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/mversion
name:             mversion
caption:          Keeping track of document versions
author:           Michael Schmeing
copyright:        Michael Schmeing (2011)
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          1.0.1
description:      (no language specified) The package enables the user to keep track of different versions of a LaTeX document. The command  \version prints 
                  the version and build numbers; each time you compile your document, the build number is increased by 
                  one.

                  By placing  \version in the header or footer, each page can be marked with the unique build number 
                  describing the progress of your document.

year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) mwcls is a set of document classes for LaTeX2e designed with Polish typographical tradition in mind. 
                  Classes include: ‘ mwart ’ (which is a replacement for ‘ article ’), ‘ mwrep ’ (replacing 
                  ‘ report ’), and ‘ mwbk ’ (replacing ‘ book ’). Most features present in standard classes 
                  work with mwcls classes. Some extensions/exceptions include: sectioning commands allow for second optional 
                  argument (it is possible to state different texts for running head and for TOC), new environments ‘ itemize* ’ 
                  and ‘ enumerate* ’ for lists with long items, page styles have variants for normal, opening, closing, 
                  and blank pages.

mweights -- Support for multiple-weight font packages
-----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/mweights
name:             mweights
caption:          Support for multiple-weight font packages
author:           Bob Tennent
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          (2020-01-23)
last changes:     2020-01-23
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) Many font families available for use with LaTeX are available at multiple weights. Many Type 1-oriented 
                  support packages for such fonts re-define the standard  \mddefault or \bfdefault macros. 
                  This can create difficulties if the weight desired for one font family isn’t available for another font 
                  family, or if it differs from the weight desired for another font family.

                  The package provides a solution to these difficulties.

mylatex -- Make a format containing a document’s preamble

Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/mylatex
name:             mylatex
caption:          Make a format containing a document’s preamble
author:           David Carlisle
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          (2020-10-23)
last changes:     2020-10-23
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) The file  mylatex.ltx permits you to create a format that pre-loads a set of package files (and/or 
                  other macros) that you regularly use. In some circumstances, this can be a great advantage (though on 
                  an ordinarily fast modern computer on the desktop, gains will be limited).

                  The general scheme is to initialize your usage by a command of the form:
 latex -ini mylatex.ltx 
                  &lt;document&gt; 
whick will create a format file mylatex.fmt , which you then use as:
 latex 
                  -fmt=mylatex &lt;document&gt;

namedef -- TeX definitions with named parameters
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/namedef
name:             namedef
caption:          TeX definitions with named parameters
author:           Phelype Oleinik
copyright:        Phelype Oleinik (2019-2020)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0 (2020-06-20)
last changes:     2020-06-20
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) This package provides a prefix  \named to be used in TeX definitions so that parameters can be 
                  identified by their name rather than by number, giving parameters a semantic rather than syntactic meaning, 
                  making it easy to understand long definitions.

                  A usual definition reads:

                  |
\def\SayHello#1{Hello, #1!}
| but with  namedef you can replace #1 by, say, #[person] :

                  |
\named\def\SayHello#[person]{Hello, #[person]!}
| and  \named will figure out the numbering of the parameters for you.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/namedef/namedef.pdf

caption:          Natural mathematics notation
author:           Michal Marvan
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
description:      (no language specified) Nath is a LaTeX (both 2e and 2.09) style to separate presentation and content in mathematical typography. 
                  The style delivers a particular context-dependent presentation on the basis of a rather coarsecontext-independent 
                  notation. Highlighted features: depending on thecontext, the command \frac produces either built-up 
                  or case or solidus fractions, with parentheses added whenever required for preservation of the mathematical 
                  meaning; delimiters adapt their size to the material enclosed, rendering \left and \right almost 
                  obsolete.

nccsect -- A re-implementation of sections, captions and tocs
-------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/nccsect
name:             nccsect
caption:          A re-implementation of sections, captions and tocs
author:           Alexander I. Rozhenko
copyright:        Alexander I. Rozhenko (2002-2006)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.5
description:      (no language specified) The package user has section control commands that mirror the internal controls used in LaTeX. In particular, 
                  the user may express the section level explicitly in a \startsection command, rather than by name (as 
                  in \section, \subsection, etc., in LaTeX itself, defined in terms of an internal command). By using this 
                  \startsection, the user may have astounding depths of sections, which is sometimes useful in extreme 
                  typesetting applications. A \sectionstyle command controls the appearance of predefined, or user-defined 
                  sections, and \DeclareSection allows the user to create sectioning or caption commands, or to modify 
                  existing ones.

                  The package also extends user control of the appearance of tables of contents, etc., using a command 
                  \DeclareTOCEntry.

                  This package is part of the  ncctools (https://ctan.org/pkg/ncctools) bundle.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ncctools/doc/nccsect.pdf

nccthm -- Another theorem environment
-------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/nccthm
name:             nccthm
caption:          Another theorem environment
author:           Alexander I. Rozhenko
copyright:        Alexander I. Rozhenko (2002-2004)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.1
description:      (no language specified) This package's theorems have two distinguishing characteristics. First, theorem numbering uses dynamic 
                  counters (specified by using the  dcounter (https://ctan.org/pkg/dcounter) package, which gives 
                  the user considerable flexibility in counting styles. Second, the environment isn't defined as a trivlist 
                  (as LaTeX theorems are), which gives extra flexibility in using the environment. In addition, parameter 
                  definition is explicit and well-organised, and there is a QED-symbol-placing command.

                  +  manually marked footnotes (https://ctan.org/pkg/nccfoots) ;
                  +  extension of amsmath (https://ctan.org/pkg/nccmath) ;
                  +  control of paragraph skip (https://ctan.org/pkg/nccparskip) ; an envelope to the graphicx package 
                    (https://ctan.org/pkg/nccpic) ;
                  +  dashed and multiple rules (https://ctan.org/pkg/nccrules) ;
                  +  alternative techniques for declarations of sections, captions, and toc-entries (https://ctan.org/pkg/nccsect) ;

                  +  generalised text-stretching (https://ctan.org/pkg/nccstretch) ;
                  +  generation of new theorem-like environments (https://ctan.org/pkg/nccthm) ;
                  +  control of the text area (https://ctan.org/pkg/textarea) ;
                  +  centred page layouts (https://ctan.org/pkg/tocenter) ; and
                  +  un-numbered top-level section (https://ctan.org/pkg/topsection) .

newclude -- Reimplemented \include system for LaTeX
---------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/newclude
name:             newclude
caption:          Reimplemented \include system for LaTeX
author:           Matt Swift
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          2
description:      (no language specified) A LaTeX package providing a backwards-compatible reimplementation of  \include and \includeonly . 
                  The principal new features are:

                  + the restriction that  \clearpage s must surround an included file is removed,
                  + the restriction that  \include s cannot be nested is removed, and
                  + the provision of hooks to be executed before and after the contents of an included file.
Newclude accomplishes the first two by using a single  .aux file instead of many. Newclude also 
                  provides the experimental functionality of the unsupported package includex (https://ctan.org/pkg/includex) , 
                  which allows you to include partial contents of independent LaTeX files that can also be processed on 
                  their own (that is, files that contain \documentclass , \begin{document} , etc.).

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/frankenstein/newclude.pdf
-- local file:    ./5375800607-newclude.pdf
documentation:    Bundle README (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/frankenstein/README
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/frankenstein
on MikTeX:        frankenstein
on TeXLive:       frankenstein
keyword:          subdocs (include complete documents in other documents)
see also:         standalone (standalone -- Compile TeX pictures stand-alone or as part of a document)
see also:         docmute (docmute -- Input files ignoring LaTeX preamble, etc)
see also:         includex (includex -- Extended \include)
see also:         combine (combine -- Bundle individual documents into a single document)
year:             without year

newpx -- Alternative uses of the PX fonts, with improved metrics
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/newpx
name:             newpx
caption:          Alternative uses of the PX fonts, with improved metrics
author:           Michael Sharpe
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
license:          gfl = The GUST Font License (GFL) (free)
version:          1.551 (2025-10-30)
last changes:     2025-10-30
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This package, initially based on  pxfonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/pxfonts) , provides many fixes 
                  and enhancements to that package, and splits it in two parts ( newpxtext and newpxmath ) 
                  which may be run independently of one another. It provides scaling, improved metrics, and other options.

                  For proper operation, the packages require that the packages  newtxmath (https://ctan.org/pkg/newtx) , pxfonts

----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/newtx
name:             newtx
caption:          Alternative uses of the TX fonts, with improved metrics
author:           Michael Sharpe
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.756 (2025-01-09)
last changes:     2025-01-09
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) The bundle splits  txfonts.sty (from the TX fonts (https://ctan.org/pkg/txfonts) distribution) 
                  into two independent packages, newtxtext.sty and newtxmath.sty , each with fixes and enhancements.

                  newtxmath ’s metrics have been re-evaluated to provide a less tight appearance, and to provide 
                  a libertine option that substitutes Libertine (https://ctan.org/pkg/libertineotf) italic 
                  and Greek letter for the existing math italic and Greek glyphs, making a mathematics package that matches 
                  Libertine text quite well.

                  newtxmath can also use the maths italic font provided with the garamondx (https://ctan.org/pkg/garamondx) package, 
                  thus offering a garamond-alike text-with-maths combination.

version:          1.6a (2022-10-25)
last changes:     2022-10-25
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) The package allows the definition of  \verb variants which add TeX code before and after the verbatim 
                  text (e.g., quotes or surrounding \fbox{} ). When used together with the shortvrb (https://ctan.org/pkg/shortvrb) package 
                  it allows the definition of short verbatim characters which use this package’s variant instead of the 
                  normal \verb .

                  In addition, it is possible to collect an argument verbatim to either typeset or write it into a file.

                  The  \Verbdef command defines verbatim text to a macro which can later be used to write the verbatim 
                  text to a file.

license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          7.11a (2026-07-22)
last changes:     2026-07-22
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package is based on the package  array (https://ctan.org/pkg/array) . It creates PGF/TikZ 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) nodes under the cells of the array and uses these nodes to provide functionalities 
                  to construct tabulars, arrays and matrices.

                  Among the features :

                  + continuous dotted lines for the mathematical matrices;
                  + exterior rows and columns (so-called border matrices);
                  + control of the width of the columns;
                  + tools to color rows and columns with a good PDF result;
                  + blocks of cells;
                  + tabular notes;
                  + etc.
The package requires and loads  array (https://ctan.org/pkg/array) , amsmath (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath) , pgfcore 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) , and the module shapes of PGF (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) .

nicetext -- Minimal markup for simple text (Wikipedia style) and documentation
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/nicetext
name:             nicetext
caption:          Minimal markup for simple text (Wikipedia style) and documentation
author:           Uwe Lück
copyright:        Uwe Lück (2009-2015)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          r0.67
description:      (no language specified) The bundle offers “minimal” markup syntax for various simple kinds of text. The user will typically involve 
                  little more than is printed, and will still get LaTeX quality.

                  The bundle provides four packages:

                  +  wiki (https://ctan.org/pkg/wiki) addresses general texts, marked up in the simple style used on 
                    Wikipedia;
                  +  niceverb (https://ctan.org/pkg/niceverb) is yet another means of documenting LaTeX packages: it 
                    offers syntax-aware typesetting of meta-variables (macro arguments) and for referring to commands (and 
                    their syntax) in footnotes, section titles etc.;
                  +  fifinddo (https://ctan.org/pkg/fifinddo) aims to parse plain text or (La)TeX files using TeX, 
                    and to write the results to an external file; the package is used by another member of the bundle:
                  +  makedoc (https://ctan.org/pkg/makedoc) , which provides the means to produce typeset documentation 
                    direct from package files.

non-decimal-units -- Display and manipulate historical non-decimal units
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/non-decimal-units
name:             non-decimal-units
caption:          Display and manipulate historical non-decimal units
author:           Mikkel Eide Eriksen
license:          cc-by-sa-4 = CC BY-SA 4.0 (free)
version:          (2024-01-25)
last changes:     2024-01-25
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) Many historical unit systems were non-decimal. For example, the Danish rigsdaler — where 1 rigsdaler 
                  consists of 6 mark, each again consisting of 16 skilling for a total of 96 skilling per rigsdaler — was 
                  used from 1625 to 1875, when currency was decimalised to the current system of 1 krone = 100 øre.

                  Units for such measures as length, area, weight, and so on were also often non-decimal, and in fact remain 
                  so in the few places of the world that have not made the change to the metric system.

                  The non-decimal numbers were chosen due to their larger number of division factors, which simplified 
                  mental arithmetic, eg. when sharing an amount of money or dividing goods.

                  This package enables creation and configuration of such units to facilitate their presentation in textual 
                  and tabular contexts, as well as simple arithmetic.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/non-decimal-units/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/non-decimal-units/docs/non-decimal-units.pdf
-- local file:    ./2129500268-non-decimal-units.pdf
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/mikkelee/latex-units/issues
contact:          repository: https://github.com/mikkelee/latex-units
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/non-decimal-units
on MikTeX:        non-decimal-units
on TeXLive:       non-decimal-units
keyword:          units (uniform typesetting of units)
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

nopageno -- No page numbers in LaTeX documents
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/nopageno
name:             nopageno
caption:          No page numbers in LaTeX documents
author:           David Carlisle
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          (1989-01-01)
last changes:     1989-01-01
year:             1989
description:      (no language specified) LaTeX’s standard styles use two page styles, one on normal pages and one on ‘opening’ pages with  \maketitle or \chapter , 
                  etc. Unfortunately there is only easy access to changing one of these two so if you want something other 
                  than ‘plain’ on the opening pages you must use \thispagestyle on each such page. The fancyhdr 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/fancyhdr) package does provide a more flexible interface, but if you just want 
                  an empty page style on all pages then this package will do the job.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/nopageno/nopageno.pdf
-- local file:    ./6686010337-nopageno.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/nopageno

noprot -- Avoid the need for protection
---------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/noprot
name:             noprot
caption:          Avoid the need for protection
author:           Sami Sozuer
license:          noinfo = noinfo 
version:          (2004-08-16)
last changes:     2004-08-16
year:             2004
description:      (no language specified) An approach to reducing the need for  \protect . The package re-writes the \thanks , \caption and 
                  sectioning commands ( \chapter , \section , …), \addcontentsline , \addtocontents and \bibitem , 
                  to suppress the expansion of their arguments when those arguments are written to the .aux file.

                  The mechanism is not entirely satisfactory: there is still a problem with things written with the  \mark* commands, 
                  and one loses the facility of making direct reference to the current page (i.e., one must use \pageref for 
                  such things).

year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) The package defines a new type of note, bibnote, which will always be added to the bibliography. The 
                  package allows footnotes and endnotes to be moved into the bibliography in the same way. The package 
                  can be used with natbib and BibLaTeX as well as plain LaTeX citations. Both sorted and unsorted bibliography 
                  styles are supported.

                  The package uses the  LaTeX 3 (https://ctan.org/pkg/l3kernel) macros and the associated xpackages 
                  bundle (https://ctan.org/pkg/l3packages) . It also makes use of the e-TeX extensions (any post-2005 
                  LaTeX distribution will provide these by default, but users of older systems may need to use an elatex command 
                  or equivalent).

                  The package relies on LaTeX 3 support from the  l3kernel (https://ctan.org/pkg/l3kernel) and l3packages 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/l3packages) bundles.

license:          bsd2 = Simplified BSD License (free)
version:          2.12 (2018-06-20)
last changes:     2018-06-20
year:             2018
description:      (no language specified) Noweb is designed to meet the needs of literate programmers while remaining as simple as possible. Its 
                  primary advantages are simplicity, extensibility, and language-independence. Noweb uses 5 control sequences 
                  to WEB’s 27. The noweb manual is only 4 and a bit pages; an additional page explains how to customize 
                  its LaTeX output. Noweb works “out of the box” with any programming language, and supports TeX, LaTeX, 
                  and HTML back ends. A back end to support full hypertext or indexing takes about 250 lines; a simpler 
                  one can be written in 40 lines of awk. Noweb does not prettyprint natively, but supports prettyprinting 
                  through such third-party filters as pretzel and dpp.

numberpt -- Counters spelled out in Portuguese
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/numberpt
name:             numberpt
caption:          Counters spelled out in Portuguese
author:           Miguel Vinícius Santini Frasson
copyright:        Miguel V. S. Frasson (2019)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0 (2019-07-13)
last changes:     2019-07-13
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) This packages defines commands to display counters spelled out in Portuguese.

                  The styles are

                  +  \numberpt for “all lowercase”
                  +  \Numberpt for “First word capitalized”
                  +  \NumberPt for “All Capitalized”
                  +  \NUMBERPT for “ALL UPPERCASE”
For example,  \renewcommand{\thechapter}{\NumberPt{chapter}} makes chapter titles to be rendered 
                  as “Capítulo Um”, “Capítulo Dois” etc.

                  Options are offered to select variations in the spelling of “14”, or Brazilian vs. European Portuguese 
                  forms in the spelling of “16”, “17”, and “19”.

                  The package requires  expl3 (https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3) and xparse (https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse) .

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/numberpt/README.md

numerica -- Numerically evaluate mathematical expressions in LaTeX form
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/numerica
name:             numerica
caption:          Numerically evaluate mathematical expressions in LaTeX form
author:           Andrew Parsloe
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          3.0.0
description:      (no language specified) This package defines a command to wrap around a mathematical expression in its LaTeX form and, once values 
                  are assigned to variables, numerically evaluate it. The intent is to avoid the need to modify the LaTeX 
                  form of the expression being evaluated. For programs with a preview facility like LyX, or compile-as-you-go 
                  systems, interactive back-of-envelope calculations and numerical exploration are possible within the 
                  document being worked on.

                  The package requires the bundles  l3kernel (https://ctan.org/pkg/l3kernel) and l3packages (https://ctan.org/pkg/l3packages) , 
                  and the amsmath (https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath) and mathtools (https://ctan.org/pkg/mathtools) packages.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/numerica/numerica.pdf
-- local file:    ./2753156200-numerica.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/numerica/README.txt
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/numerica
on MikTeX:        numerica
on TeXLive:       numerica

numprint -- Print numbers with separators and exponent if necessary
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/numprint
name:             numprint
caption:          Print numbers with separators and exponent if necessary
author:           Harald Harders
copyright:        Harald Harders (2000-2005, 2007, 2008, 2012)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          1.39
description:      (no language specified) The package numprint prints numbers with a separator every three digits and converts numbers given as 
                  12345.6e789 to 12\,345,6\cdot 10^{789}. Numbers are printed in the current mode (text or math) in order 
                  to use the correct font.

                  Many things, including the decimal sign, the thousand separator, as well as the product sign can be changed 
                  by the user, e.g., to reach 12,345.6\times 10^{789}.

                  If an optional argument is given it is printed upright as unit. Numbers can be rounded to a given number 
                  of digits. The package supports an automatic, language-dependent change of the number format.

                  Tabular alignment using the tabular(*), array, tabularx, and longtable environments (similar to the dcolumn 
                  and rccol packages) is supported using all features of numprint. Additional text can be added before 
                  and after the formatted number.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/numprint/numprint.pdf
-- local file:    ./1591557849-numprint.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/numprint
on MikTeX:        numprint
on TeXLive:       numprint
keyword:          numbers (formatting numbers, etc)
keyword:          tagged-pdf-partially (tagged PDF partially compatible)
year:             2012
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

oberdiek -- A bundle of packages submitted by Heiko Oberdiek
------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/oberdiek
name:             oberdiek
caption:          A bundle of packages submitted by Heiko Oberdiek
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
author:           Heiko Oberdiek
copyright:        Heiko Oberdiek (2007, 2009-2011)
copyright:        Oberdiek Package Support Group (2016-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          (2026-05-13)
last changes:     2026-05-13
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The bundle comprises packages to provide:

                  +  bmpsize (https://ctan.org/pkg/bmpsize) : get bitmap size and resolution data;
                  +  centernot (https://ctan.org/pkg/centernot) : a horizontally-centred \not symbol;
                  +  chemarr (https://ctan.org/pkg/chemarr) : extensible chemists’ reaction arrows;
                  +  classlist (https://ctan.org/pkg/classlist) : record information about document class(es) used;

                  +  colonequals (https://ctan.org/pkg/colonequals) : poor man’s mathematical relation symbols;
                  +  dvipscol (https://ctan.org/pkg/dvipscol) : dvips colour stack management;
                  +  engord (https://ctan.org/pkg/engord) : define counter-printing operations producing English ordinals;

                  +  eolgrab (https://ctan.org/pkg/eolgrab) : collect arguments delimited by end of line;
                  +  flags (https://ctan.org/pkg/flags) : setting and clearing flags in bit fields and converting the 
                    bit field into a decimal number;
                  +  holtxdoc (https://ctan.org/pkg/holtxdoc) : extra documentation macros;
                  +  hypbmsec (https://ctan.org/pkg/hypbmsec) : bookmarks in sectioning commands;
                  +  hypgotoe (https://ctan.org/pkg/hypgotoe) : experimental package for links to embedded files;
                  +  hyphsubst (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyphsubst) : substitute hyphenation patterns;
                  +  ifdraft (https://ctan.org/pkg/ifdraft) : switch for option draft;
                  +  iflang (https://ctan.org/pkg/iflang) : provides expandable checks for the current language;
                  +  pdfcolparallel (https://ctan.org/pkg/pdfcolparallel) : fixes colour problems in package parallel 
                    (https://ctan.org/pkg/parallel) ;
                  +  pdfcolparcolumns (https://ctan.org/pkg/pdfcolparcolumns) : fixes colour problems in package parcolumns 
                    (https://ctan.org/pkg/parcolumns) ;
                  +  pdfcrypt (https://ctan.org/pkg/pdfcrypt) : setting PDF encryption;
                  +  protecteddef (https://ctan.org/pkg/protecteddef) : define a command that protected against expansion;

                  +  resizegather (https://ctan.org/pkg/resizegather) : automatically resize overly large equations;

                  +  rotchiffre (https://ctan.org/pkg/rotchiffre) : performs simple rotation cyphers;
                  +  scrindex (https://ctan.org/pkg/scrindex) : redefines environment ‘theindex’ of package ‘index’, 
                    if a class from KOMA-Script is loaded;
                  +  setouterhbox (https://ctan.org/pkg/setouterhbox) : set \hbox in outer horizontal mode;
                  +  settobox (https://ctan.org/pkg/settobox) : getting box sizes;
                  +  stackrel (https://ctan.org/pkg/stackrel) : extensions of the \stackrel command;
                  +  stampinclude (https://ctan.org/pkg/stampinclude) : selects the files for \include by inspecting 
                    the timestamp of the .aux file(s);
                  +  thepdfnumber (https://ctan.org/pkg/thepdfnumber) : canonical numbers for use in PDF files and 
                    elsewhere;
                  +  twoopt (https://ctan.org/pkg/twoopt) : commands with two optional arguments;
Each of the packages is represented by two files, a  .dtx (documented source) and a PDF file; the .ins file 
                  necessary for installation is extracted by running the .dtx file with Plain TeX.

ocgtools -- Manipulate OCG layers in PDF presentations

caption:          Manipulate OCG layers in PDF presentations
author:           Robert Mařík
copyright:        Robert Mařík (2010)
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          0.95a
description:      (no language specified) The package provides the means to insert OGC (Optional Group Content, commonly known as layers) into 
                  PDF presentations. This allows the user to insert any TeX material into separate layers in a PDF document 
                  and also insert links which toggle these layers on and off. Parts of the PDF document, such as formatted 
                  text, tables, maths formulas or graphics may be switched to visible or invisible state by clicking active 
                  links or buttons.

                  The documentation discusses the package’s relation to various apparently similar packages.

ocgx -- Use OCGs within a PDF document without JavaScript
---------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/ocgx
name:             ocgx
caption:          Use OCGs within a PDF document without JavaScript
author:           Paul Gaborit
copyright:        Paul Gaborit (2012)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          0.5
description:      (no language specified) The package extends the  ocg package, which allows you to create OCGs ( 'Optional Content Group' s) 
                  in PDF documents. (The ocg package is distributed as part of Asymptote (https://ctan.org/pkg/asymptote) .)

                  Every OCG includes TeX material into a layer of the PDF file. Each of these layers can be displayed or 
                  not. Links can enable or disable the display of OCGs.

                  The ocgx package does not use Javascript embedded in the PDF document to enable (to show) or disable 
                  (to hide) OCGs.

documentation:    Package demo (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ocgx/demo-ocgx.pdf

octavo -- Typeset books following classical design and layout
-------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/octavo
name:             octavo
caption:          Typeset books following classical design and layout
author:           Stefan A Revets
copyright:        Stefan A. Revets (2003, 2007)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.2
description:      (no language specified) The octavo class is a modification of the standard LaTeX book class. Its purpose is to typeset books 
                  following classical design and layout principles, with the express intention of encouraging the making 
                  of beautiful books by anyone with access to a good printer and with an inclination towards venerable 
                  crafts, e.g., bookbinding.

                  The octavo class differs from the book class by implementing many of the proposals and insights of respected 
                  experts, especially Jan Tschichold and Hugh Williamson.

                  The documentation discusses methods to organise and print out any text into signatures, which can then 
                  be gathered, folded and sewn into a book.

year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) This package is the solution no one asked for, to a problem nobody had.

                  Have you ever thought to yourself “wow, I sure do dislike having to remember multiple macros for my odes 
                  and pdes” and the author of this package has to agree, wholeheartedly. In the modern world of “tik-toking” 
                  and “family guy surfing” our brains have rotted beyond salvage for even basic levels of cognitive recall. 
                  This package aims to fix this, through two macros that have been set to each have an identical form and 
                  function with an emphasis on intuitive use. Through setting options, the multiple common notational style 
                  are easily swapped between, all by a single option.

                  You're Welcome.

ofs -- Macros for managing large font collections
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/ofs
name:             ofs
caption:          Macros for managing large font collections
author:           Petr Olšák
license:          knuth = Knuth License (free)
version:          (2004-05-31)
last changes:     2004-05-31
year:             2004
description:      (no language specified) OFS (Olsak's Font System) is a set of Plain TeX and LaTeX macros for managing large font collections; 
                  it has been used by Czech/Slovak users for many years. Main features include:

                  + Mapping from long names of fonts to the metric file name. The user can specify only exact long names 
                    in documents.
                  + Support for many font encodings.
                  + Printing of catalogues of fonts and test samples of font families; the interactive macro \showfonts shows 
                    all font families you have installed via OFS.
                  + The user interface is the same for Plain TeX and for LaTeX, but the implementation differs: the LaTeX 
                    variant of OFS uses NFSS, but the Plain variant implements its own font management (which may even be 
                    better than NFSS)
                  + Support for math fonts including TX fonts.

documentation:    Package documentation (Czech): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/ofs/doc/ofsdoc.pdf
