pslatex -- Use PostScript fonts by default
------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pslatex
name:             pslatex
caption:          Use PostScript fonts by default
author:           David Carlisle
copyright:        David Carlisle (1994, 1996, 2021, 2023)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          1.3 (2023-06-24)
last changes:     2023-06-24
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) A small package that makes LaTeX default to ‘standard’ PostScript fonts. It is basically a merger of 
                  the  times (https://ctan.org/pkg/times) and the (obsolete) mathptm (https://ctan.org/pkg/mathptm) packages 
                  from the psnfss suite. You must have installed standard LaTeX and the psnfss (https://ctan.org/pkg/psnfss) PostScript 
                  fonts to use this package. The main novel feature is that the pslatex package tries to compensate for 
                  the visual differences between the Adobe fonts by scaling Helvetica by 90%, and ‘condensing’ Courier 
                  (i.e. scaling horizontally) by 85%. The package is supplied with a (unix) shell file for a ‘pslatex‘ 
                  command that allows standard LaTeX documents to be processed, without needing to edit the file.

                  Note that current  psnfss (https://ctan.org/pkg/psnfss) uses a different technique for scaling 
                  Helvetica, and treats Courier as a lost cause (there are better free fixed-width available now, than 
                  there were when pslatex was designed). As a result, pslatex is widely considered obsolete.

documentation:    Package Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/pslatex/README.txt
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/davidcarlisle/dpctex/issues
contact:          repository: https://github.com/davidcarlisle/dpctex
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/pslatex
on MikTeX:        pslatex
on TeXLive:       pslatex
keyword:          font-supp (metrics, macro incantations and other font support)
keyword:          obsolete (package declared obsolete)
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-08-02

psnfss -- Font support for common PostScript fonts
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/psnfss
name:             psnfss
caption:          Font support for common PostScript fonts
author:           Sebastian Rahtz
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
author:           Walter A. Schmidt
author:           Keiran Harcombe
copyright:        Sebastian Rahtz, Walter Schmidt (1995-2020)
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          9.3
description:      (no language specified) Font definition files, macros and font metrics for freely-available Adobe Type 1 fonts. The font set 
                  consists of the ‘LaserWriter 35’ set (originally ‘freely available’ because embedded in PostScript printers), 
                  and a variety of other free fonts, together with some additions. Note that while many of the fonts are 
                  available in PostScript (and other) printers, most publishers require fonts  'embedded' in documents, 
                  which requires that you have the fonts in your TeX system. Fortunately, there are free versions of the 
                  fonts from URW (available in the URW base5 (https://ctan.org/pkg/urw-base35) bundle).

                  The base set of text fonts covered by PSNFSS are: AvantGarde, Bookman, Courier, Helvetica, New Century 
                  Schoolbook, Palatino, Symbol, Times Roman and Zapf Dingbats. In addition, the fonts  Bitstream Charter 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/charter) and Adobe Utopia (https://ctan.org/pkg/utopia) are covered (those 
                  fonts were contributed to the Public Domain by their commercial foundries).

                  Separate packages are provided to load each font for use as main text font. The packages  helvet (https://ctan.org/pkg/helvet) (which 
                  allows Helvetica to be loaded with its size scaled to something more nearly appropriate for its use as 
                  a Sans-Serif font to match Times) and pifont (https://ctan.org/pkg/pifont) (which provides the 
                  means to select single glyphs from symbol fonts) are tailored to special requirements of their fonts.

                  Mathematics are covered by the  mathptmx (https://ctan.org/pkg/mathptmx) package, which constructs 
                  passable mathematics from a combination of Times Roman, Symbol and some glyphs from Computer Modern, 
                  and by Pazo Math (https://ctan.org/pkg/mathpazo) (optionally extended with the fpl (https://ctan.org/pkg/fpl) small-caps 
                  and old-style figures fonts) which uses Palatino as base font, with the mathpazo fonts.

                  The bundle as a whole is part of the  LaTeX ‘required’ (https://ctan.org/pkg/required) set of packages.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/psnfss/psnfss2e.pdf
-- local file:    ./9118348665-psnfss2e.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/psnfss/README
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/psnfss
on MikTeX:        psnfss
on TeXLive:       psnfss
keyword:          tagged-pdf (tagged PDF compatible)
keyword:          font-use (font selection, mapping, etc.)
keyword:          font-supp (metrics, macro incantations and other font support)

language(s):      nls: no language specified

version:          1.0.0
description:      (no language specified) An LED 5 x 7 dot matrix is a rectangular grid of 35 light-emitting diodes arranged in 5 columns and 7 
                  rows. This PSTricks-based graphic art package converts the input text string and maps character data 
                  into precise column and row signals to lit the led display using simple option passed to the commands. 
                  It bridges the gap between retro aesthetic design and professional document typesetting. It allows users 
                  to programmatically generate scalable, clean matrix-style graphics, such as custom alphanumeric characters 
                  or pixel art, without relying on external image editors. It integrates pixel or matrix-style graphics 
                  natively into standard documents, making it ideal for technical documentation, science tutorials, or 
                  retro-computing projects.

pst-cox -- Drawing regular complex polytopes with PSTricks

Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pst-cox
name:             pst-cox
caption:          Drawing regular complex polytopes with PSTricks
author:           Jean-Gabriel Luque
license:          lgpl = GNU Lesser General Public License (free)
version:          0.98 Beta
description:      (no language specified) Pst-cox is a  PSTricks (https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base) package for drawing 2-dimensional projections 
                  of complex regular polytopes (after the work of Coxeter).

                  The package consists of a macro library for drawing the projections. The complex polytopes appear in 
                  the study of the root systems and play a crucial role in many domains related to mathematics and physics. 
                  These polytopes have been completely described by Coxeter in his book “Regular Complex Polytopes”.

                  There exist only a finite numbers of exceptional regular complex polytopes (for example the icosahedron) 
                  and some infinite series (for example, one can construct a multi-dimensional analogue of the hypercube 
                  in any  'finite' dimension).

                  The library contains two packages. The first, pst-coxcoor, is devoted to the exceptional complex regular 
                  polytopes whose coordinates have been pre-computed. The second, pst-coxeterp, is devoted to the infinite 
                  series.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pstricks/contrib/pst-cox/README
documentation:    Documentation for pst-coxeterp (English): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pstricks/contrib/pst-cox/doc/pst-coxeterp/pst-coxeterp_doc.pdf
-- local file:    ./5397629876-pst-coxeterp_doc.pdf
documentation:    Documentation for pst-coxcoor (English): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pstricks/contrib/pst-cox/doc/pst-coxcoor/pst-coxcoor_doc.pdf
-- local file:    ./6615553158-pst-coxcoor_doc.pdf

pst-diffraction -- Print diffraction patterns from various apertures
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pst-diffraction
name:             pst-diffraction
caption:          Print diffraction patterns from various apertures
author:           Herbert Voß
author:           Manuel Luque
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          2.06a
description:      (no language specified) The package enables the user to draw (using  PSTricks (https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base) ) the 
                  diffraction patterns for different geometric forms of apertures for monochromatic light (using PSTricks 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base) ). The aperture stops can have rectangular, circular or triangular 
                  openings. The view of the diffraction may be planar, or three-dimensional.

                  Options available are the dimensions of the aperture under consideration and of the particular optical 
                  setting, e.g. the radius in case of an circular opening. Moreover one can choose the wavelength of the 
                  light (the associated color will be calculated by the package).

pst-func -- PSTricks package for plotting mathematical functions
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pst-func
name:             pst-func
caption:          PSTricks package for plotting mathematical functions
author:           Herbert Voß
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.02a (2024-03-31)
last changes:     2024-03-31
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) The package is built for use with  PSTricks (https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base) . It provides 
                  macros for plotting and manipulating various mathematical functions:

                  + polynomials and their derivatives  'f(x)=an*x^n+an-1*x^(n-1)+...+a0' defined by the coefficients 'a0 
                    a1 a2 ...' and the derivative order;
                  + the Fourier sum  'f(x) = a0/2+a1cos(omega x)+...+b1sin(omega x)+...' defined by the coefficients 'a0 
                    a1 a2 ... b1 b2 b3 ...' ;
                  + the Bessel function defined by its order;
                  + the Gauss function defined by  'sigma' and 'mu' ;
                  + Bézier curves from order 1 (two control points) to order 9 (10 control points);
                  + the superellipse function (the Lamé curve);
                  + Chebyshev polynomials of the first and second kind;
                  + the Thomae (or popcorn) function;
                  + the Weierstrass function;
                  + various integration-derived functions;
                  + normal, binomial, poisson, gamma, chi-squared, student’s t, F, beta, Cauchy and Weibull distribution 
                    functions and the Lorenz curve;
                  + the zeroes of a function, or the intermediate point of two functions;
                  + the  Vasicek function (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasicek_model) for describing the evolution 
                    of interest rates; and
                  + implicit functions.
The plots may be generated as volumes of rotation about the X-axis, as well.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pstricks/contrib/pst-func/doc/pst-func-doc.pdf
-- local file:    ./1616489096-pst-func-doc.pdf

contact:          repository: https://archiv.dante.de/~herbert/TeXnik/

pst-geo -- Geographical Projections
-----------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pst-geo
name:             pst-geo
caption:          Geographical Projections
author:           Herbert Voß
author:           Manuel Luque
author:           Giuseppe Matarazzo
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.09a (2026-06-30)
last changes:     2026-06-30
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package offers a set of  PSTricks (https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base) related packages for 
                  various cartographic projections of the terrestrial sphere. The package pst-map2d provides conventional 
                  projections such as Mercator, Lambert, cylindrical, etc.

                  The package  pst-map3d treats representation in three dimensions of the terrestrial sphere. Packages pst-map2dII and pst-map3dII allow 
                  use of the CIA World DataBank II (http://www.evl.uic.edu/pape/data/WDB/) . Various parameters of 
                  the packages allow for choice of the level of the detail and the layouts possible (cities, borders, rivers 
                  etc).

                  Substantial data files are provided, in an (internally) compressed format. Decompression happens on-the-fly 
                  as a document using the data is displayed, printed or converted to PDF format. A Perl script is provided 
                  for the user to do the decompression, if the need should arise.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pstricks/contrib/pst-geo/README
documentation:    Documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pstricks/contrib/pst-geo/doc/pst-geo-doc.pdf

pst-math -- Enhancement of PostScript math operators to use with PSTricks
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pst-math
name:             pst-math
caption:          Enhancement of PostScript math operators to use with PSTricks
author:           Herbert Voß
author:           Christophe Jorssen
copyright:        Herbert Voss (2023)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          0.67 (2023-07-03)
last changes:     2023-07-03
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) PostScript lacks a lot of basic operators such as tan, acos, asin, cosh, sinh, tanh, acosh, asinh, atanh, 
                  exp (with e base). Also (oddly) cos and sin use arguments in degrees.

                  Pst-math provides all those operators in a header file  pst-math.pro with wrappers pst-math.sty and pst-math.tex .

                  In addition, sinc, gauss, gammaln and bessel are implemented (only partially for the latter). The package 
                  is designed essentially to work with  pst-plot (https://ctan.org/pkg/pst-plot) but can be used 
                  in whatever PS code (such as PSTricks SpecialCoor "!" , which is useful for placing labels).

                  The package also provides a routine SIMPSON for numerical integration and a solver of linear equation 
                  systems.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pstricks/contrib/pst-math/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pstricks/contrib/pst-math/doc/pst-math-doc.pdf
-- local file:    ./3898440870-pst-math-doc.pdf

on MikTeX:        pst-math
on TeXLive:       pst-math

description:      (no language specified) The package defines  \pstODEsolve for solving initial value problems for sets of Ordinary Differential 
                  Equations (ODE) using the Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg (RKF45) method with automatic step size adjustment.

                  The result is stored as a PostScript object and may be plotted later using macros from other PSTricks 
                  packages, such as  \listplot ( pst-plot (https://ctan.org/pkg/pst-plot) ) and \listplotThreeD ( pst-3dplot 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pst-3dplot) ), or may be further processed by user-defined PostScript procedures. 
                  Optionally, the computed state vectors can be written as a table to a text file.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pstricks/contrib/pst-ode/README.md

pst2pdf -- A script to compile PSTricks documents via pdfTeX
------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pst2pdf
name:             pst2pdf
caption:          A script to compile PSTricks documents via pdfTeX
author:           Pablo González Luengo
author:           Herbert Voß
copyright:        Herbert Voß and Pablo González (2011-2020)
license:          gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
version:          0.20
description:      (no language specified) The script extracts the preamble of the document and runs all

                  \begin{postscript}...\end{postscript} 
 \begin{pspicture}...\end{pspicture} and
 \pspicture...\endpspicture 

                  separately through LaTeX with the same preamble as the original document; thus it creates EPS, PNG and 
                  PDF files of these snippets. In a final pdfLaTeX run the script replaces the environments with  \includegraphics to 
                  include the processed snippets.

                  Detail documentation is acquired from the document itself via Perldoc.

pstool -- Support for psfrag within pdfLaTeX
--------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pstool
name:             pstool
caption:          Support for psfrag within pdfLaTeX
author:           Will Robertson
author:           Zebb Prime
copyright:        Will Robertson (2008-2018)
copyright:        Zebb Prime (2008-2014)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.5e (2018-01-20)
last changes:     2018-01-20
year:             2018
description:      (no language specified) The package works in the same sort of way as  pst-pdf (https://ctan.org/pkg/pst-pdf) , but it also 
                  processes the PostScript graphics with psfrag (https://ctan.org/pkg/psfrag) to add labels within 
                  the graphic, before conversion. Thus the bundle replaces two steps of an ordinary workflow. (Naturally, 
                  the package requires that \write 18 is enabled.)

                  Pstool ensures that each version of each graphic is compiled once only (the graphic is (re-)compiled 
                  only if it has changed since the previous compilation of the document). This drastically speeds up the 
                  running of the package in the typical case (though the first run of any document is inevitably just as 
                  slow as with any similar package).

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/pstool/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/pstool/pstool.pdf

on TeXLive:       pstool

pstricks-base -- PostScript macros for TeX
------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base
alias:            pstricks
name:             pstricks-base
caption:          PostScript macros for TeX
author:           Timothy Van Zandt
author:           Denis Girou
author:           Herbert Voß
copyright:        Denis Girou (2000-2003)
copyright:        Herbert Voß (2006-2025)
copyright:        Timothy Van Zandt (1993, 1994, 2000)
copyright:        Herbert Voß and Rolf Niepraschk (2004-2005)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          3.22a (2025-12-13)
last changes:     2025-12-13
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) PSTricks offers an extensive collection of macros for generating PostScript that is usable with most 
                  TeX macro formats, including Plain TeX, LaTeX, AMS-TeX, and AMS-LaTeX. Included are macros for colour, 
                  graphics, pie charts, rotation, trees and overlays. It has many special features, including a wide variety 
                  of graphics (picture drawing) macros, with a flexible interface and with colour support. There are macros 
                  for colouring or shading the cells of tables.

                  The package  pstricks-add (https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-add) contains bug-fixes and additions 
                  for PSTricks (among other things).

                  PSTricks ordinarily uses PostScript  \special commands, which are not supported by pdf(La)TeX. 
                  This limitation may be overcome by using either the pst-pdf (https://ctan.org/pkg/pst-pdf) or the pdftricks 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pdftricks) package, to generate a PDF inclusion from a PSTricks diagram.

                  PSTricks macros can also generate PDF output when the document is processed  XeTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/xetex) , 
                  without the need for other supporting packages.

description:      (no language specified) The font was generated from a MetaPost version of the sources of the  ‘original’ punk font (https://ctan.org/pkg/punk) .

                  font; rather, the font contains several variants of each glyph, and uses the OpenType  'randomize' function

purifyeps -- Make EPS work with both LaTeX/dvips and pdfLaTeX
-------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/purifyeps
name:             purifyeps
caption:          Make EPS work with both LaTeX/dvips and pdfLaTeX
author:           Scott Pakin
copyright:        Scott Pakin (2009)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.1
description:      (no language specified) While pdfLaTeX has a number of nice features, its primary shortcoming relative to standard LaTeX+dvips 
                  is that it is unable to read ordinary Encapsulated PostScript (EPS) files, the most common graphics format 
                  in the LaTeX world. Purifyeps converts EPS files into a ‘purified’ form that can be read by both LaTeX+dvips 
                  and pdfLaTeX. The trick is that the standard LaTeX2e graphics packages can parse MetaPost-produced EPS 
                  directly. Hence, purifyeps need only convert an arbitrary EPS file into the same stylized format that 
                  MetaPost outputs.

pwebmac -- Consolidated WEB macros for DVI and PDF output
---------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pwebmac
name:             pwebmac
caption:          Consolidated WEB macros for DVI and PDF output
author:           Andreas Scherer
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
version:          5.1 (2025-03-16)
last changes:     2025-03-16
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) The original  WEB (https://ctan.org/pkg/web) system by Donald Knuth has the macros webmac.tex that 
                  produce DVI output only; for historic reasons, it will never be modified (apart from catastrophic errors). 
                  Hàn Thế Thành has modified these macros in his pdfwebmac.tex for PDF output (only) with pdfTeX 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pdftex) . Jonathan Kew’s XeTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/xetex) has similar 
                  macros xewebmac.tex by Khaled Hosny that 'modify'  webmac.tex for PDF output; these 
                  macros can only be used with a specific “TeX engine” each.

                  The present  pwebmac package integrates these three WEB macro files similar to cwebmac.tex in 
                  Silvio Levy’s and Don Knuth’s CWEB (https://ctan.org/pkg/cweb) system, so pwebmac.tex can 
                  be used with “plain TeX”, pdfTeX, and XeTeX alike.

                  Its initial application is the production of PDF files for all major WEB programs for “TeX and friends” 
                  as distributed in  TeX Live (https://www.tug.org/texlive) . For this purpose, the shell script makeall was 
                  whipped together; it provides various commandline options and works around several “quirks” in the WEB 
                  sources.

                  WEB programmers who want to use  pwebmac.tex instead of the default webmac.tex in their programs 
                  have to change the first line in the TeX file created by weave . From there, all depends on the 
                  “TeX engine” you use.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/web/pwebmac/README.md
contact:          support: https://lists.tug.org/tex-k
contact:          repository: https://github.com/ascherer/web
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/web/pwebmac
on TeXLive:       pwebmac

name:             pxchfon
caption:          Japanese font setup for pLaTeX and upLaTeX
author:           Takayuki Yato
copyright:        Takayuki YATO (2009-2023)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          2.3
description:      (no language specified) This package enables users to declare in their document which physical fonts should be used for the standard 
                  Japanese (logical) fonts of pLaTeX and upLaTeX. Font setup is realized by changing the font mapping of 
                  dvipdfmx (https://ctan.org/pkg/dvipdfmx) , and thus users can use any (monospaced) physical fonts 
                  they like, once they properly install this package, without creating helper files for each new font.

                  This package also supports setup for the fonts used in the  japanese-otf (https://ctan.org/pkg/japanese-otf) package.

                  System requirements:

                  + TeX format: LaTeX.
                  + TeX engine:  pTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/ptex) or upTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/uptex) .
                  + DVIware:  dvipdfmx (https://ctan.org/pkg/dvipdfmx) .
                  + Prerequisite packages:  atbegshi (https://ctan.org/pkg/atbegshi) .

pxjodel -- Help change metrics of fonts from japanese-otf
---------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pxjodel
name:             pxjodel
caption:          Help change metrics of fonts from japanese-otf
author:           Takayuki Yato
copyright:        Takayuki YATO (aka. “ZR”) (2019-2025)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          0.3a
description:      (no language specified) This package changes the setup of the  japanese-otf (https://ctan.org/pkg/japanese-otf) package 
                  so that the TFMs for direct input are all replaced by new ones with prefixed names; for example, nmlminr-h will 
                  be replaced by foo--nmlminr-h , where foo is a prefix specified by the user.

                  This 
                  function will assist users who want to use the japanese-otf (https://ctan.org/pkg/japanese-otf) package 
                  together with tailored TFMs of Japanese fonts.

                  The “jodel” part of the package name stands for “ 'j' apanese- 'o' tf 'del' uxe”. Here 
                  “deluxe” is the name of japanese-otf (https://ctan.org/pkg/japanese-otf) ’s option for employing 
                  multi-weight Japanese font families. This option is probably the most likely reason for using japanese-otf 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/japanese-otf) . So pxjodel is really about japanese-otf (https://ctan.org/pkg/japanese-otf) ’s 
                  “deluxe” option, hence the name. It is not related to yodel singing, although some sense of word-play 
                  is intended.

pxufont -- Emulate non-Unicode Japanese fonts using Unicode fonts

name:             pxufont
caption:          Emulate non-Unicode Japanese fonts using Unicode fonts

license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          0.7 (2023-07-07)
last changes:     2023-07-07
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) The set of the Japanese logical fonts (JFMs) that are used as standard fonts in  pTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/ptex) and upTeX 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/uptex) contains both Unicode JFMs and non-Unicode JFMs. This bundle provides 
                  an alternative set of non-Unicode JFMs that are tied to the virtual fonts (VFs) that refer to the glyphs 
                  in the Unicode JFMs. Moreover it provides a LaTeX package that redefines the NFSS settings of the Japanese 
                  fonts of (u)pLaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/uplatex) so that the new set of non-Unicode JFMs will 
                  be employed. As a whole, this bundle allows users to dispense with the mapping setup on non-Unicode JFMs.

                  Such a setup is useful in particular when users want to use OpenType fonts (such as Source Han Serif) 
                  that have a glyph encoding different from Adobe-Japan1, because mapping setups from non-Unicode JFMs 
                  to such physical fonts are difficult to prepare.

pyluatex -- Execute Python code on the fly in your LaTeX documents
------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pyluatex
name:             PyLuaTeX
caption:          Execute Python code on the fly in your LaTeX documents
author:           Tobias Enderle
copyright:        Tobias Enderle (2021-2026)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.7.0
description:      (no language specified) PyLuaTeX allows you to execute Python code and to include the resulting output in your LaTeX documents 
                  in a  'single compilation run' . LaTeX documents must be compiled with LuaLaTeX for this to work.

                  PyLuaTeX runs a Python  'InteractiveInterpreter' (actually several if you use different sessions) 
                  in the background for on-the-fly code execution. Python code from your LaTeX file is sent to the background 
                  interpreter through a TCP socket. This approach allows your Python code to be executed and the output 
                  to be integrated in your LaTeX file in a single compilation run. No additional processing steps are needed. 
                  No intermediate files have to be written. No placeholders have to be inserted.

pythonimmediate -- Library to run Python code
---------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pythonimmediate
name:             pythonimmediate
caption:          Library to run Python code
author:           user202729
copyright:        user202729 (2022-2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.6.0 (2025-08-24)
last changes:     2025-08-24
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) Just like  PerlTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/perltex) or PyLuaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/pyluatex) (and 
                  unlike PythonTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/pythontex) or lt3luabridge (https://ctan.org/pkg/lt3luabridge) ), 
                  this only requires a single run, and variables are persistent throughout the run.

                  Unlike PerlTeX or PyLuaTeX, there is no restriction on compiler or script required to run the code.

                  There are also debugging functionalities: TeX errors result in Python traceback, and Python errors result 
                  in TeX traceback. Errors in code executed with the  pycode environment give the correct traceback 
                  point to the Python line of code in the TeX file.

                  For advanced users, this package allows the user to manipulate the TeX state directly from within Python, 
                  so you don’t need to write a single line of TeX code.

                  CAUTION: In addition to this LaTeX package you need the Python  pythonimmediate-tex package, which 
                  can be obtained from https://pypi.org/project/pythonimmediate-tex/ (https://pypi.org/project/pythonimmediate-tex/) .

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/pythonimmediate/README

pythontex -- Run Python from within a document, typesetting the results
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/pythontex
name:             pythontex
caption:          Run Python from within a document, typesetting the results
author:           Geoffrey Poore
copyright:        Geoffrey M. Poore (2012-2026)
license:          bsd3 = 3-clause BSD License (free)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.19 (2026-02-15)
last changes:     2026-02-15
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package allows you to enter Python code within a LaTeX document, execute the code, and access its 
                  output in the original document. There is also support for Bash, JavaScript, Julia, Octave, Perl, R, 
                  Raku (Perl 6), Ruby, Rust, and SageMath.

                  Code is only executed when it has been modified, or when it meets user-specified criteria. Code may be 
                  divided into user-defined sessions, which automatically run in parallel.

                  Errors and warnings are synchronized with the LaTeX document, so that they refer to the document's line 
                  numbers. External dependencies can be tracked, so that code is re-executed when the data it depends on 
                  is modified. PythonTeX also provides syntax highlighting for code in LaTeX documents via the Pygments 
                  syntax highlighter.

                  The package provides a  depythontex utility. This creates a copy of the document in which all Python 
                  code has been replaced by its output. This is useful for journal submissions, sharing documents, and 
                  conversion to other formats.

qcm -- A LaTeX2e class for making multiple choice questionnaires

caption:          A LaTeX2e class for making multiple choice questionnaires
author:           Didier Verna
copyright:        Didier Verna (2004)
license:          lppl1.1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.1 
version:          2.1
description:      (no language specified) QCM is a package for making multiple choices questionnaires under LaTeX2e (“QCM” is the French acronym 
                  for this style of test). A special environment allows you to define questions and possible answers. You 
                  can specify which answers are correct and which are not. QCM not only formats the questions for you, 
                  but also generates a ‘form’ (a grid that your students will have to fill in), and a ‘mask’ (the same 
                  grid, only with correct answers properly checked in). You can then print the mask on a slide and correct 
                  the questionnaires more easily by superimposing the mask on top of students' forms. QCM can also typeset 
                  exam corrections automatically, and comes with support for  AUC-TeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/auctex) .

qrcodetikz -- Prettier QR codes
-------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/qrcodetikz
name:             qrcodetikz
caption:          Prettier QR codes
author:           Miguel Vinícius Santini Frasson
copyright:        Miguel V. S. Frasson (2025)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.0 (2025-05-28)
last changes:     2025-05-28
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This package improves the display of QR codes provided by  qrcode (https://ctan.org/pkg/qrcode) .

                  The Quick Response (QR) codes provided by package  qrcode (https://ctan.org/pkg/qrcode) show white 
                  borders on each square (from little to very prominent, depending on the pdf viewer). This is because 
                  the QR code is printed square by square, not the connected regions of squares as such, and pdf screen 
                  viewers show these undesired borders.

                  This package overwrites the  qrcode (https://ctan.org/pkg/qrcode) printing functions to fill connected 
                  regions of the QR code using TikZ (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) , allowing prettier qrcodes on screen 
                  visualization, with possibility of customization.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/qrcodetikz/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/qrcodetikz/qrcodetikz.pdf
-- local file:    ./7550435849-qrcodetikz.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/qrcodetikz
on MikTeX:        qrcodetikz
on TeXLive:       qrcodetikz
keyword:          qrcode (typeset quick response codes)
keyword:          pgf-tikz (package uses PGF-TikZ)

qtree -- Draw tree structures
-----------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/qtree
name:             qtree
caption:          Draw tree structures
author:           Alexis Dimitriadis
author:           Jeffrey Siskind
copyright:        Alexis Dimitriadis (2006)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          3.1b
description:      (no language specified) The package offers support for drawing tree diagrams, and is especially suitable for linguistics use. 
                  It allows trees to be specified in a simple bracket notation, automatically calculates branch sizes, 
                  and supports both DVI/PostScript and PDF output by use of  pict2e (https://ctan.org/pkg/pict2e) facilities.

description:      (no language specified) This package provides the preferred document class for papers to be submitted to “Quantum — the open 
                  journal of quantum science”. It is based on the widely used  article (https://ctan.org/pkg/article) document 
                  class and designed to allow a seamless transition from documents typeset with the article (https://ctan.org/pkg/article) , revtex4-1 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/revtex4-1) , and elsarticle (https://ctan.org/pkg/elsarticle) document 
                  classes. As a service to authors, the document class comes with a predefined bibilography style quantum.bst that 
                  is optimized to be used with the quantumarticle document class. Additionally, the quantumview documentclass 
                  is provided, which can be used as a proxy to typeset the HTML-only editorial pieces in Quantum Views 
                  in a LaTeX editor.

                  The quantumarticle document class also offers an option to remove the Quantum-related branding. In that 
                  way, users appreciating the esthetics of this document class can use it for their notes as well.

qworld -- Drawing string diagrams for monoidal categories and quantum theory in TeX
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/qworld
name:             QWorld
caption:          Drawing string diagrams for monoidal categories and quantum theory in TeX
author:           Niina Ryota
copyright:        Niina Ryota (2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.1.2
description:      (no language specified) This LaTeX package has been designed for the typesetting of  'graphical languages' grounded in 'monoidal 
                  category theory' and its extensions. It provides a declarative, LaTeX-native interface for rendering 'string 
                  diagrams' , eliminating the need for any external graphics software or manual image management.

                  The package supports a wide spectrum of categorical structures frequently encountered in  'categorical 
                  quantum mechanics' , algebraic structures, and diagrammatic reasoning, including but not limited to:

                  
                  + Monoidal and symmetric monoidal categories
                  + Dual objects and pivotal / rigid categories
                  + Dagger categories
                  + Frobenius algebras and Hopf algebras
                  + Braided, balanced, and ribbon categories
Internally, QWorld builds upon the  TikZ (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) graphics framework, but introduces 
                  a domain-specific layer of abstraction that aligns diagram syntax closely with categorical semantics. 
                  This design facilitates accurate and transparent visual representations of morphisms, tensor products, 
                  and composition, thereby supporting both formal exposition and pedagogical use.

                  QWorld is intended for researchers and educators working in categorical logic, quantum foundations,  'topological 
                  quantum field theory' ( 'TQFT' ), and related domains where graphical calculi constitute an 
                  essential mode of reasoning.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/qworld/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (English) (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/qworld/doc/qworld_en.pdf
-- local file:    ./9922183681-qworld_en.pdf
documentation:    Package documentation (Japanese): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/qworld/doc/qworld.pdf
-- local file:    ./4431714150-qworld.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/qworld

r2bib -- Convert refer and EndNote files to BibTeX
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/r2bib
name:             r2bib
caption:          Convert refer and EndNote files to BibTeX
author:           Richard J Mathar
license:          other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
version:          (2015-12-07)
last changes:     2015-12-07
year:             2015
description:      (no language specified) R2bib and EndNote2bib read files (respectively in refer and EndNote format) and produces a BibTeX reference 
                  list on the standard output.

                  Since refer files are inherently unstructured, r2bib only does a passable job (for example, it may need 
                  to invent a key for an entry, and it has to guess what BibTeX entry type to generate).

                  EndNote tags may not always match those recognised by EndNote2bib; a further filter program EndNoteTag 
                  is provided

author:           Robin Höns

description:      (no language specified) This is a compatible rewrite of  LaTeXDB (https://ctan.org/pkg/latexdb) (by Hans-Georg Eßer) in 
                  Ruby.

                  It is a preprocessor which performs SQL queries on a database and creates LaTeX code for the resulting 
                  rows. Ratexdb implements a few improvements, e.g. regexp postprocessing, command-line options, some protection

rawfonts -- Low level font compatibility mode for LaTeX
-------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/rawfonts
name:             rawfonts
caption:          Low level font compatibility mode for LaTeX
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
author:           Alan Jeffrey
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.01
description:      (no language specified) A package to define the low-level font commands that existed in LaTeX 2.09, for the benefit of old documents 
                  (or packages) that used them.

                  Since this is potentially an expensive operation (loading lots of fonts), the package allows you to chop 
                  and choose:

                  |
\usepackage[only,tenrm,sevsf]{rawfonts}
| will load just  \tenrm and \sevsf . (This facility uses the somedefs (https://ctan.org/pkg/somedefs) package).

description:      (no language specified) The rcs package utilizes the inclusion of RCS supplied data in LaTeX documents. It's upward compatible 
                  to *all* rcs styles I know of.

                  In particular, you can easily

                  + access values of every RCS field in your document
                  + put the checkin date on the titlepage
                  + put RCS fields in a footline

                  You can also configure the rcs package easily to do special things for any keyword.

                  style information for AUC-TeX, and test cases.

readprov -- Provides GetFileInfo without the need to load the file
------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/readprov
name:             readprov
caption:          Provides GetFileInfo without the need to load the file
author:           Uwe Lück
copyright:        Uwe Lück (2008-2010)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.5
description:      (no language specified) The package provides a  \GetFileInfo command (as in the LaTeX standard doc (https://ctan.org/pkg/doc) package, 
                  but without the need to load the doc package). The package also provides new robust (expandable) variants 
                  of \GetFileInfo , even without loading the file itself (reading the file is stopped when the requisite 
                  information is found). So, for example, you can describe packages that are incompatible with each other 
                  or with packages that your document uses, or even report about class files (that are plainly not loadable).

                  Files examined in this way also enter the output of  \listfiles .

                  The package is part of the  fileinfo (https://ctan.org/pkg/fileinfo) bundle.

version:          0.2
description:      (no language specified) The package uses the author’s package  collectbox (https://ctan.org/pkg/collectbox) to define variants 
                  of common box related macros which read the content as real box and not as macro argument. This enables 
                  the use of verbatim or other special material as part of this content.

                  The provided macros have the same names as the original versions but start with an upper-case letter 
                  instead. The “long-form” macros, like  \Makebox , can also be used as environments, but not the 
                  “short-form” macros, like \Mbox . However, normally the long form uses the short form anyway when 
                  no optional arguments are used.

register -- Typeset programmable elements in digital hardware (registers)

name:             register
caption:          Typeset programmable elements in digital hardware (registers)

copyright:        Matthew B. Lovell (2001-2020)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.0 (2020-03-22)
last changes:     2020-03-22
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) This package is designed for typesetting the programmable elements in digital hardware, i.e., registers. 
                  Such registers typically have many fields and can be quite wide; they are thus a challenge to typeset 
                  in a consistent manner. Register is similar in some aspects to the  bytefield (https://ctan.org/pkg/bytefield) and bitpattern 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/bitpattern) packages. Anyone doing hardware documentation using LaTeX should 
                  examine those packages.

                  Register requires version 2001/07/25 or newer of the  float (https://ctan.org/pkg/float) package.

                  An example Perl module and script are provided, to convert the register specifications into structures 
                  suitable for, say, a pre-silicon test environment.

reptheorem -- Repetition of theorem environments
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/reptheorem
name:             reptheorem
caption:          Repetition of theorem environments
author:           Jesse Straat
copyright:        Jesse Straat (2024-)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.4.1 (2025-09-03)
last changes:     2025-09-03
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) When writing a large manuscript, it is sometimes beneficial to repeat a theorem (or lemma or...) at an 
                  earlier or later point for didactical purposes. However,  thmtools (https://ctan.org/pkg/thmtools) ’s 
                  built-in restatable only allows replicating theorems 'after' they have been stated, and only 
                  in the same document.

                  This package solves the issue by making use of the  .aux file, and also introduces its own file 
                  extension, .thm , to replicate theorems in other files.

caption:          Multi-color highlight builder featuring block and inline revision badges
author:           Fu Zhang
copyright:        Fu Zhang (2026)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          1.2
description:      (no language specified) The revbadge package provides an elegant, column-safe framework designed specifically for tracking major 
                  revisions and minor modifications in academic manuscripts. This package can also be used as a handy highlighting 
                  tool.

                  The  revbadge block environment for handling long paragraphs, multi-line equations, lists, and 
                  sections; revbadgemultiline shares the same purpose but allows you to build multi-line badge labels; 
                  and the \revbadgeinline macro for executing tight, mid-sentence word corrections without disrupting 
                  standard line spacing. Both components feature a dynamic colored badge mechanism that labels modifications 
                  on the fly.

                  The package provides native, automated integration with  hyperref (https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref) and cleveref 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/cleveref) under a unified highlight reference counter. Additionally, revbadge 
                  comes pre-packaged with a vibrant, 24-theme colour palette accessible via highly memorable 4-letter macro 
                  colour identifiers (e.g., blue , gren , orng , purp , ylow , grey ).

rmligs -- Remove incorrect ligatures in German documents
--------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/rmligs
name:             rmligs
caption:          Remove incorrect ligatures in German documents
author:           Björn Jacke
copyright:        Björn Jacke (1999-2002)
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          0.84
description:      (no language specified) Ligatures, which are a pleasing feature of TeX's use of fonts, should not be placed in German words between 
                  the word stem and the rest of the word.

                  The rmligs package is a perl script that takes input in ISO 8859-1 or -15, UTF-8 or LaTeX-style umlaut 
                  encodings ( "a , "u , etc.), and inserts a break where an inappropriate ligature would appear. 
                  So, for example, Auflage will be changed to Auf"|lage , which typesets in a typographically 
                  correct fashion.

author:           Rowland McDonnell

description:      (no language specified) The package lets you change page layout parameters in small steps over a range of values using options.

romandeadf -- Romande ADF fonts and LaTeX support
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/romandeadf
name:             romandeadf
caption:          Romande ADF fonts and LaTeX support
author:           Clea F. Rees
license:          gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.1
description:      (no language specified) Romande ADF is a serif font family with oldstyle figures, designed as a substitute for Times, Tiffany 
                  or Caslon. The family currently includes upright, italic and small-caps shapes in each of regular and 
                  demi-bold weights and an italic script in regular. The support package renames the fonts according to 
                  the Karl Berry fontname scheme and defines four families. Two of these primarily provide access to the 
                  “standard” or default characters while the “alternate” families support alternate characters, additional 
                  ligatures and the long s. The included package files provide access to these features in LaTeX as explained 
                  in the documentation.

                  The LaTeX support requires the  nfssext-cfr (https://ctan.org/pkg/nfssext-cfr) and the xkeyval 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/xkeyval) packages.

rotating -- Rotation tools, including rotated full-page floats
--------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/rotating
name:             rotating
caption:          Rotation tools, including rotated full-page floats
author:           Sebastian Rahtz
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
author:           Robin Fairbairns
copyright:        Sebastian Rahtz and Leonor Barroca (1995-1999)
copyright:        Robin Fairbairns (2001-2003, 2007-2009)
copyright:        LaTeX3 Project (2016-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.16e (2026-05-17)
last changes:     2026-05-17
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) A package built on the standard LaTeX  graphics (https://ctan.org/pkg/graphics) package to perform 
                  all the different sorts of rotation one might like, including complete figures and tables with their 
                  captions.

                  If you want continuous text (i.e., more than one page) set in landscape mode, use the  lscape (https://ctan.org/pkg/lscape) package 
                  instead. The rotating packages only deals in rotated boxes (or floats, which are themselves boxes), and 
                  boxes always stay on one page.

                  If you need to use the facilities of the  float (https://ctan.org/pkg/float) in the same document, 
                  load rotating.sty via rotfloat (https://ctan.org/pkg/rotfloat) , which smooths the path between 
                  the rotating and float packages.

                  The package is now part of the  latex-graphics (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-graphics) bundle, which 
                  is one of the collections in the LaTeX ‘required’ (https://ctan.org/pkg/required) set of packages.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/graphics/rotating.pdf

rtkinenc -- Input encoding with fallback procedures
---------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/rtkinenc
name:             rtkinenc
caption:          Input encoding with fallback procedures
author:           Lars Hellström
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) The rtkinenc package is functionally similar to the standard LaTeX package  inputenc (https://ctan.org/pkg/inputenc) : 
                  both set up active characters so that an input character outside the range of 7-bit visible ASCII is 
                  converted into one or more corresponding LaTeX commands. The main difference lies in that rtkinenc allows 
                  the user to specify a fallback procedure to use when the text command corresponding to some input character 
                  isn't available.

                  Names of commands in rtkinenc have been selected so that it can read inputenc encoding definition files, 
                  and the aim is that rtkinenc should be backwards compatible with inputenc. rtkinenc is not a new version 
                  of inputenc though, nor is it part of standard LaTeX.

                  For an example of how rtkinenc is used, the user may look at the  tclldoc (https://ctan.org/pkg/tclldoc) class.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/rtkinenc/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/rtkinenc/rtkinenc-doc.pdf
-- local file:    ./6652576125-rtkinenc-doc.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/rtkinenc
on MikTeX:        rtkinenc
on TeXLive:       rtkinenc
keyword:          inputenc (input encoding support for TeX engines)
year:             without year
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

runtexfile -- Automate the process of compiling (La)TeX documents with index, bibliography, …
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/runtexfile
name:             runtexfile
caption:          Automate the process of compiling (La)TeX documents with index, bibliography, …
author:           Herbert Voß
copyright:        Herbert Voß (2025)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.06 (2025-10-08)
last changes:     2025-10-08
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This package provides a small script like  latexmk (https://ctan.org/pkg/latexmk) to run a TeX 
                  or LaTeX document controlled from within the document itself. The commands have to be defined at the 
                  beginning of the document, e.g.:

                  |
%! HV lualatex --shell-escape
%! HV biber
%! HV lualatex --shell-escape 
%! HV xindex 
%! HV xindex  --config DIN2 -l DE -o test2.vwd 
%! HV xindex --config DIN2 -l DE -o test2.dbd 
%! HV lualatex --shell-escape 
%! HV lualatex --shell-escape 

\documentclass[...]{...} 
…
| The script itself does not parse the log file.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/runtexfile/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/runtexfile/doc/runtexfile-doc.pdf

keyword:          compilation (the document compilation process)

year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) In short, a TeX-style shebang ( %#! ) is a special kind of TeX comment that you include in your 
                  TeX/LaTeX document file to tell the operating system’s shell how to run the file for the rest of the 
                  file:

%#!lualatex foo.tex
\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
Hello, {\LaTeX} World!

Happy {\TeX}ing.
\end{document}

If you are using a TeX-style shebang, it must appear on the line that matched 20 lines or less in your 
                  LaTeX document, and it has to start with a TeX comment symbol ( % ) followed by a hash sign ( # ) 
                  and an exclamation mark ( ! ), colloquially known as the bang, hence the name shebang for TeX/LaTeX.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): pkg:/README.md
home page:        https://github.com/munepi/runtexshebang
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/munepi/runtexshebang/issues
contact:          repository: https://github.com/munepi/runtexshebang.git
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/runtexshebang
on MikTeX:        runtexshebang
on TeXLive:       runtexshebang

rviewport -- Relative Viewport for Graphics Inclusion
-----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/rviewport
name:             rviewport
caption:          Relative Viewport for Graphics Inclusion
author:           Boris Veytsman
copyright:        Boris Veytsman (2011)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) Package  graphicx (https://ctan.org/pkg/graphicx) provides a useful keyword viewport which allows 
                  to show just a part of an image. However, one needs to put there the actual coordinates of the viewport 
                  window. Sometimes it is useful to have relative coordinates as fractions of natural size. For example, 
                  one may want to print a large image on a spread, putting a half on a verso page, and another half on 
                  the next recto page. For this one would need a viewport occupying exactly one half of the file's bounding 
                  box, whatever the actual width of the image may be.

                  This package adds a new keyword rviewport to the graphicx package specifying Relative Viewport for graphics 
                  inclusion: a window defined by the given fractions of the natural width and height of the image.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/rviewport/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/rviewport/rviewport.pdf

rvwrite -- Increase the number of available output streams in LaTeX
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/rvwrite
name:             rvwrite
caption:          Increase the number of available output streams in LaTeX
author:           C. V. Radhakrishnan
copyright:        C. V. Radhakrishnan (2010)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          1.2
description:      (no language specified) The package addresses, for LaTeX documents, the severe limitation on the number of output streams that 
                  TeX provides.

                  The package uses a single TeX output stream, and writes “marked-up” output to this stream. The user may 
                  then post-process the marked-up output file, using LaTeX, and the document’s output appears as separate 
                  files, according to the calls made to the package.

                  The output to be post-processed uses macros from the widely-available  ProTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/protex) package.

sam2p -- Convert bitmap formats to compact PS/PDF
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/sam2p
name:             sam2p
caption:          Convert bitmap formats to compact PS/PDF
author:           Péter Szabó
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          0.49.4
description:      (no language specified) Sam2p is a UNIX command line utility written in ANSI C++ that converts many raster (bitmap) image formats 
                  into Adobe PostScript or PDF files and several other formats. The images are not vectorized. sam2p gives 
                  full control to the user to specify standards-compliance, compression, and bit depths. In some cases 
                  sam2p can compress an image 100 times smaller than the PostScript output of many other common image converters. 
                  Sam2p provides ZIP, RLE and LZW (de)compression filters even on output destined for PostScript Level 
                  1 devices.

                  The author provides a script bundle,  a2ping (https://ctan.org/pkg/a2ping) , that uses sam2p as

savesym -- Redefine symbols where names conflict
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/savesym
name:             savesym
caption:          Redefine symbols where names conflict
author:           Jürgen Göbel
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.2 (2013-09-02)
last changes:     2013-09-02
year:             2013
description:      (no language specified) There are a number of symbols (e.g.,  \Square ) that are defined by several packages. In order 
                  to typeset all the variants in a document, we have to give the glyph a unique name. To do that, we define \savesymbol{XXX} , 
                  which renames a symbol from \XXX to \origXXX , and \restoresymbols{yyy}{XXX} , which 
                  renames \origXXX back to \XXX and defines a new command, \yyyXXX , which corresponds 
                  to the most recently loaded version of \XXX .

description:      (no language specified) The goal of the savetrees package is to pack as much text as possible onto each page of a LaTeX document.

                  paper when printing draft copies of a document. It can also be useful when trying to meet a tight page-length 
                  requirement for a conference or journal submission.

                  Most of the package options cover specific modifications to typesetting rules, but there are also options 
                  subtle , moderate and extreme options for the “broad brush” approach.

scalefnt -- Rescale fonts to arbitrary sizes
--------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/scalefnt
name:             scalefnt
caption:          Rescale fonts to arbitrary sizes
author:           David Carlisle
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
description:      (no language specified) \scalefont{2} selects the current font in twice the current size. \scalefont{.75} reduces 
                  the current font size by three quarters.

                  Note that the effectiveness of such operations depends on the LaTeX font selection for that font; it 
                  will typically work well for ordinary Type 1 fonts, but Metafont fonts are usually set up to work only 
                  at a discrete set of sizes.

                  The package is distributed as part of the  carlisle (https://ctan.org/pkg/carlisle) bundle.

sciposter -- Make posters of ISO A3 size and larger
---------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/sciposter
name:             sciposter
caption:          Make posters of ISO A3 size and larger
author:           Michael Wilkinson
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.18
description:      (no language specified) This collection of files contains LaTeX packages for posters of ISO A3 size and larger (ISO A0 is the 
                  default size). American paper sizes and custom paper are supported. In particular, sciposter.cls defines 
                  a document class which allows cutting and pasting most of an article to a poster without any editing 
                  (save reducing the size) — see the manual.

                  Sciposter does work for LaTeX, not just pdfLaTeX. However, xdvi produces strange results, though a recent 
                  version of dvips does create good ps-files from the dvi files.

                  Also note that logos must either be put in the current working directory or in the directories of your 
                  LaTeX distribution. For some reason graphicspath settings are ignored.

description:      (no language specified) This package allows you to create and print scrambled environments for purposes such as randomized hint 
                  environments. You can mark a location with a series of hints, and then print the hints at the end in 
                  a pseudo-random order.

                  The general structure follows: there is an outer environment which creates the label, an inner environment

                  This generalizes beyond hints; one can create scrambled solutions as well, etc.

scrhack -- Compatibility package to emulate the former KOMA-Script package scrhack
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/scrhack
name:             scrhack
caption:          Compatibility package to emulate the former KOMA-Script package scrhack
author:           Markus Kohm
copyright:        Markus Kohm (2008-2024)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          3.42 (2024-09-04)
last changes:     2024-09-04
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) Up to version 3.41, the scrhack package was part of  KOMA-Script (https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script) . 
                  It was originally intended to improve the compatibility of third-party packages with KOMA-Script. However, 
                  most of the so-called hacks also added additional functionality to the corresponding third-party package. 
                  On the other hand, it was sometimes urgent to react to a change in such a third-party package, which 
                  was difficult to do from within a large collection like KOMA-Script. Therefore, the scrhack part of KOMA-Script 
                  was split into several independent packages. And the scrhack spin-off was made to emulate the former 
                  KOMA-Script package of the same name.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): pkg:/scrhack.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): pkg:/README.md
home page:        https://github.com/komascript/third-party-enhancements
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/komascript/third-party-enhancements/issues
contact:          repository: https://github.com/komascript/third-party-enhancements/tree/main/scrhack
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/scrhack
on MikTeX:        scrhack
on TeXLive:       scrhack
keyword:          bugfix (correct a problem, ahead of the “proper” fix)
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/scrindex
name:             scrindex
caption:          Make index package work with KOMA-Script classes
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
author:           Heiko Oberdiek
copyright:        Heiko Oberdiek (2008)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.2 (2016-05-16)
last changes:     2016-05-16
year:             2016
description:      (no language specified) This package redefines environment `theindex' of package `index', if a class from  KOMA-Script (https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script) is 
                  loaded. Also option `idxtotoc' is supported. Index preambles can be given either by means of package 
                  `index' or via the interface provided by KOMA-Script (https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script) .

                  The package is part of the  oberdiek (https://ctan.org/pkg/oberdiek) bundle.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/oberdiek/scrindex.pdf

installation:     https://ctan.org/tex-archive/install/macros/latex/contrib/oberdiek.tds.zip
on MikTeX:        oberdiek
on TeXLive:       oberdiek
keyword:          index (index support)
language(s):      nls: no language specified

scripture -- A LaTeX style for typesetting Bible quotations
-----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/scripture
name:             scripture
caption:          A LaTeX style for typesetting Bible quotations
author:           David Purton
copyright:        David Purton (2022-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.4 (2026-06-12)
last changes:     2026-06-12
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The  scripture package provides a set of macros for typesetting quotations from the Bible. It provides 
                  many features commonly seen in Bibles such as dropped text for chapter numbers, superscripts for verse 
                  numbers, indented lines for poetry sections, narrow sections and hanging paragraphs. A reference for 
                  the quotation can optionally be added.

                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script) itself.

---------------------------------------------------------------------

caption:          Control note columns parallel to the main text
author:           Markus Kohm
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.3.4145 (2025-05-13)
last changes:     2025-05-13
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) The package provides an end user interface to define and manage note columns, above  scrlayer (https://ctan.org/pkg/scrlayer) .

                  The note columns provide similar facilities to those of the LaTeX  \marginpar command, extending 
                  them to more than a single column. The package provides page breaks inside note columns, and synchronisation 
                  between the main text and note columns.

scrlayer-scrpage -- Define and manage page styles
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/scrlayer-scrpage
name:             scrlayer-scrpage
caption:          Define and manage page styles
author:           Markus Kohm
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          3.49 (2026-02-02)
last changes:     2026-02-02
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package is the part of the  Koma-Script (https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script) bundle that provides 
                  an end user interface to scrlayer (https://ctan.org/pkg/scrlayer) , allowing the user to define 
                  and manage page styles by controlling page headers and footers. The end user interface is compatible 
                  enough to that of the earlier scrpage2 (https://ctan.org/pkg/scrpage2) package, so that users should 
                  easily be able to switch from the older package to the newer, more powerful, one.

selnolig -- Selectively disable typographic ligatures
-----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/selnolig
name:             selnolig
caption:          Selectively disable typographic ligatures
author:           Mico Loretan
copyright:        Mico Loretan (2013-2015)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.302 (2015-10-26)
last changes:     2015-10-26
year:             2015
description:      (no language specified) The package suppresses typographic ligatures selectively, i.e., based on predefined search patterns. 
                  The search patterns focus on ligatures deemed inappropriate because they span morpheme boundaries. For 
                  example, the word  shelfful , which is mentioned in the TeXbook as a word for which the ff ligature 
                  might be inappropriate, is automatically typeset as shelf\/ful rather than as shel{ff}ul .

                  For English and German language documents, the package provides extensive rules for the selective suppression 
                  of so-called “common” ligatures. These comprise the  ff , fi , fl , ffi , and ffl ligatures 
                  as well as the ft and fft ligatures. Other f-ligatures, such as fb , fh , fj and fk , 
                  are suppressed globally, while exceptions are made for names and words of non-English/German origin, 
                  such as Kafka and fjord .

                  For English language documents, the package further provides ligature suppression macros for a number 
                  of so-called “discretionary” or “rare” ligatures such as  ct , st , and sp .

                  The package requires use of a recent LuaLaTeX format (for example those from TeX Live 2012 or 2013, or 
                  MiKTeX 2.9).

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/selnolig/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/selnolig/selnolig.pdf
-- local file:    ./5151174600-selnolig.pdf
contact:          repository: https://github.com/micoloretan/selnolig
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/selnolig
on MikTeX:        selnolig
on TeXLive:       selnolig
keyword:          luatex (LuaTeX and packages that require it)
keyword:          tagged-pdf (tagged PDF compatible)

semantex -- Semantic, keyval-based mathematics
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/semantex
name:             SemanTeX
caption:          Semantic, keyval-based mathematics
author:           Sebastian Ørsted
copyright:        Sebastian Ørsted (2020-2023)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.525 (2023-01-23)
last changes:     2023-01-23
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) The SemanTeX package for LaTeX delivers a more semantic, systematized way of writing mathematics, compared 
                  to the classical math syntax in LaTeX. The system uses keyval syntax, and the user can define their own 
                  keys and customize the system down to the last detail. At the same time, care has been taken to make 
                  the syntax as simple, natural, practical, and lightweight as possible.

                  Furthermore, the package has a companion package, called stripsemantex, which allows you to completely 
                  strip your documents of SemanTeX markup to prepare them e.g. for publication.

                  The package is still in beta, but is considered feature-complete and more or less stable, so using it 
                  at this point should be safe. Still, suggestions, ideas, and bug reports are more than welcome!

version:          (2020-01-29)
last changes:     2020-01-29
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) The package provides simple commands to allow authors (especially scholars in the humanities) to write 
                  with a focus on content rather than presentation. The commands are inspired by the XML elements of the 
                  Text Encoding Initiative (https://www.tei-c.org) . Commands like \term and \foreign are 
                  aliases for \emph . \quoted and \soCalled are aliases for quoting commands. These commands 
                  could be easily redefined for different formats.

                  The package also provides a footnote environment so that long footnotes can be more cleanly separated 
                  from the main text.

                  Because the author is a music scholar, the package also includes some macros for musical symbols and 
                  other basic notations for musical analysis.
