description:      (no language specified) When one needs to type long sequences of letters (such as in base-sequences in genes) or of numbers (such 
                  as calculations of transcendental numbers), there's no obvious break points to be found. The package 
                  provides a command  \seqsplit , which makes its argument splittable anywhere, and then leaves the 
                  TeX paragraph-maker to do the splitting.

                  While the package may obviously be used to typeset DNA sequences, the user may consider the  dnaseq 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/dnaseq) as a rather more powerful alternative.

setbuilder -- Mathematical sets with correctly scaled braces and separator
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/setbuilder
name:             setbuilder
caption:          Mathematical sets with correctly scaled braces and separator
author:           Vseslav Sekorin
copyright:        Vseslav Sekorin (2026)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          0.2.0
description:      (no language specified) The package provides a  \set command for set-builder notation: \set{x \in \mathbb{R} \given 
                  x^2 &lt; 2} . The separator (a vertical bar, or a colon with the colon option) is typeset with 
                  correct thin spaces, which automatically vanish in sub- and superscripts. The starred form \set* scales 
                  the braces and the separator together; \set[\Big] sets a fixed size. A synonym=&lt;name&gt; package 
                  option defines the same command under a different name, e.g. when \set is already taken by another 
                  package. The package is based on mathtools (https://ctan.org/pkg/mathtools) .

&amp;$L$ &amp;$M$\\

$B$ &amp;$3,0$ &amp;$0,9$

shadethm -- Theorem environments that are shaded
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/shadethm
name:             Shaded theorems
caption:          Theorem environments that are shaded
author:           Jim Hefferon
copyright:        Jim Hefferon (1999-2020)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          (2020-01-08)
last changes:     2020-01-08
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) Extends the  \newtheorem command. If you say \newshadetheorem{theorem}{Theorem} in the preamble 
                  then your regular \begin{theorem} .. \end{theorem} will produce a theorem statement in a shaded 
                  box. It supports all the options of \newtheorem , including forms \newshadetheorem{..}[..]{..} and \newshadetheorem{..}{..}[..] .

                  Environments declared using the package require their body to remain on one page; the  mdframed (https://ctan.org/pkg/mdframed) package 
                  can frame and shade theorems, and 'its' environments break at the end of a page; users are generally 
                  recommended, therefore, to use mdframed (https://ctan.org/pkg/mdframed) .

                  In the same spirit, the author told us in January 2020: “These materials are obsolete. There are a number 
                  of more recent, more powerful packages that have capabilities that greatly extend the simple ones here. 
                  A new project should use one of those. These files only continue to be available to help people who are 
                  working with an old project.”

shapepar -- A macro to typeset paragraphs in specific shapes
------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/shapepar
name:             shapepar
caption:          A macro to typeset paragraphs in specific shapes
author:           Donald Arseneau
copyright:        Donald Arseneau (1993, 2002, 2006)
license:          other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
version:          2.2
description:      (no language specified) \shapepar is a macro to typeset paragraphs in a specific shape. The size is adjusted automatically so 
                  that the entire shape is filled with text. There may not be displayed maths or ‘ \vadjust ’ material 
                  (no \vspace ) in the argument of \shapepar . The macros work for both LaTeX and plain TeX. 
                  For LaTeX, specify \usepackage{shapepar} ; for Plain, \input shapepar.sty .

                  \shapepar works in terms of user-defined shapes, though the package does provide some predefined 
                  shapes: so you can form any paragraph into the form of a heart by putting \heartpar{sometext...} inside 
                  your document. The tedium of creating these polygon definitions may be alleviated by using the shapepatch 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/shapepatch) extension to transfig (https://ctan.org/pkg/transfig) which 
                  will convert xfig output to \shapepar polygon form.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/shapepar/shapepar.pdf
-- local file:    ./7111643909-shapepar.pdf
documentation:    Package README (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/shapepar/README.shapepar
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/shapepar
on MikTeX:        shapepar
on TeXLive:       shapepar
keyword:          tagged-pdf-incompatible (tagged PDF incompatible)
keyword:          parshape (non-standard paragraph shapes)
keyword:          text-flow (flow text round an insertion in the paragraph)
keyword:          micro-layout (paragraph shapes, margin adjustments, etc.)
year:             2006
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14


shapepatch -- Transfig patch supporting shapepar
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/shapepatch
name:             shapepatch
caption:          Transfig patch supporting shapepar
author:           Christian Gollwitzer
license:          bsd = BSD Style License (free)
version:          1.1
description:      (no language specified) ShapePatch is a patch against  Transfig (https://ctan.org/pkg/transfig) , which adds the capability 
                  to export XFig (https://ctan.org/pkg/xfig) figures to shape definitions for shapepar (https://ctan.org/pkg/shapepar) . 
                  Shapepar itself will form a paragraph into a specified shape, and the size of the shape is automatically 
                  adjusted so that the given paragraph completely fills the shape. ShapePatch effort: one simply draws 
                  the required shape with XFig and then convert it to a shape definition for shapepar, either by calling 
                  fig2dev manually or by choosing “Export/Shape” in XFig (if you install the additional XFig patch).

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/transfig-shapepatch/shapepatch.README
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/transfig-shapepatch/shape-patch.3.2.4-shape-1.1.tar.gz

keyword:          micro-layout (paragraph shapes, margin adjustments, etc.)
year:             without year

last access:      2026-07-14

shipunov -- A collection of LaTeX packages and classes
------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/shipunov
name:             shipunov
caption:          A collection of LaTeX packages and classes
author:           Alexey Shipunov
copyright:        Alexey Shipunov (2010-2019)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.2
description:      (no language specified) The bundle collects packages and classes, along with one bibliography style and examples and scripts 
                  for converting TeX files. Many of the files in the collection are designed to support field biologists 
                  and/or Russian writers, while others have wider application.

                  The collection includes:

                  + add2 – Save trees. Quick way to fit as many as possible into one page.  Good for handouts.
                  +  altverse (https://ctan.org/pkg/altverse) – Typesetting verses. Straightforward typesetting, using 
                    the xtab (https://ctan.org/pkg/xtab) package to aid layout.
                  +  autolist (https://ctan.org/pkg/autolist) – More lists. A means to define various sorts of list.

                  +  biokey (https://ctan.org/pkg/biokey) – Flexible identification key tables in LaTeX. The package 
                    provides straightforward macros to typeset sets of biological identification keys. Layout is flexible, 
                    and the macros will be useful in other disciplines.
                  +  biolist (https://ctan.org/pkg/biolist) – List observed species. Pretty formatting of species lists 
                    of flora and fauna.
                  +  boldline (https://ctan.org/pkg/boldline) – Heavier lines in tables. The package provides commands 
                    replacing \hline and \cline , as well as a table preamble element that generates heavy lines.

                  +  cassete (https://ctan.org/pkg/cassette-shipunov) (with one ‘t’) – Print labels for audio cassettes. 
                    This is a LaTeX2e class file (the only other cassette package on CTAN is cassette (https://ctan.org/pkg/cassette) (with 
                    two ‘t’), written for Plain TeX).
                  +  classif2 (https://ctan.org/pkg/classif2) – Biological classification tables. The package defines 
                    an environment classif that simplifies the process of typesetting classification tables.
                  + dline – Double line on the left of text.
                  +  drcaps (https://ctan.org/pkg/drcaps) – Simple dropped capitals. The package offers simple macros 
                    for dropped capitals, in a couple of forms.
                  + etiketka – Class for typesetting business-card-sized information (including business cards).
                  + flower – Typesetting lists of flower formulas.
                  + isyntax – Interactively check LaTeX file syntax.
                  + numerus – Spell numbers in Russian words.
                  + punct – Within italicized text, punctuation is still straight, this is typographically more aesthetic.

                  + qqru – Universal quotation marks, for Russian and English. It is able also to convert uniform typewriter 
                    “quotes” into left or right typographic quotes.
                  + rusnat – Bibliography style file, now deprecated.
                  +  sltables (https://ctan.org/pkg/sltables) – Simplified tables for LaTeX. These macros develop the 
                    concepts of the stables, which are designed to offer table macros whose use is “as simple as one might 
                    hope”. Some would claim that LaTeX’s built-in table specifications are as simple as one might hope, but 
                    this package offers many short-cuts and optimization of the mechanisms of tables.
                  + starfn – Stars as footnote marks.
                  + textfrac – Simple slanted fractions.

documentation:    Readme (English): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/shipunov/doc/README
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/shipunov
on MikTeX:        shipunov
on TeXLive:       shipunov
keyword:          collection (a collection of packages)
year:             2019

                  document. In particular, the multiple calls of the LaTeX command necessary in order to create a table

                  or PDF format) by calling an external program. It is possible to stress characters in documents wich 
                  use the \input and \include commands to make references to some external files, and that in a transparent 
                  way by compiling only the main source file. Available in English and French languages.

                  Latin, and Cyrillic scripts. It is available in two weights—regular and bold. The font is designed with

                  scientific and technical documents.

                  Bombay (https://www.iitb.ac.in) , and builds upon the following two fonts for its Devanāgarī and Latin 
                  components respectively: (i) Yashomudra (https://github.com/RajyaMarathiVikasSanstha/Yashomudra) by Rājya 
                  Marāṭhī Vikās Saṃsthā (https://rmvs.marathi.gov.in/) , and (ii) PT Serif (https://fonts.google.com/specimen/PT+Serif) by ParaType 
                  (https://www.paratype.com) . We would like to thank both these organisations for releasing their fonts 
                  under the SIL Open Font Licence, which has enabled us to create Shobhika.

sidenotesplus -- Place referenced notes, alerts, figures and tables into the document margin
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/sidenotesplus
name:             sidenotesplus
caption:          Place referenced notes, alerts, figures and tables into the document margin
author:           Anton Vrba
copyright:        Anton Vrba (2022-2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.05 (2025-02-18)
last changes:     2025-02-18
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) Sidenotesplus is a comprehensive package for placing labeled or referenced notes, temporary alerts, bibliography 
                  references, figures and tables into the margin. Marginals can be either floated or at fixed positions 
                  relative to the text. Twoside symmetry is preserved. For BibLaTeX users, macros for side references are 
                  provided.

                  Three margin styles are provided. Two-page symmetric layouts either as (i) Ragged outer with note reverences 
                  in the margin separator or (ii) justified with last line ragged outer. And (iii) a classic look, justified 
                  with last line ragged right and note reference to the left of the note, but two-page symmetry is lost.

                  The command  \sidenote mimics the \footnote command and provides labelled (numbers, alphabetic, 
                  roman) references. However, un-numbered and custom symbols can also be specified.

                  Temporary sidealerts are rendered only if the package option  alerton is specified. Alerts are 
                  useful as to do reminders during document development.

                  Furthermore, captions for figures and tables can also be placed into margin. Also, full width environments 
                  for figures, tables and text are provided. The text environment can be partially widened, suitable if 
                  that extra space for an equation is required.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/sidenotesplus/README.txt
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/sidenotesplus/sidenotesplus.pdf

description:      (no language specified) This package provides a simple way for typesetting grammars in Backus-Naur form (BNF). The included  bnf environment 
                  parses BNF expressions (possibly annotated), so users can write readable BNF expressions in their documents. 
                  It features a flexible configuration system, allowing for the customization of the domain-specific language 
                  (DSL) used in typesetting the grammar. Additionally, the package comes with sensible defaults.

                  The package requires  expl3 (https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3) , xparse (https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse) , mathtools 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/mathtools) , and tabularray. (https://ctan.org/pkg/tabularray) .

simpler-wick -- Simpler Wick contractions
-----------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/simpler-wick
name:             simpler-wick
caption:          Simpler Wick contractions
author:           Joshua Ellis
copyright:        Joshua Ellis (2014-2015)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.0.0 (2015-12-11)
last changes:     2015-12-11
year:             2015
description:      (no language specified) In every quantum field theory course, there will be a chapter about Wick’s theorem and how it can be 
                  used to convert a very large product of many creation and annihilation operators into something more 
                  tractable and normal ordered.

                  The contractions are denoted with a square bracket over the operators which are being contracted, which 
                  used to be rather annoying to typeset in LaTeX as the only other package available was  simplewick 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/simplewick) , which is rather unwieldy.

                  This package provides a simpler syntax for Wick contractions.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/simpler-wick/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/simpler-wick/simpler-wick.pdf

on TeXLive:       simpler-wick

                  as books, theses, or extensive lecture notes.

                  The core design philosophy of this package is to maximize the separation of content and structure. It 
                  provides an automated file and block management system that frees content creators from constantly managing 
                  global document structure and stylistic details.

                  Key features include:

                  + Automated subfile management: Section files are automatically added to the TOC upon import.
                  + A flexible Block System for theorems, definitions, and proofs.
                  + Dynamic cross-referencing that generates and manages anchors automatically.
                  + Automated generation of block indexes (e.g., List of Theorems).
                  + Highly customizable styling via dynamic display arguments and conditional statements.

siunitx -- A comprehensive (SI) units package
---------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/siunitx
name:             siunitx
caption:          A comprehensive (SI) units package
author:           Joseph Wright
copyright:        Joseph Wright (2008-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          3.5.5 (2026-05-15)
last changes:     2026-05-15
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) Physical quantities have both numbers and units, and each physical quantity should be expressed as the 
                  product of a number and a unit. Typesetting physical quantities requires care to ensure that the combined 
                  mathematical meaning of the number-unit combination is clear. In particular, the SI units system lays 
                  down a consistent set of units with rules on how these are to be used.

                  However, different countries and publishers have differing conventions on the exact appearance of numbers 
                  (and units). The  siunitx package provides a set of tools for authors to typeset quantities in 
                  a consistent way. The package has an extended set of configuration options which make it possible to 
                  follow varying typographic conventions with the same input syntax. The package includes automated processing 
                  of numbers and units, and the ability to control tabular alignment of numbers.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): pkg:/README.md

version:          1.5.3
description:      (no language specified) This package provides macros and fonts in Metafont format which can be used to typeset chess games using 
                  PGN, and to show diagrams of the current board in a document. The package builds on  work by Piet 
                  Tutelaers (https://ctan.org/pkg/chess) — the main novelty is the use of PGN for input instead of the 
                  more cumbersome coordinate notation ( g1f3 becomes the more readable Nf3 in PGN).

                  An Adobe Type 1 implementation of skak's fonts is available as package  skaknew (https://ctan.org/pkg/skaknew) ; 
                  an alternative chess notational scheme is available in package texmate (https://ctan.org/pkg/texmate) , 
                  and a general mechanism for selecting chess fonts is provided in chessfss (https://ctan.org/pkg/chessfss) .

skb -- Tools for a repository of long-living documents
------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/skb
name:             skb
caption:          Tools for a repository of long-living documents
author:           Sven van der Meer
copyright:        Sven van der Meer (2010)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.52
description:      (no language specified) The package provides macros that help to build a document repository for long living documents. It focuses 
                  on structure and re-use of text, code, figures etc. The basic concept is first to separate structure 
                  from content (i.e., text about a topic from the structure it is presented by) and then separating the 
                  content from the actual published document, thus enabling easy re-use of text blocks in different publications 
                  (i.e., text about a protocol in a short article about this protocol as well as in a book about many protocols); 
                  all without constantly copying or changing text.

                  As a side effect, using the document classes provided, it hides a lot of LaTeX from someone who just 
                  wants to write articles and books.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/skb/README
documentation:    User guide (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/skb/doc/user-guide.pdf

-- local file:    ./8324262727-skb.pdf
contact:          repository: https://sourceforge.net/projects/latex-skb
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/skb
on MikTeX:        skb

keyword:          archival (creating archival copies, or copies for distribution)

sketch -- A 3d sketch language translator

Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/sketch
name:             sketch
caption:          A 3d sketch language translator
author:           Eugene K. Ressler
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          0.2
description:      (no language specified) Sketch is a small, simple system for producing line drawings of two- or three-dimensional objects and 
                  scenes. It began as a way to make illustrations for a textbook after we could find no suitable tool for 
                  this purpose. Existing scene processors emphasized GUIs and/or photo-realism, neither of which was useful 
                  to us. We wanted to produce finely wrought, mathematically-based illustrations with no extraneous detail.

                  The input language is reminiscent of  PSTricks (https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base) , so will be 
                  easy for current PSTricks users to learn; output is for use either by pstricks (https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base) itself, 
                  or by pgf (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) .

description:      (no language specified) This package attempts to make it easy for even a LaTeX novice to prepare proficiency tests, especially 
                  in combination with the  exam (https://ctan.org/pkg/exam) document class. Thus, almost all command

smartref -- Extend LaTeX's \ref capability
------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/smartref
name:             smartref
caption:          Extend LaTeX's \ref capability
author:           Giuseppe Bilotta
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.9
description:      (no language specified) The package extends the LaTeX labelling system: whenever a label is set, the values of counters (selected 
                  by the user) are recorded, along with the label. The value of these counters can be recalled with a command 
                  similar to  \pageref .

                  The package also adds commands  \s[name]ref (for each counter [name] that the user has selected); 
                  these commands display something only if the value of the [name] counter is changed from when the 
                  label was set. Many commands are provided to serve as a macro programming environment for using the extended 
                  labels.

snapshot -- List the external dependencies of a LaTeX document
--------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/snapshot
name:             snapshot
caption:          List the external dependencies of a LaTeX document
author:           The American Mathematical Society
author:           Michael J. Downes
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.14
description:      (no language specified) The snapshot package helps the owner of a LaTeX document obtain a list of the external dependencies of 
                  the document, in a form that can be embedded at the top of the document. It provides a snapshot of the 
                  current processing contextof the document, insofar as it can be determined from inside LaTeX. If a document 
                  contains such a dependency list, then it becomes possible to arrange that the document be processed always 
                  with the same versions of everything, in order to ensure the same output. This could be useful for someone 
                  wanting to keep a LaTeX document on hand and consistently reproduce an identical DVI file from it, on 
                  the fly; or for someone wanting to shield a document during the final stages of its production cycle 
                  from unexpected side effects of routine upgrades to the TeX system.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): pkg:/snapshot.pdf

softmakerfreefont -- Support files for SoftMaker free fonts
-----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/softmakerfreefont
alias:            softmaker-freefont
name:             softmakerfreefont
caption:          Support files for SoftMaker free fonts
author:           Josef Kleber
copyright:        Josef Kleber (2010)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.1
description:      (no language specified) In June 2009  SoftMaker (https://www.freefont.de) offered a handwriting font for free download: 
                  The Softmaker Stone Handwriting. As handwriting fonts are a quite limited resource in the LaTeX world, 
                  the author decided to create support files for the font. Since then, the author has added support files 
                  for the fonts Alte Schwabacher, Artistic (regular), Baskerville-Nova (regular + bold + italic + bold 
                  italic), Bonita (regular), Broadway (regular + engraved), Canossa (regular + bold + light), Congress 
                  (regular + bold + italic), Delano-Caps, Digital (regular + bold + italic + bold italic), EgyptienneStd 
                  (light + bold + light italic + bold italic), Flagstaff (regular), Grenoble(regular + bold + italic + 
                  bold italic), Helium (regular + bold), Heliumtwo (regular + bold + shadow), Henderson (regular), Iceberg 
                  (regular + bold), Inverserif (regular), Jugendstil (regular), Marseille (regular + bold + italic + bold 
                  italic), Moab (regular), Nevada (regular + bold), Newcastle (regular + demibold + bold), Old Blackletter, 
                  Quadrat (regular + bold + italic + bold italic), Stone Handwriting, Sunset (regular + bold), Tampa (regular), 
                  VAGRounded (regular), Velo (regular), Veracruz (regular + bold + italic + bold italic).

                  This is the base package for all other softmakerfreefont packages, namely:

                  +  Alte Schwabacher (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-alteschwabacher) 
                  +  Artistic (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-artistic) 
                  +  Baskerville-Nova (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-baskervillenova) 
                  +  Bonita (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-bonita) 
                  +  Broadway (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-broadway) 
                  +  Canossa (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-canossa) 
                  +  Congress (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-congress) 
                  +  Delano Caps (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-delanocaps) 
                  +  Digital (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-digital) 
                  +  EgyptienneStd (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-egyptiennestd) 
                  +  Flagstaff (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-flagstaff) 
                  +  Grenoble (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-grenoble) 
                  +  Helium (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-helium) 
                  +  Heliumtwo (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-heliumtwo) 
                  +  Henderson (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-henderson) 
                  +  Iceberg (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-iceberg) 
                  +  /pkg/softmaker-inverserif (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-inverserif) 
                  +  Jugendstil (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-jugendstil) 
                  +  Marseille (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-marseille) 
                  +  Moab (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-moab) 
                  +  Nevada (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-nevada) 
                  +  Newcastle (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-newcastle) 
                  +  Old Blackletter (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-oldblackletter) 
                  +  Quadrat (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-quadrat) 
                  +  Stone Handwriting (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-stonehand) 
                  +  Sunset (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-sunset) , and
                  +  Tampa (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-tampa) 
                  +  VAGrounded (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-vagrounded) 
                  +  Velo (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-velo) 
                  +  Veracruz (https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-veracruz) .
These packages do not include the fonts themselves.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/softmakerfreefont/softmakerfreefont/README
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/softmakerfreefont/softmakerfreefont
installation:     https://ctan.org/tex-archive/install/fonts/softmakerfreefont/softmakerfreefont.tds.zip
keyword:          font-supp-misc (metrics, macro incantations and other support for miscellaneous fonts (not on CTAN))
year:             2010
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

description:      (no language specified) The  LaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex) system is provided as a large number of separate modules. 
                  The interested user may process each module separately, to produce formatted documentation. Formatted 
                  documentation of the entire system, however, is a more substantial undertaking; source2e.tex provides 
                  what the user needs to produce a complete listing of the LaTeX kernel. It not only includes the relevant 
                  modules in the ‘correct’ order, but it also guides the user through the rather complex compilation process 
                  (by writing messages to the terminal and log).

                  The document also includes a command index.

spalign -- Typeset matrices and arrays with spaces and semicolons as delimiters
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/spalign
name:             spalign
caption:          Typeset matrices and arrays with spaces and semicolons as delimiters
author:           Joseph Rabinoff
copyright:        Joseph Rabinoff (2016)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          (2016-10-05)
last changes:     2016-10-05
year:             2016
description:      (no language specified) Typeset matrices and arrays with spaces and semicolons as delimiters.

                  The purpose of this package is to decrease the number of keystrokes needed to typeset small amounts of 
                  aligned material (matrices, arrays, etc.). It provides a facility for typing alignment environments and 
                  macros with spaces as the alignment delimiter and semicolons (by default) as the end-of-row indicator. 
                  For instance, typeset a matrix using \spalignmat{1 12 -3; 24 -2 2; 0 0 1}, or a vector using \spalignvector{22 
                  \frac{1}{2} -14}.

                  This package also contains utility macros for typesetting augmented matrices, vectors, arrays, systems 
                  of equations, and more, and is easily extendable to other situations that use alignments.

                  People who have to typeset a large number of matrices (like linear algebra teachers) should find this 
                  package to be a real time saver.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/spalign/spalign.pdf

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/spalign/README.md
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/spalign
on MikTeX:        spalign
on TeXLive:       spalign

spanish-mx -- Typeset Spanish as in Mexico
------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/spanish-mx
name:             spanish-mx
caption:          Typeset Spanish as in Mexico
author:           Luis Rivera
copyright:        J. Luis Rivera N. (2008)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.1a
description:      (no language specified) The bundle provides files to support typesetting of texts in Spanish according to Mexican current practices, 
                  using  babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) . The files merge earlier work on a mexican.ldf , 
                  or may be used to define a configuration that will typeset all documents (that request babel’s spanish option) 
                  to use the Mexican language facilities. (Note that this facility is only available with version &gt;=4.2b 
                  releases of the Spanish option.)

                  However, according to the author, the purpose of this package is nowadays better served by the  babel 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) package with option spanish.mexico .

sparklines -- Drawing sparklines: intense, simple, wordlike graphics
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/sparklines
name:             sparklines
caption:          Drawing sparklines: intense, simple, wordlike graphics
author:           Andreas Löffler
author:           Daniel H. Luecking
author:           Emil van Miltenburg
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.7
description:      (no language specified) Sparklines are intense, simple, wordlike graphics (so named by Edward Tufte). In lieu of a more detailed 
                  introduction,  Professor Tufte's site (https://www.edwardtufte.com/) has an early release of a 
                  chapter on sparklines. A PHP implementation may be found at SourceForge (https://sparkline.sourceforge.net/) .

                  A sparkline can be added using the sparkline environment. Also, you can add sparkling rectangles for 
                  the median and special sparkling dots in red or blue. The package requires pdfLaTeX; sparklines cannot 
                  appear in a  dvi file. The sparklines package uses pgf (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) , and does 
                  not work with pictex (https://ctan.org/pkg/pictex) .

spectralsequences -- Print spectral sequence diagrams using PGF/TikZ
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/spectralsequences
name:             spectralsequences
caption:          Print spectral sequence diagrams using PGF/TikZ
author:           Hood Chatham
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.3.3 (2023-01-28)
last changes:     2023-01-28
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) The package is a specialized tool built on top of PGF/TikZ for drawing spectral sequences. It provides 
                  a powerful, concise syntax for specifying the data of a spectral sequence, and then allows the user to 
                  print various pages of spectral sequences, automatically choosing which subset of the classes, differentials, 
                  and structure lines to display on each page. It also handles most of the details of the layout.

                  At the same time, it is extremely flexible.  spectralsequences is closely integrated with TikZ 
                  to ensure that users can take advantage of as much as possible of its expressive power. It is possible 
                  to turn off most of the automated layout features and draw replacements using TikZ commands. The package 
                  also provides a carefully designed error reporting system intended to ensure that it is as clear as possible 
                  what is going wrong.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/spectralsequences/README.md

spelatex -- Create PDF documents with hyperlinks to audiofragments
------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/spelatex
name:             SpeLaTeX
caption:          Create PDF documents with hyperlinks to audiofragments
author:           Walter Daems
copyright:        Walter Daems (2025-2026)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.96 (2026-04-09)
last changes:     2026-04-09
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package equips the PDF that is generated with LaTeX with hyperlinks to audio files that contain 
                  the spoken equivalent of the original text, equations, figures and tables.

                  The audio files can be automatically generated using a Perl-script called  spel-wizard.pl (part 
                  of the SpeL::Wizard module available on CPAN). This script interfaces with locally installed text-to-speech 
                  software or with online available (paying) cloud services to generate the audio files. To this end, the 
                  LaTeX chunks of your text are parsed and translated to “natural language”.

                  SpeLaTeX is babel-enabled such that your text is read with the correct pronunciation corresponding to 
                  your language. So far, it provides the languages English and Dutch, but it will be extended in the future.

                  You can package your PDF together with the audio-files (in your favorite archive format) and make it 
                  available to your users, such that the only requirements to read your text and listen to the audio are 
                  a suited PDF reader and media player.

                  For the text-to-speech conversion, one can use free options (festival, balabolka, ...) or paying services 
                  (e.g. AWS polly).

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/spelatex/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/spelatex/spelatex.pdf

spiderweb -- A tool for building WEB systems
--------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/spiderweb
name:             spiderweb
caption:          A tool for building WEB systems
author:           Norman Ramsey
copyright:        Norman Ramsey (1989-1992)
license:          other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
description:      (no language specified) Spidery WEB is built around the tool Spider, that reads a description of a programming language, and 
                  writes source code for a Weave and a Tangle which support that language. The base sources derive from 
                  CWEB (https://ctan.org/pkg/cweb) , so that the resulting programs inherit some properties of that 
                  system (e.g., the ability to read multiple files). Spider itself is written in Awk, and the Weave and 
                  Tangle output is in C.

                  Spidery WEB is no longer supported: its author used lessons learned from the development to produce the 
                  still more compact  noweb (https://ctan.org/pkg/noweb) system.

spix -- Yet another TeX compilation tool: simple, human readable, no option, no magic
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/spix
name:             SpiX
caption:          Yet another TeX compilation tool: simple, human readable, no option, no magic
author:           Louis Paternault
copyright:        Louis Paternault (2020-2022)
license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
version:          1.3.0 (2022-11-18)
last changes:     2022-11-18
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) SpiX offers a way to store information about the compilation process for a  tex file inside the tex file 
                  itself. Just write the commands as comments in the tex files, and SpiX will extract and run those 
                  commands.

                  Everything is stored in the  tex file (so that you are not missing some piece of information that 
                  is located somewhere else), in a human-readable format (no need to know SpiX to understand it).

splitindex -- Unlimited number of indexes
-----------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/splitindex
name:             splitindex
caption:          Unlimited number of indexes
author:           Markus Kohm
copyright:        Markus Kohm (2002-2013)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.2c
description:      (no language specified) SplitIndex consists of a LaTeX package,  splitidx , and a small program, splitindex . The 
                  package may be used to produce one index or several indexes. Without splitindex (for example, using the index 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/index) package), the number of indexes is limited by the number of TeX’s output 
                  streams. But using the program you may use even more than 16 indexes: splitidx outputs only a single 
                  file \jobname.idx and the program splits that file into several raw index files and calls your 
                  favorite index processor for each of the files.

author:           Scott Pakin
copyright:        Scott Pakin (2009)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) LaTeX's  \verb macro treats its argument as an unbreakable unit of text. This can lead to poor 
                  typesetting, especially when the argument is long. The spverbatim package provides an \spverb macro 
                  that is analogous to \verb and an spverbatim environment that is analogous to verbatim with 
                  the difference being that \spverb and spverbatim allow LaTeX to break lines at space characters.

sqltex -- An SQL Preprocessor for LaTeX
---------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/sqltex
name:             SQLTeX
caption:          An SQL Preprocessor for LaTeX
author:           Oscar van Eijk
copyright:        Oscar van Eijk (2001-2024)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          3.0 (2024-09-20)
last changes:     2024-09-20
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) SQLTeX is a preprocessor that enables the use of SQL statements in LaTeX. The SQLTeX perl script reads 
                  an input file containing the LaTeX source with SQL commands, and writes a LaTeX file in which the SQL 
                  commands have been replaced by the values from their execution. It is possible to select a field for 
                  substitution in your LaTeX document, or to be used as input in another SQL command. (When an SQL command 
                  returns multiple fields and/or rows, the values can only be used within the document.)

                  The default is to use MySQL databases, but Pg, Sybase, Oracle, Ingres, mSQL and PostgreSQL are also supported.

documentation:    Package README (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/sqltex/README.md

sshrc-insight -- A LaTeX class for SSHRC Insight Grant proposals
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/sshrc-insight
name:             sshrc-insight
caption:          A LaTeX class for SSHRC Insight Grant proposals
author:           Tristan Miller
copyright:        Steven B. Segletes (2021)
copyright:        Tristan Miller (2024, 2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2025.0.0 (2025-08-14)
last changes:     2025-08-14
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) The sshrc-insight LaTeX class facilitates the preparation of funding proposals for the Insight Grants 
                  program of Canada’s Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC). It has the following key 
                  features:

                  + Formats the proposal according to the SSHRC’s specifications.
                  + Allows parts of the proposal to be compiled into separate PDFs to attach to the appropriate places in 
                    the online application form.
                  + Alternatively, allows the proposal to be compiled into a single PDF in order to facilitate the writing 
                    and pre-submission reviewing process.
                  + Ensures that citation numbering remains consistent regardless whether the proposal is compiled as separate 
                    PDFs or a single PDF.
                  + Provides character counts for long-answer form fields.
                  + Supports preparation of proposals in either English or French.
                  + Compatible with pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX, and LuaLaTeX.

statementsp -- Theorem and proposition boxes with preview and recall functions
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

name:             statementsp
caption:          Theorem and proposition boxes with preview and recall functions
author:           Rirai Ikeda
copyright:        Rirai Ikeda (2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) This package provides a convenient way to create customizable theorem and proposition boxes using  tcolorbox 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/tcolorbox) .

                  Its most distinctive feature is the automatic Preview and Recall mechanism. By using a single command 
                  (\refcallsp), you can display a statement box anywhere in your document. The package automatically determines 
                  its position relative to the main definition: if placed before, it generates a “Preview” box; if placed 
                  after, it generates a “Recall” box. Both automatically include hyperlinks jumping directly to the main 
                  definition.

statistics -- Compute and typeset statistics tables and graphics

name:             statistics
caption:          Compute and typeset statistics tables and graphics
author:           Julien Rivaud

license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
version:          2.2 (2019-09-29)
last changes:     2019-09-29
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) The 'statistics' package can compute and typeset statistics like frequency tables, cumulative distribution 
                  functions (increasing or decreasing, in frequency or absolute count domain), from the counts of individual 
                  values, or ranges, or even the raw value list with repetitions.

                  It can also compute and draw a bar diagram in case of individual values, or, when the data repartition 
                  is known from ranges, an histogram or the continuous cumulative distribution function.

                  You can ask 'statistics' to display no result, selective results or all of them. Similarly 'statistics' 
                  can draw only some parts of the graphs. Every part of the generated tables or graphics is customizable.

statrep -- Displays SAS code and results of running the code
------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/statrep
name:             StatRep
caption:          Displays SAS code and results of running the code
author:           Martial Phélippé-Guinvarc'h
copyright:        Martial Phélippé-Guinvarc'h (2026)
copyright:        SAS Institute Inc. (2014-2015)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.0
description:      (no language specified) The StatRep package provides a system for creating reproducible research documents that combine LaTeX 
                  markup with SAS code and output. It allows authors to write a single LaTeX source document that simultaneously 
                  serves as the analysis script and the final report.

                  The package provides two environments ( Datastep and Sascode ) to display SAS code, and two 
                  tags ( Listing and Graphic ) to display SAS output. At compile time, StatRep automatically 
                  generates a SAS program that captures all requested output using the SAS Output Delivery System (ODS).

                  This updated version brings the following improvements over the original StatRep package:

                  + Improved path resolution with the SASmode option: WorkStation mode uses the current directory as root, 
                    while Server mode dynamically resolves the path from the  _SASPROGRAMFILE SAS macro variable, enabling 
                    use in SAS Studio and SAS OnDemand for Academics.
                  + Full UTF-8 encoding support for SAS output files, with automatic detection from the inputenc package 
                    and fallback to UTF-8 by default.
                  + New SAS macros ( STATREPResults , STATREPAllResults , STATREPMACROVAR ) for automatic 
                    export of SAS numeric results and macro variables directly into LaTeX via \def commands , using 
                    predefined formatting for numbers, percentages, and dates
The package also includes the  longfigure (https://ctan.org/pkg/longfigure) package for multi-page 
                  figures, a complete suite of SAS macros (statrep_macros.sas), and full documentation including a user's 
                  guide and a quickstart example.

                  This is an updated and maintained version of the original StatRep package developed by Tim Arnold and 
                  Warren F. Kuhfeld at SAS Institute Inc.

stealcaps -- “Steal” small capitals
-----------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/stealcaps
name:             stealcaps
caption:          “Steal” small capitals
author:           Ruben Giannotti
copyright:        Ruben Giannotti (2018-2022)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.1 (2022-11-07)
last changes:     2022-11-07
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) This little package is mainly meant to be used when there is a (TrueType or OpenType) font that does 
                  not provide real small capitals. As a workaround, this package helps to borrow, or “steal”, the small 
                  capitals from another font. This might also be useful in the rare case that someone does not like the 
                  present small capitals, and wants to change them, or likes those from another font better.

                  To achieve the borrowing, one only needs to load the package and specify the name of the target font 
                  via the  from option.

                  Package dependencies:  pgfopts (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgfopts) , iftex (https://ctan.org/pkg/iftex) , fontspec 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec) .

stellenbosch -- Stellenbosch thesis bundle (legacy version)
-----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/stellenbosch
name:             stellenbosch
caption:          Stellenbosch thesis bundle (legacy version)
author:           Daniel Els
copyright:        Danie Els (2003-2015)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          11a
description:      (no language specified) Note: This bundle should only be used for typesetting legacy documents. For new documents, its successor 
                  stellenbosch-2 (https://ctan.org/pkg/stellenbosch-2) is available.

                  The usthesis class/style files are provided to typeset reports, theses and dissertations that conform 
                  to the requirements of the Engineering Faculty of the University of Stellenbosch.

                  The class file  usthesis.cls is based on the standard LaTeX book class, while usthesis.sty is 
                  a style file to be loaded on top of the very powerful memoir (https://ctan.org/pkg/memoir) class. 
                  Both options give identical output, but the benefit of the using memoir is that it has many additional 
                  command and environments for formatting and processing of a document.

                  Usthesis is primarily concerned with the formatting of the front matter such as the title page, abstract, 
                  etc. and a decent page layout on A4 paper. It also works together with the babel package to provide language 
                  options to typeset documents in Afrikaans or in English.

                  Additional packages are provided for bibliographic matter, note title pages, lists of symbols, as well 
                  as various graphic files for logos.

description:      (no language specified) The STEP fonts are a free Times-like (i.e., Times replacement) font family, implementing a design first 
                  created for The Times of London in 1932. These fonts are meant to be compatible in design with Adobe’s 
                  digitization of Linotype Times, commonly used in publishing.

                  The fonts were forked from  XITS (https://ctan.org/pkg/xits) /STIX and Type 1 support is provided 
                  for legacy TeX engines.

last changes:     2025-06-18
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) The stfloats package provides:

                  + commands to control  \baselineskip , that actually permit stretch and shrink, allowing a different 
                    value for use within floats;
                  + commands to control whether footnotes will appear above (as standard) or below a bottom float;
                  + a command that declares that double floats should be placed at the bottom (rather than the top) of a 
                    page.

stix2-type1 -- Type1 versions of the STIX Two OpenType fonts
------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/stix2-type1
name:             stix2-type1
caption:          Type1 versions of the STIX Two OpenType fonts
author:           David M. Jones
author:           The STI Pub Companies
copyright:        STI Pub Companies (2001-2018, 2021)
license:          ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.0.2
description:      (no language specified) The stix2 package provides minimal support for using the STIX Two fonts with versions of TeX that are 
                  limited to TFM files, Type 1 PostScript fonts, and 8-bit font encodings.

                  Version 2.0.0 of the STIX fonts are being released in this format in hopes of easing the transition from 
                  legacy TeX engines to modern fully Unicode-compatible systems.

                  The Type 1 versions are merely a repackaging of the original OpenType versions and should not be viewed 
                  as independent entities. Some glyphs that are traditionally available in TeX math fonts are not yet available 
                  in the STIX Two OpenType fonts. In such cases, we have chosen to omit them from the stix2 package rather 
                  than create incompatibilities between the OpenType and Type 1 versions. In addition, while development 
                  of the OpenType versions is ongoing, no further updates are planned to the Type 1 versions of the fonts.

license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.0.1 (2026-01-01)
last changes:     2026-01-01
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package  geometry (https://ctan.org/pkg/geometry) is excellent for customizing the page layout. 
                  However, using the \newgeometry command to change the page size in the middle of the document only 
                  affects the typing area and does not affect the real paper (stock) size. This package circumvents this 
                  situation by resizing the paper (stock) size to the new page layout.

sty2dtx -- Create a .dtx file from a .sty file
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/sty2dtx
name:             sty2dtx
caption:          Create a .dtx file from a .sty file
author:           Martin Scharrer
copyright:        Martin Scharrer (2010-2022)
license:          gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
version:          2.4 (2022-10-18)
last changes:     2022-10-18
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) The package provides a Perl script that converts a  .sty file (LaTeX package) to .dtx format 
                  (documented LaTeX source), by surrounding macro definitions with macro and macrocode environments. 
                  The macro name is automatically inserted as an argument to the macro environment.

                  Code lines outside macro definitions are wrapped only in  macrocode environments. Empty lines are 
                  removed.

                  The script should not be thought to be fool proof and 100% accurate but rather as a good start to the 
                  business of making a  .dtx file from an undocumented style file.

                  Full  .dtx files are generated. A template based on the skeleton file from dtxtut (https://ctan.org/pkg/dtxtut) is 
                  used. User level macros are added automatically to the “Usage” section of the .dtx file. A corresponding .ins file 
                  can be generated as well.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): pkg:/README.txt

styleitems -- Independent auto-numbered list labels drawn with TikZ
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/styleitems
name:             styleitems
caption:          Independent auto-numbered list labels drawn with TikZ
author:           Faris Hameed
copyright:        Faris Hameed (null)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) The package provides a fully self-contained auto-numbering system for decorative list labels based on 
                  TikZ. Unlike packages such as enumitem, each label is rendered as a live TikZ node, allowing full control 
                  over shape, colour, stroke, and numbering style. Each list instance maintains its own counter using an 
                  internal stack mechanism, ensuring that nested lists at any depth remain independent and never interfere 
                  with their parent counters.

                  Available label shapes (16 total): Circle, Square, Rectangle, Diamond, Triangle, Pentagon, Hexagon, Octagon, 
                  Star (5-point), Star (12-point), Ellipse Callout (left/right), Cloud Callout (left/right), and four arrow 
                  directions (right, left, up, down). Every shape is available in two modes: vertical and inline.

                  Numbering styles (8): arabic, indic (Arabic-Indic digits), alph, Alph, roman, Roman, aralph (Hijai order), 
                  aralphabjad (Abjad order).

                  All environments accept optional arguments for colour, numbering style, text rotation, and text scale. 
                  The package fully supports bidirectional (Arabic/RTL) documents alongside standard LTR typesetting.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/styleitems/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/styleitems/styleitems-doc.pdf

                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3) . It can effectively manage both upper and lower bids, while also considering 
                  bottom bid, top bid, and hanging bid.

                  The package offers a unique environment for drawing abacuses, denoted as  suanpan . Within this 
                  environment, 7 specialized macros are available for the creation of abacuses. The \rod macro is 
                  used to lay out a single rod, while the \rod* macro draws a counting point on this rod’s beam. 
                  The \rods macro is capable of laying out a set of rods. The \bid macro colors the specified 
                  bid. The \bids macro colors all inner bids that are near the beam, while the \bids* macro 
                  colors all outer bids that are far from the beam. Lastly, the \lrframe macro is used to lay out 
                  the left and right frames of an abacus.

                  At the same time, the package offers customization options for abacus, including line width, draw color, 
                  fill color, bid space, rod space, etc. These can be configured through package options,  suanpan environment 
                  options, or the \suanpanset macro.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/suanpan-l3/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (Chinese + English): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/suanpan-l3/suanpan-l3.pdf

subfig -- Figures broken into subfigures
----------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/subfig
name:             subfig
caption:          Figures broken into subfigures
author:           bidi-tex GitHub Organisation
author:           Steven Douglas Cochran
author:           Vafa Khalighi
copyright:        Steven Douglas Cochran (2003-2005)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.3
description:      (no language specified) The package provides support for the manipulation and reference of small or ‘sub’ figures and tables 
                  within a single figure or table environment. It is convenient to use this package when your subfigures 
                  are to be separately captioned, referenced, or are to be included in the List-of-Figures. A new  \subfigure command 
                  is introduced which can be used inside a figure environment for each subfigure. An optional first argument 
                  is used as the caption for that subfigure.

                  This package supersedes the  subfigure (https://ctan.org/pkg/subfigure) package (which is no longer 
                  maintained). The name was changed since the package is not completely backward compatible with the older 
                  package The major advantage of the new package is that the user interface is keyword/value driven and 
                  easier to use. To ease the transition from the subfigure package, the distribution includes a configuration 
                  file ( subfig.cfg ) which nearly emulates the subfigure (https://ctan.org/pkg/subfigure) package.

                  The functionality of the package is provided by the (more recent still)  subcaption (https://ctan.org/pkg/subcaption) package.

substnote -- Substitution notation with a switchable convention
---------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/substnote
name:             substnote
caption:          Substitution notation with a switchable convention
author:           Vseslav Sekorin
copyright:        Vseslav Sekorin (2026)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          0.1.0 (2026-07-30)
last changes:     2026-07-30
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package provides a single command for the notation of substitution,  \subst{\varphi}{x}{t} , 
                  and lets the convention be chosen once in the preamble. Seven conventions are supported, among them the 
                  two mirror-image readings of the slash, the assignment colon, the arrow and the up-down form with the 
                  variable above the term. Simultaneous substitutions are written as two comma lists paired by index, and 
                  lists of different lengths are reported as an error. The delimiters are selected with a key and scale 
                  to their contents in the starred form, and the colon of the assignment convention is centred on the mathematical 
                  axis. The commands are mode-aware and robust, so they may be used in section titles and captions. The 
                  package requires only a recent LaTeX kernel and loads nothing else.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/substnote/README.md

author:           Paul Abraham
copyright:        Paul Abraham (2005)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) The sudoku package provides an environment for typesetting sudoku grids.

                  A sudoku puzzle is a 9x9 grid where some of the squares in the grid contain numbers. The rules are simple: 
                  every column can only contain the digits 1 to 9, every row can only contain the digits 1 to 9 and every 
                  3x3 box can only contain the digits 1 to 9.

                  More information, including help and example puzzles, can be found at  sudoku.org.uk (http://www.sudoku.org.uk) . 
                  This site also has blank sudoku grids (or worksheets), but you will not need to print them from there 
                  if you have this package installed.

author:           Philip Ilten

year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) This bundle contains the two packages  svg and svg-extract .

                  The  svg package is intended for the automated integration of SVG graphics into LaTeX documents. 
                  Therefore the capabilities provided by Inkscape — or more precisely its command line tool — are 
                  used to export the text within an SVG graphic to a separate file, which is then rendered by LaTeX. For 
                  this purpose the two commands \includesvg and \includeinkscape are provided which are very 
                  similar to the \includegraphics command of the graphicx (https://ctan.org/pkg/graphicx) package.

                  In addition, the package  svg-extract allows the extraction of these graphics into independent 
                  files in different graphic formats, exactly as it is rendered within the LaTeX document, using either ImageMagick or Ghostscript .

svg-animate -- Generate animated SVG diagrams with TikZ
-------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/svg-animate
name:             svg-animate
caption:          Generate animated SVG diagrams with TikZ
author:           Sébastien Gross
copyright:        Sébastien Gross (2026)
license:          agpl3 = GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 (free)
version:          1.1 (2026-04-28)
last changes:     2026-04-28
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package provides step-by-step animations for TikZ diagrams in SVG format. The resulting animations 
                  run natively in web browsers and do not require JavaScript or plugins.

                  From a single source file, both an animated SVG and a static PDF can be generated. In the PDF output, 
                  steps may be stacked or collapsed into a single frame.

                  The animation model is based on discrete  'steps' . A TikZ picture is enclosed in \begin{animate} , 
                  material to be shown at a given step is marked with \reveal{...} , and \animstep is used 
                  to advance to the next step.

                  Additional features include per-step durations, visibility over multiple steps or step ranges, blinking 
                  elements, one-shot or looping playback, and a  \noanimate fallback for PDF output.

                  In SVG output, visibility changes are implemented by means of SMIL animations with instantaneous opacity 
                  transitions.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/svg-animate/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/svg-animate/svg-animate.pdf

swimgraf -- Graphical/textual representations of swimming performances
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/swimgraf
name:             Swimgraf
caption:          Graphical/textual representations of swimming performances
author:           Martin J. Osborne
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          (2002-05-30)
last changes:     2002-05-30
year:             2002
description:      (no language specified) The package provides two macros that produce representations of a swimmer's performances. The user records 
                  data in a text file and specifies as arguments of the macros the date range of interest. The macros extract 
                  the relevant information from the file and process it:  \swimgraph produces a graph of the times 
                  in a single swimming event (specified as an argument), plotting long course and short course times in 
                  separate lines. Records and qualifying times, stored in text files, may optionally be included on the 
                  graph. \swimtext produces a written record of the times in all events.

                  Files of current world and Canadian records are included.

                  The package requires the  PSTricks (https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base) and keyval (https://ctan.org/pkg/keyval) packages. 
                  For attractive output it also requires a colour output device.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/swimgraf/README

t1infos -- Utilities for PostScript fonts
-----------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/t1infos
name:             t1infos
caption:          Utilities for PostScript fonts
author:           Thomas Baruchel
license:          bsd = BSD Style License (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) There are here two little programs written in C (using t1lib) for scanning Type 1 fonts, and doing:
– 
                  compute the ‘black area’ of each glyph, with how much percent of the square containing the glyph is black, 
                  and
– checking if the ‘extremas’ (see Adobe Type 1 specifications) of the outline are correct, and 
                  tell which one are missing.

                  There is also here a PostScript dictionary containing three algorithms for automatic kerning (the kerning 
                  is computed ‘on the fly’ instead of being pre-computed by external software like TeX, groff or lout; 
                  very useful for some PostScript hacking). Two of these algorithms are quite classical; the third is original 
                  and is PostScript-optimized. The PostScript file in the distribution contains both demonstration code 
                  and the dictionary itself.

documentation:    README file (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/utilities/t1infos/README
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/utilities/t1infos
keyword:          ps-manip (manipulate PostScript files)
year:             without year
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

                  are done in the header.

t1utils -- Simple Type 1 font manipulation programs
---------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/t1utils
name:             t1utils
caption:          Simple Type 1 font manipulation programs
author:           Lee Hetherington
author:           Eddie Kohler
copyright:        I. Lee Hetherington (1992)
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
description:      (no language specified) A collection of simple programs for manipulating Adobe Type 1 fonts, comprising:
– t1ascii : 
                  convert PFB (binary) to PFA (ascii) fonts;
– t1binary : convert PFA to PFB fonts;
– t1disasm : 
                  convert PFA or PFB fonts to human-readable and -editable format;
– t1asm : reassemble such editable 
                  formats to a font;
– t1unmac : extract font resources from a Macintosh font file; and
– t1mac : 
                  generate a Macintosh font from a Type 1 font.

tableof -- Tagging tables of contents
-------------------------------------

name:             tableof
caption:          Tagging tables of contents
author:           Jean-François Burnol
copyright:        Jean-François Burnol (2012, 2013, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.4d (2024-09-17)
last changes:     2024-09-17
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) The package provides the commands to flag chapters or sections (or anything else destined to become a 
                  TOC line). The command  \nexttocwithtags{req1,req2,...}{excl1,excl2,...} specifies which tags are 
                  to be required and which ones are to be excluded by the next \tableofcontents (or equivalent) command. 
                  In a document that uses a class where \tableofcontents may only be used once, the command \tableoftaggedcontents{req1,req2,...}{excl1,excl2,...} may 
                  be used to provide several tables.

                  styles and a bugfix command for lists in tables.

                  However, the author told us in March 2023: “I wrote [this package] about ten years ago, [...] since at 
                  that time no package with layout options for tabulars was available. [...] However since nowadays much 
                  better packages are available that do the same job, but are much more professional in code base, usability 
                  and results, I want to remove my package from CTAN.”

description:      (no language specified) \tabto{&lt;length&gt;} moves the typesetting position to &lt;length&gt; from the left margin 
                  of the paragraph. If the typesetting position is already further along, \tabto starts a new line; 
                  the command \tabto* will move position backwards if necessary, so that previous text may be overwritten.

                  typesetting position to the next defined ‘tab stop’.

tabu -- Flexible LaTeX tabulars
-------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tabu
name:             tabu
caption:          Flexible LaTeX tabulars
author:           Florent Chervet
copyright:        Florent Chervet (2010)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.9 (2019-01-11)
last changes:     2019-01-11
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) The package provides an environment,  tabu , which will make any sort of tabular (that doesn’t 
                  need to split across pages), and an environment longtabu which provides the facilities of tabu in 
                  a modified longtable (https://ctan.org/pkg/longtable) environment. (Note that this latter offers 
                  an enhancement of ltxtable (https://ctan.org/pkg/ltxtable) .)

                  The package requires the  array (https://ctan.org/pkg/array) package, and needs e-TeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/etex) to 
                  run (since array.sty is present in every conforming distribution of LaTeX, and since every publicly 
                  available LaTeX format is built using e-TeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/etex) , the requirements are 
                  provided by default on any reasonable system). The package also requires xcolor (https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor) for 
                  coloured rules in tables, and colortbl (https://ctan.org/pkg/colortbl) for coloured cells. The longtabu environment 
                  further requires that longtable (https://ctan.org/pkg/longtable) be loaded. The package itself 
                  does not load any of these packages for the user.

                  The  tabu environment may be used in place of tabular , tabular* and tabularx environments, 
                  as well as the array environment in maths mode. It overloads tabularx ’s X -column 
                  specification, allowing a width specification, alignment ( l , r , c and j ) 
                  and column type indication ( p , m and b ).

                  \begin{tabu} to &lt;dimen&gt; specifies a target width, and \begin{tabu} spread &lt;dimen&gt; enlarges 
                  the environment’s “natural” width.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/tabu/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/tabu/tabu.pdf

on MikTeX:        tabu
on TeXLive:       tabu
