tabularray -- Typeset tabulars and arrays with LaTeX3
-----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tabularray
name:             tabularray
caption:          Typeset tabulars and arrays with LaTeX3
author:           Jianrui Lyu
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2025C (2025-11-27)
last changes:     2025-11-27
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) LaTeX tables are implemented using TeX commands such as  \halign , \noalign , \span , 
                  and \omit . In order to implement new features, many macro packages have modified the inner table 
                  commands inside LaTeX. This makes package code complicated, difficult to maintain, and often conflicts 
                  with each other.

                  At present, the LaTeX3 programming layer is basically mature. This  tabularray package will discard 
                  the old \halign commands and directly use LaTeX3 functions to parse the table, and then typeset 
                  the entire table. Under the premise of being compatible with the basic syntax of LaTeX2 tables, this 
                  macro package will completely separate the content and style of the table, and the style of the table 
                  can be completely set in keyval way.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/tabularray/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/tabularray/tabularray.pdf

tabulary -- Tabular with variable width columns balanced

author:           David Carlisle

version:          0.11 (2024-06-04)
last changes:     2024-06-04
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) The package defines a  tabular* -like environment, tabulary , taking a ‘total width’ argument 
                  as well as the column specifications. The environment uses column types L , C , R and J for 
                  variable width columns ( \raggedright ', \centering , \raggedleft , and normally justified). 
                  In contrast to tabularx (https://ctan.org/pkg/tabularx) 's X columns, the width of each column

talk -- A LaTeX class for presentations
---------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/talk
name:             talk
caption:          A LaTeX class for presentations
author:           Martin Wiebusch
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.0
description:      (no language specified) The talk document class allows you to create slides for screen presentations or printing on transparencies. 
                  It also allows you to print personal notes for your talk. You can create overlays and display structure 
                  information (current section / subsection, table of contents) on your slides. The main feature that distinguishes 
                  talk from other presentation classes like  beamer (https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer) or prosper (https://ctan.org/pkg/prosper) is 
                  that it allows the user to define an arbitrary number of slide styles and switch between these styles 
                  from slide to slide. This way the slide layout can be adapted to the slide content. For example, the 
                  title or contents page of a talk can be given a slightly different layout than the other slides.

                  The talk class makes no restrictions on the slide design whatsoever. The entire look and feel of the 
                  presentation can be defined by the user. The style definitions should be put in a separate sty file. 
                  Currently the package comes with two sets of pre-defined slide styles ( talk-simple.sty and talk-sidebars.sty ). 
                  Contributions from people who are artistically more gifted than the author are more than welcome!

documentation:    Example of use (1) (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/talk/simple-example.pdf
-- local file:    ./9904615397-simple-example.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/talk/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/talk/talkdoc.pdf
-- local file:    ./5430521590-talkdoc.pdf
documentation:    Example of use (2) (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/talk/sidebars-example.pdf

ted -- A (primitive) token list editor
--------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/ted
name:             ted
caption:          A (primitive) token list editor
author:           Manuel Pégourié-Gonnard
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.06
description:      (no language specified) Just like sed is a stream editor, ted is a token list editor. Actually, it is not as powerful as sed, 
                  but its main feature is that it really works with tokens, not only characters.

                  The ted package provides two user macros:  \Substitute and \ShowTokens . The first is maybe 
                  the most useful: it performs substitutions in token lists (even inside braces). The second displays each 
                  token of the list (one per line) with its catcode (in the list, not just the current one), and can be 
                  useful for debugging or for TeX learners.

                  Ted is designed to work well even if strange tokens (that is, unusual {charcode, catcode} pairs or tokens 
                  with a confusing meaning) occur in the list.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ted/README
documentation:    Package documentation (English) (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ted/ted.pdf
-- local file:    ./9371470277-ted.pdf
documentation:    Package documentation (French): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ted/ted-fr.pdf
-- local file:    ./8616472255-ted-fr.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ted

on TeXLive:       ted

testeq -- An equality test for use in MetaPost
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/testeq
name:             testeq
caption:          An equality test for use in MetaPost
author:           Ulrik Vieth
license:          noinfo = noinfo 
version:          1.05
description:      (no language specified) This file provides a general equality test macro for objects of any type based on code from Appendix 
                  D of The Metafont book, but adapted for MetaPost. Unfortunately it is no longer fully general, because 
                  MetaPost lacks the bitmap-oriented operations like cull and totalweight, which are needed when testing 
                  for the equality of two pictures.

                  A particular useful feature of this package is the patheq macro to test for equality of two paths. This 
                  might prove handy when processing data files with the MetaPost graph package, that contain data for an 
                  unknown number of paths separated by blank lines. In that case one might use patheq to check whether 
                  the last path read is actually the same as the first one, having started over from the beginning.

on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/metapost/contrib/macros/misc/testeq.mp
keyword:          mp-supp (support tools and macros for MetaPost programming)
year:             without year
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

                  and customisation.

                  teTeX. With the appearance of  TeX Live 2007 (https://ctan.org/pkg/texlive) (whose Unix-system 
                  TeX support originally derived from teTeX), no-one should be using teTeX at all, in new applications.

                  One of the “schemes” available when installing TeX Live provides a configuration very close to that of 
                  the old teTeX, but using modern versions of programs and packages.

-----------------------------------------

version:          3.141592653 (2021-02-05)
last changes:     2021-02-05
year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) TeX is a typesetting system that incorporates a macro processor. A TeX source document specifies or incorporates 
                  a number of macro definitions that instruct the TeX engine how to typeset the document. The TeX engine 
                  also uses font metrics generated by  Metafont (https://ctan.org/pkg/metafont) , or by any of several 
                  other mechanisms that incorporate fonts from other sources into an environment suitable for TeX.

                  TeX has been, and continues, a basis and an inspiration for several other programs, including  e-TeX 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/etex) and PDFTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/pdftex) .

                  The distribution includes the source of Knuth’s  'TeX book' ; this source is there to read, as 
                  an example of writing TeX — it should not be processed without Knuth’s direct permission.

tex-extensions -- Proposals for extensions to TeX
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tex-extensions
name:             tex-extensions
caption:          Proposals for extensions to TeX
author:           Matthias Clasen
license:          noinfo = noinfo 
version:          (2003-02-07)
last changes:     2003-02-07
year:             2003
description:      (no language specified) A bundle of proposals for extensions to TeX, implemented as change files to  web2c v7.2. The extensions 
                  cover:

                  + replacing floating point by integer arithmetic, in glue calculations;
                  + introducing hyphenation classes (with a corresponding change to  patgen );
                  + implementing demerits for more than 2 consecutive hyphens;
                  + providing ‘nestable’ and ‘under’ math accents; a primitive to switch to ‘cramped’ styles; provides generalised 
                    radicals with a left- and right-delimiter; implementation work for using the hz algorithm;
                  + marginal tokens for hanging punctuation and hyphens.
Several files offering examples of use are also provided.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/systems/tex-extensions/clasen/README

tex-gyre -- TeX Fonts extending freely available URW fonts
----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tex-gyre
name:             tex-gyre
caption:          TeX Fonts extending freely available URW fonts
author:           Bogusław Jackowski
author:           Janusz Marian Nowacki
license:          gfl = The GUST Font License (GFL) (free)
version:          2.501
description:      (no language specified) The TeX-GYRE bundle consists of six font families:

                  TeX Gyre Adventor (https://ctan.org/pkg/tex-gyre-adventor) is based on the URW Gothic L family 
                  of fonts (which is derived from ITC Avant Garde Gothic, designed by Herb Lubalin and Tom Carnase).

                  TeX Gyre Bonum (https://ctan.org/pkg/tex-gyre-bonum) is based on the URW Bookman L family (from 
                  Bookman Old Style, designed by Alexander Phemister).

                  TeX Gyre Chorus (https://ctan.org/pkg/tex-gyre-chorus) is based on URW Chancery L Medium Italic 
                  (from ITC Zapf Chancery, designed by Hermann Zapf in 1979).

                  TeX-Gyre Cursor (https://ctan.org/pkg/tex-gyre-cursor) is based on URW Nimbus Mono L (based on 
                  Courier, designed by Howard G. Kettler in 1955, for IBM).

                  TeX Gyre Heros (https://ctan.org/pkg/tex-gyre-heros) is based on URW Nimbus Sans L (from Helvetica, 
                  prepared by Max Miedinger, with Eduard Hoffmann in 1957).

                  TeX Gyre Pagella (https://ctan.org/pkg/tex-gyre-pagella) is based on URW Palladio L (from Palatino, 
                  designed by Hermann Zapf in the 1940s).

                  TeX Gyre Schola (https://ctan.org/pkg/tex-gyre-schola) is based on the URW Century Schoolbook 
                  L family (from Century Schoolbook, designed by Morris Fuller Benton for the American Type Founders).

                  TeX Gyre Termes (https://ctan.org/pkg/tex-gyre-termes) is based on the URW Nimbus Roman No9 L 
                  family of fonts (from Times New Roman, designed by Stanley Morison together with Starling Burgess and 
                  Victor Lardent and first offered by Monotype).

                  The constituent standard faces of each family have been greatly extended (though Chorus omits Greek support 
                  and has no small-caps family). Each family is available in Adobe Type 1 and Open Type formats, and LaTeX 
                  support (for use with a variety of encodings) is provided. Vietnamese characters were added by Han The 
                  Thanh.

                  There are companion maths fonts for several of these designs, listed in the  TeX Gyre Math (https://ctan.org/pkg/tex-gyre-math) package.

license:          gfl = The GUST Font License (GFL) (free)
version:          2.003
description:      (no language specified) The TeX Gyre Chorus font is based on the URW Chancery L Medium Italic. The original font, ITC Zapf Chancery, 
                  was designed in 1979 by Hermann Zapf who was inspired by handwritten letterforms of the Italian Renaissance.

                  Chorus has been greatly extended. Unlike the rest of the TeX Gyre bundle, there are no Greek glyphs, 
                  and there are no small caps. The font is available both in Adobe Type 1 and in OpenType formats, and 
                  LaTeX support (for use with a variety of encodings) is provided. Vietnamese characters were added by 
                  Han The Thanh.

                  TeX Gyre Chorus is distributed as part of the  TeX Gyre collection (https://ctan.org/pkg/tex-gyre) .

tex4ht -- Convert (La)TeX to HTML/XML
-------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tex4ht
name:             TeX4ht
caption:          Convert (La)TeX to HTML/XML
author:           The TeX4ht Team
author:           Eitan M. Gurari
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
description:      (no language specified) A converter from TeX and LaTeX to SGML-based formats such as (X)HTML, MathML, OpenDocument, and Docbook, 
                  providing a configurable (La)TeX-based authoring system for hypertext.

                  TeX4ht does not independently parse (La)TeX source (so it avoids the difficulties encountered by many 
                  other converters, arising from the irregularity of (La)TeX syntax). Instead, TeX4ht uses (La)TeX itself 
                  (with myriad macro modifications) to produce a helper DVI file that it can then process. This technique 
                  allows TeX4ht to approach the robustness characteristic of restricted-syntax systems such as  gellmu 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/gellmu) .

                  Full releases of TeX4ht are no longer made, both because it is technically difficult to do so and because 
                  their utility is questionable. Nevertheless, TeX4ht is actively maintained. So, current source files 
                  are held on CTAN, and updated from the development repository frequently. Creating the myriad derived 
                  files from them is nontrivial, and generally done with the Makefile in development, from which the TeX4ht 
                  package in TeX Live is updated.

documentation:    Original introductory paper (no language specified): https://tug.org/TUGboat/tb25-1/gurari.pdf
-- local file:    ./5384775228-gurari.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/TeX4ht/README
documentation:    More recent paper including customization (no language specified): https://tug.org/TUGboat/tb40-1/tb124hoftich-make4ht.pdf
-- local file:    ./1504009311-tb124hoftich-make4ht.pdf
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://tug.org/applications/tex4ht/mn.html
home page:        https://tug.org/tex4ht
contact:          support: https://lists.tug.org/tex4ht
contact:          bugs: https://puszcza.gnu.org.ua/bugs/?group=tex4ht
contact:          repository: https://puszcza.gnu.org.ua/projects/tex4ht/
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/TeX4ht
on MikTeX:        tex4ht
on TeXLive:       tex4ht
keyword:          tagged-pdf-incompatible (tagged PDF incompatible)
keyword:          cvt-html (generate HTML from TeX-ish sources)

texdef -- Display the definitions of TeX commands
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/texdef
name:             texdef
caption:          Display the definitions of TeX commands
author:           Martin Scharrer
copyright:        Martin Scharrer (2011-2025)
license:          gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
version:          1.10 (2025-02-17)
last changes:     2025-02-17
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This (Perl) script displays the definitions of (La)TeX command sequences/macros. Various options allow 
                  the selection of the used class as well as package files and other factors that may influence the definition 
                  (before/after the preamble, inside an environment, …).

                  The script creates a temporary TeX file which is then compiled using (La)TeX to find the ‘ \meaning ’ 
                  of the command sequence. The result is formatted and presented to the user. Length or number command 
                  sequences (dimensions, \char… , count registers, …) are recognized and the contained value is also 
                  shown (using \the ). Special definitions like protected macros are also recognized and the underlying 
                  macros are shown as well.

                  The script will show plain TeX definitions by default. LaTeX and ConTeXt are supported, including flavours 
                  (pdf(La)TeX, Lua(La)TeX, Xe(La)TeX, …). The flavour can be selected using a command line option, or via 
                  the script name:  latexdef will use LaTeX as default, etc.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): pkg:/README.txt

texecole -- A French-prose document composition language
--------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/texecole
name:             texecole
caption:          A French-prose document composition language
author:           Gérard Dubard
license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
version:          1.1 (2026-07-30)
last changes:     2026-07-30
year:             2026
description:      (French) texecole est une classe LuaLaTeX construite autour d’un langage de balises en prose française – sans 
                  anglicisme – qui permet de créer simplement des documents de grande qualité tout en bénéficiant de toute 
                  la puissance de LaTeX. Chaque document texecole est traduit en code LaTeX à la compilation. texecole 
                  n’a pas pour objectif de remplacer LaTeX, mais d’en faciliter l’accès et d’en permettre l'apprentissage 
                  progressif. Il s'adresse à tous : collégiens, lycéens, étudiants, enseignants, chercheurs, ingénieurs, 
                  auteurs de documentation, et plus généralement à toute personne souhaitant produire des documents scientifiques, 
                  techniques ou pédagogiques. texecole couvre les cadres et grilles à zones nommées, les tableaux, les 
                  images, les listes, un mini-langage mathématique (fractions, sommes, intégrales, dérivées, matrices et 
                  systèmes linéaires), les graphiques de fonctions, la géométrie plane et les solides, ainsi que les statistiques 
                  et probabilités. Un moteur de calcul interne couvre l’essentiel des besoins ; Python (SymPy et SciPy) 
                  peut être appelé en complément pour le calcul formel et numérique étendu.

description:      (English) This package provides a new LuaLaTeX document class for teachers who want print-ready worksheets without 
                  writing LaTeX. Documents are written in a French-only prose tag language (no anglicisms), which the class 
                  translates to LaTeX at compile time. It covers layout frames and grids, tables, images, a math mini-language 
                  (fractions, sums, integrals, derivatives, matrices), function plotting, plane and solid geometry, and 
                  statistics/probability diagrams. An internal computation engine handles most needs; Python (SymPy/SciPy) 
                  can be used for extended symbolic and numeric computation.

texgit -- Download, access, and potentially execute files from git
------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/texgit
name:             texgit
caption:          Download, access, and potentially execute files from git
author:           Thomas Weise
copyright:        Thomas Weise (2023-2025)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.9.7 (2025-06-26)
last changes:     2025-06-26
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This package allows you to do the following things:

                  + download files from a  git repository and access them from LaTeX,
                  + apply some post-processor to the downloaded files (e.g., strip comments and type hints from Python code) 
                    and access the post-processed files instead,
                  + execute scripts or programs — either locally or downloaded from  git repositories — and fetch their 
                    output into local files accessible from LaTeX,
                  + create local paths accessible from LaTeX which can be passed as arguments to the scripts or programs 
                    that are executed, e.g., as argument to a Python script that creates and stores a “matplotlib” plot under 
                    the path that it received as argument, allowing you to programmatically create figures and include them 
                    in LaTeX documents.
The package works a bit like  BibTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex) : Let’s say your document is named document.tex . During the first pdflatex run, executed as |pdflatex document| , all the requests mentioned above, say, to download files from git repositories, are stored in the aux file. The paths corresponding to the requests point to an empty file at this stage. Then you would apply the texgit post-processor by calling |python3 -m texgit.run document| . This Python program (https://pypi.org/project/texgit) executes all the requests and caches their results locally. During the second run of |pdflatex document| , the paths corresponding to the requests then point to the actual downloaded or generated files. All downloaded or generated files will be locally cached in a folder named __git__ in your document’s directory. You can delete this folder to refresh the files.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/texgit/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/texgit/texgit-doc.pdf
-- local file:    ./9682386213-texgit-doc.pdf
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/thomasWeise/texgit_tex/issues
contact:          repository: https://github.com/thomasWeise/texgit_tex
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/texgit
on MikTeX:        texgit
keyword:          data-import (importing data into documents)

version:          2026.9999-2
description:      (no language specified) The package solves a problem relating to use of TeX Live under a Linux distribution: Linux distributions 
                  typically require LaTeX by default, but only distribute a rather out-of-date version. So, by default, 
                  the user who wants to use current TeX Live has to undertake “dirty tricks” to override the default Linux 
                  TeX.

                  The solution is to declare that LaTeX is already installed; a later installation of TeX Live will therefore 
                  have no problem running on the system. The present package solves the problem for openSUSE Linux distributions.

texlogsieve -- Filter and summarize LaTeX log files
---------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/texlogsieve
name:             texlogsieve
caption:          Filter and summarize LaTeX log files
author:           Nelson Lago
copyright:        Nelson Lago (2021-2026)

version:          1.6.1 (2026-01-12)
last changes:     2026-01-12
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) texlogsieve reads a LaTeX log file (or the standard input if no file is specified), filters out less 
                  relevant messages, and displays a summary report. It is a texlua script, similar in spirit to tools such 
                  as  texfot (https://ctan.org/pkg/texfot) , texloganalyser (https://ctan.org/pkg/texloganalyser) , rubber-info 
                  (https://gitlab.com/latex-rubber/rubber) , textlog_extract (https://ctan.org/pkg/texlog-extract) , texlogparser 
                  (https://github.com/reitzig/texlogparser) , texlogfilter (https://gricad-gitlab.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/labbeju/latex-packages) , pulp 
                  (https://github.com/dmwit/pulp) , and others. Highlights:

                  + Two reports: the most important messages from the log file followed by a summary of repeated messages, 
                    undefined references etc.;
                  + The program goes to great lengths to correctly handle TeX line wrapping and does a much better job at 
                    that than existing tools;
                  + Multiline messages are treated as a single entity;
                  + Several options to control which messages should be filtered out;
                  + No messages are accidentally removed;
                  + The summary report is currently simple, but useful.

texmacs -- Structured text editor for TeX
-----------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/texmacs
name:             TeXmacs
caption:          Structured text editor for TeX
author:           Joris van der Hoeven
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          1.0.7.20
description:      (no language specified) TeXmacs is a “structured text editor” with special support for mathematical expressions. The typesetting 
                  quality of the produced documents is intended to be as high as possible, i.e., comparable to the quality 
                  of documents produced with TeX; The user interface aims to be as natural and powerful as possible. In 
                  particular, the text you see on the screen corresponds exactly to what you get after printing. TeXmacs 
                  comes with a typed lisp extension language. Like emacs, this allows you for instance to redefine keyboard 
                  and menu actions. TeXmacs can also be used as an interface for computer algebra systems. In particular, 
                  automatically generated mathematical formulas are typeset in a satisfactory way. It is possible to generate 
                  LaTeX and PostScript output from TeXmacs. After compilation, the LaTeX output will resemble the PostScript 
                  output, although we guarantee no complete compatibility between TeXmacs and TeX. It is also possible 
                  to import “well written” LaTeX documents. The present release includes an interface with Ghostscript, 
                  which enables you to include PostScript (and some other formats) of images.

texmate -- Comprehensive chess annotation in LaTeX
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/texmate
name:             TeXmate
caption:          Comprehensive chess annotation in LaTeX
author:           Federico Garcia-De Castro
copyright:        Federico Garcia (2005, 2006)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          2
description:      (no language specified) TeXmate formats chess games from very simple ascii input. The clean “           . e4 e5; 2. Nf3 Nc6; 3. Bb5 
                  a6 ” will produce the same results as the sloppier “            e4 e5; Nf3 Nc6 3.. Bb5 a6 ”. The resulting 
                  format is fully customizable.

                  There are 4 levels of commentary: 1 is the main game, 2-3 are commentaries. Each has its fonts, punctuation 
                  marks, etc., and these are also customizable. The package includes a tool for the creation of diagrams.

                  The package works in conjunction with  skak (https://ctan.org/pkg/skak) to produce diagrams of 
                  the current position automatically. For chess fonts, the package uses the chessfss (https://ctan.org/pkg/chessfss) system.

texnegar -- Kashida justification in XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX
---------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/texnegar
name:             texnegar
caption:          Kashida justification in XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX
author:           Hossein Movahhedian
copyright:        Hossein Movahhedian (2020-2021)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.1e (2021-02-09)
last changes:     2021-02-09
year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) In some cursive scripts such as Persian or Arabic, kashida is used to create justification. In this type 
                  of justification characters are elongated rather than expanding spaces between words.

                  The kashida justification in  xepersian (https://ctan.org/pkg/xepersian) has many bugs. Also it 
                  has problems with some fonts. The xepersian-hm (https://ctan.org/pkg/xepersian-hm) package was 
                  the first attempt to fix these bugs in xepersian (https://ctan.org/pkg/xepersian) , which uses 
                  the XeTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/xetex) engine.

                  This package extends the kashida justification to be used with the  LuaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/luatex) engine, 
                  too.

                  Explanation of the package name: 
 'Negar' , in Persian, is the present stem of 'negaashtan' meaning 
                  to design, to paint, to write; and as a noun it means “sweetheart, idol, beloved, figuratively referring 
                  to a beautiful woman, pattern, painting, and artistic design”.

texosquery -- Cross-platform Java application to query OS information
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/texosquery
name:             texosquery
caption:          Cross-platform Java application to query OS information
author:           Nicola Talbot
copyright:        Nicola Talbot (2016-2020)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.7 (2020-02-04)
last changes:     2020-02-04
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) This package provides a cross-platform Java application to query OS information designed for use in TeX’s 
                  shell escape mechanism.

                  The application can query the following:

                  + locale and codeset
                  + current working directory
                  + user home directory
                  + temporary directory
                  + OS name, arch and version
                  + Current date and time in PDF format (for TeX formats that don’t provide  \pdfcreationdate )
                  + Date-time stamp of a file in PDF format (for TeX formats that don't provide  \pdffilemoddate )
                  + Size of a file in bytes (for TeX formats that don’t provide  \pdffilesize )
                  + Contents of a directory (captured as a list)
                  + Directory contents filtered by regular expression (captured as a list)
                  + URI of a file
                  + Canonical path of a file
All paths use a forward slash as directory divider so results can be used, for example, in commands like 
                  \includegraphics .

                  There are files provided for easy access in TeX documents:

                  +  texosquery.tex : generic TeX code
                  +  texosquery.sty : LaTeX package
This provides commands to run  texosquery using TeX’s shell escape mechanism and capture the result 
                  in a control sequence. The category code of most of TeX’s default special characters (and some other 
                  potentially problematic characters) is temporarily changed to 12 while reading the result.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/texosquery/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/texosquery/texosquery.pdf
-- local file:    ./1554026692-texosquery.pdf
contact:          repository: https://github.com/nlct/texosquery
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/texosquery

caption:          A minimal (La)TeX distribution
author:           Zhenyu Wu
license:          gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
version:          0.3.6
description:      (no language specified) TeXRocks is a minimal (La)TeX distribution powered by Luarocks/Lux and LuaTeX. It has the following features:

                  
                  + virtual environment: all TeX packages are installed to  .lux/5.3/XXXXX-package_name@version/ , 
                    like nodejs's node_modules/ and python's .venv/ . After development of PDF, you can delete 
                    it safely, and it will not affect your next development of PDF.
                  + minimal: we only install required packages
                  + package version control: when you declare  latex-base == "2025.06.01-1" , it will install exactly latex-base 
                    (https://luarocks.org/modules/freed-wu/latex-base/2025.06.01-1) and no other versions! Pin the version 
                    like nodejs's package.json and python's requirements.txt 
                  + package installation in parallel: install many packages at the same time
                  + a server to host compiled TeX packages:  TeXRocks (https://ustctug.github.io/texrocks) 
                  + use Lua to develop TeX packages:  texmf (https://luarocks.org/m/texmf) 
We also provide some related TeX tools, like  kpsewhich (https://texrocks.readthedocs.io/en/latest/topics/kpathsea.md.html) and texdef 
                  (https://texrocks.readthedocs.io/en/latest/modules/texdef.html) written in Lua. See official website TeXRocks 
                  (https://texrocks.readthedocs.io/)

textcase -- Case conversion ignoring mathematics, etc
-----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/textcase
name:             textcase
caption:          Case conversion ignoring mathematics, etc
author:           David Carlisle
copyright:        David Carlisle (1997, 1998, 2019, 2022, 2023, 2025)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.05 (2025-02-16)
last changes:     2025-02-16
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) The textcase package offers commands  \MakeTextUppercase and \MakeTextLowercase which are 
                  similar to the standard \MakeUppercase and \MakeLowercase , but they do not change the case 
                  of any sections of mathematics, or the arguments of \cite , \label and \ref commands 
                  within the argument. A further command \NoCaseChange does nothing but suppress case change within 
                  its argument, so to force uppercase of a section including an environment, one might say:

                  \MakeTextUppercase{...\NoCaseChange{\begin{foo}} ...\NoCaseChange{\end{foo}}...} 

                  In current LaTeX this package is obsolete. You can use the standard  \MakeUppercase and \MakeLowercase , 
                  but it defines legacy names \MakeTextUppercase and \MakeTextLowercase .

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/textcase/textcase.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/textcase/README
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/davidcarlisle/dpctex/issues
contact:          repository: https://github.com/davidcarlisle/dpctex
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/textcase
on MikTeX:        textcase
on TeXLive:       textcase

keyword:          macro-supp (support for development of (La)TeX macros)

textfit -- Fit text to a desired size
-------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/textfit
name:             textfit
caption:          Fit text to a desired size
author:           Philip Taylor
author:           Sebastian Rahtz
copyright:        Sebastian Rahtz and Phil Taylor (1994)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          5
description:      (no language specified) Package to fit text to a given width or height by scaling the font. For example:  \scaletowidth{3in}{This} . 
                  (The job is done by calculating a magstep and applying it to the current font; thus “This” will 
                  be very tall, as well as very wide; to scale in just one dimension, use the facilities of the graphicx 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/graphicx) package.)

theanodidot -- TheanoDidot fonts with LaTeX support
---------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/theanodidot
name:             theanodidot
caption:          TheanoDidot fonts with LaTeX support
author:           Bob Tennent
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
license:          ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
version:          (2022-09-26)
last changes:     2022-09-26
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) This package provides the TheanoDidot font designed by Alexey Kryukov, in both TrueType and Type1 formats, 
                  with support for both traditional and modern LaTeX processors. An artificially-emboldened variant has 
                  been provided but there are no italic variants. The package is named after Theano, a famous Ancient Greek 
                  woman philosopher, who was first a student of Pythagoras, and supposedly became his wife.

                  The Didot family were active as designers for about 100 years in the 18th and 19th centuries. They were 
                  printers, publishers, typeface designers, inventors and intellectuals. Around 1800 the Didot family owned 
                  the most important print shop and font foundry in France. Pierre Didot, the printer, published a document 
                  with the typefaces of his brother, Firmin Didot, the typeface designer. The strong clear forms of this 
                  alphabet display objective, rational characteristics and are representative of the time and philosophy 
                  of the Enlightenment.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/theanodidot/README

thepdfnumber -- Print PDF numbers with minimal digits
-----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/thepdfnumber
name:             thepdfnumber
caption:          Print PDF numbers with minimal digits
author:           Heiko Oberdiek
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
copyright:        Heiko Oberdiek (2011)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          1.1 (2016-05-16)
last changes:     2016-05-16
year:             2016
description:      (no language specified) The package provides a command ( \thepdfnumber ) that converts its argument to a “canonical” form. 
                  Conversion strips all leading and trailing zeros (but leaves a leading zero if 0&lt; 'arg' &lt;1); 
                  it also strips + signs, and removes pairs of - signs.

                  The package is part of the  oberdiek (https://ctan.org/pkg/oberdiek) bundle.

thermodynamics -- Macros for multicomponent thermodynamics documents
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/thermodynamics
name:             thermodynamics
caption:          Macros for multicomponent thermodynamics documents
author:           Karl D. Hammond
copyright:        Karl D. Hammond (2022-2024)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.04 (2026-03-22)
last changes:     2026-03-22
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package makes typesetting quantities found in thermodynamics texts relatively simple. The commands 
                  are flexible and intended to be relatively intuitive. It handles several sets of notation for total, 
                  specific, and molar quantities; allows changes between symbols (e.g., A vs. F for Helmholtz free energy); 
                  and greatly simplifies the typesetting of symbols and partial derivatives commonly encountered in mixture 
                  thermodynamics. Changes of one’s notes from one textbook to another can be achieved relatively easily 
                  by changing package options.

                  The package offers a collection of macros and environments which are intended to make typesetting thermodynamics 
                  documents faster, more convenient, and more reliable. Macros include symbols for extensive, molar, specific, 
                  and partial molar properties; excess and residual (departure) properties; partial derivatives; heat capacities, 
                  compressibilities, and expansivities; saturation, mixture, and pure-component properties; Henry’s Law 
                  parameters and activity coefficients; changes on mixing, fusion, reaction, sublimation, and vaporization; 
                  and sets of all moles/mole fractions/masses/etc. being held constant in derivatives. Conversion of notes 
                  between textbooks is trivial for textbooks supported by the package, and more general changes in notation 
                  are also possible through package options.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/thermodynamics/thermodynamics.pdf
-- local file:    ./8884388327-thermodynamics.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/thermodynamics/README.md
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/thermodynamics
on MikTeX:        thermodynamics

license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          (2021-06-24)
last changes:     2021-06-24
year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) This package implements an idea by Thorsten G. for assessment using PDF quizzes produced by the  exerquiz 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/exerquiz) package. Thorsten not only wanted to pose multiple choice, multiple 
                  selection, and fill-in type questions, but also wanted to ask extended response questions that would 
                  be manually evaluated. Once the quiz is graded, the instructor may optionally pass the quizzes through 
                  an Acrobat action sequence to extract the student’s name and grade from the quizzes. The extracted information 
                  is saved to a tab-delimited TXT file. The instructor can later merge this file into a larger spreadsheet.

                  WARNING: Adobe Acrobat DC or Adobe Acrobat XI is required for post PDF-creation. Any PDF-creator application 
                  is supported.

                  number (or whatever shall be marked by the thumb marks) increases. Additionally an overview page/table

tib -- A bibliographic preprocessor
-----------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tib
name:             tib
caption:          A bibliographic preprocessor
author:           Hans-Peter Kolb
author:           Sebastian Kremer
author:           James Alexander
license:          noinfo = noinfo 
version:          (1989-12-11)
last changes:     1989-12-11
year:             1989
description:      (no language specified) Tib is a collection of four programs for making citations and reference lists in TeX documents. The main 
                  program, Tib, operates on a TeX file with incomplete or keyed citations, looks up the reference in a 
                  database, makes the complete citation and on command, makes a list of the references. The citations in 
                  the source document are enclosed in (non-TeX) escape characters which Tib recognizes. The output of Tib 
                  is another TeX file with complete citations and reference list formatted with a number of TeX control 
                  sequences and with definitions for these control sequences, ready to be processed by Plain TeX, LaTeX, 
                  or whatever.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/tib/tibdoc.pdf

                  command names with the tkz prefix instead of the original French pst names, and all option

tikz-feynhand -- Feynman diagrams with TikZ
-------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tikz-feynhand
name:             TikZ-FeynHand
caption:          Feynman diagrams with TikZ
author:           Max Dohse
copyright:        Joshua Ellis (2016)
copyright:        Max Dohse (2019)
license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
version:          1.1.0 (2019-08-19)
last changes:     2019-08-19
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) This package lets you draw Feynman diagrams using TikZ.

                  It is a low-end modification of the  TikZ-Feynman (https://ctan.org/pkg/tikz-feynman) package, 
                  one of whose principal advantages is the automatic generation of diagrams, for which it needs LuaTeX 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/luatex) . TikZ-FeynHand only provides the manual mode and hence runs in LaTeX 
                  without any reference to LuaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/luatex) .

                  In addition it provides some new styles for vertices and propagators, alternative shorter keywords in 
                  addition to  TikZ-Feynman (https://ctan.org/pkg/tikz-feynman) ’s longer ones, some shortcut commands 
                  for quickly customizing the diagrams’ look, and the new feature of putting one propagator “on top“ of 
                  another.

                  It also includes a quick user guide for getting started, with many examples and a 5-minute introduction 
                  to  TikZ (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) .

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/tikz-feynhand/README.md

tikz-karnaugh -- Typeset Karnaugh maps using TikZ
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tikz-karnaugh
name:             tikz-karnaugh
caption:          Typeset Karnaugh maps using TikZ
author:           Luís Paulo Laus
copyright:        Luis Paulo Laus (2017-2022)
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          1.5 (2022-02-15)
last changes:     2022-02-15
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) The  tikz-karnaugh package is a LaTeX package used to draw Karnaugh maps. It uses TikZ to produce 
                  high quality graph from 1 to 12 variables, but this upper limit depends on the TeX memory usage and can 
                  be different for you. It is very good for presentation since TikZ allows for a better control over the 
                  final appearance of the map. You can control colour, styles and distances.

                  It can be considered as an upgrade and extension of Andreas W. Wieland's  karnaugh (https://ctan.org/pkg/karnaugh) package 
                  towards TikZ supporting. Upgrade because uses TikZ for more option on typesetting and overall higher 
                  quality. Extension because it also supports American style and inputting the values as they would appear 
                  in the map or in the truth table. Complex maps with solution (implicants) pointed out can be generated 
                  with external java software (see documentation for details).

                  It supports both American and traditional (simplified labels) styles and from version 1.3 on American 
                  style is natively supported, therefore, no more addition work is required to typeset Gray coded labels, 
                  variable names etc. From version 1.4, two new macros allow typesetting a map much more similarly as it 
                  should appear. Original order, as the values appear in the truth table, still being supported.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/tikz-karnaugh/doc/tikz-karnaugh-doc.pdf
-- local file:    ./4804162068-tikz-karnaugh-doc.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/tikz-karnaugh/README.txt
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/tikz-karnaugh
on MikTeX:        tikz-karnaugh
on TeXLive:       tikz-karnaugh
keyword:          pgf-tikz (package uses PGF-TikZ)

description:      (no language specified) This package allows for drawing a map of a particle accelerator just by giving a list of elements — similar 
                  to lattice files for simulation software. The package includes 12 common element types like dipoles, 
                  quadrupoles, cavities, or screens, as well as automatic labels with element names, a legend, a rule, 
                  and an environment to fade out parts of the accelerator.

                  The coordinate of any element can be saved and used for custom TikZ drawings or annotations. Thereby, 
                  lattices can be connected to draw injection/extraction or even a complete accelerator facility.

tikzphysics -- TikZ-native shapes and anchors for classical physics diagrams
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

name:             tikzphysics
caption:          TikZ-native shapes and anchors for classical physics diagrams
author:           Vaibhav Blayer
copyright:        Vaibhav Blayer (2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0.0
description:      (no language specified) The package extends TikZ with reusable shapes, styles, keys,
    and geometric anchors for classical-physics diagrams. It
    provides contact surfaces and inclined planes, blocks and pulleys, and
    a curved optical lens. All objects use ordinary TikZ node and path
    syntax, accept unit-aware dimensions, and expose named and parametric
    anchors for composing larger diagrams.

caption:          A TikZ library for drawing tiles and tilings
author:           Andrew Stacey
copyright:        Andrew Stacey (2014-2023)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.0
description:      (no language specified) This package provides a  TikZ (https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf) library for working with tiles, tilings, 
                  and tessellations. Using it, one can define tiles, place tiles, deform tiles, and — in some cases — apply 
                  replacement rules to generate tessellations. It has pre-defined tiles for most of the Penrose tile sets 
                  and the aperiodical polykite tiles.

                  This is a replacement for the  penrose (https://ctan.org/pkg/penrose) package, renamed as it now 
                  deals with more extensive tiles than just the Penrose tile sets.

tipauni -- Producing Unicode characters with TIPA commands
----------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tipauni
name:             tipauni
caption:          Producing Unicode characters with TIPA commands
author:           निरंजन
copyright:        निरंजन (2021-2023)
license:          fdl = Free Documentation License (free)
license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
version:          0.7a (2023-02-13)
last changes:     2023-02-13
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) Package  TIPA (https://ctan.org/pkg/tipa) uses the T3 encoding for producing IPA characters. The 
                  package is widely used in the field of linguistics, but because of the old encoding, the output documents 
                  are less productive than Unicode-based documents.

                  This package redefines most of the  TIPA (https://ctan.org/pkg/tipa) -commands for outputting Unicode 
                  characters. Users can now use their beloved TIPA shortcuts with the benefits of Unicode, i.e. searchability, 
                  copy-pasting, changing the font and many more.

                  As this package needs the  fontspec (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec) package for loading an IPA 
                  font, it needs to be compiled with XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX.

                  This package can also be viewed as an ASCII-based input method for producing IPA characters in Unicode.

                  It needs the  New Computer Modern (https://ctan.org/pkg/newcomputermodern) font for printing IPA 
                  characters.

documentation:    Sample file (no language specified): pkg:/tipauni-commands.pdf
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): pkg:/tipauni.pdf

documentation:    Example of use (no language specified): pkg:/tipauni-example.pdf

on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/unicodetex/latex/tipauni

tlaunch -- A Windows GUI to run a networked TeX Live as if installed locally
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tlaunch
name:             tlaunch
caption:          A Windows GUI to run a networked TeX Live as if installed locally
author:           Siep Kroonenberg
copyright:        Siep Kroonenberg (2017)
license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
version:          0.5.3 (2017-06-29)
last changes:     2017-06-29
year:             2017
description:      (no language specified) TLaunch, or the TeX Live launcher, is a Windows GUI to run a shared or networked TeX Live. It takes care 
                  of all the configuration which would be done otherwise by a local installer.

                  The interface and file associations are configured via an ini file, which can be edited to give access 
                  to additional TeX-related software.

                  The author told us in March 2023: “Please move tlaunch to obsolete. It is TeX Live-specific, and already

tocdata -- Adds names to chapters, sections, figures in the TOC and LOF
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tocdata
name:             tocdata
caption:          Adds names to chapters, sections, figures in the TOC and LOF
author:           Brian Dunn
copyright:        Brian Dunn (2016-2024)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.07 (2024-01-20)
last changes:     2024-01-20
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) The tocdata package may be used to add a small amount of data to an entry in the table of contents or 
                  list of figures, between the section or caption name and the page number. The typical use would be to 
                  add the name of an author or artist of a chapter or section, such as in an anthology or a collection 
                  of papers.

                  Additionally, user-level macros are provided which add the author’s name to a chapter or section, along 
                  with an optional prefix and/or suffix, and add to a figure the artist’s name, prefix, and suffix, plus 
                  optional additional text. Author and artist names are also added to the index. Additional user-level 
                  macros control formatting.

                  tocdata works with the TOC/LOF formatting of the default LaTeX classes,  memoir (https://ctan.org/pkg/memoir) , koma-script 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script) , and with titletoc (https://ctan.org/pkg/titletoc) , tocloft 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/tocloft) , tocbasic (https://ctan.org/pkg/tocbasic) , and tocstyle 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/tocstyle) .

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/tocdata/tocdata.pdf
-- local file:    ./5250208271-tocdata.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/tocdata/README.txt

tokcycle -- Build tools to process tokens from an input stream
--------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tokcycle
name:             tokcycle
caption:          Build tools to process tokens from an input stream
author:           Steven B. Segletes
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.5 (2025-04-02)
last changes:     2025-04-02
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) The tokcycle package helps one to build tools to process tokens from an input stream. If a macro to process 
                  an arbitrary single token can be built, then tokcycle can provide a wrapper for cycling through an input 
                  stream (including macros, spaces, and groups) on a token-by-token basis, using the provided macro on 
                  each successive character.

                  tokcycle characterizes each successive token in the input stream as a Character, a Group, a Macro, or 
                  a Space. Each of these token categories are processed with a unique directive, to bring about the desired 
                  effect of the token cycle. If condition flags are provided to identify active, implicit, and catcode-6 
                  tokens as they are digested. The package provides a number of options for handling groups.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/tokcycle/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/tokcycle/tokcycle-doc.pdf
-- local file:    ./4129789187-tokcycle-doc.pdf
documentation:    Examples of use (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/tokcycle/tokcycle-examples.pdf
-- local file:    ./7993467531-tokcycle-examples.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/tokcycle
on MikTeX:        tokcycle
on TeXLive:       tokcycle

tokenizer -- A tokenizer
------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tokenizer
name:             tokenizer
caption:          A tokenizer
author:           Sascha Herpers
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          1.1.0
description:      (no language specified) A tokenizer for LaTeX.  \GetTokens{Target1}{Target2}{Source} splits source into two tokens at the 
                  first encounter of a comma. The first token is saved in a newly created command with the name passed 
                  as &lt;Target1&gt; and the second token likewise. A package option ‘ trim ’ causes leading 
                  and trailing space to be removed from each token; with this option, the \TrimSpaces command is 
                  defined, which removes leading and trailing spaces from its argument.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/tokenizer/tokenizer.pdf

tokmap -- Iterate over a token list expandably, without dropping spaces or braced groups
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tokmap
name:             tokmap
caption:          Iterate over a token list expandably, without dropping spaces or braced groups
author:           plante
copyright:        plante (2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) Usage:  |\tokmap &lt;command&gt; { &lt;tokens&gt; }| applies command over the token list tokens. Space tokens, left and right braces are replaced with the marker tokens \tokmap@space , \tokmap@bgroup , and \tokmap@egroup respectively (which are \ifx -equal to themselves exclusively). For convenience, command may contain multiple tokens. It is assumed that { and } are the only characters with category codes 1 (beginning of group) and 2 (end of group) respectively. Expandable.

                  This package may be used in LaTeX by  |\usepackage{tokmap}| , or in plain TeX and other formats by |\input{tokmap}| .

                  See the  visualtoks (https://ctan.org/pkg/visualtoks) package for an example application.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/tokmap/README.md

tokstools -- Tools for manipulating tokens
------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tokstools
name:             tokstools
caption:          Tools for manipulating tokens
author:           Christian Tellechea
copyright:        Christian Tellechea (2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.2
description:      (no language specified) This package is still in the experimental stage. Therefore, its behavior is not guaranteed to match the 
                  description in the manual, and bugs of varying severity may occur.

                  Additionally, some features, as well as their syntax, may be subject to change.

                  It requires any modern engine that supports etex primitives and can therefore be used with either TeX 
                  or LaTeX.

                  The tokstools package provides tools for manipulating tokens and implements “PEG”-style grammars in TeX. 
                  Predefined elementary patterns can be combined to form grammars that search for matches within tokens.

                  Two categories of macros are provided: 
                  + those operating on individual tokens ( |\toksdo| , |\tokscount| , and |\printtoks| );
                  + those operating on tokens that have matched a grammar ( |\ifpegmatch| , |\pegcount| , and |\pegreplace| )

documentation:    Package documentation (French): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/tokstools/tokstools-fr.pdf

caption:          Use TTF “Tolkien” fonts from the WWW with pdfTeX
author:           Ariel Barton
copyright:        Ariel Barton (2009)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.0
description:      (no language specified) The virtual fonts in this package allow the user to easily write English, Quenya and Sindarin in several 
                  modes with J.R.R. Tolkien's tengwar, cirth, sarati and valmaric scripts, using freely available TrueType 
                  fonts found on the internet.

                  Support is at very nearly the highest possible level; the point of this package was to avoid bizarre 
                  spellings or lots of special commands.

                  Fonts supported are Tengwar Annatar, Cirth Erebor, Sarati and Valmaric Eldamar, and (with a little more 
                  work) Tengwar Parmaite, Eldamar, Noldor, Quenya and Sindarin.

topiclongtable -- Extend longtable with cells that merge hierarchically
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/topiclongtable
name:             topiclongtable
caption:          Extend longtable with cells that merge hierarchically
author:           Paolo Brasolin
copyright:        Paolo Brasolin (2017-2020)
license:          mit = MIT License (free)
version:          1.3.2 (2020-04-12)
last changes:     2020-04-12
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) This LaTeX package extends  longtable (https://ctan.org/pkg/longtable) implementing cells that:

                  
                  + merge with the one above if it has the same content,
                  + do not merge with the one above unless the ones on the left are merged,
                  + are well behaved with respect to longtable chunking on page breaks,
                  + and automatically draw the correct separation lines.
The typical use case is a table spanning multiple pages that contains a list of hierarchically organized 
                  topics (hence the package name).

                  The package depends on  array (https://ctan.org/pkg/array) , expl3 (https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3) , longtable 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/longtable) , multirow (https://ctan.org/pkg/multirow) , xparse (https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse) , 
                  and zref-abspage (https://ctan.org/pkg/oberdiek) .

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/topiclongtable/README.md

topsection -- An un-numbered top level section
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/topsection
name:             topsection
caption:          An un-numbered top level section
author:           Alexander I. Rozhenko
copyright:        Alexander I. Rozhenko (2005)
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) The package implements a command  \topsection , which creates an un-numbered section at the top 
                  level (chapter in book- or report-like classes, section in article-like classes). The section is used 
                  when the table of contents, index, etc., are prepared, so that documents can in some sense be class independent.

                  In collaboration with the  nccsect (https://ctan.org/pkg/nccsect) package, the details of the \topsection may 
                  be written to the .aux file, and hence to the table of contents.

                  The package is part of the  NCC tools (https://ctan.org/pkg/ncctools) bundle.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ncctools/doc/topsection.pdf

tpslifonts -- A LaTeX package for configuring presentation fonts
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tpslifonts
name:             tpslifonts
caption:          A LaTeX package for configuring presentation fonts
author:           Stephan Lehmke
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          0.6
description:      (no language specified) This package aims to improve of font readability in presentations, especially with maths. The standard 
                  cm maths fonts at large design sizes are difficult to read from far away, especially at low resolutions 
                  and low contrast color choice. Using this package leads to much better overall readability of some font 
                  combinations. The package offers a couple of ‘harmonising’ combinations of text and maths fonts from 
                  the (distant) relatives of computer modern fonts, with a couple of extras for optimising readability. 
                  Text fonts from computer modern roman, computer modern sans serif, SliTeX computer modern sans serif, 
                  computer modern bright, or concrete roman are available, in addition to maths fonts from computer modern 
                  maths, computer modern bright maths, or Euler fonts.

                  The package is part of the TeXPower bundle.

tpx -- A drawing tool for Windows
---------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tpx
name:             TpX
caption:          A drawing tool for Windows
author:           Alexander Tsyplakov
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          1.5
description:      (no language specified) TpX is a lightweight, easy-to-use graphical editor for Windows platform for creating drawings and including 
                  them into TeX files in publication-ready form. It can also be used as a stand-alone editor for vector 
                  graphics.

                  The output is a file (with extension .TpX) containing the drawing as TeX code or as an \includegraphics 
                  link to an external file created by the program. The user can choose between several output formats. 
                  TpX saves its own data in TeX file comments so that the drawing can be loaded into TpX and edited again. 
                  This internal TpX format is based on XML and can easily be understood and edited.

                  TpX can import EMF/WMF pictures created by other Windows applications, including many applications producing 
                  scientific graphs. In most cases the result is nice, though sometimes the imported picture needs some 
                  manual editing. So TpX can be used as an EMF-to-any converter.

trace -- Make sensible use of TeX tracing in LaTeX
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/trace
name:             trace
caption:          Make sensible use of TeX tracing in LaTeX
author:           Frank Mittelbach
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
copyright:        The LaTeX Project (1993-2023)
copyright:        Frank Mittelbach (1999-2019)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.1f (2021-04-18)
last changes:     2021-04-18
year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) The package provides the means to suppress excessive (and usually unnecessary) tracing inside some particularly 
                  verbose parts of LaTeX (such as the font selection routines, or the  calc (https://ctan.org/pkg/calc) package's 
                  parsing of expressions).

                  The package therefore redefines a number of key commands to turn off tracing while they execute (those 
                  the author finds most annoying and noisy). Since it potentially modifies the content of other packages, 
                  the package should be loaded last in a document's preamble.

                  The package is part of the  latex-tools (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-tools) bundle in the LaTeX required 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/required) distribution.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools/trace.pdf

tracking -- Adjust tracking of strings
--------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tracking
name:             tracking
caption:          Adjust tracking of strings
author:           Dmitry A. Glazkov
license:          other-nonfree = License that prevents distribution (not free)
description:      (no language specified) Automatically adjust spaces between symbols in words or phrases to fit them into a specified length. 
                  Any chain of symbols (including spaces) in the current font may be treated.

                  Commands  \track{&lt;length&gt;}{&lt;string&gt;} (add space &lt;length&gt; , which may be 
                  &lt;0, after each symbol of &lt;string&gt; ), \fittrack{&lt;length&gt;}{&lt;string&gt;} (make &lt;string&gt; fit 
                  into width &lt;length&gt; , which may be smaller than the original width) and \ratiotrack{&lt;ratio&gt;}{&lt;string&gt;} (as \fittrack , 
                  with &lt;length&gt; replaced by &lt;ratio&gt; of the natural length of &lt;string&gt; ).

on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/tracking/tracking.sty

transparent-io -- Show for approval the filenames used in \input, \openin, or \openout
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/transparent-io
name:             Transparent-IO
caption:          Show for approval the filenames used in \input, \openin, or \openout
author:           Udo Wermuth
copyright:        Udo Wermuth (2022)
license:          gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
version:          (2022-04-30)
last changes:     2022-04-30
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) This package provides macros to make the file I/O in plain TeX more transparent. That is, every  |\input| , |\openin| , and |\openout| operation by TeX is presented to the user who must check carefully if the file name of the source is acceptable. The user must sometimes enter additional text and has to specify the file name that the TeX operation should use.

                  The macros require a complex installation procedure; the package contains  sed and bash scripts 
                  to do this on a UNIX-like operating system. Every installation is different from any other as password-protected 
                  macro names and private messages have to be chosen by the installer. Therefore, the files in the package 
                  cannot be used directly. The files carry the extension .org , and only after the user has performed 
                  an individual customization for a private installation the changed files are renamed and have the extension .tex . 
                  For details see the manual.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/plain/contrib/transparent-io/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/plain/contrib/transparent-io/Transparent-IO-doc.pdf
-- local file:    ./3401125531-Transparent-IO-doc.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/plain/contrib/transparent-io
on TeXLive:       transparent-io
keyword:          security (document security measures)
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14


tree-dvips -- Trees and other linguists' macros
-----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tree-dvips
name:             tree-dvips
caption:          Trees and other linguists' macros
author:           Emma Pease
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
version:          .91
description:      (no language specified) The package defines a mechanism for specifying connected trees that uses a tabular environment to generate 
                  node positions. The package uses PostScript code, loaded by  dvips (https://ctan.org/pkg/dvips) , 
                  so output can only be generated by use of dvips.

                  The package  lingmacros.sty defines a few macros for linguists: \enumsentence for enumerating 
                  sentence examples, simple tabular-based non-connected tree macros, and gloss macros.

version:          1.11 (2023-12-02)
last changes:     2023-12-02

description:      (no language specified) Provides the trigonometric functions  sin , cos and tan , for use in the graphics 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/graphics) and graphicx (https://ctan.org/pkg/graphicx) packages.

                  Before any trigonometric value is used, it must be pre-calculated, so a usage sequence might be  \CalculateSin{22.5} 
                  ... \UseSin{22.5} ; the argument may also be a LaTeX count, as in \UseTan{\value{mycounter}} , 
                  or a count register, as in \CalculateCos{\count@} .

                  The package is part of the  latex-graphics (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-graphics) bundle, which 
                  is one of the collections in the LaTeX ‘required’ (https://ctan.org/pkg/required) set of packages.

                  It contains Type 1 fonts converted from Metafont fonts and provides all of the EC and TC fonts. The glyph 
                  CharStrings are not optimized for size, and there are even some minor visual distortions from the original.

                  For an alternative, see the  cm-super (https://ctan.org/pkg/cm-super) package, which covers the 
                  EC/TC family as well as other fonts.
