tudscr -- Corporate Design of Technische Universität Dresden
------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tudscr
name:             tudscr
caption:          Corporate Design of Technische Universität Dresden
author:           Falk Hanisch
copyright:        Falk Hanisch (2012-2022)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.06o (2022-08-09)
last changes:     2022-08-09
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) The TUD-Script bundle provides both classes and packages in order to create LaTeX documents in the corporate 
                  design of the Technische Universität Dresden. It bases on the KOMA-Script bundle, which must necessarily 
                  be present.

                  For questions, problems and comments, please refer to either the  LaTeX forum of the Dresden University 
                  of Technology (https://latex.wcms-file3.tu-dresden.de/phpBB3/) or the GitHub “tudscr” repository 
                  (https://github.com/tud-cd/tudscr/issues) .

                  The bundle offers:

                  + the three document classes  tudscrartcl , tudscrreprt , and tudscrbook which serve 
                    as wrapper classes for scrartcl (https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script) , scrreprt (https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script) , 
                    and scrbook (https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script) ,
                  + the class  tudscrposter for creating posters,
                  + the package  tudscrsupervisor providing environments and macros to create tasks, evaluations and 
                    notices for scientific theses,
                  + the package  tudscrfonts , which makes the corporate design fonts of the Technische Universität 
                    Dresden available for LaTeX standard classes and KOMA-Script classes,
                  + the package  fix-tudscrfonts , which provides the same fonts to additional corporate design classes 
                    not related to TUD-Script,
                  + the package  tudscrcomp , which simplifies the switch to TUD-Script from external corporate design 
                    classes,
                  + the package  mathswap for swapping math delimiters within numbers (similar to ionumbers ),

                  + the package  twocolfix for fixing the positioning bug of headings in twocolumn layout, and
                  + a comprehensive user documentation as well as several tutorials.

                  + len, sum, min, max, mean, med, quantile, standard deviation, get item, position of item
                  + sort, add or set(*) items, filter, operations, composition(*), split(*), formatting and display

                  |

                  + len, sum, min, max, mean, med, quantile, écart type, get item, position d’un élément
                  + tri, ajout ou modification(*) d’éléments, filtre, opérations, composition(*), coupure(*), formattage 
                    et affichage
Le tout avec une syntaxe concise et d'un usage facile et intuitif :

                  |
              object.methode1.methode2...
| (*) : méthode non développable

turkce-sayi -- Automatic Turkish suffix handling for reference numbers
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/turkce-sayi
name:             turkce-sayi
caption:          Automatic Turkish suffix handling for reference numbers
author:           Sonat Süer
copyright:        Sonat Süer (2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0 (2026-06-11)
last changes:     2026-06-11
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) When a number in a Turkish document is generated by a cross-reference ( \ref , \pageref , \cite ), 
                  the correct form of any appended suffix depends on how that number is pronounced, an information that 
                  is not available at the time of editing. Specifying a suffix works for some numbers, but for others it 
                  silently results in incorrect output.

                  This package solves this problem at compile time via LuaTeX. It determines the phonological properties 
                  of the Turkish name of the number and applies the appropriate transformation rules.

documentation:    Package documentation (Turkish): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/turkce-sayi/dokumanlar.pdf
-- local file:    ./3514738946-dokumanlar.pdf

-- local file:    ./3755781325-ornek.pdf
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/turkce-sayi/README.md
home page:        https://github.com/sonatsuer/turkce-sayi-latex
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/sonatsuer/turkce-sayi-latex/issues
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/turkce-sayi
on MikTeX:        turkce-sayi
on TeXLive:       turkce-sayi
keyword:          turkish (documentation in, and support for typesetting Turkish)

tuzuk -- Turkish bylaws and regulations document class
------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/tuzuk
name:             tuzuk
caption:          Turkish bylaws and regulations document class
author:           Özcan Oğuz
copyright:        Özcan Oğuz (2021-2024)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0.0 (2024-03-13)
last changes:     2024-03-13
year:             2024
description:      (no language specified) The  tuzuk class provides a standardized format for writing bylaws and regulations in Turkish-governmental 
                  style. It includes features for creating numbered articles, subsections, and signature areas commonly 
                  found in legal documents.

                  'Features:' 

                  + Easy creation of numbered articles with the  \madde command,
                  + Section titles with  \bolumadi ,
                  + Automatic lettered lists with the  fikra environment,
                  + Built-in signature area formatting with  \imzalar ,
                  + Full Turkish language support.
Built originally for creating the regulation for Özgür Yazılım Derneği (The Free Software Association 
                  in Turkey),  https://oyd.org.tr/ (https://oyd.org.tr/) .

                  Explanation of the package name: “tüzük” in Turkish means “regulations”, as a document. For example, 
                  GDPR, which stands for “General Data Protection Regulation”, translates as “Genel Veri Koruma Tüzüğü”. 
                  In Turkish law, the non-profit associations have a “tüzük” as their constitution-like governing document.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/tuzuk/tuzuk-doc.pdf

type1cm -- Arbitrary size font selection in LaTeX
-------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/type1cm
name:             type1cm
caption:          Arbitrary size font selection in LaTeX
author:           David Carlisle
license:          lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
description:      (no language specified) LaTeX, by default, restricts the sizes at which you can use its default computer modern fonts, to a fixed 
                  set of discrete sizes (effectively, a set specified by Knuth). The type1cm package removes this restriction; 
                  this is particularly useful when using scalable versions of the cm fonts (Bakoma, or the versions from 
                  BSR/Y&amp;Y, or True Type versions from Kinch, PCTeX, etc.). In fact, since modern distributions will 
                  automatically generate any bitmap font you might need, type1cm has wider application than just those 
                  using scaleable versions of the fonts.

                  Note that the LaTeX distribution now contains a package  fix-cm (https://ctan.org/pkg/fix-cm) , 
                  which performs the task of type1cm, as well as doing the same job for T1- and TS1-encoded ec (https://ctan.org/pkg/ec) fonts.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/type1cm/type1cm-doc.pdf

caption:          Eliminate errors by enforcing the types of labels
author:           Gregory Seidman
author:           James Ashton
copyright:        Gregory Seidman (2001-2013)
license:          other-nonfree = License that prevents distribution (not free)
version:          1.1
description:      (no language specified) The package is provided to help users avoid cross-reference errors; it replaces  \ref with \figureref , \sectionref , \eqref , 
                  etc., so that you're forced to specify the kind of label you’re referencing. Each reference command also 
                  generates appropriate text automatically, so that instead of typing Figure~\ref{figure:key} , all 
                  you need is \figureref{figure:key} . The \label command is redefined to record the type with 
                  the label defined, so that each type of label has its own namespace.

typeface -- Select a balanced set of fonts
------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/typeface
name:             typeface
caption:          Select a balanced set of fonts
author:           Geoffrey Jones
copyright:        Geoffrey Jones (2012)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.1
description:      (no language specified) The package provides the means of establishing a consistent set of fonts for use in a LaTeX document. 
                  It allows mixing and matching the Type 1 font sets available on the archive (and it may be extended, 
                  via its configuration file, to support other fonts).

                  Font-set definition takes the form of a set of options that are read when the package is loaded: for 
                  each typographic category (main body font, sans-serif font, monospace font, mathematics fonts, text figures, 
                  and so on), a font or a transformation is given in those options.

                  The approach enables the user to remember their own configurations (as a single command) and to borrow 
                  configurations that other users have developed.

                  The present release is designated “for review”.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/typeface/README

description:      (no language specified) This package provides macros for measuring alphabet lengths (i.e. the length occupied by the characters 
                  “abcd…xyz”), em-widths and ex-heights, which may help in making typesetting decisions.

                  The package is compatible with pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, and XeLaTeX, and will accept font family switches 
                  defined via the  fontspec (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec) package.

                  The plan is that future versions shall be able to provide even more diagnostic tools, and some LuaTeX-specific 
                  special commands, too.

                  The package relies on the following other LaTeX packages:  expl3 (https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3) , array 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/array) , booktabs (https://ctan.org/pkg/booktabs) , and siunitx (https://ctan.org/pkg/siunitx) .

typog -- Typographic fine-tuning and micro-typographic enhancements
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/typog
name:             typog
caption:          Typographic fine-tuning and micro-typographic enhancements
author:           Chris Spiel
copyright:        Ch. L. Spiel (2024)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.5 (2025-10-27)
last changes:     2025-10-27
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This package provides macros for micro-typographic enhancements. It covers a variety of topics:

                  + Precise hyphenation control
                  + Disable/break ligatures
                  + Manual italic correction
                  + Extra kerning for slash and hyphen
                  + Raising selected characters (e.g. hyphen, en-dash, and em-dash)
                  + Aligning of the last line of a paragraph
                  + Filling of the last line of a paragraph
                  + Word spacing control
                  + Microtype front-end
                  + Slightly sloppy paragraphs
                  + Vertically partially-tied paragraphs
                  + Breakable displayed equations
                  + Setspace front-end
                  + Smooth ragged-right paragraphs
Moreover, typog provides an environment to flag interesting parts of the information deluge typically 
                  accumulating in a LaTeX log-file and an associated tool,  typog-grep , that selectively retrieves 
                  these parts.

version:          (2023-03-18)
last changes:     2023-03-18
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) ucalgmthesis.cls is a LaTeX class file that produces documents according to the thesis guidelines 
                  (https://grad.ucalgary.ca/current-students/thesis-based-students/thesis/building-thesis) of the University 
                  of Calgary Faculty of Graduate Studies (https://grad.ucalgary.ca/) .

                  It uses the  memoir (https://ctan.org/pkg/memoir) class, which provides very powerful and flexible 
                  mechanisms for book design and layout. All memoir commands for changing chapter and section headings, 
                  page layout, fancy foot- and endnotes, typesetting poems, etc., can be used. (Memoir is meant as a replacement 
                  for the standard LaTeX classes, so all standard LaTeX commands such as \chapter , \section , 
                  etc., still work.) Likewise, any of memoir ’s class options can be passed as options to ucalgmthesis , 
                  in particular 12pt to select 12 point type (11 point is the default).

ucs -- Extended UTF-8 input encoding support for LaTeX
------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/ucs
name:             ucs
caption:          Extended UTF-8 input encoding support for LaTeX
author:           Dominique Unruh
author:           David Carlisle
author:           Wolfgang Jeltsch
copyright:        David Carlisle (2022)
copyright:        Wolfgang Jeltsch (2011-2013)
copyright:        Dominique Unruh (2000-2001)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          2.4 (2023-11-09)
last changes:     2023-11-09
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) The bundle provides the  ucs package, and utf8x.def , together with a large number of support 
                  files.

                  The  utf8x.def definition file for use with inputenc (https://ctan.org/pkg/inputenc) covers 
                  a wider range of Unicode characters than does utf8.def in the LaTeX distribution. The package provides 
                  facilities for efficient use of its large sets of Unicode characters.

                  Glyph production may be controlled by various options, which permits use of non-ASCII characters when 
                  coding mathematical formulae.

                  Note that the bundle previously had an alias “ unicode ”; that alias has now been withdrawn, and 
                  no package of that name now exists.

ukdate -- Typeset date in a UK-ish form
---------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/ukdate
name:             ukdate
caption:          Typeset date in a UK-ish form
author:           Adrian Clark
license:          noinfo = noinfo 
version:          1.0
description:      (no language specified) Prints dates in a traditional English way: “&lt;day-of-week&gt; &lt;ordinal-day-of-month&gt; &lt;month&gt; 
                  &lt;year&gt;”, so for example “Thursday 2nd February 2006”. The ordinal letters (“nd” in the example) 
                  are underlined and raised.

                  Note that  Babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) British style also has an English date style, which 
                  has no day name, and which doesn't raise or underline the ordinal letters.

on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex209/contrib/misc/ukdate.sty

year:             without year
language(s):      nls: no language specified

uktex -- The UK TeX digest
--------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/uktex
name:             UK-TeX
caption:          The UK TeX digest
license:          pd = Public Domain Software (free)
description:      (no language specified) The UK TeX digest started (at a time when TeXhax was also available), at least partly justified by the 
                  oddities of internet access in the UK. The organisation of the digest was odd: a team of enthusiasts 
                  tried to provide answers to questions before the digest was published, so that readers would encounter 
                  a problem closely followed by a solution in the same issue.

                  Eventually, the UK TeX digest was merged with the TeXhax digest, and the merged list was run in the UK 
                  for a time, but without the distinctive experts group.

                  The archives are arranged by year, and run from 1987 to 1994.

on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/info/digests/uktex

description:      (no language specified) The package provides an  \ul (underline) command which will break over line ends; this technique

                  out (line through words) and crossing out ( /// over words).

underscore -- Control the behaviour of “_” in text
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/underscore
name:             underscore
caption:          Control the behaviour of “_” in text
author:           Donald Arseneau
copyright:        Donald Arseneau (1998, 2001, 2005, 2006)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          (2006-09-13)
last changes:     2006-09-13
year:             2006
description:      (no language specified) With the package,  \_ in text mode (i.e., \textunderscore ) prints an underscore so that 
                  hyphenation of words either side of it is not affected; a package option controls whether an actual hyphenation 
                  point appears after the underscore, or merely a break point.

                  The package also arranges that, while in text, ‘ _ ’ itself behaves as \textunderscore (the 
                  behaviour of _ in maths mode is not affected).

unfonts-core -- TrueType version of Un-fonts
--------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/unfonts-core
name:             unfonts-core
caption:          TrueType version of Un-fonts
author:           Koaunghi Un
license:          gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
version:          (2018-12-19)
last changes:     2018-12-19
year:             2018
description:      (no language specified) The Un-fonts come from the HLaTeX as type1 fonts in 1998 by Koaunghi Un, he made type1 fonts to use with 
                  Korean TeX ( HLaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/hlatex-fonts) ) in the late 1990's and released it under 
                  the GPL license.

                  They were converted to TrueType with the FontForge (PfaEdit) by Won-kyu Park in 2003.

                  Core families (9 fonts): 
                  + UnBatang, UnBatangBold: serif
                  + UnDotum, UnDotumBold: sans-serif
                  + UnGraphic, UnGraphicBold: sans-serif style
                  + UnPilgi, UnPilgiBold: script
                  + UnGungseo: cursive, brush-stroke

unicode-alphabets -- Macros for using characters from Unicode’s Private Use Area
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/unicode-alphabets
name:             unicode-alphabets
caption:          Macros for using characters from Unicode’s Private Use Area
author:           Mikkel Eide Eriksen
license:          cc-by-sa-4 = CC BY-SA 4.0 (free)
version:          (2023-02-27)
last changes:     2023-02-27
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) While Unicode supports the vast majority of use cases, there are certain specialized niches which require 
                  characters and glyphs not (yet) represented in the standard. Thus the Private Use Area (PUA) at code 
                  points E000–F8FF, which enables third parties to define arbitrary character sets.

                  This package allows configuring a number of macros for using various PUA character sets in LaTeX (AGL, 
                  CYFI, MUFI, SIL, TITUS, UCSUR, UNZ), to enable transcription and display of medieval and other documents.

unicode-data -- Unicode data and loaders for TeX
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/unicode-data
name:             unicode-data
caption:          Unicode data and loaders for TeX
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
author:           Joseph Wright
copyright:        The LaTeX3 Project (2015-2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
license:          other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
version:          1.19 (2025-09-26)
last changes:     2025-09-26
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This bundle provides generic access to Unicode Consortium data for TeX use. It contains a set of text 
                  files provided by the Unicode Consortium which are currently all from Unicode 8.0.0, with the exception 
                  of  MathClass.txt which is not currently part of the Unicode Character Database.

                  Accompanying these source data are generic TeX loader files allowing this data to be used as part of 
                  TeX runs, in particular in building format files. Currently there are two loader files: one for general 
                  character set up and one for initialising XeTeX character classes as has been carried out to date by 
                  unicode-letters.tex .

                  The source data are distributed in accordance with the license stipulated by the Unicode Consortium. 
                  The bundle as a whole is co-ordinated by the LaTeX3 Project as a general resource for TeX users.

caption:          Give notes a unique front page for every chapter and section

version:          1.0 (2023-05-07)
last changes:     2023-05-07
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) This package can help you format your notes easily and give them a unique front page for every chapter 
                  and section.

                  It calculates your progress and then displays the progress bar under the title.

                  It also displays a partial table of contents under every progress bar and only shows the subdirectories 
                  of the current part.

                  To generate this, you can simply enter your current completed titles with a command that accepts Variable 
                  Arguments. Still, that also helps you review your notes.

                  You can also customise the colour of the bar.

version:          0.2 (2022-04-29)
last changes:     2022-04-29
year:             2022
description:      (no language specified) LaTeX produces small caps with  |\textsc{text}| or {\scshape text} . Neither of these commands produce small caps in Unicode. If the output text is copied and pasted somewhere it shows the same characters as used in the input. This package aims to internally convert all the characters provided to the commands mentioned above. It assumes that the file using this package is compiled with Lua/XeLaTeX and a good Unicode font which has the small caps characters, e.g., Charis SIL (https://ctan.org/pkg/charissil) .

caption:          Typesetting units in LaTeX
author:           Patrick Happel
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          0.2
description:      (no language specified) Many packages for typesetting units have been written for use in LaTeX2e. Some define macros to typeset 
                  a lot of units but do not suit to the actual font settings, some make the characters needed available 
                  but do not predefine any unit. This package tries to comply with both requirements. It predefines common 
                  units, defines an easy to use interface to define new units and changes the output concerning to the 
                  surrounding font settings.

upquote -- Show “realistic” quotes in verbatim
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/upquote
name:             upquote
caption:          Show “realistic” quotes in verbatim
author:           Michael Covington
author:           Frank Mittelbach
author:           Markus Kuhn
copyright:        Michael A. Covington, Frank Mittelbach (2003)
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          1.3
description:      (no language specified) Typewriter-style fonts are best for program listings, but Computer Modern Typewriter prints  ` and ' as 
                  bent opening and closing single quotes. Other fonts, and most programming languages, print ` as 
                  a grave accent and ' upright; ' is used both to open and to close quoted strings.

                  The package switches the typewriter font to Computer Modern Typewriter in  OT1 encoding, and modifies 
                  the behaviour of verbatim , verbatim* , \verb , and \verb* to print in the “ ` and ' way”. 
                  It does this regardless of other fonts or encodings in use, so long as the package is loaded after the 
                  other fonts were.

                  The package does not affect  \tt , \texttt , etc.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/upquote/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/upquote/upquote.pdf
-- local file:    ./1879660046-upquote.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/upquote
on MikTeX:        upquote
on TeXLive:       upquote
keyword:          tagged-pdf (tagged PDF compatible)
keyword:          verbatim (verbatim typesetting, etc.)
year:             2003
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

url -- Verbatim with URL-sensitive line breaks
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/url
name:             url
caption:          Verbatim with URL-sensitive line breaks
author:           Donald Arseneau
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          3.4 (2013-09-16)
last changes:     2013-09-16
year:             2013
description:      (no language specified) The command  \url is a form of verbatim command that allows linebreaks at certain characters or 
                  combinations of characters, accepts reconfiguration, and can usually be used in the argument to another 
                  command. (The \urldef command provides robust commands that serve in cases when \url doesn't 
                  work in an argument.) The command is intended for email addresses, hypertext links, directories/paths, 
                  etc., which normally have no spaces, so by default the package ignores spaces in its argument. However, 
                  a package option “allows spaces”, which is useful for operating systems where spaces are a common part 
                  of file names.

user-persona -- Typesetting User Persona sheets for UX and HCI (Human-Computer Interaction)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/user-persona
name:             user-persona
caption:          Typesetting User Persona sheets for UX and HCI (Human-Computer Interaction)
author:           Claire Tam
copyright:        fractuscontext (2026)
copyright:        Claire Tam (2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.0.0
description:      (no language specified) This package provides a structured environment and command set for typesetting professional user persona 
                  sheets in LaTeX. A user persona is a research-grounded representation of a target user group, synthesizing 
                  observed behaviours, goals, and frustrations into a humanized archetype (Cooper, 1999).

                  The package is intended for User Experience (UX) researchers, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) practitioners, 
                  and product designers who maintain documentation within a LaTeX workflow.

                  The central  persona environment produces a two-column layout comprising a portrait image, an identity 
                  table, a pull-quote, and a set of colour-coded content cards. Cards may be placed in the left column, 
                  right column, or as a full-width span below both columns. Predefined semantic colours are supplied for 
                  common persona sections (Goals, Behaviours, Pain Points,Context). Inline pill labels and icon badges 
                  are supported via \personapill and \personabrand (using fontawesome5 (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontawesome5) ).

varioref -- Intelligent page references
---------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/varioref
name:             varioref
caption:          Intelligent page references
author:           Frank Mittelbach
copyright:        The LaTeX3 Project et al. (1993-2023)
copyright:        Frank Mittelbach (1992-2020)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.6i (2026-05-04)
last changes:     2026-05-04
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) The package introduces commands  \vref and \vpageref . The \vref command refers to 
                  labels in the same way as does \ref , but if the thing referred to is on a different page, the 
                  result will be decorated with “on the facing page” or “on page &lt;n&gt;”, and so on, as appropriate. 
                  The \vpageref command similarly decorates a page number; there are also commands \vrefrange and \vpagerefrange for 
                  ranges of labels.

                  The package is language-sensitive, and has definitions for its ‘decorative’ words in several languages.

                  The package is part of the  latex-tools (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-tools) bundle in the LaTeX required 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/required) distribution.

documentation:    The document itself (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools/varioref.pdf

on MikTeX:        latex-tools
on TeXLive:       tools

description:      (no language specified) The package provides a  verbbox environment (which uses techniques similar to those of the boxedverbatim environment 
                  of the moreverb (https://ctan.org/pkg/moreverb) package) to place its contents into a globally

                  part of any LaTeX distribution).

verbdef -- Define commands which expand to verbatim text

caption:          Define commands which expand to verbatim text
author:           David Carlisle
author:           Robin Fairbairns
license:          lppl1.1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.1 
version:          0.2
description:      (no language specified) The package defines a single command  \verbdef (which has a *-form, like \verb ). \verbdef will 
                  define a robust command whose body expands to verbatim text. By using commands defined by \verbdef , 
                  one can put verbatim text into the arguments of commands; since the defined command is robust, it doesn't 
                  matter if the argument is moving. (Full details of syntax and caveats about use are in comments in the 
                  file itself.)

version:          (2021-02-05)

year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) Virtual font metrics are usually created in a textual form, the Virtual Property List, but programs that 
                  use them need to use binary files (the Virtual Font and the TeX Font Metric). The present two programs 
                  translate between the two forms:
– vptovf takes a VPL file and generates a VF file and a TFM file;
– 
                  vftovp takes a VF file and a TFM file and generates a VPL file.

                  The programs are to be found in every distribution of TeX.

                  by a vector of articulation parameters according to the  'S. Maeda' model. Animation may be achieved 
                  by providing a sequence of vectors over time (e.g., from Matlab). A sequence of vectors for certain German 
                  phonemes is embedded in the package, which allows for animation when no other vector is available.

vowel -- Draw vowel charts for phonetic research
------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/vowel
name:             vowel
caption:          Draw vowel charts for phonetic research
author:           Fukui Rei
copyright:        Fukui Rei (2002)
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          1.1
description:      (no language specified) Vowel inventories are usually displayed on a quadrilateral whose axes represent height and backness.

web2w -- Converting TeX from WEB to CWEB
----------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/web2w
name:             web2w
caption:          Converting TeX from WEB to CWEB
author:           Martin Ruckert
copyright:        Martin Ruckert (2017)
license:          gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
version:          0.4
description:      (no language specified) This package contains a project to convert the TeX source code written by Donald E. Knuth as a WEB into 
                  a CWEB.

                  A WEB is a literate program, i.e. a program which is written as a form of literature and consequently 
                  published as a book. Of course there is a way of converting such a piece of literature into an ordinary 
                  program: it contains Pascal code. 
Over the years, the support for Pascal as a major programming language 
                  has decreased and Pascal was replaced by C as the system programming language of choice. Consequently, 
                  WEB was replaced by CWEB, leading to the obvious question: can we convert the TeX source code to CWEB. 
                  And the answer is: yes and no.

                  No, because TeX is rather a large program, so translating it manually is very expensive, and translating 
                  literature by means of an automatic process is not feasible either.

                  Yes, because the program contained in this project, a literate program itself, is specifically tailored 
                  to the TeX source code and achieves a good approximation to such a translation.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/web/web2w/README
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/web/web2w/web2w.pdf
-- local file:    ./6403185392-web2w.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/web/web2w
keyword:          litprog (literate programming)
year:             2017
language(s):      nls: no language specified
last access:      2026-07-14

withargs -- In-place argument substitution
------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/withargs
name:             withargs
caption:          In-place argument substitution
author:           Michiel Helvensteijn
copyright:        Michiel Helvensteijn (2013-2016)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.3.1 (2019-11-04)
last changes:     2019-11-04
year:             2019
description:      (no language specified) The  \withargs command provides a clean way to populate
    a template (containing #1 , #2 , etc.) using
    LaTeX argument substitution.
    It also allows you to carefully control argument expansion using
    a LaTeX3-style argument specification.
    Uses range from creating readable string templates (akin to
    C’s printf function) to performing otherwise

                  languages, the  LH font set (https://ctan.org/pkg/lh) , or an Unicode font that offers cyrillic 
                  glyphs, is necessary. The LH fonts are also available in Adobe Type 1 format as part of the CM-super

                  by the same author. However, as of 2017-03-05, some features of assoccnt (https://ctan.org/pkg/assoccnt) are 
                  not (yet) contained in xassoccnt so that the older package cannot yet be regarded as obsolete.

xbmks -- Create a cross-document bookmark tree
----------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/xbmks
name:             xbmks
caption:          Create a cross-document bookmark tree
author:           Donald P. Story
copyright:        D. P. Story (2016-2018)
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          (2020-01-16)
last changes:     2020-01-16
year:             2020
description:      (no language specified) The package defines the concept of a document bundle, which is a collection of documents that are to 
                  be built separately, but have a common bookmark tree.

                  The only options are driver options, these are dvips (Acrobat Distiller or ps2pdf these can be used as 
                  the PDF creator), pdfLaTeX (and LuaLaTeX, which is treated the same as pdfLaTeX), and XeLaTeX.

                  The package auto-detects pdfLaTeX and XeLaTeX, and dvips is the default, so there is actually no need 
                  to pass the driver option.

version:          (2026-04-28)
last changes:     2026-04-28
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) Coffins are boxes which contain typeset material. Along with the box itself, the coffin structure holds 
                  information about the size and shape of the box, and alignment information in the form of a set of “poles” 
                  (horizontal and vertical lines at particular positions defined relative to the box). The points where 
                  these poles intersect are “handles”, which are the points used to define the placing of a coffin.

                  The package provides a design-level interface to the LaTeX 3 kernel functions which provide coffins.

                  The package is part of the  l3experimental (https://ctan.org/pkg/l3experimental) bundle.

version:          1.40 (2024-11-03)

description:      (no language specified) The package defines an environment that  'only' typesets specified environments within its scope.

                  So, for example, if you want nothing but the  figure and table environments in your document, 
                  you can enclose the whole document with an xcomment environment that excludes everything but. This 
                  is a lot easier than excluding the chunks of text between the environments you want, or creating an entire

                  The package was previously part of the  seminar (https://ctan.org/pkg/seminar) bundle for typesetting 
                  presentations.

xdoc -- Extending the LaTeX doc system
--------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/xdoc
name:             xdoc
caption:          Extending the LaTeX doc system
author:           Lars Hellström
license:          lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
version:          prot2.5
description:      (no language specified) Xdoc is a project to rewrite the implementation of the LaTeX doc package (in a broader sense) to make 
                  its features more general and flexible. For example, where doc only provides commands for documenting 
                  macros and environments, xdoc also provides commands for similarly documenting package options and switches. 
                  This is furthermore done in such a way that it is very easy to add more such commands for documenting 
                  things, such as e.g., templates (an important concept in the future LaTeX3) and program components for 
                  other languages (functions, classes, procedures, etc.). A side effect is that many minor bugs in doc 
                  are fixed.

                  The design aims to take advantage of many still experimental features of future versions of LaTeX, but 
                  since these are neither reasonably stable nor widely available, the configuration interfaces and package 
                  author commands of xdoc are likely to change. To still provide a stable interface for other packages 
                  to build upon, the actual package names include a “major version number” of sorts. The drop-in replacement 
                  package for standard doc is xdoc2; it requires nothing outside standard LaTeX2e.

                  The  docindex / docidx2e package changes the index and list of changes typesetting so that 
                  none of the formatting has to be controlled via the index style file. The docindex package provides control 
                  of formatting via templates (nice interface, but requires several experimental packages), whereas the 
                  docidx2e package has traditional raw macro interfaces and works with standard LaTeX2e.

documentation:    Package Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xdoc/README
documentation:    docindex documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xdoc/docindex.pdf
-- local file:    ./8997781949-docindex.pdf
documentation:    xdoc2 documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xdoc/xdoc2.pdf
-- local file:    ./1523030747-xdoc2.pdf
documentation:    Demonstration of usage (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xdoc/xdocdemo.pdf

description:      (no language specified) This LaTeX package bundle offers support for  xdvipsk , an extension of the dvips (https://ctan.org/pkg/dvips) binary.

                  xdvipsk supports BMP, PCX, TIFF, JPEG, and PNG formats and performs scaling, rotating, trim, and 
                  viewport operations like EPS images. The xdvispk.def driver for the graphics package offers a LaTeX 
                  interface. However, it lacks clipping, trimming, and viewport operations.

                  The LuaLaTeX package  xdvipskmaps provides OpenType font support for xdvipsk . It generates 
                  map files containing information about OpenType fonts used in DVI files.

xetex -- An extended variant of TeX for use with Unicode sources
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/xetex
name:             xetex
caption:          An extended variant of TeX for use with Unicode sources
author:           The TeX Live Team
author:           Jonathan Kew
author:           Arthur Rosendahl
author:           Khaled Hosny
license:          x11 = X11 License (free)
description:      (no language specified) XeTeX is a TeX typesetting engine using Unicode and supporting modern font technologies such as OpenType, 
                  TrueType or Apple Advanced Typography (AAT), including OpenType mathematics fonts. XeTeX supports many 
                  extensions that reflect its origins in linguistic research; it also supports micro-typography (as available 
                  in pdfTeX). XeTeX was developed by the  SIL (https://scripts.sil.org/xetex) (the first version 
                  was specifically developed for those studying linguistics, and using Macintosh computers).

                  XeTeX’s immediate output is an extended variant of DVI format, which is ordinarily processed by a tightly 
                  bound processor (called  xdvipdfmx ), that produces PDF.

                  XeTeX is released as part of TeX Live; documentation has arisen separately. Source code is available 
                  from  ctan:/systems/texlive/Source/ (https://mirror.ctan.org/systems/texlive/Source/) .

xfp -- Interface to the LaTeX3 floating point unit
--------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/xfp
name:             xfp
caption:          Interface to the LaTeX3 floating point unit
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
copyright:        The LaTeX3 Project (2017-2024)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          (2025-10-09)
last changes:     2025-10-09
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This package is deprecated in favor of methods integrated into the LaTeX kernel from 2022-06-01.

                  This package provides a LaTeX2e document-level interface to the LaTeX3 floating point unit (part of  expl3 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3) ).

                  The expandable command  \fpeval takes as its argument a floating point expression and will produce 
                  a result using the normal rules of mathematics. As this command is expandable it can be used where TeX 
                  requires a number and for example within a low-level \edef operation to give a purely numerical 
                  result.

                  From 2022-06-01 release of LaTeX this will be included in the format so that the package doesn't need 
                  loading any longer.

xgreek -- Greek Language Support for XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX
---------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/xgreek
name:             xgreek
caption:          Greek Language Support for XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX
author:           Apostolos Syropoulos
copyright:        Apostolos Syropoulos (2007-2026)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          3.5.1 (2026-07-06)
last changes:     2026-07-06
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package has been designed so to allow people to typeset Greek language documents using XeLaTeX or 
                  LuaLaTeX. It is released in the hope that people will use it and spot errors, bugs, features so to improve 
                  it. Practically, it provides all the capabilities of the greek option of the babel package. The package 
                  can be invoked with any of the following options:  monotonic (for typesetting modern monotonic 
                  Greek), polytonic (for typesetting modern polytonic Greek), and ancient (for typesetting 
                  ancient texts). The default option is monotonic .

                  The command  \setlanguage{&lt;lang&gt;} activates the hyphenation patterns of the language &lt;lang&gt; . 
                  This, however, can only be done if the format file has not been built with the babel (https://ctan.org/pkg/babel) mechanism.

xint -- Expandable arbitrary precision floating point and integer operations
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/xint
alias:            xintexpr
name:             xint
caption:          Expandable arbitrary precision floating point and integer operations
author:           Jean-François Burnol
copyright:        Jean-François Burnol (2013-2022, 2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.4o (2025-09-06)
last changes:     2025-09-06
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) Loading  xintexpr provides \xinteval and \xintfloateval .

                  \xintfloateval evaluates numerical expressions. The floating point precision defaults to 16 decimal 
                  digits and can be set by user. Trigonometry, exponential and logarithms are implemented up to a maximal 
                  precision of 62 decimal digits.

                  \xinteval computes exactly with integers, fractions, and decimal numbers or numbers in scientific 
                  notation. Note though that multiplying two floating point numbers will about double the number of digits, 
                  and so on, because the algebra is done exactly.

                  Both are compatible with expansion-only context.

                  Loading  xintexpr imports automatically various other modules that it depends upon. Among them:

                  
                  +  xinttools : utilities such as expandable and non-expandable loops,
                  +  xint : macros implementing in particular the basic operations on arbitrarily long integers,
                  +  xintbinhex : conversions between decimal and binary, octal, or hexadecimal bases for arbitrarily 
                    long integers,
                  +  xintfrac : macros implementing in particular the basic operations on arbitrarily large fractions, 
                    decimal numbers, or numbers in scientific notation.
Further modules of independent interest include  xintgcd , xintseries and xintcfrac .

                  You can use  xintexpr (and the other components) with LaTeX (via \usepackage ) or also with 
                  Plain TeX, OpTeX, or ConTeXt (via \input xintexpr.sty ).

                  All the components are documented in the file  xint.pdf , which also contains the commented source 
                  code.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): pkg:/xint.pdf
documentation:    Changes (no language specified): pkg:/xintchanges.md
documentation:    Readme (no language specified): pkg:/README.md
home page:        https://jfbu.github.io/xint
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/jfbu/xint/issues
contact:          repository: https://github.com/jfbu/xint
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/xint

xintsession -- Interactive computing sessions (fractions, floating points, polynomials)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/xintsession
name:             xintsession
caption:          Interactive computing sessions (fractions, floating points, polynomials)
author:           Jean-François Burnol
copyright:        Jean-François Burnol (2021)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.4alpha (2021-11-01)
last changes:     2021-11-01
year:             2021
description:      (no language specified) This package provides support for interactive computing sessions with  etex (https://ctan.org/pkg/etex) (or pdftex 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/pdftex) ) executed on the command line, on the basis of the xintexpr (https://ctan.org/pkg/xint) and polexpr 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/polexpr) packages.

                  Once xintsession is loaded,  eTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/etex) becomes an interactive computing 
                  software capable of executing arbitrary precision calculations, or exact calculations with arbitrarily 
                  big fractions. It can also manipulate polynomials as algebraic entities.

                  Numerical variables and functions can be defined during the session, and each evaluation result is stored 
                  in automatically labeled variables. A file is automatically created storing inputs and outputs.

xlop -- Calculates and displays arithmetic operations
-----------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/xlop
name:             xlop
caption:          Calculates and displays arithmetic operations
author:           Jean-Côme Charpentier
copyright:        Jean-Côme Charpentier (2005-2020)
license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
version:          0.28
description:      (no language specified) Xlop (eXtra Large OPeration) will typeset arithmetic problems either in-line or “as in school” (using 
                  French school conventions). So for example,  \opadd{2}{3} can give either $2+3=5$ or something 
                  similar to: \begin{tabular}{r} 2\\ +3\\ \hline 5\end{tabular} .

                  Furthermore, numbers may be very large, e.g 200 figures (with a very long compilation time). Many other 
                  features allow to deal with numbers (tests, display, some high level operations, etc.)

caption:          “Extras” for LaTeX users of XeTeX
author:           Will Robertson
copyright:        Will Robertson (2006-2018)

version:          0.7
description:      (no language specified) This package was previously used to provide a number of features that were useful for typesetting documents 
                  with XeLaTeX. Many of those features have now been incorporated into the  fontspec (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec) package 
                  and other packages, but the package persists for backwards compatibility. Nowadays, loading xltxtra will: 
                  load the fontspec (https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec) , metalogo (https://ctan.org/pkg/metalogo) , 
                  and realscripts (https://ctan.org/pkg/realscripts) packages; redefine \showhyphens so it 
                  works correctly; and define two extra commands: \vfrac and \namedglyph .

xmpincl -- Include eXtensible Metadata Platform data in pdfLaTeX
----------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/xmpincl
name:             xmpincl
caption:          Include eXtensible Metadata Platform data in pdfLaTeX
author:           Maarten Sneep
license:          gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
version:          2.4
description:      (no language specified) The XMP (eXtensible Metadata platform) is a framework to add metadata to digital material to enhance 
                  the workflow in publication. The essence is that the metadata is stored in an XML file, and this XML 
                  stream is then embedded in the file to which it applies. How you create this XML file is up to you, but 
                  the author started investigating this because he wanted to embed licensing information in the files he 
                  created. The license the author chose is one of the Creative Commons licenses, and their web-site offers 
                  this information in a valid XML-file, suitable for direct inclusion.

Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/xpunctuate
name:             xpunctuate
caption:          Process trailing punctuation which may be redundant
author:           Philip G. Ratcliffe
copyright:        Philip G. Ratcliffe (2012-2023)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.0 (2023-08-13)
last changes:     2023-08-13
year:             2023
description:      (no language specified) The package provides commands enabling the user (or package writer) to insert punctuation after a macro. 
                  The method is similar to that of  xspace (https://ctan.org/pkg/xspace) , but goes further.

                  The package provides the commands  \xperiod , \xcomma and \xperiodcomma , which follow 
                  a similar procedure to that of \xspace , and insert punctuation 'if and only if' it is necessary.

                  It also provides  \xperiodafter , \xcommaafter , \xperiodcommaafter and \xspaceafter , 
                  which all take one argument, the word or phrase to be punctuated. These then avoid problems with the 
                  spacing of periods and commas after emphasised words.

                  + LaTeX → dvips → ps2pdf/Distiller

xsipa -- Short XSAMPA-based commands for IPA transcription in LaTeX

author:           Josué Kouamé Akpoué

version:          1.0 (2025-05-16)
last changes:     2025-05-16
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This LaTeX package provides a lightweight phonetic transcription system inspired by XSAMPA. It translates 
                  modified XSAMPA sequences into proper IPA symbols, using either the  tipa (https://ctan.org/pkg/tipa) package 
                  (for pdfTeX users) or Unicode IPA symbols via xunicode (https://ctan.org/pkg/xunicode) (for XeTeX 
                  and LuaTeX users).

                  The package was designed to simplify phonetic transcription in LaTeX by offering concise macros such 
                  as  \xsE for \textepsilon , and \xs*...* as a shortcut for multi-symbol sequences (e.g., \xs*EO* for ɛɔ ). 
                  These commands are modeled after XSAMPA but adapted for LaTeX compatibility — including custom replacements 
                  for reserved characters.

xspace -- Define commands that appear not to eat spaces
-------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/xspace
name:             xspace
caption:          Define commands that appear not to eat spaces
author:           Morten Høgholm
author:           David Carlisle
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
copyright:        The LaTeX3 Project et al. (1993-2023)
copyright:        David Carlisle (1991-1997)
copyright:        David Carlisle, Morten Høgholm (2004-2006)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          1.13 (2014-10-28)
last changes:     2014-10-28
year:             2014
description:      (no language specified) The xspace package provides a single command that looks at what comes after it in the command stream, 
                  and decides whether to insert a space to replace one “eaten” by the TeX command decoder. The decision 
                  is based on what came after any space, not on whether there was a space (which is unknowable): so if 
                  the next thing proves to be punctuation, the chances are there was no space, but if it’s a letter, there’s 
                  probably a need for space. This technique is not perfect, but works in a large proportion of cases.

                  The package is part of the  latex-tools (https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-tools) bundle in the LaTeX required 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/required) distribution.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools/xspace.pdf
-- local file:    ./7013390408-xspace.pdf
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools
installation:     https://ctan.org/tex-archive/install/macros/latex/required/latex-tools.tds.zip
on MikTeX:        latex-tools
on TeXLive:       tools
keyword:          macro-supp (support for development of (La)TeX macros)
keyword:          tagged-pdf (tagged PDF compatible)

yathesis -- A LaTeX class for writing a thesis following French rules

description:      (no language specified) The purpose of  yathesis is to facilitate the typesetting of theses prepared in France, whatever 
                  the disciplines and institutes. It implements most notably recommendations from the Ministry of Higher 
                  Education and Research, and this transparently to the user. It has also been designed to (optionally) 
                  take advantage of powerful tools available in LaTeX, including packages:

                  +  BibLaTeX (https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex) for the bibliography;
                  +  glossaries (https://ctan.org/pkg/glossaries) for the glossary, list of acronyms and symbols list.

The  |yathesis| class, based on the |book| class, aims to be both simple to use and, to some extent, (easily) customizable.

                  |yathesis| comes with templates and samples in the |doc/latex/yathesis/french/exemples/| directory in the distribution. They can also be tested on Overleaf ( template (https://www.overleaf.com/latex/templates/template-of-a-thesis-written-with-yathesis-class/nhtmtthnqwtd) and specimen (https://www.overleaf.com/latex/examples/sample-of-a-thesis-written-with-yathesis-class/nbcfvfqgnjfq) ).

                  Note: The “ ya ” in the package name stands for “yet another”.

yax -- Yet Another Key System
-----------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/yax
name:             yax
caption:          Yet Another Key System
author:           Yuri Robbers
author:           Paul Isambert
license:          lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
version:          1.03
description:      (no language specified) YaX is advertised as a key system, but it rather organizes attributes in parameters, which parameters 
                  can be executed, so that YaX is halfway between key management and macro definition (and actually hopes 
                  to provide a user’s interface).

                  Values assigned to attributes can be retrieved and tested in various ways, with full expandability ensured 
                  as much as possible.

                  Finally, YaX’s syntax is a quite peculiar (as few braces as possible), but may be customized.

                  YaX is based on  texapi (https://ctan.org/pkg/texapi) and thus requires e-TeX.

                  etc.)

                  This is an alpha release, and should probably not (yet) be used with other packages, since the implementation 
                  might change. Nevertheless, the author uses it to document his own packages.

name:             yfonts-otf
caption:          OpenType version of the Old German fonts designed by Yannis Haralambous
author:           Daniel Flipo

license:          lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
license:          ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
version:          0.61 (2025-11-16)
last changes:     2025-11-16
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This is an OpenType version of the Old German fonts  yfrak (https://ctan.org/pkg/yfrak) , ygoth 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/ygoth) , yswab (https://ctan.org/pkg/yswab) designed by Yannis Haralambous 
                  in Metafont. The OpenType features make it easier to deal with the long/round s and with older forms 
                  of umlauts (small e over the letter).

                  A style file  yfonts-otf.sty is provided as a replacement, for LuaLaTeX and XeLaTeX, of yfonts.sty 
                  (https://ctan.org/pkg/mfnfss) or oldgerm.sty (https://ctan.org/pkg/mfnfss) .

yquant -- Typesetting quantum circuits in a human-readable language
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/yquant
name:             yquant
caption:          Typesetting quantum circuits in a human-readable language
author:           Benjamin Desef
copyright:        Benjamin Desef (2019-2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.9 (2026-01-03)
last changes:     2026-01-03
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This LaTeX package allows to quickly draw quantum circuits.

                  It bridges the gap between the two groups of packages that already exist: those that use a logic-oriented 
                  custom language, which is then translated into TeX by means of an external program; and the pure TeX 
                  versions that mainly provide some macros to allow for an easier input.

                  yquant is a pure-LaTeX solution — i.e., it requires no external program — that introduces a logic oriented 
                  language and thus brings the best of both worlds together. It builds on and interacts with TikZ, which 
                  brings an enourmous flexibility for customization of individual circuits.

documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): pkg:/doc/yquant-doc.pdf

zeckendorf -- Knuth Fibonacci multiplication, Zeckendorf and Bergman representations of big integers
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/zeckendorf
name:             zeckendorf
caption:          Knuth Fibonacci multiplication, Zeckendorf and Bergman representations of big integers
author:           Jean-François Burnol
copyright:        Jean-François Burnol (2025)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.9d (2025-11-16)
last changes:     2025-11-16
year:             2025
description:      (no language specified) This package extends the  \xinteval syntax to do algebra in Q(phi) (where phi is the golden ratio), 
                  and compute Fibonacci numbers, Zeckendorf representations of positive integers and Bergman phi-representations 
                  of the positive elements of Z[phi]. The $ character is used to compute the Knuth Fibonacci multiplication.

                  The package can be used either in a LaTeX document, or with Plain eTeX, or on the command line in an 
                  interactive session using eTeX.

                  Being based upon  xintexpr (https://ctan.org/pkg/xint) , it allows to compute with “arbitrarily” 
                  big integers, the reasonable use being with integers of at most a few hundreds of digits.

zref -- A new reference scheme for LaTeX
----------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/zref
name:             zref
caption:          A new reference scheme for LaTeX
author:           Heiko Oberdiek
author:           The LaTeX Project Team
copyright:        Oberdiek Package Support Group (2016-2026)
copyright:        Heiko Oberdiek (2006-2012)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          2.37 (2026-03-07)
last changes:     2026-03-07
year:             2026
description:      (no language specified) This package offers a means to remove the limitation, of only two properties, that is inherent in the 
                  way LaTeX’s reference system works. The package implements an extensible referencing system, where properties 
                  may be defined and used in the course of a document. It provides an interface for macro programmers to 
                  access the new reference scheme and some modules that use it.

                  Modules available are:

                  +  zref-user , use zref for “traditional” labels and references;
                  +  zref-abspage , retrieve absolute page numbers (physical pages, as opposed to the ‘logical’ page 
                    number that is normally typeset when a page number is requested;
                  +  zref-lastpage , provide a zref-label for the last page of the document;
                  +  zref-nextpage , provide the page number of the next page of the document;
                  +  zref-totpages , provide the total number of pages in the document;
                  +  zref-pagelayout , provide the page layout parameters of a each page (which may then be printed 
                    at the end of the document);
                  +  zref-perpage , make a counter reset for each new page;
                  +  zref-titleref , make section title or caption text available through the reference system; zref-savepos , 
                    make positions on a page available;
                  +  zref-dotfill , controlled dot-filling;
                  +  zref-env , record the latest environment’s name and the line it started on; and
                  +  zref-xr , provide the facilities of the xr (https://ctan.org/pkg/xr) and xr-hyper (https://ctan.org/pkg/xr-hyper) packages.

documentation:    Readme (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/zref/README.md
documentation:    Package documentation (no language specified): https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/zref/zref.pdf
-- local file:    ./9887065697-zref.pdf
contact:          bugs: https://github.com/LaTeX-Package-Repositories/zref/issues
contact:          repository: https://github.com/LaTeX-Package-Repositories/zref
on CTAN:          https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/zref

zref-check -- Flexible cross-references with contextual checks based on zref
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web page on CTAN: https://ctan.org/pkg/zref-check
name:             zref-check
caption:          Flexible cross-references with contextual checks based on zref
author:           gusbrs
copyright:        gusbrs (2021-2024)
license:          lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
version:          0.3.7
description:      (no language specified) This package provides an user interface for making LaTeX cross-references flexibly, while allowing to 
                  have them checked for consistency with the document structure as typeset. 

                  Statements such 
                  as “above”, “on the next page”, “previously”, “as will be discussed”, “on the previous chapter” and so 
                  on can be given to \zcheck in free-form, and a set of “checks” can be specified to be run against 
                  a given “label”, which will result in a warning at compilation time if any of these checks fail.

                  \zctarget and 
                  the zcregion environment are also defined as a means to easily set label targets to arbitrary places 
                  in the text which can be referred to by \zcheck .
